# Carbon Components Svelte

A complete [Svelte](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte) component library that implements the [IBM Carbon Design System](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/). Ship accessible, consistent, production-ready interfaces.

- **100+ components** -- from inputs to data tables
- **5 built-in themes** -- two light, three dark
- **Fully typed TypeScript API** -- props, events, and slots
- **WCAG 2.1 AA** -- keyboard and screen-reader ready

## Quick start

Install the library, pick a theme, and render your first component. Three steps to a running app, plus customization options below.

### 1. Install the package

```sh
# npm
npm i carbon-components-svelte

# pnpm
pnpm add carbon-components-svelte

# Yarn
yarn add carbon-components-svelte

# Bun
bun add carbon-components-svelte
```

### 2. Apply a theme stylesheet

Import one precompiled Carbon theme. The Carbon Design System supports five themes (2 light, 3 dark): White, Gray 10, Gray 80, Gray 90, Gray 100.

Import this once at the top-level, like `index.js` or `src/+layout.svelte`.

```javascript
// White theme
import "carbon-components-svelte/css/white.css";

// Gray 10 theme
import "carbon-components-svelte/css/g10.css";

// Gray 80 theme
import "carbon-components-svelte/css/g80.css";

// Gray 90 theme
import "carbon-components-svelte/css/g90.css";

// Gray 100 theme
import "carbon-components-svelte/css/g100.css";

// All themes (for dynamic theming)
import "carbon-components-svelte/css/all.css";
```

### 3. Import a component

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Button>Hello Carbon</Button>
```

Explore the full [component index](/component-index).

## Dynamic theming

To switch themes at runtime, import the combined `all.css` stylesheet instead of a single theme. It bundles all five themes and toggles between them through a `theme` attribute on the HTML element.

Import the stylesheet once, at the top-level entry point of your app:

```javascript
import "carbon-components-svelte/css/all.css";
```

Then set the theme reactively in Svelte:

```svelte
<script>
  let theme = "white"; // "white" | "g10" | "g80" | "g90" | "g100"

  $: document.documentElement.setAttribute("theme", theme);
</script>
```

Or statically in your HTML:

```html
<html theme="white"></html>
```

Or use the [Theme component](/components/Theme) to manage the theme reactively.

## Faster builds, smaller bundles

The fast path is enough to build. [carbon-preprocess-svelte](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-preprocess-svelte) trims build times and bundle size with three drop-in tools: faster HMR in development, and leaner CSS and JavaScript when you ship. Each works on its own.

Add carbon-preprocess-svelte as a dev dependency:

```sh
# npm
npm i -D carbon-preprocess-svelte

# pnpm
pnpm add -D carbon-preprocess-svelte

# Yarn
yarn add -D carbon-preprocess-svelte

# Bun
bun add -D carbon-preprocess-svelte
```

### optimizeImports

Rewrites barrel imports to direct source paths, dramatically cutting cold build and HMR times.

### optimizeCss

Tree-shakes unused Carbon CSS at build time, often removing hundreds of kilobytes from production bundles. In typical apps it removes 60-80% of the stylesheet. Set `propAware: true` to also remove styles for prop values your app never passes, which removes over 80%.

### optimizeComponents

Rewrites each Carbon component your app renders for the props it passes, removing branches and child components that can never run. In typical apps it removes 18-27% of the production JavaScript. Your own wrapper components are rewritten the same way when every place that renders them is in `content`. It runs on production builds only, and fails the build if a module outside its `content` globs renders a Carbon component or a rewritten wrapper, including through a re-export or a dynamic `import()`. For Webpack and Rspack, use `OptimizeComponentsPlugin`.

```javascript
// vite.config.js
import { svelte } from "@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte";
import {
  optimizeComponents,
  optimizeCss,
  optimizeImports,
} from "carbon-preprocess-svelte";

export default {
  plugins: [
    optimizeComponents(),
    svelte({ preprocess: [optimizeImports()] }),
    optimizeCss({ propAware: true }),
  ],
};
```

### Configure your bundler

Add `optimizeImports` to your Svelte preprocessor and `optimizeCss` to your bundler plugins.

**Vite:**

```javascript
// vite.config.js
import { svelte, vitePreprocess } from "@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte";
import { optimizeCss, optimizeImports } from "carbon-preprocess-svelte";

export default {
  plugins: [
    svelte({
      preprocess: [vitePreprocess(), optimizeImports()],
    }),
    optimizeCss(),
  ],
};
```

**SvelteKit:**

```javascript
// vite.config.js
import adapter from "@sveltejs/adapter-static";
import { sveltekit } from "@sveltejs/kit/vite";
import { vitePreprocess } from "@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte";
import { optimizeCss, optimizeImports } from "carbon-preprocess-svelte";

export default {
  plugins: [
    sveltekit({
      preprocess: [vitePreprocess(), optimizeImports()],
      adapter: adapter(),
    }),
    optimizeCss(),
  ],
};
```

On SvelteKit 2, pass the same `preprocess` in `svelte.config.js` and the adapter under `kit`.

**Rollup:**

```javascript
// rollup.config.js
import svelte from "rollup-plugin-svelte";
import { optimizeCss, optimizeImports } from "carbon-preprocess-svelte";

const production = !process.env.ROLLUP_WATCH;

export default {
  plugins: [
    svelte({
      preprocess: [optimizeImports()],
    }),
    production && optimizeCss(),
  ],
};
```

**Webpack:**

Rspack implements Webpack's plugin and loader APIs, so the same configuration works in `rspack.config.mjs`.

```javascript
// webpack.config.mjs
import { OptimizeCssPlugin, optimizeImports } from "carbon-preprocess-svelte";

export default {
  module: {
    rules: [
      {
        test: /\.svelte$/,
        use: {
          loader: "svelte-loader",
          options: {
            preprocess: [optimizeImports()],
          },
        },
      },
    ],
  },
  plugins: [new OptimizeCssPlugin()],
};
```

## Icons and pictograms

The icon and pictogram sets ship as separate packages of individual Svelte components. Both are professionally designed, original iconography crafted to complement the scale and grid of Carbon components. Each is optional, so install only what you need.

### Icons

2,700+ icons designed for product UI, in four sizes (16, 20, 24, and 32 pixels), set with a single prop.

```sh
# npm
npm i carbon-icons-svelte

# pnpm
pnpm add carbon-icons-svelte

# Yarn
yarn add carbon-icons-svelte

# Bun
bun add carbon-icons-svelte
```

```svelte
<script>
  import Add from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Add.svelte";
</script>

<Add size={24} />
```

### Pictograms

1,500+ illustrative pictograms for empty states, onboarding, hero sections, and feature callouts. Larger than icons, 64px by default.

```sh
# npm
npm i carbon-pictograms-svelte

# pnpm
pnpm add carbon-pictograms-svelte

# Yarn
yarn add carbon-pictograms-svelte

# Bun
bun add carbon-pictograms-svelte
```

```svelte
<script>
  import Cloud from "carbon-pictograms-svelte/lib/Cloud.svelte";
</script>

<Cloud />
```

## Documentation for LLMs

Documentation is available in LLM-friendly plain text for use with coding assistants, plus a standalone Markdown document for every component. Append `.md` to any component's URL to read it.

- **[llms.txt](/llms.txt)** -- A component index where each entry links to its per-component Markdown doc, sized for model context windows.
- **[llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt)** -- The full component documentation in a single plain-text file.

## Collection

The Carbon Svelte collection includes packages for icons, pictograms, and data visualization:

- **Carbon Components Svelte** -- 100+ components -- [GitHub](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-components-svelte)
- **Carbon Icons Svelte** -- 2,700+ icons -- [GitHub](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-icons-svelte)
- **Carbon Pictograms Svelte** -- 1,500+ pictograms -- [GitHub](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-pictograms-svelte)
- **Carbon Charts Svelte** -- 25+ charts, powered by d3 -- [GitHub](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-charts/tree/master/packages/svelte)
- **Carbon Preprocess Svelte** -- Svelte preprocessors and build plugins -- [GitHub](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-preprocess-svelte)

## Accordion

### Basic

Use the accordion and accordion item components to compose a collapsible list of items.

By default, the chevron icon is on the right side of the accordion item.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem title="Billing and invoices">
    <p>
      Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for
      your organization's subscription.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="API access">
    <p>
      Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook
      endpoints for programmatic access.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Team permissions">
    <p>
      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer
      workspace resources.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

### Layout

Adjust chevron alignment and container spacing. The two interact: flush has no effect when the chevron is left-aligned.

#### Left-aligned chevron

Align the chevron icon to the left side of the accordion item by setting `align` to `"start"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion align="start">
  <AccordionItem title="Billing and invoices">
    <p>
      Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for
      your organization's subscription.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="API access">
    <p>
      Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook
      endpoints for programmatic access.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Team permissions">
    <p>
      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer
      workspace resources.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

#### Flush

Set `flush` to remove the accordion's gutter, aligning it flush with the edges of its container. This works well in full-bleed layouts and side panels. `flush` has no effect when `align` is `"start"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion flush>
  <AccordionItem title="Billing and invoices">
    <p>
      Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for
      your organization's subscription.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="API access">
    <p>
      Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook
      endpoints for programmatic access.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Team permissions">
    <p>
      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer
      workspace resources.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

### Title

Customize the item heading content and its accessible name.

#### Custom title slot

Customize the title content with the title slot instead of the title prop for more complex layouts with multiple elements.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem>
    <svelte:fragment slot="title">
      <h5>Billing and invoices</h5>
      <div>Finance</div>
    </svelte:fragment>
    <p>
      Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for
      your organization's subscription.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem>
    <svelte:fragment slot="title">
      <h5>API access</h5>
      <div>Developer tools</div>
    </svelte:fragment>
    <p>
      Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook
      endpoints for programmatic access.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem>
    <svelte:fragment slot="title">
      <h5>Team permissions</h5>
      <div>Access control</div>
    </svelte:fragment>
    <p>
      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer
      workspace resources.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

#### Accessible label

Set `ariaLabel` to give the item's heading button an accessible name that's independent of its visible content. This matters when the title slot doesn't render readable text, such as an icon-only title, since screen readers would otherwise have nothing to announce for the control.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";
</script>

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem ariaLabel="Notifications">
    <svelte:fragment slot="title">
      <Notification />
    </svelte:fragment>
    <p>You have no new notifications.</p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

### Open state

Control which items are open by default, exclusively, or programmatically.

#### First item open

Set `open` on an item to have it expanded by default when the accordion is first rendered.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem open title="Billing and invoices">
    <p>
      Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for
      your organization's subscription.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="API access">
    <p>
      Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook
      endpoints for programmatic access.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Team permissions">
    <p>
      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer
      workspace resources.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

#### Single-open

Set `type` to `"single"` so that opening an item automatically closes any other open item. This is useful for FAQs, step-by-step wizards, or settings panels where only one section should be expanded at a time. The default is `"multiple"`, which allows any number of items to be open simultaneously.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion type="single">
  <AccordionItem open title="Billing and invoices">
    <p>
      Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for
      your organization's subscription.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="API access">
    <p>
      Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook
      endpoints for programmatic access.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Team permissions">
    <p>
      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer
      workspace resources.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

#### Programmatic example

Programmatically control the accordion items with the `bind:open` directive, expanding and collapsing items based on user interactions or application state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    {
      title: "Billing and invoices",
      description:
        "Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for your organization's subscription.",
    },
    {
      title: "API access",
      description:
        "Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook endpoints for programmatic access.",
    },
    {
      title: "Team permissions",
      description:
        "Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer workspace resources.",
    },
  ];

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button kind="ghost" size="field" on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
  {open ? "Collapse" : "Expand"}
  all
</Button>

<Accordion>
  {#each items as item}
    <AccordionItem title={item.title} {open}>
      <p>{item.description}</p>
    </AccordionItem>
  {/each}
</Accordion>
```

#### Reacting to toggles

Listen for `toggle` on an item to react when a user expands or collapses it. The event's `detail.open` is the item's next open state, so a parent can track which item was toggled and to what state without binding to `open`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    {
      title: "Billing and invoices",
      description:
        "Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for your organization's subscription.",
    },
    {
      title: "API access",
      description:
        "Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook endpoints for programmatic access.",
    },
    {
      title: "Team permissions",
      description:
        "Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer workspace resources.",
    },
  ];

  let lastToggled = "None yet";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <div>Last toggled: <strong>{lastToggled}</strong></div>
  <Accordion>
    {#each items as item}
      <AccordionItem
        title={item.title}
        on:toggle={(e) => {
          const { open } = e.detail;
          lastToggled = `${item.title} (${open ? "opened" : "closed"})`;
        }}
      >
        <p>{item.description}</p>
      </AccordionItem>
    {/each}
  </Accordion>
</Stack>
```

### Nested

Put an `Accordion` inside an `AccordionItem` to compose nested clusters. Nested items keep their own open state, independent of the parent.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Accordion,
    AccordionItem,
    Stack,
    Text,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem open title="Platform services">
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={6}>
      <Accordion>
        <AccordionItem open title="Authentication service">
          <Stack gap={5}>
            <Text type="body-01" color="secondary">
              Handles user login, session tokens, and single sign-on across all
              connected applications.
            </Text>
            <Stack gap={2}>
              <Text type="label-01" color="secondary">Region</Text>
              <Text type="body-compact-01">us-east-1</Text>
            </Stack>
          </Stack>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>
      <Accordion>
        <AccordionItem open title="Notification service">
          <Stack gap={5}>
            <Text type="body-01" color="secondary">
              Delivers email, SMS, and in-app alerts triggered by workflow
              events.
            </Text>
            <Stack gap={2}>
              <Text type="label-01" color="secondary">Region</Text>
              <Text type="body-compact-01">eu-west-1</Text>
            </Stack>
          </Stack>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>
    </Stack>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

### Lazy loading

Set `lazy` on an accordion item to defer mounting its panel content until the item first opens. Use it for panels with heavy content, such as API-fetched data or charts, so they mount only when needed. The content stays mounted after the item collapses.

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Set `lazy` on items with heavy content, or in long accordions most visitors only skim. | A collapsed item still builds all its content; `lazy` waits until the item first opens. |
| Leave it off when the content must be in server-rendered markup. | Deferred content isn't in the page until its item opens. |

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem lazy title="Billing and invoices">
    <p>
      Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for
      your organization's subscription.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem lazy title="API access">
    <p>
      Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook
      endpoints for programmatic access.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem lazy title="Team permissions">
    <p>
      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer
      workspace resources.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

#### Small

Set `size` to `"sm"` for a smaller accordion in compact layouts or when space is limited.

```svelte
<script>

      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer

```

### Disabled

Disable the whole accordion or individual items.

#### All

Set `disabled` on the accordion to disable all items at once. Users can no longer expand or collapse any item.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion disabled>
  <AccordionItem title="Billing and invoices">
    <p>
      Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for
      your organization's subscription.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="API access">
    <p>
      Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook
      endpoints for programmatic access.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Team permissions">
    <p>
      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer
      workspace resources.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

#### Batch

Programmatically toggle the disabled state of all accordion items. In this example, disabling all items also collapses them.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Accordion,
    AccordionItem,
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let disabled = false;

  const items = [
    {
      title: "Billing and invoices",
      description:
        "Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for your organization's subscription.",
    },
    {
      title: "API access",
      description:
        "Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook endpoints for programmatic access.",
    },
    {
      title: "Team permissions",
      description:
        "Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer workspace resources.",
    },
  ];

  let open = false;
</script>

<ButtonSet>
  <Button size="field" {disabled} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
    {open ? "Collapse" : "Expand"}
    all
  </Button>
  <Button
    kind="ghost"
    size="field"
    on:click={() => {
      disabled = !disabled;
      if (disabled) {
        open = false;
      }
    }}
  >
    {disabled ? "Enable" : "Disable"}
    all
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>

<Accordion {disabled}>
  {#each items as item}
    <AccordionItem title={item.title} {open}>
      <p>{item.description}</p>
    </AccordionItem>
  {/each}
</Accordion>
```

#### Item

Disable an individual item by setting `disabled` on a specific accordion item for finer control over which items are interactive.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem disabled title="Billing and invoices">
    <p>
      Manage payment methods, view invoice history, and download receipts for
      your organization's subscription.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="API access">
    <p>
      Generate and manage API keys, set rate limits, and configure webhook
      endpoints for programmatic access.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Team permissions">
    <p>
      Assign roles and control which team members can view, edit, or administer
      workspace resources.
    </p>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

### Skeleton

Use `AccordionSkeleton` to show a loading state while content loads.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AccordionSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AccordionSkeleton />
```

#### Left-aligned chevron

Align the chevron icon to the left side by setting `align` to `"start"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AccordionSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AccordionSkeleton align="start" />
```

#### Custom count

By default, the skeleton displays 4 items. Set `count` to specify the number of skeleton items to display.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AccordionSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AccordionSkeleton count={3} />
```

#### Closed

By default, the first skeleton item is open. Set `open={false}` to render the skeleton collapsed.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AccordionSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AccordionSkeleton open={false} />
```

#### Extra-large

Set `size` to `"xl"` for an extra-large skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AccordionSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AccordionSkeleton size="xl" />
```

#### Small

Set `size` to `"sm"` for a small skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AccordionSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AccordionSkeleton size="sm" />
```

#### Flush

Set `flush` to remove the skeleton's gutter, matching the flush variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AccordionSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AccordionSkeleton flush />
```

---

### Component API

#### `Accordion` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `"start" \| "end"` | Specify alignment of accordion item chevron icon. | `"end"` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Specify the size of the accordion.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (the 40px default) and `"lg"` (`"xl"`). | _undefined_ |
| `flush` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the gutter around the accordion, aligning it flush with its container.<br />Has no effect when `align` is `"start"`. | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the accordion | `false` |
| `skeleton` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to display the skeleton state | `false` |
| `type` | `"single" \| "multiple"` | Specify the expansion behavior of the accordion.<br />Set to `"single"` so that opening an item closes all other items. | `"multiple"` |

#### `Accordion` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Accordion` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `Accordion` $$restProps

`Accordion` spreads `$$restProps` to the `ul` element.

#### `AccordionItem` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the first accordion item. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLButtonElement` | Obtain a reference to the heading button HTML element. | `null` |
| `title` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the title of the accordion item heading.<br />Alternatively, use the "title" slot. | _undefined_ |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the accordion item | `false` |
| `ariaLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a custom label for the accordion button.<br />This is important for accessibility when the accordion has no visible title. | _undefined_ |
| `lazy` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to defer mounting the panel content until the item is first opened.<br />Once mounted, the content stays mounted for subsequent collapses. | `false` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the top-level element.<br />The heading button and panel ids derive from it as `{id}-button` and<br />`{id}-content`. | `uniqueId()` |

#### `AccordionItem` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `title`   | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `AccordionItem` forwarded events

| Event             |
| ----------------- |
| `on:animationend` |
| `on:blur`         |
| `on:click`        |
| `on:focus`        |
| `on:keydown`      |
| `on:mouseenter`   |
| `on:mouseleave`   |
| `on:mouseover`    |

#### `AccordionItem` dispatched events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on:toggle` | `{ open: boolean }` | Dispatched with the next open state after a header click. |

#### `AccordionItem` $$restProps

`AccordionItem` spreads `$$restProps` to the `li` element.

#### `AccordionSkeleton` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `number` | Specify the number of accordion items to render | `4` |
| `align` | `"start" \| "end"` | Specify alignment of accordion item chevron icon. | `"end"` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Specify the size of the accordion.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (the 40px default) and `"lg"` (`"xl"`). | _undefined_ |
| `flush` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the gutter around the accordion, aligning it flush with its container.<br />Has no effect when `align` is `"start"`. | `false` |
| `open` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to close the first accordion item | `true` |

#### `AccordionSkeleton` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `AccordionSkeleton` $$restProps

`AccordionSkeleton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `ul` element.


## ActionSet

### Basic

Use `ActionSet` for custom footers you compose yourself, typically [ComposedModal](/components/ComposedModal#custom-footer-with-actionset)'s `ModalFooter` slot. [Modal](/components/Modal) builds its footer from props and has no footer slot.

Compose `ActionSet` from ordinary `Button` children, the same way as [ButtonSet](/components/ButtonSet). `size` cascades to every child button that doesn't set its own `size`. The set fills with the current layer color, so a ghost action sits on the same surface as the others.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ActionSet, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ActionSet>
  <Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</ActionSet>
```

### Kinds

Buttons are ordered automatically by `kind`: ghost and `"danger-ghost"` first, primary and danger last. Reversed when the set stacks, so the primary action stays closest to the reading direction's end in both layouts. DOM order does not matter.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ActionSet, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ActionSet size="lg">
  <Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  <Button kind="danger">Delete</Button>
  <Button kind="ghost">Learn more</Button>
</ActionSet>
```

`ActionSet` warns in the console when its actions break Carbon's rules: one primary and one ghost action at most, four actions at most (three once they stack), and no ghost action in a stack with others.

### Sizes

Set `size` to control the layout. `"sm"` always stacks; `"md"` stacks once there are more than two actions; `"lg"`, `"xl"`, and `"2xl"` never stack and give actions progressively more room.

#### Small

```svelte
<script>
  import { ActionSet, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ActionSet size="sm">
  <Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</ActionSet>
```

#### Large

```svelte
<script>
  import { ActionSet, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ActionSet size="lg">
  <Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  <Button kind="danger">Delete</Button>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</ActionSet>
```

#### Extra large

```svelte
<script>
  import { ActionSet, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ActionSet size="2xl">
  <Button kind="ghost">Learn more</Button>
  <Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  <Button kind="danger">Delete</Button>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</ActionSet>
```

### Sticky

Set `sticky` to `true` to stick the action set to the bottom of its nearest scroll container. Use this for a save bar under a long scrolling form so the actions stay visible.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ActionSet, Box, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box height="8rem" border="subtle" overflowY="auto">
  <Box height="12rem" padding={5}
    >Scroll to see the sticky action set below.</Box
  >
  <ActionSet sticky>
    <Button kind="secondary">Discard</Button>
    <Button>Save</Button>
  </ActionSet>
</Box>
```

### Disable stacking

Set `disableStacking` to `true` to force a horizontal layout even at a size that would normally stack.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ActionSet, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ActionSet size="sm" disableStacking>
  <Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  <Button kind="danger">Delete</Button>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</ActionSet>
```

### Server rendering

`ActionSet` counts its actions in the browser, so the stacking and row layout classes are applied after mount. A server-rendered page can reflow on hydration.

---

### Component API

#### `ActionSet` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "2xl"` | Specify the size of the action set. Different button arrangements are<br />used at different sizes to make the best use of available space. Also<br />sets the default size for child `Button`s that don't set their own<br />`size`. | `"md"` |
| `disableStacking` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to prevent automatic stacking, even when `size` would<br />normally trigger it (`"sm"`, or `"md"` with more than two actions). | `false` |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to stick the action set to the bottom of its nearest<br />scroll container, for example a save bar under a long form. | `false` |

#### `ActionSet` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `ActionSet` $$restProps

`ActionSet` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## AILabel

### Basic

Click the label to open the explanation. Put the explanation in the default slot.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Stack, Text } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AILabel>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <Text type="label-01" color="secondary">AI explained</Text>
    <p>
      This forecast was generated from the last 90 days of usage across your
      workspace.
    </p>
  </Stack>
</AILabel>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to control the button size. The default is `"xs"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5}>
  {#each ["mini", "2xs", "xs", "sm", "md", "lg", "xl"] as size}
    <AILabel {size}>
      <p>Generated from the last 90 days of usage across your workspace.</p>
    </AILabel>
  {/each}
</Stack>
```

### Inline

Set `variant` to `"inline"` to render the label as text. Use `labelText` to add text beside it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5}>
  <AILabel variant="inline" size="sm">
    <p>Summarized from the incident timeline and the on-call notes.</p>
  </AILabel>
  <AILabel variant="inline" size="md" labelText="Generated summary">
    <p>Summarized from the incident timeline and the on-call notes.</p>
  </AILabel>
  <AILabel variant="inline" size="lg" labelText="Generated summary">
    <p>Summarized from the incident timeline and the on-call notes.</p>
  </AILabel>
</Stack>
```

### Actions

Add `AILabelActions` at the end of the explanation for related actions. The bar runs along the bottom edge of the explanation, and a primary button sits last.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    AILabel,
    AILabelActions,
    Button,
    Stack,
    Text,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AILabel>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <Text type="label-01" color="secondary">AI explained</Text>
    <p>
      Anomalies were flagged by comparing request latency with the same hour
      last week.
    </p>
  </Stack>
  <AILabelActions>
    <Button kind="ghost">View details</Button>
    <Button>Tune model</Button>
  </AILabelActions>
</AILabel>
```

#### Icon buttons

Icon-only buttons sit before the primary button. Wrap them in a [TooltipGroup](/components/TooltipGroup): the first tooltip waits for the hover delay, and once it shows, the next shows right away as the pointer moves along the bar. The primary button can take an `icon` too.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    AILabel,
    AILabelActions,
    Button,
    Stack,
    Text,
    TooltipGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import ArrowRight from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/ArrowRight.svelte";
  import FolderOpen from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/FolderOpen.svelte";
  import View from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/View.svelte";
</script>

<AILabel>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <Text type="label-01" color="secondary">AI explained</Text>
    <p>
      Spend is projected to grow 12% next month, mostly from storage in
      us-east-1.
    </p>
  </Stack>
  <AILabelActions>
    <TooltipGroup>
      <Button
        kind="ghost"
        iconOnly
        icon={View}
        iconDescription="Show the source data"
      />
      <Button
        kind="ghost"
        iconOnly
        icon={FolderOpen}
        iconDescription="Open the forecast report"
      />
    </TooltipGroup>
    <Button icon={ArrowRight}>View forecast</Button>
  </AILabelActions>
</AILabel>
```

### Detailed explanation

An explanation can hold more than a sentence: a headline figure, what it measures, and the model behind it. Build it from `Text`, `Stack`, and `Divider`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    AILabel,
    AILabelActions,
    Button,
    Divider,
    Stack,
    Text,
    TooltipGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import FolderOpen from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/FolderOpen.svelte";
  import Folders from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Folders.svelte";
  import View from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/View.svelte";
</script>

<AILabel>
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <Text type="label-01" color="secondary">AI explained</Text>
      <Text type="heading-06">84%</Text>
    </Stack>
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <Text type="heading-compact-01">Confidence score</Text>
      <Text type="body-compact-01"
        >How closely the forecast matched actual spend over the last six months.
        Scores above 80% are reliable enough to set a budget from.</Text
      >
    </Stack>
    <Divider decorative />
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <Text type="label-01" color="secondary">Model type</Text>
      <Text type="heading-compact-01">Time-series forecasting model</Text>
    </Stack>
  </Stack>
  <AILabelActions>
    <TooltipGroup>
      <Button
        kind="ghost"
        iconOnly
        icon={View}
        iconDescription="Show the source data"
      />
      <Button
        kind="ghost"
        iconOnly
        icon={FolderOpen}
        iconDescription="Open the forecast report"
      />
      <Button
        kind="ghost"
        iconOnly
        icon={Folders}
        iconDescription="Compare past forecasts"
      />
    </TooltipGroup>
    <Button>View details</Button>
  </AILabelActions>
</AILabel>
```

### Fields

Put an AI label in the `decorator` slot of a field to mark its value as AI-generated. The field shows the AI gradient, and the label always renders at the `"mini"` size. Text inputs, text areas, number inputs, selects, dropdowns, combo boxes, multiselects, and date pickers have the slot.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    AILabel,
    Box,
    ComboBox,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Dropdown,
    NumberInput,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    Stack,
    TextArea,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box maxWidth={320}>
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <TextInput
      labelText="Incident title"
      value="Database failover in us-east-1"
    >
      <AILabel slot="decorator">
        <p>Suggested from the alert that opened this incident.</p>
      </AILabel>
    </TextInput>
    <TextArea
      labelText="Summary"
      value="Primary database failed over after a storage node stopped responding."
    >
      <AILabel slot="decorator">
        <p>Written from the incident timeline and the database logs.</p>
      </AILabel>
    </TextArea>
    <NumberInput labelText="Replicas" value={3}>
      <AILabel slot="decorator">
        <p>Recommended from peak load over the last 30 days.</p>
      </AILabel>
    </NumberInput>
    <Select labelText="Severity" selected="sev2">
      <SelectItem value="sev1" text="Sev 1" />
      <SelectItem value="sev2" text="Sev 2" />
      <AILabel slot="decorator">
        <p>Set from the number of affected customers and the error rate.</p>
      </AILabel>
    </Select>
    <Dropdown
      labelText="Owning team"
      selectedId="db"
      items={[
        { id: "db", text: "Database platform" },
        { id: "net", text: "Networking" },
      ]}
    >
      <AILabel slot="decorator">
        <p>Matched to the team that owns the failed service.</p>
      </AILabel>
    </Dropdown>
    <ComboBox
      labelText="Region"
      selectedId="us-east-1"
      items={[
        { id: "us-east-1", text: "US East (N. Virginia)" },
        { id: "eu-west-1", text: "EU West (Ireland)" },
      ]}
    >
      <AILabel slot="decorator">
        <p>Detected from the host that sent the first alert.</p>
      </AILabel>
    </ComboBox>
    <DatePicker datePickerType="single">
      <DatePickerInput labelText="Follow-up date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy">
        <AILabel slot="decorator">
          <p>Scheduled two business days after the incident closes.</p>
        </AILabel>
      </DatePickerInput>
    </DatePicker>
  </Stack>
</Box>
```

### Selection controls

Checkboxes, radio buttons, and their groups have a `decorator` slot too. The label follows the label text or the legend.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    AILabel,
    Checkbox,
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Checkbox labelText="Enable automatic failover" checked>
    <AILabel slot="decorator">
      <p>Recommended because this database had two outages last quarter.</p>
    </AILabel>
  </Checkbox>
  <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Billing cycle" selected="annual">
    <AILabel slot="decorator">
      <p>Annual billing costs less for usage that has been steady all year.</p>
    </AILabel>
    <RadioButton labelText="Monthly" value="monthly" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Annual" value="annual" />
  </RadioButtonGroup>
</Stack>
```

### Tags

In a tag, the label renders as inline text in the tag's color.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Stack, Tag } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={3}>
  <Tag type="blue"
    >Forecast<AILabel slot="decorator"
      ><p>Generated from the last 90 days of usage.</p></AILabel
    ></Tag
  >
  <Tag type="green" filter
    >us-east-1<AILabel slot="decorator"
      ><p>
        Suggested because most of the alerts came from this region.
      </p></AILabel
    ></Tag
  >
</Stack>
```

### Tiles

Tiles, clickable tiles, selectable tiles, radio tiles, and expandable tiles show the AI surface and put the label in the top-right corner (top-left in a right-to-left layout), with room kept clear for it so text never runs under it. On interactive tiles, the label sits outside the link, button, or label element.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    AILabel,
    Box,
    SelectableTile,
    Stack,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5} wrap="wrap">
  <Box width="16rem">
    <Tile>
      <h4>Usage forecast</h4>
      <p>Spend is projected to grow 12% next month.</p>
      <AILabel slot="decorator">
        <p>Projected from the last six months of spend.</p>
      </AILabel>
    </Tile>
  </Box>
  <Box width="16rem">
    <SelectableTile>
      Recommended plan: Team
      <AILabel slot="decorator">
        <p>Recommended for a workspace with 8 to 20 active members.</p>
      </AILabel>
    </SelectableTile>
  </Box>
</Stack>
```

### Loading

While AI generates content, show an AI skeleton in its place. Set `ai` on [SkeletonText](/components/SkeletonText#ai), [SkeletonPlaceholder](/components/SkeletonPlaceholder#ai), or [SkeletonIcon](/components/SkeletonIcon#ai).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    AILabel,
    Box,
    SkeletonText,
    Stack,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box width="16rem">
  <Tile>
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <h4>Usage forecast</h4>
      <SkeletonText ai paragraph lines={2} noMargin />
    </Stack>
    <AILabel slot="decorator">
      <p>Projecting from the last six months of spend.</p>
    </AILabel>
  </Tile>
</Box>
```

### Data tables

A data table has three slots: `decorator` beside the title, `headerDecorator` for AI columns, and `rowDecorator` for AI rows. The cells of an AI column take the AI gradient, as the cells of an AI row do. See [DataTable](/components/DataTable#ai-label).

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const headers = [
    { key: "service", value: "Service" },
    { key: "region", value: "Region" },
    { key: "forecast", value: "Forecast" },
  ];

  const rows = [
    {
      id: "a",
      service: "billing-api",
      region: "us-east-1",
      forecast: "+12%",
      generated: true,
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      service: "search",
      region: "eu-west-1",
      forecast: "+3%",
      generated: false,
    },
    {
      id: "c",
      service: "auth",
      region: "us-west-2",
      forecast: "-1%",
      generated: true,
    },
  ];
</script>

<DataTable
  title="Monthly spend"
  description="Forecast for next month"
  {headers}
  {rows}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="decorator">
    <AILabel>
      <p>Forecasts are generated from 90 days of billing data.</p>
    </AILabel>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="headerDecorator" let:header>
    {#if header.key === "forecast"}
      <AILabel>
        <p>Every value in this column is generated.</p>
      </AILabel>
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="rowDecorator" let:row>
    {#if row.generated}
      <AILabel>
        <p>This service was added by the cost assistant.</p>
      </AILabel>
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```

### Modals

`Modal` and `ComposedModal` show the AI surface and put the label beside the close button. See [Modal](/components/Modal#ai-label).

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Review forecast</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Usage forecast"
  primaryButtonText="Apply budget"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:submit={() => (open = false)}
>
  <AILabel slot="decorator">
    <p>Generated from 90 days of billing data across your workspace.</p>
  </AILabel>
  <p>
    Spend is projected to grow 12% next month. Raise the monthly budget to
    $4,800 to avoid overage alerts.
  </p>
</Modal>
```

### Revert

Set `edited` to `true` after the user edits an AI-generated value. The label turns into a revert button. Clicking it sets `edited` back to `false` and dispatches `revert`, so you can restore the AI value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, TextInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const suggestion = "Database failover in us-east-1";

  let value = suggestion;
  let edited = false;
</script>

<TextInput
  labelText="Incident title"
  bind:value
  on:input={() => (edited = value !== suggestion)}
>
  <AILabel slot="decorator" bind:edited on:revert={() => (value = suggestion)}>
    <p>Suggested from the alert that opened this incident.</p>
  </AILabel>
</TextInput>
```

### Alignment

Set `align` to place the explanation. The first part names the side it opens on: `"top"`, `"right"`, `"bottom"`, or `"left"`. The optional second part lines it up along that side: `"start"` or `"end"`. Without it, the explanation is centered. The default is `"bottom-start"`. Inside a field, it is `"bottom-end"`. The caret always points at the label.

#### Sides

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={10}>
  <AILabel variant="inline" size="md" labelText="Top" align="top">
    <p>Opens above the label.</p>
  </AILabel>
  <AILabel variant="inline" size="md" labelText="Right" align="right">
    <p>Opens to the right of the label.</p>
  </AILabel>
  <AILabel variant="inline" size="md" labelText="Bottom" align="bottom">
    <p>Opens below the label.</p>
  </AILabel>
  <AILabel variant="inline" size="md" labelText="Left" align="left">
    <p>Opens to the left of the label.</p>
  </AILabel>
</Stack>
```

#### Start and end

Below or above the label, `"start"` lines the explanation up with the left side and `"end"` with the right side. In a right-to-left layout, the two swap. To the left or right, `"start"` lines it up with the top and `"end"` with the bottom.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={7}>
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={10}>
    <AILabel
      variant="inline"
      size="md"
      labelText="Bottom start"
      align="bottom-start"
    >
      <p>Opens below, lined up with the label's left side.</p>
    </AILabel>
    <AILabel
      variant="inline"
      size="md"
      labelText="Bottom center"
      align="bottom"
    >
      <p>Opens below, centered on the label.</p>
    </AILabel>
    <AILabel
      variant="inline"
      size="md"
      labelText="Bottom end"
      align="bottom-end"
    >
      <p>Opens below, lined up with the label's right side.</p>
    </AILabel>
  </Stack>
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={10}>
    <AILabel
      variant="inline"
      size="md"
      labelText="Right start"
      align="right-start"
    >
      <p>Opens to the right, lined up with the label's top.</p>
    </AILabel>
    <AILabel variant="inline" size="md" labelText="Right center" align="right">
      <p>Opens to the right, centered on the label.</p>
    </AILabel>
    <AILabel variant="inline" size="md" labelText="Right end" align="right-end">
      <p>Opens to the right, lined up with the label's bottom.</p>
    </AILabel>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

#### Not enough room

If a start- or end-aligned explanation would run past its container, such as a table's scroll area, it opens toward the other side. This label is aligned to the start at the right edge of a scroll box, so it opens to the left.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Box } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box
  display="flex"
  justify="end"
  overflowX="auto"
  maxWidth="24rem"
  padding={5}
  paddingBottom="12rem"
  border="subtle"
>
  <AILabel align="bottom-start">
    <p>
      Aligned to the start, but there is no room on the right, so it opens to
      the left.
    </p>
  </AILabel>
</Box>
```

### Portal

Set `portalTooltip` to `true` to render the explanation in a portal, so a container with `overflow: hidden` cannot clip it. Inside a `Modal`, the explanation is portalled by default.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Box } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box overflow="hidden" padding={5} border="subtle">
  <AILabel portalTooltip>
    <p>Generated from your last three billing cycles.</p>
  </AILabel>
</Box>
```

### Server rendering

A filled `decorator` slot renders the AI surface on the server, so the surface does not pop in after the page loads. The server can't tell what the slot holds. If it holds another element, or a label with `edited` set, the surface drops once the page loads. Data table rows and `headerDecorator` columns can each differ, so their gradient appears once the page loads.

---

### Component API

#### `AILabel` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `edited` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` after the user edits an AI-generated value.<br />The label turns into a revert button.<br />Clicking the revert button sets it back to `false`. | `false` |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the explanation. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLButtonElement` | Obtain a reference to the button HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"mini" \| "2xs" \| "xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | Set the size of the button.<br />Inside a component's `decorator` slot, the component sets the size:<br />`"mini"` in fields, checkboxes, and radio buttons, and `"xs"` in tiles. | `"xs"` |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "inline"` | Set the form of the label.<br />The inline variant renders as text and can show `labelText` next to it.<br />Inside a `Tag`, the variant is always `"inline"`. | `"default"` |
| `aiText` | `string` | Specify the AI text in the button | `"AI"` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify extra text shown beside the AI text in the inline variant | `""` |
| `iconDescription` | `string` | Specify the text that screen readers hear after `aiText`.<br />The inline variant is named by its visible text and ignores it. | `"Show information"` |
| `revertText` | `string` | Specify the tooltip text of the revert button | `"Revert to AI input"` |
| `align` | `"top" \| "top-start" \| "top-end" \| "bottom" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-end" \| "left" \| "left-start" \| "left-end" \| "right" \| "right-start" \| "right-end" \| undefined` | Set where the explanation opens: the side of the button, then its<br />alignment along that side.<br />Above and below the button, `start` and `end` name inline sides, so<br />they swap under `dir="rtl"`.<br />Defaults to `"bottom-end"` inside a field or tile `decorator` slot,<br />otherwise `"bottom-start"`. | _undefined_ |
| `portalTooltip` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to render the explanation in a portal,<br />preventing it from being clipped by `overflow: hidden` containers.<br />By default, the explanation is portalled when inside a `Modal`. | _undefined_ |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the label's toggletip.<br />The explanation id derives from it as `{id}-content`. | `uniqueId()` |

## AspectRatio

### Basic

Display a 2:1 aspect ratio container by default. The container fills the width of its parent, and its height is derived from the ratio.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio>2x1</AspectRatio>
```

### Ratios

Set `ratio` to change the aspect ratio. Supported values include `2x1`, `2x3`, `16x9`, `4x3`, `1x1`, `3x4`, `3x2`, `9x16`, and `1x2`.

#### 2x3

Display content with a 2:3 aspect ratio.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="2x3">2x3</AspectRatio>
```

#### 16x9

Display content with a 16:9 aspect ratio.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="16x9">16x9</AspectRatio>
```

#### 4x3

Display content with a 4:3 aspect ratio.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="4x3">4x3</AspectRatio>
```

#### 1x1

Display content with a 1:1 (square) aspect ratio.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="1x1">1x1</AspectRatio>
```

#### 3x4

Display content with a 3:4 aspect ratio.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="3x4">3x4</AspectRatio>
```

#### 3x2

Display content with a 3:2 aspect ratio.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="3x2">3x2</AspectRatio>
```

#### 9x16

Display content with a 9:16 aspect ratio.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="9x16">9x16</AspectRatio>
```

#### 1x2

Display content with a 1:2 aspect ratio.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="1x2">1x2</AspectRatio>
```

#### Custom ratio

Set `ratio` to any positive `"WxH"` string for a ratio outside the named list, such as `"21x9"` for ultrawide video. Decimals are allowed, for example `"2.35x1"`. A value that is neither a named ratio nor a valid `WxH` pair falls back to `2x1`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="21x9">21x9</AspectRatio>
```

### Fill

Set `fill` to `true` so the slotted content stretches to fill the aspect box, instead of sizing to its own content. This replaces setting `height: 100%` by hand on the content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="16x9" fill>
  <Tile>Incident postmortem recording, Q3 outage</Tile>
</AspectRatio>
```

### Alignment

Set `align` or `justify` to position content that doesn't fill the aspect box, such as a placeholder icon or short caption. Setting either makes the aspect box a flex container.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio ratio="16x9" align="center" justify="center">
  <Tile>Centered</Tile>
</AspectRatio>
```

### Custom element

The outer element renders a `<div>` by default. Set `tag` to render a semantic element such as `figure`, `section`, or `article` without wrapping the component in an extra element.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AspectRatio, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<AspectRatio tag="figure" ratio="16x9" fill>
  <Tile>Rendered as a `figure`.</Tile>
</AspectRatio>
```

### Usage

Wrap content like tiles, images, or videos in an aspect ratio container to maintain consistent proportions across screen sizes. See [Fill](#fill) above for making that content stretch to the container.

#### Grid columns

To keep column heights consistent within a `Grid`, use the `aspectRatio` prop on `Column` instead--see [Grid: Aspect ratio](/components/Grid#aspect-ratio) for aligning columns of differing content across a row.

---

### Component API

#### `AspectRatio` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ratio` | `"2x1" \| "2x3" \| "16x9" \| "4x3" \| "1x1" \| "3x4" \| "3x2" \| "9x16" \| "1x2" \| `${number}x${number}`` | Specify the aspect ratio. Accepts one of the named ratios, or any<br />positive `"WxH"` string (decimals allowed, e.g. `"21x9"` or `"2.35x1"`)<br />for a ratio outside that list. A string that is neither a named ratio<br />nor a valid positive `WxH` pair falls back to `"2x1"`. | `"2x1"` |
| `fill` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to stretch the slotted content to fill the aspect box | `false` |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| undefined` | Align the slotted content along the cross axis. Makes the aspect box a flex container. | _undefined_ |
| `justify` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "space-between" \| "space-around" \| "space-evenly" \| undefined` | Justify the slotted content along the main axis. Makes the aspect box a flex container. | _undefined_ |
| `tag` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` | Specify the HTML tag to render for the outer element. | `"div"` |

#### `AspectRatio` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `AspectRatio` $$restProps

`AspectRatio` spreads `$$restProps` to the `svelte:element` element.


## BadgeIndicator

### Basic

Compose a `BadgeIndicator` in the `badge` slot of an icon-only [Button](/components/Button) to overlay a badge on it. Omit `count`, or set it to `0`, to render an empty dot that signals presence without a number.

```svelte
<script>
  import { BadgeIndicator, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";
</script>

<Button kind="ghost" icon={Notification} iconDescription="Notifications">
  <BadgeIndicator slot="badge" />
</Button>
```

### Count

Control the badge content with `count`.

#### Numeric

Set `count` to a number. Values greater than `999` display as `999+`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { BadgeIndicator, Button, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={7}>
  <Button kind="ghost" icon={Notification} iconDescription="Notifications">
    <BadgeIndicator slot="badge" count={4} />
  </Button>
  <Button kind="ghost" icon={Notification} iconDescription="Notifications">
    <BadgeIndicator slot="badge" count={25} />
  </Button>
  <Button kind="ghost" icon={Notification} iconDescription="Notifications">
    <BadgeIndicator slot="badge" count={1000} />
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

#### Formatted

Pass a string to `count` to override the built-in numeric display. String values bypass the `999+` cap.

```svelte
<script>
  import { BadgeIndicator, Button, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Email from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Email.svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";

  const notifications = 1200;
  const messages = 2_500_000;

  function formatCount(value) {
    return value.toLocaleString(undefined, {
      notation: "compact",
      maximumFractionDigits: 1,
    });
  }
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={7}>
  <Button
    kind="ghost"
    icon={Notification}
    iconDescription="Notifications"
    tooltipAlignment="start"
  >
    <BadgeIndicator slot="badge" count={formatCount(notifications)} />
  </Button>
  <Button kind="ghost" icon={Email} iconDescription="Messages">
    <BadgeIndicator slot="badge" count={formatCount(messages)} />
  </Button>
  <Button kind="ghost" icon={Notification} iconDescription="Notifications">
    <BadgeIndicator slot="badge" count="99+" />
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

### In UI Shell

Use the [UI Shell](/components/UIShell) for header notifications and other utility indicators.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    BadgeIndicator,
    Column,
    Content,
    Grid,
    Header,
    HeaderGlobalAction,
    HeaderUtilities,
    Row,
    SideNav,
    SideNavItems,
    SideNavLink,
    SideNavMenu,
    SideNavMenuItem,
    SkipToContent,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Help from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Help.svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";
  import UserAvatarFilledAlt from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/UserAvatarFilledAlt.svelte";

  let isSideNavOpen = false;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" bind:isSideNavOpen>
  <svelte:fragment slot="skipToContent"><SkipToContent /></svelte:fragment>
  <HeaderUtilities>
    <HeaderGlobalAction
      iconDescription="Notifications"
      tooltipAlignment="start"
      icon={Notification}
    >
      <BadgeIndicator slot="badge" count={4} />
    </HeaderGlobalAction>
    <HeaderGlobalAction iconDescription="Help" icon={Help}>
      <BadgeIndicator slot="badge" count={0} />
    </HeaderGlobalAction>
    <HeaderGlobalAction
      iconDescription="Profile"
      tooltipAlignment="end"
      icon={UserAvatarFilledAlt}
    />
  </HeaderUtilities>
</Header>

<SideNav bind:isOpen={isSideNavOpen}>
  <SideNavItems>
    <SideNavLink href="/dashboard" text="Dashboard" />
    <SideNavLink href="/resources" text="Resource list" />
    <SideNavLink href="/activity" text="Activity tracker" />
    <SideNavMenu text="Kubernetes">
      <SideNavMenuItem href="/kubernetes/clusters" text="Clusters" />
      <SideNavMenuItem href="/kubernetes/worker-pools" text="Worker pools" />
      <SideNavMenuItem href="/kubernetes/registry" text="Container registry" />
    </SideNavMenu>
  </SideNavItems>
</SideNav>

<Content>
  <Grid>
    <Row>
      <Column><h1>Dashboard</h1></Column>
    </Row>
  </Grid>
</Content>
```
