#### Clear selection

Use `bind:this` to access the component instance and call `ComboBox.clear()` to clear the selection. Pass `focus: false` in the options to prevent re-focusing the input.

Pressing <kbd>Escape</kbd> in the input closes the menu and also clears the selection and the text.

Clearing a selection with the clear button, <kbd>Escape</kbd>, or `clear()` is announced to screen readers through a polite live region. Override the message with `selectionClearedText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let ref;
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  selectedId="1"
  bind:this={ref}
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
<br />
<Button on:click={() => ref.clear()}>Clear</Button>
<Button on:click={() => ref.clear({ focus: false })}>Clear (no focus)</Button>
<Button on:click={() => ref.clear({ open: true })}>Clear (reopen menu)</Button>
```

#### Open on clear

By default, the dropdown menu is closed after clearing the selection.

Set `openOnClear` to `true` to reopen the dropdown menu after clearing the selection. This lets users immediately browse all available items without needing to click the input again.

Clearing with <kbd>Escape</kbd> never reopens the menu, even with `openOnClear`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  openOnClear
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  selectedId="1"
  value="Email"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Multiple combo boxes

See how to manage multiple comboboxes in a form.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ];

  let comboBox1_selectedId;
  let comboBox2_selectedId;

  const formatSelected = (id) =>
    items.find((item) => item.id === id)?.text ?? "N/A";

  $: primary = formatSelected(comboBox1_selectedId);
  $: secondary = formatSelected(comboBox2_selectedId);
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <ComboBox
    bind:selectedId={comboBox1_selectedId}
    labelText="Primary alert channel"
    placeholder="Select primary alert channel"
    {items}
  />
  <div>Primary: {primary}</div>
  <ComboBox
    bind:selectedId={comboBox2_selectedId}
    labelText="Secondary alert channel"
    placeholder="Select secondary alert channel"
    {items}
  />
  <div>Secondary: {secondary}</div>
</Stack>
```

### Typeahead and auto-highlight

Auto-highlight and typeahead both assist users while typing. Auto-highlight highlights a matching item as you type so it can be selected with <kbd>Enter</kbd> alone. Typeahead completes the input inline with the untyped portion of a match. They work independently or together.

#### Auto-highlight

Set `autoHighlight` to `"first-match"` to automatically highlight the first matching item as you type. Select it by pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> without using arrow keys.

The default filter is case-insensitive substring matching (for example, "mar" matches "Marketing").

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  autoHighlight="first-match"
  labelText="Department"
  placeholder="Select a department"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Accounting" },
    { id: "1", text: "Accounts Payable" },
    { id: "2", text: "Billing" },
    { id: "3", text: "Business Development" },
    { id: "4", text: "Business Intelligence" },
    { id: "5", text: "Customer Success" },
    { id: "6", text: "Customer Support" },
    { id: "7", text: "Engineering" },
    { id: "8", text: "Marketing" },
    { id: "9", text: "Product" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Case-sensitive filter

Use `autoHighlight="first-match"` with a custom `shouldFilterItem` to control which items appear. The auto-highlight respects the custom filter; only items that pass the filter are considered for highlighting.

In this example, the filter is case-sensitive.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  autoHighlight="first-match"
  shouldFilterItem={(item, value) => item.text.startsWith(value)}
  labelText="Department"
  placeholder="Select a department"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Accounting" },
    { id: "1", text: "Accounts Payable" },
    { id: "2", text: "Billing" },
    { id: "3", text: "Business Development" },
    { id: "4", text: "Business Intelligence" },
    { id: "5", text: "Customer Success" },
    { id: "6", text: "Customer Support" },
    { id: "7", text: "Engineering" },
    { id: "8", text: "Marketing" },
    { id: "9", text: "Product" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Typeahead

Set `typeahead` to `true` to enable autocomplete. As users type, the input suggests and completes matching items.

By default, typeahead uses case-insensitive prefix matching against each item's displayed label (`itemToString`). When a match is found, the suggestion shows the untyped portion highlighted so users can accept it or keep typing.

Pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd> accepts the suggestion: it selects the matching item, normalizes the value to the item's casing, and closes the dropdown. <kbd>Tab</kbd> still moves focus to the next control. Clicking away accepts the suggestion the same way. When the typed text matches no item, the suggestion is not committed.

Pressing <kbd>→</kbd> or <kbd>End</kbd> accepts the inline suggestion in place: it commits the completed text into the value (keeping your casing) and collapses the cursor to the end, but keeps focus in the input and leaves the dropdown open so you can continue editing. Unlike <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Tab</kbd>, it does not select an item or close the menu.

You can provide a custom `shouldFilterItem` to change the filtering logic. See the [fuzzy filter](#fuzzy-filter) example below.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedId;
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Department"
  placeholder="Select a department"
  bind:selectedId
  typeahead
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Accounting" },
    { id: "1", text: "Accounts Payable" },
    { id: "2", text: "Billing" },
    { id: "3", text: "Business Development" },
    { id: "4", text: "Business Intelligence" },
    { id: "5", text: "Customer Success" },
    { id: "6", text: "Customer Support" },
    { id: "7", text: "Engineering" },
    { id: "8", text: "Marketing" },
    { id: "9", text: "Product" },
  ]}
/>
<br />
<Button
  disabled={selectedId === undefined}
  on:click={() => (selectedId = undefined)}
>
  Set to undefined (unselected)
</Button>
```

#### Combined with auto-highlight

Combine `typeahead` and `autoHighlight="first-match"` for the full autocomplete experience: the input text is completed and the matching item is visually highlighted.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  typeahead
  autoHighlight="first-match"
  labelText="Department"
  placeholder="Search for a department"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Accounting" },
    { id: "1", text: "Accounts Payable" },
    { id: "2", text: "Billing" },
    { id: "3", text: "Business Development" },
    { id: "4", text: "Business Intelligence" },
    { id: "5", text: "Customer Success" },
    { id: "6", text: "Customer Support" },
    { id: "7", text: "Engineering" },
    { id: "8", text: "Marketing" },
    { id: "9", text: "Product" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Fuzzy filter

Provide a custom `shouldFilterItem` to override the default prefix matching used by typeahead. This example reuses the built-in `fuzzyMatch` utility, exported from `carbon-components-svelte`, as the predicate. It matches items whose text contains the typed characters in order (for example, "acc" matches "Accounting" and "Accounts Payable"). Only the `matched` boolean is used here; the `score` and `indices` it also returns rank and highlight matches, as shown in [Highlight matches](#highlight-matches) below.

Inline completion only fills in the input when the top match starts with the typed text, so a fuzzy match like "pdt" against "Product" filters the list without completing the input. Pair the custom filter with `autoHighlight="first-match"` so the matched item is highlighted and <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd> selects it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox, fuzzyMatch } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedId;

  // Reuse the built-in fuzzy matcher as the filter predicate. Each typed
  // character must appear in order within the item text, so "acc" matches
  // "Accounting" and "Accounts Payable". Only the `matched` boolean is used here.
  const shouldFilterItem = (item, value) =>
    fuzzyMatch(item.text, value).matched;
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Department"
  placeholder="Select a department"
  bind:selectedId
  typeahead
  autoHighlight="first-match"
  {shouldFilterItem}
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Accounting" },
    { id: "1", text: "Accounts Payable" },
    { id: "2", text: "Billing" },
    { id: "3", text: "Business Development" },
    { id: "4", text: "Business Intelligence" },
    { id: "5", text: "Customer Success" },
    { id: "6", text: "Customer Support" },
    { id: "7", text: "Engineering" },
    { id: "8", text: "Marketing" },
    { id: "9", text: "Product" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Highlight matches

Besides `matched`, `fuzzyMatch` returns the `indices` of the characters that matched. Pass them to the `highlightSegments` utility (also exported from `carbon-components-svelte`) to split the item text into matched and unmatched runs, then bold the matched runs in the default slot. Bind `value` to read the typed query inside the slot.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    ComboBox,
    fuzzyMatch,
    highlightSegments,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: "Accounting" },
    { id: "1", text: "Accounts Payable" },
    { id: "2", text: "Billing" },
    { id: "3", text: "Business Development" },
    { id: "4", text: "Business Intelligence" },
    { id: "5", text: "Customer Success" },
    { id: "6", text: "Customer Support" },
    { id: "7", text: "Engineering" },
    { id: "8", text: "Marketing" },
    { id: "9", text: "Product" },
  ];

  // One matcher drives filtering and highlighting. `shouldFilterItem` keeps
  // the items whose text fuzzy-matches the typed value; the default slot
  // reuses the same match and bolds the characters that matched. Bind `value`
  // to read the typed query inside the slot.
  const shouldFilterItem = (item, value) =>
    fuzzyMatch(item.text, value).matched;
</script>

<ComboBox
  bind:value
  labelText="Department"
  placeholder="Search for a department"
  {shouldFilterItem}
  {items}
  let:item
>
  {#each highlightSegments(item.text, fuzzyMatch(item.text, value).indices) as segment}
    {#if segment.match}
      <strong>{segment.text}</strong>
    {:else}
      {segment.text}
    {/if}
  {/each}
</ComboBox>
```

### Groups

Set `group` on items to list them under a non-selectable header. Items without a group are listed first, without a header, followed by the groups in the order they first occur in `items`. The arrow keys move between options and skip the headers. While filtering, a group with no matching items is hidden, header and all.

Each group is exposed to screen readers as a group named by its label. The selection is still a single id.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Region"
  placeholder="Select a region"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Frankfurt", group: "Europe" },
    { id: "1", text: "Toronto", group: "Americas" },
    { id: "2", text: "London", group: "Europe" },
    { id: "3", text: "São Paulo", group: "Americas" },
    { id: "4", text: "Global (any region)" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Custom header

Override the `group` slot to customize a header. Use `let:group` for the label and `let:items` for the group's items. The slot changes the visible header only; screen readers still announce the plain label.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Region"
  placeholder="Select a region"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Frankfurt", group: "Europe" },
    { id: "1", text: "Toronto", group: "Americas" },
    { id: "2", text: "London", group: "Europe" },
    { id: "3", text: "São Paulo", group: "Americas" },
    { id: "4", text: "Global (any region)" },
  ]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="group" let:group let:items={groupItems}>
    {group} ({groupItems.length})
  </svelte:fragment>
</ComboBox>
```

### Filtering

By default, combobox filtering is synchronous and client-side. Customize the filter logic, label rendering, and when results reset.

While a filter is active, the number of matching options is announced to screen readers once typing pauses. Override the message with `filterResultsText`, a function of the count.

#### Filterable

Enable filtering to let users search through the options.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  function shouldFilterItem(item, value) {
    if (!value) return true;
    return item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase());
  }
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
  {shouldFilterItem}
/>
```

#### Filter mode

By default (`filterMode="remove"`), filtering unmounts non-matching options and recreates them when they match again.

Set `filterMode` to `"hide"` to keep every option mounted and hide non-matching ones with the `hidden` attribute. Keyboard navigation, `aria-setsize`, and `aria-posinset` still follow the matching items only. `"hide"` falls back to `"remove"` when virtualization is enabled or items are [grouped](#groups). For typical ComboBox lists, `"remove"` is faster per keystroke because it only updates matching option nodes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  filterMode="hide"
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Empty state

When the filter matches nothing, the menu shows "No results" in place of the options. Screen readers already hear the count from `filterResultsText`, so the message is hidden from them.

Set `emptyText` to change the message, or pass a function that builds it from the typed text. Set it to `""` to leave the menu empty instead.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Type to filter"
  emptyText="No matching channels"
  shouldFilterItem={(item, value) =>
    item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase())}
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

Use the `empty` slot for richer content. `let:value` is the typed text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Type to filter"
  shouldFilterItem={(item, value) =>
    item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase())}
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="empty" let:value>
    No channel named "{value}". Check the spelling or add it in Settings.
  </svelte:fragment>
</ComboBox>
```

#### Custom label

Set `itemToString` to customize how items display in the filterable combobox.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const translation = {
    Slack: 'Custom label for "Slack"',
    Email: 'Custom label for "Email"',
    Webhook: 'Custom label for "Webhook"',
  };

  function itemToString(item) {
    return translation[item.text];
  }

  function shouldFilterItem(item, value) {
    if (!value) return true;
    const comparison = value.toLowerCase();
    return (
      item.text.toLowerCase().includes(comparison) ||
      itemToString(item).toLowerCase().includes(comparison)
    );
  }
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
  {shouldFilterItem}
  {itemToString}
/>
```

#### Clear filter on open

After selecting an item in a filterable combobox, reopening the dropdown normally shows only the results matching that selection. Set `clearFilterOnOpen` to `true` to clear the filter on open, showing all items so you can browse and change the selection.

The original value is automatically restored if you close the dropdown without making a new selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  function shouldFilterItem(item, value) {
    if (!value) return true;
    return item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase());
  }
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
  {shouldFilterItem}
  clearFilterOnOpen
  selectedId="1"
  helperText="Select an item, then reopen to see all items again"
/>
```

#### Async

For async (for example, server-side) filtering, bind to `value` and update `items` when input changes. This example simulates async behavior with a debounced input value change.

Set `loading` to `true` while a request is in flight. The menu shows a loading row after the options, is marked busy for screen readers, and holds back the empty state until the results arrive.

Set `loadingDelay` to wait a number of milliseconds after `loading` becomes `true` before showing the loading row. Work that finishes within the delay shows no row. Once shown, the row stays for at least 500 ms so it does not flash. The menu is marked busy, and the empty state held back, as soon as `loading` is `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import { onMount } from "svelte";

  let items = [];
  let loading = false;
  let timeoutId;
  let inputValue = "";

  // Simulate fetching data from a remote server.
  async function fetchItems(query) {
    if (!query) {
      return [];
    }

    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 300));

    const allItems = [
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "PagerDuty" },
      { id: "3", text: "Webhook" },
      { id: "4", text: "Microsoft Teams" },
      { id: "5", text: "SMS" },
      { id: "6", text: "Opsgenie" },
      { id: "7", text: "ServiceNow" },
      { id: "8", text: "VictorOps" },
      { id: "9", text: "Zoom" },
    ];

    return allItems.filter((item) =>
      item.text.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()),
    );
  }

  onMount(() => {
    // Fetch initial items.
    fetchItems("")
      .then((data) => {
        items = data;
      })
      .catch(() => {});

    return () => {
      clearTimeout(timeoutId);
    };
  });

  $: {
    clearTimeout(timeoutId);
    // Debounce input value changes.
    timeoutId = setTimeout(async () => {
      const query = inputValue;
      loading = true;
      const results = await fetchItems(query);
      // A newer search has started; let it report instead.
      if (query !== inputValue) return;
      items = results;
      loading = false;
    }, 150);
  }
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Type to search..."
  bind:value={inputValue}
  {items}
  {loading}
  emptyText={(value) =>
    value ? `No channels match "${value}"` : "Type to search"}
/>
```

#### Load more

`scrollend` fires when the menu is scrolled near the bottom. Use it to append the next page of `items`. The component does not fetch or mutate `items` for you.

This is a library load-more signal, named like Modal's lowercase `transitionend`. It is not the browser's native `scrollend` (scroll stopped).

Keep prior items visible while the next page loads, and set `loading` while the request is in flight to show a loading row after them. The options stay selectable.

`scrollend` fires once per approach to the bottom. It re-arms after the user scrolls away, and when `items` grows so another page can be requested. Holding the scrollbar at the bottom does not spam the handler. The raw DOM `scroll` event is still forwarded via `on:scroll`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const PAGE_SIZE = 40;
  const TOTAL = 200;

  let items = [];
  let loading = false;
  let hasMore = true;

  function makePage(offset) {
    return Array.from({ length: PAGE_SIZE }, (_, i) => {
      const n = offset + i;
      return { id: String(n), text: `Invoice #${n + 1}` };
    }).filter((item) => Number(item.id) < TOTAL);
  }

  async function loadMore() {
    if (loading || !hasMore) return;
    loading = true;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 400));
    const next = makePage(items.length);
    items = [...items, ...next];
    hasMore = items.length < TOTAL;
    loading = false;
  }

  loadMore();
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <ComboBox
    labelText="Load more on scroll"
    placeholder="Open and scroll to the bottom..."
    {items}
    shouldFilterItem={() => true}
    virtualize={{ containerHeight: 240, threshold: 1 }}
    {loading}
    loadingText="Loading more..."
    on:scrollend={loadMore}
  />
  {#if !hasMore}
    <p>Loaded all {TOTAL} items.</p>
  {:else}
    <p>
      {items.length}
      of {TOTAL} loaded. Scroll the menu to fetch the next page.
    </p>
  {/if}
</Stack>
```

#### Allow custom value

Set `allowCustomValue` to `true` to let users enter custom text that is not in the predefined list. By default, user-entered text is cleared when the combobox loses focus without selecting an item. With allowCustomValue enabled, custom text is preserved.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedId;
  let value = "";
</script>

<Stack gap={2}>
  <ComboBox
    allowCustomValue
    labelText="Deployment region"
    placeholder="Select or enter a region"
    helperText="Select a common region or enter a custom one"
    bind:selectedId
    bind:value
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "us-east-1" },
      { id: "1", text: "us-west-2" },
      { id: "2", text: "eu-west-1" },
      { id: "3", text: "ap-southeast-1" },
    ]}
    shouldFilterItem={(item, value) => {
      if (!value) return true;
      return item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase());
    }}
    on:select={(e) => {
      console.log("Selected item:", e.detail);
    }}
  />
  <div>
    <div><strong>Selected ID:</strong> {selectedId ?? "none"}</div>
    <div><strong>Current value:</strong> {value || "empty"}</div>
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Select text on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to `true` to select all text in the input when it receives focus (for example, on tab or click). Users can replace the value by typing without manually selecting first.

An alternative is [clear filter on open](#clear-filter-on-open), which clears the filter when opening so all options are visible.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  selectTextOnFocus
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  selectedId="1"
  value="Email"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Virtualization

Virtualization renders only the items currently visible in the viewport, improving performance for large lists. By default, the combo box virtualizes lists with more than 100 items.

Besides the options shown below, `virtualize` also accepts `containerHeight` (the maximum height in pixels of the dropdown container, default 300) and `maxItems` (a cap on the number of items rendered, default unlimited) for further tuning.

#### Large lists

In the example below, 10,000 items are provided to the combobox but only 11 items (8 visible items + 3 overscan items) are rendered in the DOM.

Set `virtualize={false}` to explicitly disable virtualization, even for large lists. Or customize the threshold at which virtualization activates. See the [custom threshold](#custom-threshold) example below.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Customer ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let value = "";
  let selectedId;
  $: selectedItem = items.find((item) => item.id === selectedId);
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <ComboBox
    labelText="Virtualized ComboBox (10,000 items)"
    placeholder="Filter..."
    {items}
    shouldFilterItem={(item, value) =>
      item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase())}
    bind:selectedId
    bind:value
  />
  <div>
    <strong>Selected:</strong>
    {selectedItem?.text}
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Custom overscan

Overscanning is the process of rendering extra items above and below the viewport to ensure smooth scrolling. The default overscan value is 3.

Specify a custom value for `overscan` to control how many extra items render above and below the viewport for smoother scrolling.

During very fast scrolling, higher overscan values may cause more flickering due to increased DOM updates. For fast-scrolling scenarios, use a lower overscan value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Server ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let value = "";
  let selectedId;
</script>

<ComboBox
  virtualize={{ overscan: 100 }}
  labelText="High overscan (10,000 items, overscan: 100)"
  placeholder="Filter..."
  {items}
  shouldFilterItem={(item, value) =>
    item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase())}
  bind:selectedId
  bind:value
/>
```

#### Fast scrolling

During a scroll faster than the menu can render, such as a quick drag of the scrollbar, the options can briefly disappear. Set `optimizeFastScroll: true` to keep the options already rendered in view until the new ones arrive.

The options then follow the scroll a frame behind, and pause while the page is busy running scripts. Leave it off when the menu sits on a page that often does heavy work.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Server ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let value = "";
  let selectedId;
</script>

<ComboBox
  virtualize={{ optimizeFastScroll: true }}
  labelText="Optimized for fast scrolling (10,000 items)"
  placeholder="Filter..."
  {items}
  shouldFilterItem={(item, value) =>
    item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase())}
  bind:selectedId
  bind:value
/>
```

#### Custom threshold

The threshold is the minimum number of items required before virtualization activates. The default threshold value is 100, meaning lists with fewer than 100 items will not be virtualized and all items will be rendered normally.

Specify a custom value for `threshold` to control when virtualization activates. Below the threshold, all items render normally without virtualization.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 100 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Ticket #${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let value = "";
  let selectedId;
</script>

<ComboBox
  virtualize={{ threshold: 200 }}
  labelText="Custom threshold (threshold: 200)"
  placeholder="Filter..."
  {items}
  shouldFilterItem={(item, value) =>
    item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase())}
  bind:selectedId
  bind:value
/>
```

#### Custom item height

By default, item height matches the menu row for each size: 24px (`xs`), 32px (`sm`), 40px (`md`), 48px (`lg`, `xl`). Set `itemHeight` when custom slots change row height.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Employee ${i + 1}`,
    description: `ID: EMP-${100000 + i}`,
  }));

  let value = "";
  let selectedId;
</script>

<ComboBox
  virtualize={{ itemHeight: 60 }}
  labelText="Custom item height (60px)"
  placeholder="Filter..."
  {items}
  shouldFilterItem={(item, value) =>
    item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase())}
  bind:selectedId
  bind:value
  let:item
>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <strong>{item.text}</strong>
    <span>{item.description}</span>
  </Stack>
</ComboBox>

<style>
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item),
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item__option) {
    height: auto;
  }
</style>
```

### Events

Listen for selection, the menu opening and closing, and clear interactions. The `scrollend` load-more event is documented separately; see [Load more](#load-more).

#### Select

Listen for `on:select` to know when an item is selected. `event.detail` includes `selectedId` and `selectedItem`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  on:select={(e) => console.log(e.detail.selectedId, e.detail.selectedItem)}
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Open

Use `on:open` to know when the menu opens and why. `event.detail.trigger` is `"click"`, `"keydown"`, `"input"` (typing opened it), or `"programmatic"` when `open` is set from outside, such as through `bind:open`. It fires once per open, after the menu renders, and not for a combo box rendered already open.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Contact"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  on:open={(e) => console.log(e.detail.trigger)}
/>
```

#### Close

Listen for `on:close` to know when the dropdown menu closes and why. `event.detail.trigger` is `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, or `"select"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  on:close={(e) => console.log(e.detail.trigger)}
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Clear

Listen for `on:clear` to know when the user activates the clear ("x") button that appears once there is a selection, whether by click or by keyboard. `event.detail` is the originating `KeyboardEvent` or `MouseEvent`. This is distinct from calling the [imperative `clear()` method](#clear-selection) directly, which does not dispatch `clear`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  selectedId="1"
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  on:clear={(e) => console.log(e.type)}
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Menu placement

Control where and how the dropdown menu renders relative to the input.

#### Direction

Set `direction` to `"top"` to make the dropdown menu appear above the input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  direction="top"
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Portal menu

A dropdown menu that a container would cut off, such as a box with `overflow: hidden` or a scroll area, opens in a floating portal. The container in the example below hides its overflow, so the menu moves to a portal when it opens. Inside a [Modal](/components/Modal#modal-with-dropdowns), the menu always opens in a portal.

Set `portalMenu` to `true` to always render the menu in a portal, for example to escape a z-index stacking context. Set it to `false` to keep the menu in place. A portalled menu leaves its container in the DOM, so CSS that targets the menu as a descendant of the container does not match it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box
  display="flex"
  direction="column"
  gap={4}
  overflow="hidden"
  border="subtle"
  borderStyle="dashed"
  padding={5}
  maxHeight="120px"
>
  <div>
    This container has hidden overflow. The menu would not fit, so it opens in a
    portal.
  </div>
  <ComboBox
    labelText="Alert channel"
    placeholder="Select alert channel"
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
    ]}
  />
</Box>
```

#### Wrapped options

Option labels are truncated to one line. At a 320px viewport, that hides text and can leave two options looking identical, a WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow failure.

Set `wrapOptions` to let a label take as many lines as it needs. Lines break between words, and mid-word only when a word is too long to fit a line by itself. Default slot markup wraps with the label: a [highlighted match](#highlight-matches) stays marked across the break it is split by.

It defaults to `false` because wrapping changes option heights.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, ComboBox, highlightSegments } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const roles = [
    "Chief Accessibility Officer for Regional Operations and Strategic Partnerships",
    "Deputy Director of Interdepartmental Communications and Outreach",
  ];

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: roles[0] },
    { id: "1", text: roles[1] },
    { id: "2", text: "Analyst" },
  ];

  // Past the count at which a list is windowed, so only the options on screen
  // are rendered. `wrapOptions` turns on measured row heights by itself, so
  // offsets follow the heights the wrapped options actually take.
  const manyItems = Array.from({ length: 300 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: String(i),
    text: `${i + 1}. ${roles[i % 2]}`,
  }));

  let truncatedValue = "";
  let wrappedValue = "";
  let windowedValue = "";

  const shouldFilterItem = (item, value) =>
    item.text.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase());

  // Where the typed value occurs in the label, as the character indices
  // `highlightSegments` splits on.
  function matchIndices(text, value) {
    const start = value ? text.toLowerCase().indexOf(value.toLowerCase()) : -1;
    if (start === -1) return [];
    return Array.from({ length: value.length }, (_, i) => start + i);
  }
</script>

<Box display="flex" direction="column" gap={6} maxWidth="20rem">
  <ComboBox
    labelText="Truncated (default)"
    placeholder="Try typing 'operations'"
    bind:value={truncatedValue}
    {shouldFilterItem}
    {items}
    let:item
  >
    {#each highlightSegments(item.text, matchIndices(item.text, truncatedValue)) as segment}
      {#if segment.match}
        <mark>{segment.text}</mark>
      {:else}
        {segment.text}
      {/if}
    {/each}
  </ComboBox>

  <ComboBox
    wrapOptions
    labelText="Wrapped"
    placeholder="Try typing 'operations'"
    bind:value={wrappedValue}
    {shouldFilterItem}
    {items}
    let:item
  >
    {#each highlightSegments(item.text, matchIndices(item.text, wrappedValue)) as segment}
      {#if segment.match}
        <mark>{segment.text}</mark>
      {:else}
        {segment.text}
      {/if}
    {/each}
  </ComboBox>

  <ComboBox
    wrapOptions
    labelText="Wrapped (windowed, 300 items)"
    placeholder="Try typing 'operations'"
    bind:value={windowedValue}
    {shouldFilterItem}
    items={manyItems}
  />
</Box>
```

#### Programmatic access

Bind to `open` to control the dropdown menu programmatically, such as opening it from an external trigger.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<ComboBox
  bind:open
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
<br />
<Button on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Toggle menu</Button>
```

```svelte
  warnText="This alert channel is not associated with your on-call schedule"
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Disabled

Invalid and warning states are not displayed while the combo box is disabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  fluid
  disabled
  invalid
  invalidText="Secondary alert channel must be different from the primary channel"
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Read-only

Invalid and warning states are not displayed while the combo box is read-only.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBox } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBox
  fluid
  readonly
  warn
  warnText="This alert channel is not associated with your on-call schedule"
  labelText="Alert channel"
  placeholder="Select alert channel"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Skeleton

Display a loading skeleton for the fluid combo box variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FluidComboBoxSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FluidComboBoxSkeleton />
```

### Form name

Set `name` so the combo box participates in native form submission (for example SvelteKit form actions and `FormData`). Unlike [Dropdown](/components/Dropdown#form-name), `name` lands directly on the always-mounted text input, so it submits the displayed text (`value`), not `selectedId`, empty string when nothing is selected.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Form, ComboBox, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form method="POST" action="?/alerts">
  <ComboBox
    name="alertChannel"
    labelText="Alert channel"
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "Webhook" },
    ]}
  />
  <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
</Form>
```

### Required

Set `required` to keep a surrounding form from submitting until the input has a value. `required` lands on the text input itself, like `name`. The field is marked required for screen readers.

When a submit is blocked, the field shows its invalid state instead of the browser's error bubble, and the first invalid field takes focus. Calling `checkValidity()` from code shows nothing. The state clears once the field has a value or the form resets.

Set `requiredInvalidText` to change the message, which defaults to "Select an item". Your own `invalid` and `invalidText` take precedence.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ComboBox, Form, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let submitted = false;
</script>

<Form
  on:submit={(e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    submitted = true;
  }}
>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <ComboBox
      required
      labelText="Contact"
      placeholder="Select a contact method"
      items={[
        { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
        { id: "1", text: "Email" },
        { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
      ]}
      on:select={() => (submitted = false)}
    />
    <div>
      <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
    </div>
    {#if submitted}
      <p>Submitted.</p>
    {/if}
  </Stack>
</Form>
```

### Skeleton

Show a loading state with `ComboBoxSkeleton`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBoxSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBoxSkeleton />
```

#### Sizes

Set `size` to match the field the skeleton stands in for.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ComboBoxSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ComboBoxSkeleton size="xs" />
```

### Component API

#### `ComboBox` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectedId` (Reactive) | `Item["id"] \| undefined` | Set the selected item by value id.<br />Follows the field when the owning form resets. | _undefined_ |
| `value` (Reactive) | `string` | Specify the selected combobox value.<br />Follows the field when the owning form resets. | `""` |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the combobox menu dropdown. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `listRef` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the list HTML element. | `null` |
| `items` | `ReadonlyArray<Item>` | Set the combobox items. | `[]` |
| `itemToString` | `(item: Item) => string` | Override the display of a combobox item. | `(item) => item.text ?? item.id` |
| `direction` | `"bottom" \| "top"` | Specify the direction of the combobox dropdown menu. | `"bottom"` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Set the size of the combobox.<br />Inherits the parent `Form` size when unset.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (the 40px default, which overrides a<br />`Form` size). `"lg"` and `"xl"` are both 48px. | _undefined_ |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the combobox | `false` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text of the combobox | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Specify the placeholder text | `""` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the read-only variant | `false` |
| `readonlyText` | `string` | Specify the assistive text announced to screen readers when read-only.<br />Exposed because VoiceOver does not announce `aria-readonly`. | `"Read-only"` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`. | `false` |
| `condensed` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render condensed menu items in the fluid variant.<br />Menu items use the default height instead of the taller fluid height.<br />Only applies when the fluid variant is active. | `false` |
| `allowCustomValue` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to allow custom values that are not in the items list.<br />By default, user-entered text is cleared when the combobox loses focus without selecting an item.<br />When enabled, custom text is preserved. | `false` |
| `clearFilterOnOpen` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to clear the input value when opening the dropdown.<br />This allows users to see all available items instead of only filtered results.<br />The original value is restored if the dropdown is closed without making a selection. | `false` |
| `selectTextOnFocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to select all text in the input when it receives focus (e.g. on tab or click). | `false` |
| `openOnClear` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to reopen the dropdown menu after clearing the selection.<br />This allows users to immediately see all available items after clearing. | `false` |
| `typeahead` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable autocomplete with typeahead | `false` |
| `autoHighlight` | `"none" \| "first-match"` | Control whether the first matching item is automatically highlighted as the user types.<br />- `"none"`: No auto-highlighting (default). The user must use arrow keys to highlight items.<br />- `"first-match"`: Automatically highlight the first non-disabled filtered item on each input change. | `"none"` |
| `shouldFilterItem` | `(item: Item, value: string) => boolean` | Determine if an item should be filtered given the current combobox value.<br />When `typeahead` is enabled and no custom function is provided,<br />the default case-insensitive prefix matching is used.<br />When a custom function is provided, it is used even with `typeahead`. | `() => true` |
| `filterMode` | `"remove" \| "hide"` | Set the filtering strategy used while the menu is open.<br />- `"remove"`: unmount non-matching options and recreate them when they<br /> match again.<br />- `"hide"`: keep all options mounted and hide non-matching ones with the<br /> `hidden` attribute.<br /><br />`"hide"` falls back to `"remove"` when virtualization is enabled, which<br />also keeps `wrapOptions` correct on a windowed list: a hidden option has no<br />rendered height, so measuring one would put a zero into offsets it does not<br />occupy. It also falls back when items are grouped, so a group whose items<br />all fail the filter loses its header. | `"remove"` |
| `translateWithId` | `((id: import("../ListBox/ListBoxMenuIcon.svelte").ListBoxMenuIconTranslationId) => string) \| undefined` | Override the chevron icon label based on the open state.<br />Defaults to "Open menu" when closed and "Close menu" when open. | _undefined_ |
| `translateWithIdSelection` | `((id: "clearSelection") => string) \| undefined` | Override the label of the clear button when the input has a selection.<br />Defaults to "Clear selected item" since a combo box can only have one selection. | _undefined_ |
| `selectionClearedText` | `string` | Specify the assistive text announced through the status live region when<br />a selection is cleared via the clear button, the Escape key, or `clear()`. | `"Selection cleared"` |
| `filterResultsText` | `(count: number) => string` | Build the assistive message announced through the status live region when<br />typing changes how many options match. Only used while a filter is active<br />(`typeahead` or a custom `shouldFilterItem`). | `(count) =><br />  count === 0<br />    ? "No results"<br />    : `${count} result${count === 1 ? "" : "s"} available`` |
| `emptyText` | `string \| ((value: string) => string)` | Specify the message shown in the menu when no items match the filter.<br />Pass a function to build it from the typed value.<br />Set to `""` to show no message; `filterResultsText` still announces<br />the result count. | `"No results"` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the list box component | `uniqueId()` |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a name attribute for the input. | _undefined_ |
| `required` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to require a value. Sets `required` on the input, so a<br />wrapping `<form>` blocks submission while it is empty, and the field<br />shows its invalid state with `requiredInvalidText` instead of the<br />browser's error bubble. | `false` |
| `requiredInvalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text shown when a required combo box blocks<br />submission. Cleared once the input has a value. `invalid` and<br />`invalidText` take precedence. | `"Select an item"` |
| `virtualize` | `undefined \| boolean \| { itemHeight?: number, containerHeight?: number, overscan?: number, threshold?: number, maxItems?: number, optimizeFastScroll?: boolean }` | Enable virtualization for large lists. Virtualization renders only the items currently visible in the viewport, improving performance for large lists.<br /><br />By default, virtualization is automatically enabled for lists with more than 100 items.<br /><br />Set `virtualize={false}` to explicitly disable virtualization, even for large lists.<br /><br />Set `virtualize={true}` to explicitly enable virtualization with default settings.<br /><br />Provide an object to customize virtualization behavior:<br />- `itemHeight` (default: size-based, or 64px for fluid unless `condensed`): Height of each item in pixels. Override when custom slots change row height. Under `wrapOptions`, heights are measured from the rendered options and this serves as the starting estimate for ones not yet measured.<br />- `containerHeight` (default: 300): The maximum height in pixels of the dropdown container.<br />- `overscan` (default: 3): The number of extra items to render above and below the viewport for smoother scrolling. Higher values may cause more flickering during very fast scrolling.<br />- `threshold` (default: 100): The minimum number of items required before virtualization activates. Lists with fewer items will render all items normally without virtualization.<br />- `maxItems` (default: undefined): The maximum number of items to render. When undefined, all visible items are rendered.<br />- `optimizeFastScroll` (default: false): Keep the rendered options in view during very fast scrolling, such as a scrollbar drag, instead of showing blank space until new options render. The options then follow the scroll a frame behind, and pause while the main thread is busy. | _undefined_ |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to show a loading row after the options while the menu is<br />open, such as while fetching more items on `scrollend`. Marks the menu<br />`aria-busy` and hides the empty state; the options stay interactive. | `false` |
| `loadingText` | `string` | Specify the text of the loading row | `"Loading..."` |
| `loadingDelay` | `number` | Wait this many milliseconds after `loading` turns `true` before showing<br />the loading row. Once shown, it stays for at least 500 ms, so fast work<br />shows nothing and slow work never flashes. The menu sets `aria-busy` and<br />holds back the empty state as soon as `loading` is `true`.<br />Set to `0` to show it at once. | `0` |
| `wrapOptions` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to let an option's label wrap onto as many lines as it needs<br />instead of being truncated with an ellipsis. | `false` |
| `portalMenu` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to always render the menu in a portal, or `false` to<br />keep it in place. Left unset, the menu moves to a portal inside a<br />Modal, or when a box around it (`overflow` other than `visible`)<br />would cut it off. | _undefined_ |
| `clear` | `(options?: { focus?: boolean; open?: boolean; }) => Promise<void>` | Clear the combo box programmatically.<br />By default, focuses the combo box after clearing. Set `options.focus` to `false` to prevent focusing.<br />Set `options.open` to `true` to keep the dropdown open after clearing. | _undefined_ |

#### `ComboBox` typedefs

```ts
type ComboBoxItem<Id = any> = {
  id: Id;
  text: string;
  /** Whether the item is disabled */
  disabled?: boolean;
  /** Icon component shown left of the item text */
  icon?: any;
  /** Group label. Items sharing a label render together under a non-selectable header, ungrouped items first and groups in order of first appearance. A group with no items matching the filter is hidden. */
  group?: string;
};
```

| `empty` | `{ value: string }` |
| `group` | `{<br />  group: string;<br />  items: ReadonlyArray<Item>;<br />}` |
| `icon` | `{<br />  item: Item;<br />  index: number;<br />  selected: boolean;<br />  highlighted: boolean;<br />}` |
| `iconEnd` | `{<br />  item: Item;<br />  index: number;<br />  selected: boolean;<br />  highlighted: boolean;<br />}` |
| `iconRight` | `{<br />  item: Item;<br />  index: number;<br />  selected: boolean;<br />  highlighted: boolean;<br />}` |
| `labelChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |
