`CopyButton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `button` element.


## CopyInput

### Basic

Set `value` to the string to show and copy. For install commands, see [CodeSnippet](/components/CodeSnippet); for display-only values, use [TextInput](/components/TextInput#read-only).

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput labelText="API endpoint" value="https://api.acme.io/v1" />
```

### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput labelText="API token" value="sk-1234567890abcdef">
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    API token
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="Use this token to authenticate API requests."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</CopyInput>
```

### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to select the full value when the field receives focus.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput
  selectTextOnFocus
  labelText="API endpoint"
  value="https://api.acme.io/v1"
/>
```

### Async copy

Pass an async `copy` function when the text is not available at render time, for example a token fetched on click. Feedback appears after `copy()` resolves.

While `copy()` is pending, the copy button shows a busy state and ignores clicks. On failure, the button shows `errorFeedback` (default `"Failed to copy"`) and emits `copy:error`.

Prefetch on hover with `on:mouseenter:copy-button`; `on:mouseleave:copy-button` fires when the pointer leaves the button.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const displayValue = "sk-••••••••••••";
  // For demo purposes only: NEVER hardcode secrets in production.
  const secretToken = "sk-1234567890abcdef";

  let cachedToken = null;

  async function prefetchToken() {
    if (cachedToken) return;

    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 300));
    cachedToken = secretToken;
  }

  async function copyToken() {
    if (!cachedToken) {
      await prefetchToken();
    }

    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(cachedToken);
  }
</script>

<CopyInput
  labelText="API token"
  type="password"
  value={displayValue}
  copy={copyToken}
  on:mouseenter:copy-button={prefetchToken}
  on:copy:error={(e) => {
    console.error("Copy failed", e.detail.error);
  }}
/>
```

### Obscured value

Set `type` to `"password"` to obscure the value. By default the value stays obscured; the copy button still copies the full value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput labelText="API token" type="password" value="sk-1234567890abcdef" />
```

Set `revealMode` to opt into revealing the value on interaction.

#### Reveal on focus

Use `"focus"` to reveal while the input is focused.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput
  labelText="API token"
  type="password"
  revealMode="focus"
  value="sk-1234567890abcdef"
/>
```

#### Reveal on hover or focus

Use `"hover-focus"` to reveal while the field is hovered or focused. The value stays revealed while the pointer is over the copy button. A disabled field never reveals its value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput
  labelText="API token"
  type="password"
  revealMode="hover-focus"
  value="sk-1234567890abcdef"
/>
```

### Masked value

Set `maskedValue` to show other text in place of `value`, such as a key with only its prefix and last characters. The copy button still copies `value`, and a form submits `value`. Unlike `type="password"`, browsers don't offer to save it as a password. `revealMode` works the same way.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput
  labelText="Secret key"
  value="key_9a8f2c4e1b7d34f2a"
  maskedValue="key_••••••••4f2a"
/>
```

#### Reveal with a button

To reveal on click, clear `maskedValue` from a button beside the field.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, CopyInput, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" align="end" gap={2}>
  <CopyInput
    labelText="Signing secret"
    value="sig_8c1f0a6e2b9d47a3e5f1c4b7a91f"
    maskedValue={shown ? undefined : "sig_••••••••••••a91f"}
  />
  <Button
    kind="ghost"
    size="field"
    icon={shown ? ViewOff : View}
    iconDescription={shown ? "Hide secret" : "Show secret"}
    on:click={() => (shown = !shown)}
  />
</Stack>
```

### Truncation

Long values truncate with an ellipsis when the field is narrower than the text. Focus or select the field to see the full value. Copy always uses the complete value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box maxWidth="20rem">
  <CopyInput
    labelText="Repository"
    value="git@github.com:carbon-design-system/carbon-components-svelte.git"
  />
</Box>
```

### Copy behavior

Replace or disable the default clipboard behavior.

#### Override

Pass a function to `copy` to replace the default Clipboard API behavior.

This example calls the Clipboard API directly, without the `document.execCommand("copy")` fallback.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput
  labelText="API endpoint"
  value="https://api.acme.io/v1"
  copy={(text) => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text)}
/>
```

#### Prevent

Set `copy` to a no-op function to disable copying.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput
  labelText="Read-only value"
  value="This value should not be copied"
  copy={() => {}}
/>
```

### Tooltip

On hover or focus, the copy button shows a tooltip with `iconDescription`. It renders in a floating portal so it is not clipped and flips when space is tight.

#### Direction

Set `tooltipAlign` to place the tooltip relative to the copy button, with Popover's `align` names. The default is `"bottom-end"`. It replaces `tooltipPosition` and `tooltipAlignment`, which still work and are deprecated.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput
  labelText="Top"
  value="https://api.acme.io/v1"
  iconDescription="Top"
  tooltipAlign="top"
/>
<CopyInput
  labelText="Right"
  value="https://api.acme.io/v1"
  iconDescription="Right"
  tooltipAlign="right"
/>
<CopyInput
  labelText="Bottom"
  value="https://api.acme.io/v1"
  iconDescription="Bottom"
  tooltipAlign="bottom"
/>
<CopyInput
  labelText="Left"
  value="https://api.acme.io/v1"
  iconDescription="Left"
  tooltipAlign="left"
/>
```

#### Alignment

Add `-start` or `-end` to align the tooltip with one end of the copy button.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyInput
  labelText="Start"
  value="https://api.acme.io/v1"
  iconDescription="Start"
  tooltipAlign="bottom-start"
/>
<CopyInput
  labelText="Center"
  value="https://api.acme.io/v1"
  iconDescription="Center"
  tooltipAlign="bottom"
/>
<CopyInput
  labelText="End"
  value="https://api.acme.io/v1"
  iconDescription="End"
  tooltipAlign="bottom-end"
/>
```

### Portal tooltip

The copy feedback tooltip is rendered in a floating portal by default, so it shares the same surface as the hover tooltip (the text swaps in place) and is never clipped by an `overflow: hidden` container. Set `portalTooltip` to `false` to use Carbon's inline feedback caret instead. A non-default `tooltipPosition` or `tooltipAlignment` is always portalled because the inline caret only supports the default placement.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, CopyInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<!--
  The feedback tooltip is portalled by default, so it is not clipped even when
  the input sits in an `overflow: hidden` container. Set `portalTooltip` to
  `false` to use Carbon's inline feedback caret, which is clipped here.
-->
<Box
  display="flex"
  direction="column"
  gap={4}
  overflow="hidden"
  border="subtle"
  borderStyle="dashed"
  padding={5}
  maxHeight="160px"
>
  <CopyInput labelText="Portalled (default)" value="sk-1234567890abcdef" />
  <CopyInput
    labelText="Inline caret"
    value="sk-1234567890abcdef"
    portalTooltip={false}
  />
</Box>
```

### Inside a modal

Because the feedback tooltip is portalled by default, it is not clipped inside a [Modal](/components/Modal). Set `portalTooltip` to `false` to use the inline caret.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, CopyInput, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open modal</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="API credentials"
  primaryButtonText="Done"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
>
  <CopyInput labelText="API token" value="sk-1234567890abcdef" />
</Modal>
```

```svelte
<CopyInput fluid labelText="API token" value="sk-1234567890abcdef" />
```

## CopyText

### Basic

Pass the value as the default slot. By default, the button copies the rendered text at click time using the native [Clipboard API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Clipboard/writeText), with a `document.execCommand("copy")` fallback when that API is unavailable or rejects. For a standalone icon button, use [CopyButton](/components/CopyButton); for a labeled, editable-looking field, use [CopyInput](/components/CopyInput).

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyText>postgres-prod-01.acme.io:5432</CopyText>
```

### Text

Set `text` to the string to copy. Use it when the copied value differs from what is displayed, such as a truncated URL. When the default slot is empty, `text` is also rendered as the value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyText text="https://api.acme.io/webhooks/incoming/f8a2c91d"
  >https://api.acme.io/.../f8a2c91d</CopyText
>
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyText text="f8a2c91d" />
```

### Inline in text

The value and button flow inline, so `CopyText` sits inside a sentence. Long values wrap, and the button stays on the last line of the value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyText, Text } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Text
  >Send requests to <CopyText>https://api.acme.io/v1</CopyText> with your API token
  in the <code>Authorization</code> header.</Text
>
```

### Custom feedback

Set `feedback` to customize the message shown after copying. Set `errorFeedback` to customize the message shown when copying fails (default `"Failed to copy"`). Set `feedbackTimeout` to change how long feedback stays visible, in milliseconds (default `2000`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyText text="f8a2c91d" feedback="Webhook ID copied" feedbackTimeout={4000} />
```

### Icon description

Set `iconDescription` to change the button's accessible name and hover tooltip. The value describes the button, so screen readers announce "Copy to clipboard" followed by the value. Each button on a page stays distinct with the default name.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyText
  text="postgres-prod-01.acme.io:5432"
  iconDescription="Copy endpoint"
/>
```

### Copy behavior

Pass a function to `copy` to replace the default clipboard behavior. It receives the resolved text. On failure it should reject, so the button shows `errorFeedback` and dispatches `copy:error`. The component dispatches `copy` after a successful copy.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyText
  text="f8a2c91d"
  copy={(text) => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text.toUpperCase())}
/>
```

### Tooltip

The button shows a portalled tooltip on hover and focus, and the same surface shows the feedback after copying. Set `tooltipAlign` to place it, with Popover's `align` names; see [CopyButton](/components/CopyButton#hover-tooltip) for the full behavior.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CopyText text="f8a2c91d" tooltipAlign="right" />
```

### Description list

Place `CopyText` in a `DescriptionListItem` to make one value copyable. The value is copied as rendered, or set `text` to copy something different from what is displayed.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    CopyText,
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Name">postgres-prod-01</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Endpoint"
    ><CopyText>postgres-prod-01.acme.io:5432</CopyText></DescriptionListItem
  >
  <DescriptionListItem term="Webhook"
    ><CopyText text="https://api.acme.io/webhooks/incoming/f8a2c91d"
      >https://api.acme.io/.../f8a2c91d</CopyText
    ></DescriptionListItem
  >
  <DescriptionListItem term="Region">us-east-1</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

---

### Component API

#### `CopyText` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLSpanElement` | Obtain a reference to the root element. | `null` |
| `text` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the text to copy.<br />Also rendered as the value when the default slot is empty.<br />When unset, the rendered value text is copied at click time. | _undefined_ |
| `iconDescription` | `string` | Set the title and ARIA label for the copy button | `"Copy to clipboard"` |
| `feedback` | `string` | Set the feedback text shown after clicking the button | `"Copied!"` |
| `errorFeedback` | `string` | Set the feedback text shown when copying fails | `"Failed to copy"` |
| `feedbackTimeout` | `number` | Set the timeout duration (ms) to display feedback text | `2000` |
| `copy` | `(text: string) => void \| Promise<void>` | Override the default copy behavior (`navigator.clipboard.writeText` with<br />a `document.execCommand("copy")` fallback). | `copyText` |
| `portalTooltip` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set how the "Copied!" feedback tooltip is rendered.<br />See `CopyButton` for details. | _undefined_ |
| `tooltipAlign` | `"top" \| "top-start" \| "top-end" \| "bottom" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-end" \| "left" \| "left-start" \| "left-end" \| "right" \| "right-start" \| "right-end" \| undefined` | Set the tooltip placement in floating-ui form: the side, then `start`<br />or `end` along it, as Popover's `align` takes. Above and below,<br />`start` and `end` name inline sides, so they swap under `dir="rtl"`.<br />When set, takes precedence over `tooltipPosition` and `tooltipAlignment`. | _undefined_ |
| `tooltipPosition` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | Set the position of the tooltip relative to the button. | `"bottom"` |
| `tooltipAlignment` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | Set the alignment of the tooltip relative to the button. | `"center"` |

#### `CopyText` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `CopyText` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:copy`       |
| `on:copy:error` |

#### `CopyText` $$restProps

`CopyText` spreads `$$restProps` to the `span` element.


## Countdown

### Basic

Set `seconds` to the length of the countdown. The time is written as m:ss, or h:mm:ss from an hour up, in a `role="timer"` element. The `end` event fires at zero, and right away if the time is already up.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Countdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Countdown seconds={125} />
```

### Format

Set `format` to `"h:mm:ss"` to always show hours.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Countdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Countdown seconds={1800} format="h:mm:ss" />
```

### Deadline

Set `until` to a `Date` or timestamp when the end comes from the server, such as a session timeout or a seat hold. The time left follows the clock, so it stays right after a reload and agrees across tabs. Set `seconds` to the full length too if a slot uses `fraction`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Countdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Countdown until={hold.expiresAt} seconds={600} on:end={releaseSeats} />
```

### Announcements

Screen readers hear `warnDescription` when `warnAt` seconds are left, and `expiredDescription` at zero, not every second. Neither is shown. For a session that times out, warn early enough to act: at least 20 seconds, and more when the page holds a long form. The default `warnDescription` says "One minute left", so change it when you change `warnAt`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Countdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Countdown
  until={session.expiresAt}
  warnAt={120}
  warnDescription="Two minutes until you're signed out"
/>
```

### Extend and pause

Bind `remaining` and add to it to extend the time, which also restarts a countdown that already reached zero. Bind `running` and set it to `false` to pause.

With `until`, the deadline sets the time left and changing `remaining` has no lasting effect. Extend by setting a later `until` instead, which restarts the countdown the same way.

### Custom rendering

The default slot receives `remaining`, `formatted` and `fraction` (the share of `seconds` left), such as for a ProgressBar. Below, added time fills the bar again, and the bar grows when the hold passes its first length.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Countdown,
    ProgressBar,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const HOLD = 600;
  let remaining = HOLD;
  let running = true;
  // The bar's full length. Added time fills the bar back up, and grows it
  // when the hold would pass its first length.
  let total = HOLD;

  function extend() {
    remaining += 300;
    total = Math.max(total, remaining);
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Countdown seconds={total} bind:remaining bind:running let:formatted>
    <ProgressBar
      size="sm"
      labelText="Seats held"
      value={remaining}
      max={total}
      valueText={formatted}
      helperText={remaining
        ? "Check out before the hold ends."
        : "The hold has ended."}
    />
  </Countdown>
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={3}>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={extend}>
      Add 5 minutes
    </Button>
    <Button kind="ghost" size="small" on:click={() => (running = !running)}>
      {running ? "Pause" : "Resume"}
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Countdown` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `remaining` (Reactive) | `number` | The seconds left. Starts at `seconds`, or the time to `until`; add to<br />it to extend the time, which also restarts a countdown that ended.<br />With `until`, the deadline decides the time left, so set a later<br />`until` instead. | `until == null ? seconds : secondsUntil(until)` |
| `running` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `false` to pause the countdown. | `true` |
| `seconds` | `number` | Specify the length of the countdown in seconds. With `until`, set it to<br />the full length so the slot's `fraction` is the share left. | `60` |
| `until` | `undefined \| Date \| number` | Specify when the countdown ends, as a `Date` or a timestamp in<br />milliseconds, such as a session timeout or a hold that the server set.<br />The time left then follows the clock, so it agrees across reloads and<br />tabs. Overrides `seconds` as the starting point. To extend the time,<br />set a later `until`; changing `remaining` does not move the deadline. | _undefined_ |
| `format` | `"auto" \| "m:ss" \| "mm:ss" \| "h:mm:ss"` | Specify how the time is written: `"auto"` uses h:mm:ss from an hour<br />up and m:ss below it, and `"mm:ss"` pads the minutes, as on a timer. | `"auto"` |
| `warnAt` | `number` | Specify how many seconds before the end to warn screen reader users,<br />with `warnDescription`. The countdown is not announced every second. | `60` |
| `warnDescription` | `string` | Specify the text screen readers hear `warnAt` seconds before the end.<br />It is not shown. | `"One minute left"` |
| `expiredDescription` | `string` | Specify the text screen readers hear when the time runs out | `"Time is up"` |

#### `Countdown` slots

| Slot | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | `{<br />  remaining: number;<br />  formatted: string;<br />  fraction: number;<br />}` |

#### `Countdown` dispatched events

| Event    | Detail |
| -------- | ------ |
| `on:end` | `null` |

#### `Countdown` $$restProps

`Countdown` spreads `$$restProps` to the `span` element.


## CssGrid

### Basic

`CssGrid` is the CSS Grid mode of the [Carbon grid](https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/2x-grid/overview/). It uses the same breakpoints, column counts, gutters and margins as the flexbox [Grid](/components/Grid). Each `CssColumn` is a grid item, so there is no `Row`. Columns wrap to a new row when the current one is full.

Set `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xlg` or `max` to the number of columns to span from that breakpoint up.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>sm: 2, md: 4, lg: 4</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>sm: 2, md: 4, lg: 4</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>sm: 2, md: 4, lg: 4</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>sm: 2, md: 4, lg: 4</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

| Breakpoint | Viewport width   | Columns |
| :--------- | :--------------- | :------ |
| `sm`       | 0-671px          | 4       |
| `md`       | 672-1055px       | 8       |
| `lg`       | 1056-1311px      | 16      |
| `xlg`      | 1312-1583px      | 16      |
| `max`      | 1584px and above | 16      |

Put each `CssColumn` directly inside a `CssGrid`. A wrapper element between them takes the column's place on the grid. Do not mix the two grids: a `Column` inside a `CssGrid`, or a `CssColumn` inside a `Row`, is not sized by the grid around it.

### Spans

#### Percentage

Set a span to `"25%"`, `"50%"`, `"75%"` or `"100%"` of the current column count. `span="50%"` is 2 of 4 columns at `sm`, 4 of 8 at `md` and 8 of 16 from `lg` up.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid>
  <CssColumn span="50%">span: 50%</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn span="25%">span: 25%</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn span="25%">span: 25%</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn span="75%">span: 75%</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn span="25%">span: 25%</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn span="100%">span: 100%</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

#### Responsive

Each breakpoint prop takes the same values as `span`: a number, a percentage, `true` to place the column automatically at one column wide, or a placement object. A value holds from its breakpoint up until a larger breakpoint changes it. Set `0` to hide the column, as `sm={0}` does here below `md`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid>
  <CssColumn sm={4} md={4} lg={8}>sm: 4, md: 4, lg: 8</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={2} lg={4}>sm: 2, md: 2, lg: 4</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={2} lg={4}>sm: 2, md: 2, lg: 4</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={0} md={8} lg={16}>sm: 0, md: 8, lg: 16</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

### Placement

Pass an object with `span`, `start`, `end` or `offset` to `span` or a breakpoint prop to place a column on specific grid lines. Lines count from 1, so a 16-column grid has lines 1 to 17.

#### Start and end

Set `start` and `end` to grid line numbers. Combine `start` with `span` to set the start line and the width, or with `end` to set both edges. A `start` of `0` returns the column to automatic placement.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid>
  <CssColumn sm={{ start: 2, end: 5 }} lg={{ start: 5, end: 13 }}>
    sm: lines 2 to 5, lg: lines 5 to 13
  </CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={{ span: 2, start: 3 }} lg={{ span: 4, start: 13 }}>
    sm: span 2 from line 3, lg: span 4 from line 13
  </CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

#### Offset

Set `offset` to the number of columns to skip. `offset: 2` starts the column on line 3. Set `offset` or `start`, not both.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid>
  <CssColumn sm={{ span: 1, offset: 3 }} lg={{ span: 4, offset: 12 }}>
    Offset 3, lg: 12
  </CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={{ span: 2, offset: 2 }} lg={{ span: 8, offset: 8 }}>
    Offset 2, lg: 8
  </CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={{ span: 3, offset: 1 }} lg={{ span: 12, offset: 4 }}>
    Offset 1, lg: 4
  </CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

#### Right-to-left

Grid lines count from the inline start. Under `dir="rtl"`, line 1 is at the right edge and the gutters swap sides, so the whole layout mirrors. Set the direction with [LayoutDirection](/components/LayoutDirection) or `dir` on `<html>`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    CssColumn,
    CssGrid,
    LayoutDirection,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl">
  <CssGrid narrow>
    <CssColumn sm={{ span: 2, start: 1 }} lg={{ span: 6, start: 1 }}>
      Start 1
    </CssColumn>
    <CssColumn sm={{ span: 2, start: 3 }} lg={{ span: 6, start: 11 }}>
      sm: start 3, lg: start 11
    </CssColumn>
  </CssGrid>
</LayoutDirection>
```

#### Vertical alignment

A column stretches to the height of the tallest column in its row. Set `align` to `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"` to fit a column to its content and move it to the top, middle or bottom of the row. `"stretch"` is the default. The values are the same as `align` on the flexbox `Column`. Alignment is vertical, so `dir="rtl"` does not change it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4}>
    <Stack gap={3}>
      <p>Tall</p>
      <p>column</p>
      <p>sets the</p>
      <p>row height</p>
    </Stack>
  </CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4} align="start">Start</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4} align="center">Center</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4} align="end">End</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

### Variants

#### Narrow

Set `narrow` to `true` to remove the gutter on the leading side of each column. Content hangs 16px into the gutter.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid narrow>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4}>Narrow</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4}>Narrow</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4}>Narrow</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4}>Narrow</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

#### Condensed

Set `condensed` to `true` to collapse the gutter to 1px, for dense layouts such as image grids or data displays.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid condensed>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4}>Condensed</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4}>Condensed</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4}>Condensed</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={1} md={2} lg={4}>Condensed</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

#### Column hang

Add the `bx--grid-column-hang` class to content inside a narrow or condensed column to line it up with content in a wide grid.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <CssGrid>
    <CssColumn sm={4} md={8} lg={16}>
      <p>Wide</p>
    </CssColumn>
  </CssGrid>
  <CssGrid narrow>
    <CssColumn sm={4} md={8} lg={16}>
      <p class="bx--grid-column-hang">Narrow, hung</p>
    </CssColumn>
  </CssGrid>
  <CssGrid condensed>
    <CssColumn sm={4} md={8} lg={16}>
      <p class="bx--grid-column-hang">Condensed, hung</p>
    </CssColumn>
  </CssGrid>
</Stack>
```

#### Row gap

Set `withRowGap` to `true` to add space between rows that matches the gutter. A narrow grid gets half of it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid withRowGap>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Row 1</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Row 1</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Row 2</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Row 2</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

#### Full width and alignment

The grid stops growing at 1584px and centers itself in wider containers. Set `fullWidth` to `true` to remove that maximum width. Set `align` to `"start"` or `"end"` to keep the grid at one side of a wider container instead.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid fullWidth>
  <CssColumn span="100%">Full width</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>

<CssGrid align="start">
  <CssColumn span="100%">Starts at the inline start</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

### Subgrid

#### Nested grid

Nest a `CssGrid` inside a `CssColumn` to split that column into its own grid. The nested grid is a subgrid: it has one track for each column the parent spans, and it pulls back the parent's gutters so its columns line up with the outer grid. Below, the subgrid's columns sit on the same tracks as the outer columns in the next row.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid withRowGap>
  <CssColumn sm={4} md={8} lg={4}>Outer</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={4} md={8} lg={12}>
    <CssGrid withRowGap>
      <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>Subgrid</CssColumn>
      <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>Subgrid</CssColumn>
      <CssColumn sm={4} md={8} lg={4}>Subgrid</CssColumn>
    </CssGrid>
  </CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>Outer</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>Outer</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>Outer</CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>Outer</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

Give the parent `CssColumn` a span at every breakpoint. Without one, the subgrid gets the full grid's column count. Use numbers, not percentages, for columns inside a subgrid: a percentage resolves against the page grid, so `"50%"` is 8 tracks at `lg` even in a 12-track subgrid.

#### Gutter modes

A subgrid has wide gutters by default, whatever the grid around it uses. Set `narrow` or `condensed` on the nested `CssGrid` to change them. `fullWidth` and `align` have no effect on a subgrid.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid withRowGap>
  <CssColumn sm={4} md={8} lg={16}>
    <CssGrid>
      <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Wide</CssColumn>
      <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Wide</CssColumn>
    </CssGrid>
  </CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={4} md={8} lg={16}>
    <CssGrid narrow>
      <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Narrow</CssColumn>
      <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Narrow</CssColumn>
    </CssGrid>
  </CssColumn>
  <CssColumn sm={4} md={8} lg={16}>
    <CssGrid condensed>
      <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Condensed</CssColumn>
      <CssColumn sm={2} md={4} lg={8}>Condensed</CssColumn>
    </CssGrid>
  </CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

### Custom properties

The grid reads Carbon v11's custom properties. Set them on `:root`, on any parent element, or on the `CssGrid` itself. The nearest value wins, whatever order the stylesheets load in.

| Property | Default | Sets |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `--cds-grid-gutter` | `2rem` | The gutter between columns |
| `--cds-grid-columns` | `4`, `8`, then `16` from `lg` | The column count |
| `--cds-grid-margin` | `0`, `1rem`, then `1.5rem` at `max` | The space at each side of the grid |

`--cds-grid-gutter` sets the wide gutter. A narrow grid keeps the trailing half of it. A condensed grid keeps its 1px gutter, and its column hang moves so content still lines up with a wide grid. Subgrids follow it too, whatever mode the grid around them uses. Percentage spans count the default columns, so use numbers with a custom `--cds-grid-columns`.

Set a value on `:root` to change every grid on the page, or on a parent element to change only the grids inside it.

```css
:root {
  --cds-grid-gutter: 3rem;
}

.flush {
  --cds-grid-margin: 0;
}
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div class="flush">
  <CssGrid>
    <CssColumn span="100%">3rem gutter, no outer margin</CssColumn>
  </CssGrid>
</div>
```

Set it on one grid with `style`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CssColumn, CssGrid } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<CssGrid style="--cds-grid-columns: 12">
  <CssColumn span={4}>4 of 12 columns</CssColumn>
</CssGrid>
```

---

### Component API

#### `CssGrid` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render a custom HTML element.<br />Props are destructured as `props` in the default slot. | `false` |
| `narrow` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to drop the leading gutter of each column, so content<br />hangs 16px into it. Takes precedence over `condensed`. | `false` |
| `condensed` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to collapse the gutter to 1px | `false` |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the maximum width.<br />Ignored on a nested grid. | `false` |
| `withRowGap` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to add a row gap that matches the gutter | `false` |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | Set the inline alignment of a grid narrower than its container.<br />Ignored on a nested grid. | `"center"` |

#### `CssGrid` slots

| Slot | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | `{<br />  props: {<br />    class: string;<br />    [key: string]: any;<br />  };<br />}` |

#### `CssGrid` $$restProps

`CssGrid` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.

#### `CssColumn` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render a custom HTML element.<br />Props are destructured as `props` in the default slot. | `false` |
| `span` | `CssColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the span, offset, start or end at every breakpoint. | _undefined_ |
| `sm` | `CssColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the small breakpoint (4 columns). | _undefined_ |
| `md` | `CssColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the medium breakpoint (8 columns). | _undefined_ |
| `lg` | `CssColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the large breakpoint (16 columns). | _undefined_ |
| `xlg` | `CssColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the extra large breakpoint (16 columns). | _undefined_ |
| `max` | `CssColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the maximum breakpoint (16 columns). | _undefined_ |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" \| undefined` | Set the block-axis alignment of the column in its row, as on `Column`.<br />A column stretches to the height of its row by default. | _undefined_ |

#### `CssColumn` typedefs

```ts
type CssColumnPercent = "25%" | "50%" | "75%" | "100%";

type CssColumnDescriptor = {
  /** Columns to span */
  span?: number | CssColumnPercent;
  /** Columns to skip before this one */
  offset?: number;
  /** Grid line to start at */
  start?: number;
  /** Grid line to end at */
  end?: number;
};

type CssColumnBreakpoint =
  boolean | number | CssColumnPercent | CssColumnDescriptor;
```

#### `CssColumn` slots

| Slot | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | `{<br />  props: {<br />    class: string;<br />    [key: string]: any;<br />  };<br />}` |

#### `CssColumn` $$restProps

`CssColumn` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## DataTable

### Basic

```svelte
  ]}
  rows={[
    {
      id: "a",
      name: "Load Balancer 3",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      name: "Load Balancer 1",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "c",
      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
    {
      id: "d",
      name: "Load Balancer 6",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "e",
      name: "Load Balancer 4",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "f",

```

### Cells

Customize cell rendering with `cell` and `cellHeader` slots.

#### Slotted

Use the `cell` slot to customize cell content. Access row and cell data through `let:row` and `let:cell`. Use the `cellHeader` slot for header cells.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable, Link, Tooltip } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Launch from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Launch.svelte";
</script>

<DataTable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  rows={[
    {
      id: "a",
      name: "Load Balancer 3",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      name: "Load Balancer 1",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "c",
      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
    {
      id: "d",
      name: "Load Balancer 6",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "e",
      name: "Load Balancer 4",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "f",
      name: "Load Balancer 5",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
  ]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="cellHeader" let:header>
    {#if header.key === "port"}
      {header.value} (network)
    {:else}
      {header.value}
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="cell" let:row let:cell>
    {#if cell.key === "rule" && cell.value === "Round robin"}
      <Tooltip triggerText={cell.value}>
        <p>
          Distributes requests evenly across servers.
          <Link
            icon={Launch}
            href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_DNS"
            target="_blank">Read more on Wikipedia</Link
          >
        </p>
      </Tooltip>
    {:else}
      {cell.value}
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```

#### Row state

The `cell` slot provides rowSelected and rowExpanded to conditionally render content based on row state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedRowIds = ["a", "c"];
  let expandedRowIds = ["b"];
</script>

<DataTable
  selectable
  expandable
  bind:selectedRowIds
  bind:expandedRowIds
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "status", value: "Status" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
  ]}
  rows={[
    {
      id: "a",
      name: "Load Balancer 1",
      status: "Active",
      port: 3000,
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      status: "Active",
      port: 443,
    },
    {
      id: "c",
      name: "Load Balancer 3",
      status: "Inactive",
      port: 80,
    },
  ]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="cell" let:row let:cell let:rowSelected let:rowExpanded>
    {#if cell.key === "status"}
      <span
        style="color: {rowSelected
          ? '#0f62fe'
          : cell.value === 'Active'
            ? 'green'
            : 'gray'}"
      >
        {cell.value}
        {rowExpanded ? "(expanded)" : ""}
      </span>
    {:else}
      {cell.value}
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="expandedRow" let:row let:rowSelected>
    <div>
      Additional details for <strong>{row.name}</strong>
      {rowSelected ? "(Currently selected)" : ""}
    </div>
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```

#### Editable

Use the `cell` slot to render form inputs that edit row values inline. Bind the input to the row field--for example `bind:value={row.qty}`--to update the rows array.

The table rebuilds cells only when the rows array reference changes. After an in-place edit, call `refreshRow(id)` to update columns whose display reads other fields on the same row. Use `bind:this` to obtain a reference to the component instance.

A column computed from other fields, such as a total, takes a `key` that isn't one of the row's, a `display` that computes its cells, and `sort: false`: it has no value of its own to sort by.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable, NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let dataTable;

  const rows = [
    { id: "a", item: "Enterprise seat", unitPrice: 89, qty: 12 },
    { id: "b", item: "Standard seat", unitPrice: 29, qty: 40 },
    { id: "c", item: "API overage (per 1K calls)", unitPrice: 2, qty: 150 },
  ];
</script>

<DataTable
  bind:this={dataTable}
  headers={[
    { key: "item", value: "Item" },
    { key: "unitPrice", value: "Unit price" },
    { key: "qty", value: "Quantity" },
    {
      key: "total",
      value: "Total",
      sort: false,
      display: (_value, row) => `$${row.unitPrice * row.qty}`,
    },
  ]}
  {rows}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="cell" let:row let:cell>
    {#if cell.key === "qty"}
      <NumberInput
        size="sm"
        hideLabel
        labelText="Quantity"
        min={0}
        bind:value={row.qty}
        on:input={() => {
          // Rebuild cells so the Total column picks up the new qty.
          dataTable.refreshRow(row.id);
        }}
      />
    {:else}
      {cell.display ? cell.display(cell.value, row) : cell.value}
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```

When you edit multiple painted rows in place, call `refreshCells()` once to rebuild derived columns for the visible window. Offscreen rows are computed when they scroll into view.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DataTable,
    NumberInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let dataTable;

  const rows = [
    { id: "a", item: "Enterprise seat", unitPrice: 89, qty: 12 },
    { id: "b", item: "Standard seat", unitPrice: 29, qty: 40 },
    { id: "c", item: "API overage (per 1K calls)", unitPrice: 2, qty: 150 },
  ];

  function snapshotQty() {
    return Object.fromEntries(rows.map((row) => [row.id, row.qty]));
  }

  let savedQtyById = snapshotQty();
  let hasEdits = false;

  function syncHasEdits() {
    hasEdits = rows.some((row) => row.qty !== savedQtyById[row.id]);
  }

  function updateTotals() {
    dataTable.refreshCells();
    savedQtyById = snapshotQty();
    hasEdits = false;
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Button
    kind="secondary"
    size="small"
    disabled={!hasEdits}
    on:click={updateTotals}
  >
    Update totals
  </Button>

  <DataTable
    bind:this={dataTable}
    headers={[
      { key: "item", value: "Item" },
      { key: "unitPrice", value: "Unit price" },
      { key: "qty", value: "Quantity" },
      {
        key: "total",
        value: "Total",
        sort: false,
        display: (_value, row) => `$${row.unitPrice * row.qty}`,
      },
    ]}
    {rows}
  >
    <svelte:fragment slot="cell" let:row let:cell>
      {#if cell.key === "qty"}
        <NumberInput
          size="sm"
          hideLabel
          labelText="Quantity"
          min={0}
          bind:value={row.qty}
          on:input={syncHasEdits}
        />
      {:else}
        {cell.display ? cell.display(cell.value, row) : cell.value}
      {/if}
    </svelte:fragment>
  </DataTable>
</Stack>
```

#### Menus and tooltips

The table's content scrolls, so it cuts off anything that opens past its edges. A menu, tooltip, popover or calendar in a cell that the table would cut off opens in a portal instead, over the page. Set the component's `portalMenu` or `portalTooltip` to `false` to keep it in the table.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DataTable,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    TooltipDefinition,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Edit from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Edit.svelte";

  const headers = [
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "renewal", value: "Renewal" },
    { key: "actions", empty: true, value: "Actions" },
  ];

  const rows = [
    { id: "a", name: "Load Balancer 3", protocol: "HTTP" },
    { id: "b", name: "Load Balancer 1", protocol: "HTTPS" },
  ];
</script>

<DataTable {headers} {rows}>
  <svelte:fragment slot="cell" let:row let:cell>
    {#if cell.key === "protocol"}
      <TooltipDefinition
        tooltipText={cell.value === "HTTPS"
          ? "HTTP over TLS, encrypted end to end"
          : "Plain HTTP, not encrypted"}
      >
        {cell.value}
      </TooltipDefinition>
    {:else if cell.key === "renewal"}
      <DatePicker datePickerType="single">
        <DatePickerInput
          size="sm"
          hideLabel
          labelText="Renewal date for {row.name}"
          placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
        />
      </DatePicker>
    {:else if cell.key === "actions"}
      <Button
        kind="ghost"
        size="small"
        icon={Edit}
        iconDescription="Edit {row.name}"
        tooltipAlignment="end"
      />
    {:else}
      {cell.value}
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```

### AI label

Mark AI-generated content with `AILabel` in three slots. The `decorator` slot puts a label beside the title. The `headerDecorator` slot renders for each header with `let:header`, and a column with an active label shows the AI gradient in its header and every cell. The `rowDecorator` slot renders for each row with `let:row` in a narrow leading column, and a row with an active label shows the AI gradient.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const headers = [
    { key: "service", value: "Service" },
    { key: "region", value: "Region" },
    { key: "forecast", value: "Forecast" },
  ];

  const rows = [
    {
      id: "a",
      service: "billing-api",
      region: "us-east-1",
      forecast: "+12%",
      generated: true,
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      service: "search",
      region: "eu-west-1",
      forecast: "+3%",
      generated: false,
    },
    {
      id: "c",
      service: "auth",
      region: "us-west-2",
      forecast: "-1%",
      generated: true,
    },
  ];
</script>

<DataTable
  title="Monthly spend"
  description="Forecast for next month"
  {headers}
  {rows}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="decorator">
    <AILabel>
      <p>Forecasts are generated from 90 days of billing data.</p>
    </AILabel>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="headerDecorator" let:header>
    {#if header.key === "forecast"}
      <AILabel>
        <p>Every value in this column is generated.</p>
      </AILabel>
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="rowDecorator" let:row>
    {#if row.generated}
      <AILabel>
        <p>This service was added by the cost assistant.</p>
      </AILabel>
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```

```svelte
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  rows={[
    {
      id: "a",
      name: "Load Balancer 3",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      name: "Load Balancer 1",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "c",
      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
    {
      id: "d",
      name: "Load Balancer 6",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "e",
      name: "Load Balancer 4",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "f",
      name: "Load Balancer 5",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
  ]}

```

#### Custom columns

Specify `width` or `minWidth` in `headers` to size a column. Unsized columns share the remaining space and grow to fit their content; a sized column stays at least that wide. This works with a [sticky header](#sticky-header).

Set `fixedLayout` to `true` to take each header's `width` as the column's exact rendered size instead of a floor content can grow past. Unsized columns then share the remainder equally.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name", width: "50%", minWidth: "200px" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol", width: "60px" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port", width: "60px" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule", width: "10rem" },
  ]}
  rows={Array.from({ length: 6 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: i % 3 ? (i % 2 ? 3000 : 80) : 443,
    rule: i % 3 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }))}
/>
```

#### Alignment

Set `columnAlign` in `headers` to align a column's header and cells. Values are logical: `end` is the right edge in left-to-right text and the left edge in right-to-left text; the default, `start`, is the left edge. Sortable columns keep their sort affordance.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTable
  sortable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    {
      key: "cost",
      value: "Monthly cost",
      columnAlign: "end",
      display: (cost) => "$" + cost,
    },
  ]}
  rows={[
    {
      id: "a",
      name: "Load Balancer 3",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      cost: 1240,
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      name: "Load Balancer 1",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      cost: 865,
    },
    { id: "c", name: "Load Balancer 2", protocol: "HTTP", port: 80, cost: 310 },
  ]}
/>
```

### Column visibility

Control which columns render without editing the `headers` definition.

#### Hidden columns

Set `columnHidden` to `true` on a header to skip that column in render while keeping it in `headers`. A single canonical header list keeps column order and definitions stable across toggles. Hidden columns are excluded from toolbar search, since a match the reader cannot see is a result they cannot explain. An active sort on a hidden column still applies, because hiding is presentational.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule", columnHidden: true },
  ]}
  rows={[
    {
      id: "a",
      name: "Load Balancer 3",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },

      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },

      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,

    },
```

#### Visibility menu

Add `ToolbarColumnVisibility` to a `Toolbar` for a ready-made column picker. It edits a bound `headers` array directly, so `DataTable` reflects each choice: picking an item toggles `columnHidden` for that column and keeps the menu open. Press <kbd>Escape</kbd> to close it, and the last visible column's item is disabled so a table never loses every column. Pass `toggleableKeys` to restrict the menu to a subset of columns; the rest are omitted and keep their current visibility.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarColumnVisibility,
    ToolbarContent,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let headers = [
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
    { key: "overflow", empty: true, value: "Actions" },
  ];

  const rows = [
    {
      id: "a",
      name: "Load Balancer 3",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      name: "Load Balancer 1",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "c",
      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
  ];
</script>

<DataTable
  title="Load balancers"
  description="Your organization's active load balancers."
  {headers}
  {rows}
>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarColumnVisibility
        bind:headers
        toggleableKeys={["protocol", "port", "rule"]}
      />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>
```

#### Persisting visibility

`headers` can carry functions in `display` and `sort`, so persisting the array itself through `LocalStorage` would silently drop them on the next page load. `toColumnSettings` converts a header array into a small `{ order, hidden }` object instead, safe to serialize; `applyColumnSettings` converts it back onto the original header array, keeping the functions intact. Store the settings object, not the headers, and derive `headers` from it on every change.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    applyColumnSettings,
    DataTable,
    LocalStorage,
    toColumnSettings,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarColumnVisibility,
    ToolbarContent,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const defaultHeaders = [
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ];

  const rows = [
    {
      id: "a",
      name: "Load Balancer 3",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      name: "Load Balancer 1",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "c",
      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
  ];

  let settings = toColumnSettings(defaultHeaders);

  $: headers = applyColumnSettings(defaultHeaders, settings);
</script>

<LocalStorage key="docs-column-settings" bind:value={settings} />

<DataTable
  title="Load balancers"
  description="Your organization's active load balancers."
  {headers}
  {rows}
>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarColumnVisibility
        {headers}
        on:change={(event) => (settings = event.detail.settings)}
      />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>
```

### Sticky header

Set `stickyHeader` to fix the header in place while the body scrolls.

#### Scrolling

Set `stickyHeader` to `true` to fix the header in place. This adds a maximum height to force scrolling. If the table's content is also wider than its container, scrolling horizontally moves the header and body together, with a scrollbar on the table's container.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTable
  stickyHeader
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  rows={Array.from({ length: 20 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: "Load Balancer " + (i + 1),
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: i % 3 ? (i % 2 ? 3000 : 80) : 443,
    rule: i % 3 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }))}
/>
```

#### Empty column

A header with `empty: true` shows no label, but body cells can still render content. Set its `value` to name the column for screen readers. The name stays visually hidden. Without a `value`, the header has no accessible name, and axe reports an empty table header. For row-actions overflow menus, also set `columnMenu: true` so the column stays narrow and the menu trigger stays centered. With stickyHeader enabled, the empty column stays aligned with its body cells.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTable
  stickyHeader
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
    { key: "overflow", empty: true, value: "Actions", columnMenu: true },
  ]}
  rows={Array.from({ length: 20 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: "Load Balancer " + (i + 1),
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: i % 3 ? (i % 2 ? 3000 : 80) : 443,
    rule: i % 3 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }))}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="cell" let:cell>
    {#if cell.key === "overflow"}
      <OverflowMenu flipped>
        <OverflowMenuItem text="Restart" />
        <OverflowMenuItem text="API documentation" />
        <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Stop" />
      </OverflowMenu>
    {:else}
      {cell.value}
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```

#### Max height

By default, stickyHeader caps the table height at 300px. Override the cap with `stickyHeaderMaxHeight`. Pass a number (interpreted as px) or a CSS length string such as `"24rem"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 20 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: i % 3 ? (i % 2 ? 3000 : 80) : 443,
    rule: i % 3 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }));
</script>

<DataTable
  title="Load balancers"
  description="Your organization's active load balancers."
  stickyHeader
  stickyHeaderMaxHeight={500}
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  {rows}
/>
```

### Virtualization

Set `virtualize` to render only the visible rows, improving performance for large datasets.

#### When to virtualize

Every row a table renders costs time to mount, sort, and filter. Past a few hundred rows, set `virtualize` or `pageSize` so the table only renders the rows in view or on the current page. Virtualization stays opt-in because it changes the layout: the body gets a fixed height and the header sticks.

Measured in Chromium on an Apple M2, with 1,000 rows and three columns (script, style, and layout):

| Interaction                           | Every row rendered | `virtualize` |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------ |
| Sort a column                         | about 30 ms        | under 2 ms   |
| Search, narrowing to 111 rows         | about 9 ms         | under 2 ms   |
| Clear the search, remounting 889 rows | about 40 ms        | under 2 ms   |

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Set `virtualize` or `pageSize` once a table can hold a few hundred rows. | A sort or a cleared search then touches only the rows in view, so it fits in a frame. |
| Set `debounce` on `ToolbarSearch` when a large table renders every row. | Rows filter once typing pauses, so each keystroke paints right away. |
| Set `deferFilter` on `ToolbarSearch` when clearing the search must paint at once. | The input and clear button update first, then the rows filter in the next task. Filtering becomes asynchronous. |
| Keep cell slots light, such as text and icons, in tables that render every row. | Each row mounts its cells, so a widget in every cell multiplies the mount cost. |

#### Large datasets

Virtualization renders only rows visible in the viewport, improving performance for large datasets. Set `virtualize` to `true` to enable. The header stays visible while scrolling--sticky positioning is applied automatically. Use `stickyHeader` when you need the full sticky-header layout. Container height defaults to 10 rows (itemHeight × maxVisibleRows). With `stickyHeader`, a numeric `stickyHeaderMaxHeight` drives the container height instead, so the virtual window matches the visible scroll area; a string value such as `"50vh"` does not.

The example below shows 10,000 rows with a filterable toolbar; only visible rows are rendered in the DOM.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
    ToolbarSearch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: 3000 + i * 10,
    rule: i % 2 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }));

  let filteredRowIds = [];
</script>

<DataTable
  sortable
  virtualize={true}
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  {rows}
>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch
        persistent
        placeholder="Search 10,000 rows..."
        shouldFilterRows
        bind:filteredRowIds
      />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>
```

Pass an object instead of `true` to customize behavior further. Besides the options below, `threshold` (default 100) sets the minimum row count before virtualization activates--smaller tables render normally--and `maxItems` caps how many rows are ever rendered, regardless of dataset size.

When `stickyHeader` is `false`, bind `scrollContainerRef` to obtain the scrolling element and control its position programmatically, for example resetting scroll to the top after the row data changes.

#### With a sticky header

Combine `virtualize` with `stickyHeader` and a numeric `stickyHeaderMaxHeight` to keep the virtual window sized to the visible scroll area.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 500 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: 3000 + i * 10,
    rule: i % 2 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }));
</script>

<DataTable
  title="Load balancers"
  description="500 rows, capped at 240px via stickyHeaderMaxHeight."
  stickyHeader
  stickyHeaderMaxHeight={240}
  virtualize
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  {rows}
/>
```

#### Custom row height

By default, virtual row height matches the table size variant (48px medium, 24px compact, 32px short, 64px tall). Use `rowClass` for a custom row height via CSS, and set matching `itemHeight` for correct virtualization.

#### Load more

`scrollend` fires when the virtualized table body is scrolled near the bottom. Use it to append the next page of `rows`. The component does not fetch or mutate `rows` for you.

This is a library load-more signal, not the browser's native `scrollend` (scroll stopped). It fires once per approach to the bottom, re-arming after the user scrolls away and when `rows` grows so another page can be requested.

`scrollend` only fires when `virtualize` is enabled. `pageSize` tables paginate instead of scroll-appending, and there is no scroll listener at all when both are off.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, DataTable, InlineLoading } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const PAGE_SIZE = 10;
  const TOTAL = 60;

  const headers = [
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
  ];

  let rows = [];
  let loading = false;
  let hasMore = true;

  function makePage(offset) {
    return Array.from(
      { length: Math.min(PAGE_SIZE, TOTAL - offset) },
      (_, i) => {
        const n = offset + i;
        return {
          id: String(n),
          name: `Load Balancer ${n + 1}`,
          protocol: "HTTP",
          port: 3000 + n * 10,
        };
      },
    );
  }

  async function loadMore() {
    if (loading || !hasMore) return;
    loading = true;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 400));
    rows = [...rows, ...makePage(rows.length)];
    hasMore = rows.length < TOTAL;
    loading = false;
  }

  loadMore();
</script>

<DataTable
  {headers}
  {rows}
  virtualize={{ containerHeight: 240, threshold: 1 }}
  on:scrollend={loadMore}
/>
<Box minHeight={7}>
  {#if loading}
    <InlineLoading description="Loading more..." />
  {/if}
</Box>
```

```svelte
      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
  ]}
>
  <Toolbar size="sm">
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch />
      <ToolbarMenu>
        <ToolbarMenuItem primaryFocus>Restart all</ToolbarMenuItem>
        <ToolbarMenuItem href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/loadbalancer-service"
          >API documentation</ToolbarMenuItem
        >
        <ToolbarMenuItem hasDivider danger>Stop all</ToolbarMenuItem>
      </ToolbarMenu>
      <Button>Create balancer</Button>
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>
```

#### Sticky

Set `sticky` on `Toolbar` to keep it pinned while the page or its scroll container scrolls, so batch actions stay reachable on a long table. Set `stickyOffset` to the distance from the top edge while stuck; a number is treated as pixels and a string can be any CSS length. When a UI Shell `Header` is on the page, the offset defaults to the header's 48px height so the toolbar does not slide under it. Pass `stickyOffset={0}` to opt out.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DataTable,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarBatchActions,
    ToolbarContent,
    ToolbarSearch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";

  const headers = [
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ];

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 40 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: 3000 + i * 10,
    rule: i % 2 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }));

  let selectedRowIds = [];
</script>

<DataTable batchSelection bind:selectedRowIds {headers} {rows}>
  <Toolbar sticky>
    <ToolbarBatchActions>
      <Button icon={TrashCan}>Delete</Button>
    </ToolbarBatchActions>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch persistent shouldFilterRows />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>
```

### Toolbar search with typeahead

Compose [SearchMenu](/components/SearchMenu) in the toolbar for a search typeahead with suggestions. `SearchMenu` does not read the `DataTable` context, so bind to `value` and filter the rows in the consumer. Selecting a suggestion sets `value`. For built-in row filtering without a menu, use [ToolbarSearch](#filtering).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuGroup,
    SearchMenuItem,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const headers = [
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ];

  const rows = [
    {
      id: "a",
      name: "Load Balancer 3",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "b",
      name: "Load Balancer 1",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "c",
      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
    {
      id: "d",
      name: "Load Balancer 6",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "e",
      name: "Load Balancer 4",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "f",
      name: "Load Balancer 5",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
  ];

  let value = "";

  // SearchMenu has no DataTable context, so filter the rows in the consumer.
  $: query = value.trim().toLowerCase();
  $: filteredRows = query
    ? rows.filter((row) =>
        [row.name, row.protocol, row.rule].some((cell) =>
          String(cell).toLowerCase().includes(query),
        ),
      )
    : rows;
</script>

<DataTable
  title="Load balancers"
  description="Your organization's active load balancers."
  {headers}
  rows={filteredRows}
>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <SearchMenu bind:value placeholder="Search load balancers...">
        <SearchMenuGroup label="Suggestions">
          {#each rows as row (row.id)}
            <SearchMenuItem text={row.name} />
          {/each}
        </SearchMenuGroup>
      </SearchMenu>
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>
```

### Export

Serialize headers and rows to a CSV string with `toCsv`. It applies each column's `display` formatting and skips empty and hidden columns, so the export matches what the table renders. It returns a string instead of triggering a download; pass the result to [`downloadFile`](/components/Link#download-link) (or wire it into [`LinkDownload`](/components/Link#download-link)) when you want a file. Export the current view by passing the rows matching `filteredRowIds`; values a spreadsheet would read as formulas are prefixed with a single quote unless `escapeFormulas` is `false`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DataTable,
    downloadFile,
    toCsv,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
    ToolbarSearch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const headers = [
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ];

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 10 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: 3000 + i * 10,
    rule: i % 2 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }));

  let filteredRowIds = [];

  function downloadCsv() {
    const matchedIds = new Set(filteredRowIds);
    const csv = toCsv(
      headers,
      rows.filter((row) => matchedIds.has(row.id)),
    );

    downloadFile(csv, "load-balancers.csv", "text/csv;charset=utf-8");
  }
</script>

<DataTable {headers} {rows}>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch persistent shouldFilterRows bind:filteredRowIds />
      <Button on:click={downloadCsv}>Export CSV</Button>
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>
```

### Filtering

Filter rows with `shouldFilterRows`.

#### Client-side

Set `shouldFilterRows` to `true` to enable client-side filtering. The default filter compares cell values as strings.

For pagination with filtering, bind to `filteredRowIds` and pass its length to the pagination totalItems.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    Pagination,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
    ToolbarSearch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 10 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: 3000 + i * 10,
    rule: i % 2 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }));
  let pageSize = 5;
  let page = 1;
  let filteredRowIds = [];

  $: console.log("filteredRowIds", filteredRowIds);
</script>

<DataTable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  {rows}
  {pageSize}
  {page}
>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch
        persistent
        value="round"
        shouldFilterRows
        bind:filteredRowIds
      />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>

<Pagination
  bind:pageSize
  bind:page
  totalItems={filteredRowIds.length}
  pageSizeInputDisabled
/>
```

#### Custom

Pass a function to `shouldFilterRows` to implement custom filtering logic.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    Pagination,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
    ToolbarSearch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 10 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: 3000 + i * 10,
    rule: i % 2 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }));
  let pageSize = 5;
  let page = 1;
  let filteredRowIds = [];

  $: console.log("filteredRowIds", filteredRowIds);
</script>

<DataTable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  {rows}
  {pageSize}
  {page}
>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch
        persistent
        value="round"
        shouldFilterRows={(row, value) => {
          return (
            /(6|8)$/.test(row.name) &&
            row.rule.toLowerCase().includes(String(value).toLowerCase())
          );
        }}
        bind:filteredRowIds
      />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>

<Pagination
  bind:pageSize
  bind:page
  totalItems={filteredRowIds.length}
  pageSizeInputDisabled
/>
```

#### Debounced

Set `debounce` on `ToolbarSearch` to the number of milliseconds to wait after typing stops before rows are filtered, which keeps large tables responsive. The `value` still updates on every keystroke, and clearing the search filters immediately. The default of `0` filters on every keystroke.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
    ToolbarSearch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 500 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: 3000 + i * 10,
    rule: i % 2 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }));

  let filteredRowIds = [];
</script>

<DataTable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  {rows}
>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch
        persistent
        shouldFilterRows
        debounce={300}
        bind:filteredRowIds
      />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>

<p>{filteredRowIds.length} matching rows</p>
```

#### Deferred

Set `deferFilter` on `ToolbarSearch` to let the browser paint before rows are filtered. The `value` updates at once, so the input and the clear button respond right away, and the table re-renders in the task that follows. Unlike `debounce`, clearing is deferred too, and typing is never delayed by a timer.

Filtering becomes asynchronous: `filteredRowIds` and the rows update shortly after `value`, not in the same update. Rapid changes coalesce, so only the latest value is filtered. Combine it with `debounce` to wait for typing to pause first, then yield before filtering. The first filter on mount stays synchronous.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
    ToolbarSearch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 1000 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: 3000 + i * 10,
    rule: i % 2 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }));

  let filteredRowIds = [];
</script>

<DataTable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  {rows}
>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch
        persistent
        shouldFilterRows
        deferFilter
        bind:filteredRowIds
      />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</DataTable>

<p>{filteredRowIds.length} matching rows</p>
```

#### Strategy

By default (`filterMode="remove"`), filtering unmounts non-matching rows, resetting focus, draft inputs, and open menus. This keeps the DOM small for large tables.

Set `filterMode` to `"hide"` to keep every row mounted and hide non-matching rows instead, preserving row state when cells hold inputs or other widgets. Type a note in the example, filter the row away, then clear the search--the note remains.

Setting `filterMode` to `"hide"` has no effect when pageSize is set or virtualization is enabled. Selection, select all, and filteredRowIds still reflect matching rows only.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    TextInput,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
    ToolbarSearch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const rows = Array.from({ length: 10 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: 3000 + i * 10,
    rule: i % 2 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
    note: "",
  }));
</script>

<DataTable
  filterMode="hide"
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "note", value: "Note" },
  ]}
  {rows}
>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch persistent shouldFilterRows />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
  <svelte:fragment slot="cell" let:cell let:row>
    {#if cell.key === "note"}
      <TextInput
        size="sm"
        labelText="Note for {row.name}"
        hideLabel
        placeholder="Type a note, then filter"
      />
    {:else}
      {cell.value}
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```
