| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `DataTableSkeleton` $$restProps

`DataTableSkeleton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## DatePicker

### Calendar types

DatePicker supports eight `datePickerType` values: `"simple"` (default, no calendar), `"single"`, `"multiple"`, `"range"`, `"month"`, `"quarter"`, `"year"`, and `"week"`.

#### Simple

The default `datePickerType` renders a text field without a dropdown calendar.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker>
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Subscription renewal date"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Single

Set `datePickerType` to `"single"` for one date with a dropdown calendar. Use a single DatePickerInput; clicking the field or calendar icon opens the calendar to pick one day. Bind `value` to read or set the formatted date string.

From the keyboard, <kbd>Down</kbd> in the field moves focus into the calendar, the arrow keys move by day and week, <kbd>PageUp</kbd> and <kbd>PageDown</kbd> move by month (by year with <kbd>Shift</kbd>), and <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> go to the start and end of the week. <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> picks the focused day and closes the calendar. <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it and returns focus to the field. To type a date instead, enter it and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Multiple

Set `datePickerType` to `"multiple"` to select several individual, non-contiguous dates from one calendar. Each click toggles that day; `value` holds the dates as a single string, joined with `", "`, formatted with the same `dateFormat` used by other calendar types. Shift-click a day to add the contiguous range between it and the last-clicked day to the selection; disabled dates within that range are skipped. From the keyboard, <kbd>Enter</kbd> adds or removes the focused day and the calendar stays open for the next one.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedCount = 0;

  function handleChange(event) {
    selectedCount = event.detail.selectedDates.length;
  }
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="multiple" on:change={handleChange}>
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Blackout dates"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    helperText={`${selectedCount} date${selectedCount === 1 ? "" : "s"} selected`}
  />
</DatePicker>
```

Selecting many dates never drops any of them from `value` or the `change` event's `selectedDates`; the field just visually truncates the joined string with an ellipsis once it no longer fits. Track `event.detail.selectedDates.length` (as in the example above) and surface it through `helperText` to show a count instead of relying on the truncated text.

#### Range

Set `datePickerType` to `"range"` for a start and end date. Provide two DatePickerInput components in order--start, then end--and bind `valueFrom` and `valueTo`. Both fields share one calendar: the user selects a span, and the start and end inputs update together. From the keyboard, <kbd>Enter</kbd> picks the start, then the end, and focus stays in the calendar between the two.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="range" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Report period start" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Report period end" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Month

Set `datePickerType` to `"month"` to select a month instead of a day. The calendar shows a 12-month grid for the current year; use the year stepper to change years. Pair it with a `dateFormat` that omits the day, such as `"F Y"` (for example, "January 2026").

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="month" dateFormat="F Y" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Billing month" placeholder="Month Year" />
</DatePicker>
```

##### Custom format

Pass a numeric `dateFormat`, such as `"Y-m"`, along with a matching `placeholder` for a compact "yyyy-mm" input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="month" dateFormat="Y-m" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Billing month" placeholder="yyyy-mm" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Quarter

Set `datePickerType` to `"quarter"` to pick a quarter of a year. The value is the quarter's first day in `dateFormat`; the `Q` token prints the quarter number, so `"\\QQ Y"` shows "Q2 2026".

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "Q2 2026";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="quarter" dateFormat="\QQ Y" bind:value on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Fiscal quarter" placeholder="Q1 2026" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Year

Set `datePickerType` to `"year"` to select a year instead of a day. The calendar shows a decade grid; use the prev/next controls to move between decades. Pair it with a year-only `dateFormat` such as `"Y"` (for example, "2026").

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="year" dateFormat="Y" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Fiscal year" placeholder="yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Week

Set `datePickerType` to `"week"` to select a whole week. Picking any day selects the first day of its week, per the locale, so `value` is that date in `dateFormat`. Pair it with a `displayFormat` that uses the `W` token, such as `"\\W\\e\\e\\k W, Y"`, to show the week number; it is the ISO week of the days the row shows. A `value` set from outside is kept as given. Multiple months (`showMonths`) are not supported.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <DatePicker
    datePickerType="week"
    displayFormat={"\\W\\e\\e\\k W, Y"}
    bind:value
    on:change
  >
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Sprint week" placeholder="Pick a week" />
  </DatePicker>

  <p>value: {value || "none"}</p>
</Stack>
```

#### Inline calendar

Set `inline` to `true` to render the calendar permanently below the input instead of in a popup. The input still shows the selected date. The calendar does not dispatch `open` or `close`, ignores `portalMenu`, and stops accepting selection or navigation while the input is read-only or disabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" inline on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Programmatic control

Drive the calendar from outside the component--set values, select many dates at once, or read the underlying calendar instance.

#### Open and close

Use `bind:open` to open or close the calendar from outside the component. It also updates when the user opens or dismisses the calendar. Opening through the prop dispatches `open`, and closing through it dispatches `close` with the `"programmatic"` trigger.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <div>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (open = true)}>
      Open calendar
    </Button>
  </div>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="single" bind:open>
    <DatePickerInput
      labelText="Follow-up date (open: {open})"
      placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    />
  </DatePicker>
</Stack>
```

#### Programmatic access

For everything else, use `bind:calendar`: it has `open()`, `close()`, `showMonth(date)`, `focusDate(date)`, `isOpen`, `view` (the month on show), and `selectedDates`. Set dates through `bind:selectedDates` instead.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let calendar = null;
  let weekendsDisabled = false;

  function openCalendar(e) {
    // Prevent the click from bubbling to the outside click
    // handler and closing the calendar immediately.
    e.stopPropagation();
    calendar?.open();
  }

  const weekends = [(date) => date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6];
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker
    datePickerType="single"
    bind:calendar
    disabledDates={weekendsDisabled ? weekends : []}
    on:change
  >
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Appointment" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={openCalendar}>Open calendar</Button>
    <Button
      kind="tertiary"
      on:click={() => (weekendsDisabled = !weekendsDisabled)}
    >
      {weekendsDisabled ? "Enable" : "Disable"}
      weekends
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

#### Multiple

Use `bind:calendar` to select or clear dates from outside the component with `calendar.setDate(dates, true)` and `calendar.clear(true)`. The example below selects 20 or 100 dates at once to exercise the field's truncation and rendering with a large selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedDates = [];

  function selectManyDates(count) {
    const now = new Date();
    const dates = Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => {
      const date = new Date(now);
      date.setDate(date.getDate() + i * 2);
      return date;
    });
    selectedDates = dates;
  }

  function clearAll() {
    selectedDates = [];
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="multiple" bind:selectedDates>
    <DatePickerInput
      labelText="Stress test dates"
      placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
      helperText={`${selectedDates.length} date${selectedDates.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} selected`}
    />
  </DatePicker>
  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => selectManyDates(20)}>
      Select 20 dates
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => selectManyDates(100)}>
      Select 100 dates
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={clearAll}>Clear all</Button>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

#### Range

Use `bind:valueFrom` and `bind:valueTo` to update the range from outside the component, such as preset buttons or filters.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let valueFrom = "01/01/2024";
  let valueTo = "01/31/2024";

  function advanceMonth(value) {
    const d = new Date(value);
    let month = d.getMonth() + 1;
    const year = d.getFullYear() + (month > 11 ? 1 : 0);
    month = month % 12;
    const lastDay = new Date(year, month + 1, 0).getDate();
    const day = Math.min(d.getDate(), lastDay);
    const mm = String(month + 1).padStart(2, "0");
    const dd = String(day).padStart(2, "0");
    return `${mm}/${dd}/${year}`;
  }

  function nextMonth() {
    valueFrom = advanceMonth(valueFrom);
    valueTo = advanceMonth(valueTo);
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="range" bind:valueFrom bind:valueTo on:change>
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Report period start" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Report period end" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Button on:click={nextMonth}>Next month</Button>
</Stack>
```

#### Selected dates

Use `bind:selectedDates` to read and set the selection as `Date` objects instead of strings in `dateFormat`. It stays in sync with `value` (or `valueFrom` and `valueTo`) both ways; setting it does not dispatch `change`. At mount, a non-empty `value` takes precedence. It is not supported by the `"simple"` type.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedDates = [];

  function nextWeek() {
    const start = new Date();
    start.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
    start.setDate(start.getDate() + 7);
    const end = new Date(start);
    end.setDate(end.getDate() + 6);
    selectedDates = [start, end];
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="range" bind:selectedDates>
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Sprint start" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Sprint end" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <div>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={nextWeek}>Next week</Button>
  </div>
  <p>
    selectedDates:
    {selectedDates.length
      ? selectedDates.map((date) => date.toDateString()).join(" to ")
      : "none"}
  </p>
</Stack>
```

#### Range presets

Build preset range buttons (for example "Last 7 days" or "This month") by setting `valueFrom` and `valueTo` from outside the component, the same way as the programmatic example above.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let valueFrom = "";
  let valueTo = "";

  function formatDate(date) {
    const mm = String(date.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0");
    const dd = String(date.getDate()).padStart(2, "0");
    return `${mm}/${dd}/${date.getFullYear()}`;
  }

  function selectLastDays(days) {
    const to = new Date();
    const from = new Date();
    from.setDate(from.getDate() - (days - 1));
    valueFrom = formatDate(from);
    valueTo = formatDate(to);
  }

  function selectThisMonth() {
    const now = new Date();
    valueFrom = formatDate(new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), 1));
    valueTo = formatDate(new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth() + 1, 0));
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="range" bind:valueFrom bind:valueTo on:change>
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Report period start" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Report period end" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => selectLastDays(7)}>
      Last 7 days
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => selectLastDays(30)}>
      Last 30 days
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={selectThisMonth}>
      This month
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

#### Month

Use `bind:value` to update the selected month from outside the component, such as a "previous month" button.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "03/2026";

  function previousMonth() {
    const [month, year] = value.split("/").map(Number);
    const d = new Date(year, month - 2, 1);
    const mm = String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0");
    value = `${mm}/${d.getFullYear()}`;
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="month" dateFormat="m/Y" bind:value on:change>
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Billing month" placeholder="mm/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Button on:click={previousMonth}>Previous month</Button>
</Stack>
```

#### Year

Use `bind:value` to select a year from outside the component, or `bind:calendar` to move the displayed decade--such as jumping to the current year or paging forward--without changing the selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
  let calendar = null;

  function selectCurrentYear() {
    value = String(new Date().getFullYear());
  }

  function viewNextDecade() {
    if (calendar)
      calendar.showMonth(new Date(calendar.view.getFullYear() + 10, 0, 1));
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker
    datePickerType="year"
    dateFormat="Y"
    bind:value
    bind:calendar
    on:change
  >
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Fiscal year" placeholder="yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={selectCurrentYear}>
      Select current year
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={viewNextDecade}>View next decade</Button>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Date constraints

Constrain which dates are selectable, for single, range, month, and year calendars.

#### Min and max dates

Use `minDate` and `maxDate` to constrain selectable dates. Values may be a Date, or a string in the same format as `dateFormat`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const start = new Date(2025, 0, 1);
  const end = new Date(2025, 11, 31);
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" minDate={start} maxDate={end} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Fiscal year 2025 date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Disabled dates

Set `disabledDates` to restrict which individual dates are selectable, in addition to or instead of `minDate`/`maxDate`. It accepts an array mixing date strings, `Date` objects, `{ from, to }` range objects, and predicate functions. Disabled days receive `aria-disabled` automatically.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  function formatDate(date) {
    const mm = String(date.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0");
    const dd = String(date.getDate()).padStart(2, "0");
    return `${mm}/${dd}/${date.getFullYear()}`;
  }

  const now = new Date();
  const disabledDates = [5, 15, 25].map((day) =>
    formatDate(new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), day)),
  );
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" {disabledDates} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Delivery date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

`disabledDates` is reactive: reassigning the array updates an open calendar, so most rule changes no longer need imperative control. Keep the array reference stable when the rules have not changed. A constant written in the markup is only evaluated once, but an array rebuilt in a `$:` statement, or built from an object that gets reassigned, is a new value each time. Equal dates and ranges are detected and skipped; a predicate function created inline is not, since functions can only be compared by identity, and each new one redraws the calendar.

#### Enable only specific dates

Set `enabledDates` for the inverse of [disabled dates](#disabled-dates): every date is disabled except those that match. It accepts the same entry types as `disabledDates`, and is reactive the same way.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  // Deliveries only run on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
  const enabledDates = [(date) => [1, 3, 5].includes(date.getDay())];
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" {enabledDates} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Delivery date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Range length

Set `minRangeDays` and `maxRangeDays` on a range picker to limit how many days a range may span, counting both ends. Once the start is picked, days that would make the range too short or too long are disabled until the end is picked. Only picks in the calendar are limited; typed and programmatic ranges are not checked.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="range" minRangeDays={2} maxRangeDays={14}>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Check-in" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Check-out" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Load availability for the shown month

The `view` event fires when the calendar is created and whenever it moves to another month, with the first and last dates on show in `event.detail.start` and `event.detail.end`. Use it to fetch the dates to block for that range, and pass them to `disabledDates`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    InlineLoading,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const format = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
    month: "short",
    day: "numeric",
  });

  let disabledDates = [];
  let loading = false;
  let summary = "";
  let latest = 0;

  // Stands in for a request to a booking service.
  function fetchBookedDays(start, end) {
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      setTimeout(() => {
        const booked = [];
        for (
          let day = new Date(start);
          day <= end;
          day = new Date(day.getFullYear(), day.getMonth(), day.getDate() + 1)
        ) {
          if ((day.getDate() * 7 + day.getMonth()) % 5 === 0) booked.push(day);
        }
        resolve(booked);
      }, 600);
    });
  }

  async function loadAvailability(event) {
    const { start, end } = event.detail;
    const request = ++latest;
    loading = true;
    summary = `${format.format(start)} - ${format.format(end)}`;
    const booked = await fetchBookedDays(start, end);
    if (request !== latest) return;
    disabledDates = booked;
    loading = false;
    summary = `${booked.length} fully booked days, ${format.format(start)} - ${format.format(end)}`;
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <DatePicker
    datePickerType="single"
    inline
    {disabledDates}
    on:view={loadAvailability}
  >
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Appointment date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  {#if loading}
    <InlineLoading description="Loading availability for {summary}" />
  {:else}
    <p>{summary}</p>
  {/if}
</Stack>
```

#### Keep out-of-range initial values

By default, an initial `value` outside of `minDate` and `maxDate` (or matching `disabledDates`) is cleared. Set `keepOutOfRangeValue` to keep it, for example to display legacy data that predates the current bounds.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const minDate = new Date(2025, 0, 1);
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="single" value="12/15/2024" {minDate}>
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Default (cleared)" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <DatePicker
    datePickerType="single"
    value="12/15/2024"
    {minDate}
    keepOutOfRangeValue
  >
    <DatePickerInput
      labelText="allowInvalidPreload (kept)"
      placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    />
  </DatePicker>
</Stack>
```

### Calendar options

Every calendar option is a prop: `allowInput`, `closeOnSelect`, `months`, `conjunction`, `monthLabel`, `parseDate` and `formatDate`, `align`, `direction` and `anchor`, `keepOutOfRangeValue`, `keepOpenFor`, `dayDescription` and `dayClass`, `weekNumbers`, `firstDayOfWeek`, and `animate`. The example below shows two months side by side.

#### Multiple months

The example below sets `months` so two months appear side by side in the calendar.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" months={2} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Day content

Set `dayDescription` to annotate days, such as dates with events. Return a short description for a date, or `undefined`: the text is added to the day's label for screen readers, and the day gets a marker. Set `dayClass` to add your own class to a day instead.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const now = new Date();
  const events = new Map([
    [5, "Design review"],
    [12, "Sprint planning"],
    [20, "Release"],
  ]);

  function dayDescription(date) {
    if (date.getMonth() !== now.getMonth()) return undefined;
    return events.get(date.getDate());
  }
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" {dayDescription} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Week numbers

Set `weekNumbers` to show a week number column beside the day grid. Weeks are numbered per ISO 8601. The column is only shown with a single month.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" weekNumbers on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Sprint start" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Abbreviated month label

Set `monthLabel="short"` to show the abbreviated month name from the active `locale` in the calendar header, such as "Sep" instead of "September".

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" monthLabel="short" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Enable open animation

By default, the calendar appears instantly with no animation. Set `animate` to animate the calendar as it opens and closes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" animate>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Deployment date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Calendar interaction

Control how users interact with the open calendar.

#### Calendar-only selection

By default, Carbon enables `allowInput` so typed dates work like an editable field.

Set `allowInput={false}` when you want calendar-only selection: the field still receives the chosen date and remains focusable for accessibility, but users cannot type into it; they must pick a date from the calendar. That reduces invalid or ambiguous typed values when you need strict control.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" allowInput={false} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Ship date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Handle invalid dates

By default, the calendar logs a warning and clears the field when it cannot parse a typed date. Listen for `on:error` to surface it in the UI instead. The `error` event fires before the following `change`, and that `change` has an empty `selectedDates`, so only clear the error once a `change` reports a real selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let invalidText = "";
</script>

<DatePicker
  datePickerType="single"
  on:error={(e) => (invalidText = e.detail.error.message)}
  on:change={(e) => {
    // Before the calendar is ready, the detail is the input's text.
    if (typeof e.detail !== "string" && e.detail.selectedDates.length > 0)
      invalidText = "";
  }}
>
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Meeting date"
    helperText='Type "tomorrow-ish" and press Enter'
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    invalid={!!invalidText}
    {invalidText}
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Keep open on select

By default, the calendar closes when a date is selected. Set `closeOnSelect={false}` to keep it open.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" closeOnSelect={false}>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Keep open for outside controls

By default, clicking anywhere outside the calendar closes it. Pass the elements that should not dismiss it as `keepOpenFor`, such as a preset button that updates the open calendar through `bind:selectedDates`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedDates = [];
  let todayButton = null;
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    bind:ref={todayButton}
    on:click={() => (selectedDates = [new Date()])}
  >
    Jump to today
  </Button>
  <DatePicker
    datePickerType="single"
    bind:selectedDates
    closeOnSelect={false}
    keepOpenFor={todayButton ? [todayButton] : []}
    on:change
  >
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
</Stack>
```

#### Position relative to another element

When `portalMenu` is enabled, set `anchor` to position the calendar against an element other than the input, and `align` (`"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`; `"start"` is the right edge in a right-to-left layout) and `direction` (`"auto"`, `"bottom"`, `"top"`) to place it. They have no effect while the calendar opens in place, where it is placed below the input by CSS.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor = null;
</script>

<Box bind:ref={anchor} border="strong" padding={5} width="28rem">
  <DatePicker datePickerType="single" portalMenu {anchor} align="end" on:change>
    <DatePickerInput
      labelText="Meeting date"
      helperText="The calendar aligns to the bordered container, not the input."
      placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    />
  </DatePicker>
</Box>
```

### Defaults

Preselect a date or starting month without controlling `value`.

#### Default date

Set `selectedDates` to preselect dates as `Date` objects when `value` is empty; the formatted result is written back to `value`. A non-empty `value` takes precedence.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" bind:value selectedDates={[new Date()]}>
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Start date"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    helperText="Value: {value || 'none'}"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Initial month

Set `initialMonth` to open the calendar on a specific month and year when there is no selection, such as a conference several months out. Unlike `defaultDate`, it never selects a date.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const now = new Date();
  const conferenceMonth = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth() + 6, 1);
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" initialMonth={conferenceMonth}>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Conference date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Formatting

Customize the date format and locale.

#### Date format

Use the `dateFormat` prop to customize the date format (default: `"m/d/Y"`). The input pattern attribute is automatically derived to match, ensuring native form validation works correctly.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
  let submittedValue = "";
</script>

<form on:submit|preventDefault={() => (submittedValue = value)}>
  <Stack inline gap={4}>
    <DatePicker bind:value datePickerType="single" dateFormat="Y-m-d">
      <DatePickerInput
        labelText="Contract effective date"
        placeholder="yyyy-mm-dd"
        helperText={submittedValue ? `Submitted: ${submittedValue}` : ""}
      />
    </DatePicker>
    <Button type="submit" disabled={!value}>Submit</Button>
  </Stack>
</form>
```

#### Human-readable display format

Set `displayFormat` to show a friendly date in the input while `value` and the submitted form field keep the machine format from `dateFormat`. It uses the same tokens as `dateFormat` and can change at any time. It is not supported with the range date picker type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
</script>

<DatePicker
  datePickerType="single"
  dateFormat="Y-m-d"
  displayFormat="F j, Y"
  bind:value
>
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Meeting date"
    placeholder="Select a date"
    helperText="Submitted value: {value || 'none'}"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Custom parsing and formatting

Set `formatDate` and `parseDate` when `dateFormat` tokens are not expressive enough, for example to format with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. Always set both: the calendar re-parses the input text it wrote.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const formatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
    weekday: "short",
    month: "short",
    day: "numeric",
    year: "numeric",
  });

  const formatDate = (date) => formatter.format(date);
  // Must accept whatever `formatDate` returns.
  const parseDate = (text) => new Date(text);
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" {formatDate} {parseDate} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="Select a date" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Multiple date separator

With `datePickerType="multiple"`, dates in `value` are joined with `", "` by default. Set `conjunction` to use a different separator; the same separator is used to parse typed input. It has no effect on other types.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="multiple" bind:value conjunction="; ">
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Blackout dates"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    helperText="Value: {value || 'none'}"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Locale

The `locale` prop accepts either a [BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) (for example `"de"` or `"ar-EG"`), or a partial locale object merged over the English defaults. A tag drives month and weekday names through `Intl`, and the first day of the week from the same [CLDR](https://cldr.unicode.org/) data. It defaults to `"en"`, which renders Carbon-spec single-letter weekday abbreviations (S, M, T, W, Th, F, S). Other tags use one-letter weekdays when those tell the days apart (日 月 火 for Japanese), and short names otherwise (So Mo Di for German).

To customize the weekday labels (for example, to use `Sun, Mon, Tue, ...` shorthands), pass a locale object. It may set `weekdays`, `months`, `firstDayOfWeek`, `rangeSeparator`, `weekAbbreviation`, and `yearAriaLabel`. A flatpickr locale module, such as `German` from `flatpickr/dist/l10n/de`, has this shape and can be passed as is.

The calendar's own labels are props: `calendarLabelText` names the calendar ("Choose a date"), and `previousLabelText` and `nextLabelText` name the arrows ("Previous month", "Next month"). Set them to translate the calendar for screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const englishLongShorthand = {
    weekdays: {
      shorthand: ["Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat"],
      longhand: [
        "Sunday",
        "Monday",
        "Tuesday",
        "Wednesday",
        "Thursday",
        "Friday",
        "Saturday",
      ],
    },
  };
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" locale={englishLongShorthand} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### First day of the week

The week starts on the locale's first day: Sunday for `"en"`, Monday for `"de"`. Set `firstDayOfWeek` from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday) to start it elsewhere without changing the locale.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" firstDayOfWeek={1}>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Shift start" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Non-English locale

Pass any language tag; no locale module needs to be imported. The example below uses German (`de`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" locale="de" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Termin" placeholder="tt.mm.jjjj" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Locale with year-first order

For locales where `Intl.DateTimeFormat` orders the year before the month (for example Japanese), the calendar header automatically reorders to match--"2000年1月" instead of "January 2000".

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" locale="ja" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="日付" placeholder="yyyy/mm/dd" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Right-to-left

In a right-to-left layout, the calendar runs from the right: the week starts at the right edge, and the previous month arrow sits on the right. <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> moves to the next day and <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> to the previous one. The calendar icon, the clear button, and the invalid and warning icons sit at the field's left end. A right-to-left locale such as `"ar"` names the months and weekdays and starts the week on Saturday. See [LayoutDirection](/components/LayoutDirection).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    LayoutDirection,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <DatePicker datePickerType="single" locale="ar">
      <DatePickerInput labelText="تاريخ النشر" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    </DatePicker>
    <DatePicker datePickerType="range" locale="ar">
      <DatePickerInput labelText="بداية الفترة" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
      <DatePickerInput labelText="نهاية الفترة" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    </DatePicker>
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Portal

A calendar that a container would cut off, such as a box with `overflow: hidden`, a scroll area or a [DataTable](/components/DataTable), opens in a portal for that open. Inside a [Modal](/components/Modal), the calendar always opens in a portal.

Set `portalMenu` to `true` to always render the calendar in a floating portal, which also escapes z-index stacking contexts, or to `false` to keep it in place. A portalled calendar leaves its container in the DOM, so CSS that targets the calendar as a descendant of the container does not match it.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Modal,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Select date</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  size="sm"
  modalHeading="Meeting date"
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="single">
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
</Modal>
```

#### Native dialog

When the date picker is inside a [Dialog](/components/Dialog) opened as a modal, portalMenu mounts the calendar into that dialog so it appears above the modal backdrop. The calendar uses `position: fixed` with viewport coordinates.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Dialog,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open dialog</Button>

<Dialog bind:open modal aria-label="Meeting scheduler">
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <p>
      With <code>portalMenu</code>, the calendar auto-mounts into the nearest
      <code>&lt;dialog&gt;</code>
      ancestor so it renders above the modal backdrop.
    </p>
    <DatePicker portalMenu datePickerType="single">
      <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    </DatePicker>
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => (open = false)}>Close</Button>
  </Stack>
</Dialog>
```

#### Native popover

When the date picker is inside an open element with a [popover](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/popover) attribute (see the [Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API)), portalMenu mounts the calendar into that ancestor so it stays in the popover top layer.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let popover = null;
</script>

<Button type="button" on:click={() => popover?.showPopover()}
  >Open popover</Button
>

<Box
  bind:ref={popover}
  popover="manual"
  width="min(100%, 28rem)"
  padding={5}
  border="subtle"
  borderStyle="dashed"
>
  <p>
    With <code>portalMenu</code>, the calendar auto-mounts into the nearest
    <code>[popover]</code>
    ancestor so it renders in the popover top layer instead of behind it.
  </p>
  <DatePicker portalMenu datePickerType="single">
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Button
    kind="secondary"
    type="button"
    on:click={() => popover?.hidePopover()}
  >
    Close
  </Button>
</Box>
```

### Events

Listen for calendar interactions.

#### Change

Listen for `on:change` to respond to value updates. For the `"simple"` date picker type (no calendar), `event.detail` is the input's string value. For calendar types (`"single"`, `"range"`, `"month"`, `"year"`), `event.detail` is an object with `selectedDates` (an array of `Date`) and `dateStr` (a string, or `{ from, to }` for `"range"`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Invoice due date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Close

Listen for `on:close` to know when the calendar closes and why. This event is only dispatched for calendar types (not `"simple"`). `event.detail.trigger` is `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, `"select"`, or `"programmatic"` (closed through `bind:open`); the detail also includes `selectedDates` and `dateStr`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker
  datePickerType="single"
  on:close={(e) => console.log(e.detail.trigger)}
>
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Maintenance window date"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Error

Listen for `on:error` to catch a date the calendar could not parse. `event.detail.error` is an `Error` and `event.detail.value` is the raw text that failed to parse.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker
  datePickerType="single"
  on:error={(e) => console.log(e.detail.error.message)}
>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Renewal date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Helper text

Add helper text to provide additional context or formatting instructions.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker>
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Contract start date"
    helperText="Example: 01/12/2026"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` on `DatePickerInput` to select the full value when the field receives focus.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker value="01/12/2026">
  <DatePickerInput
    selectTextOnFocus
    labelText="Contract start date"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

### Clearable

Set `clearable` to `true` on DatePicker to show a clear button while the field has a value. It takes the calendar icon's place, empties the date, dispatches `change` and then `clear`, and returns focus to the field. In a range picker, one button on the end input clears both dates. It is hidden while the input is read-only or disabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap="wrap" gap={7}>
  <DatePicker
    datePickerType="single"
    value="01/15/2024"
    clearable
    on:clear={() => console.log("cleared")}
  >
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Delivery date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <DatePicker
    datePickerType="range"
    valueFrom="01/10/2024"
    valueTo="01/20/2024"
    clearable
  >
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Check-in" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Check-out" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
</Stack>
```

### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker>
  <DatePickerInput hideLabel labelText="Report date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### AI label

Put an `AILabel` in the `decorator` slot to mark the value as AI-generated. The field shows the AI gradient. See [AI label](/components/AILabel#fields) for the revert flow.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    AILabel,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Renewal date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy">
    <AILabel slot="decorator">
      <p>Estimated from your current usage trend.</p>
    </AILabel>
  </DatePickerInput>
</DatePicker>
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Layer,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <DatePicker>
      <DatePickerInput labelText="Onboarding date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    </DatePicker>
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to `true` on DatePicker to use the fluid variant, which embeds the label inside the field. Fluid date pickers can be used standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), where the fluid variant is applied automatically.

Standalone fluid date pickers default to `288px` wide so the field matches the calendar menu. Inside a fluid form they stretch to `100%` of the column. Override the width with `style` or `class` when you need a different size (for example `style="width: 50%"`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Subscription renewal date"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Simple

The fluid variant also supports the default `"simple"` date picker type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid>
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="License expiration date"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Range

The range date picker renders both inputs inside a single fluid field.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="range">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Report period start" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Report period end" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Month

The fluid variant also supports the `"month"` date picker type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="month" dateFormat="F Y">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Billing month" placeholder="Month Year" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Year

The fluid variant also supports the `"year"` date picker type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="year" dateFormat="Y">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Fiscal year" placeholder="yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    TooltipIcon,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy">
    <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
      License expiration date
      <TooltipIcon
        tooltipText="Use the format mm/dd/yyyy."
        icon={Information}
      />
    </svelte:fragment>
  </DatePickerInput>
</DatePicker>
```

#### Invalid

Fluid date pickers display the error message inside the field boundary. Long messages wrap to multiple lines.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput
    invalid
```

### Sizes

Set `size` on DatePickerInput. The default is `md`.

#### Short

Set `short` to `true` on DatePicker for a narrower field, sized for a short format such as month and year. A full date like `mm/dd/yyyy` doesn't fit and is cut off. It only changes the field width for the default `"simple"` date picker type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker short dateFormat="m/y">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Card expiration" placeholder="mm/yy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Full width

Set `fullWidth` to `true` to fill the parent instead of the fixed field width, for example in a grid column or beside other full-width fields. A range splits the width between its two inputs.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fullWidth datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Invoice due date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Full width (range)

### Standalone calendar (experimental)

`DateCalendar` is the calendar on its own, rendered by Svelte rather than built by script: it renders on the server, and its `day` slot puts any content in a day. It picks a single date with `bind:value`, takes `minDate`, `maxDate`, `isDateDisabled`, `locale`, `firstDayOfWeek`, and `weekNumbers`, and moves with the arrow keys, Home, End, PageUp, and PageDown. Set `today` when rendering on the server, so the server and the browser mark the same day.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DateCalendar, Stack, Text } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = new Date();
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <DateCalendar bind:value />
  <Text>Picked: {value?.toDateString() ?? "nothing"}</Text>
</Stack>
```

#### Day content

The `day` slot receives `date`, `selected`, `today`, `disabled`, and `outside` (a day of the next or previous month).

```svelte
<script>
  import { DateCalendar, Stack, Text } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  // Fares by day of the month, as a flight search might show them.
  const fares = new Map([
    [3, 89],
    [9, 120],
    [14, 74],
    [21, 99],
    [27, 65],
  ]);
</script>

<DateCalendar>
  <svelte:fragment slot="day" let:date let:outside>
    {#if !outside && fares.has(date.getDate())}
      <Stack gap={0} align="center">
        {date.getDate()}
        <Text type="label-01" color="success">${fares.get(date.getDate())}</Text
        >
      </Stack>
    {:else}
      {date.getDate()}
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</DateCalendar>
```

### Migrating from flatpickr

The calendar used to be [flatpickr](https://flatpickr.js.org/). It is now built in, each flatpickr option it supports is a prop, and its markup uses Carbon's class names.

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Move each `flatpickrProps` key to its prop: `minDate`, `maxDate`, `allowInput`, `closeOnSelect`, `showMonths` → `months`, `conjunction`, `shorthandCurrentMonth` → `monthLabel="short"`, `positionElement` → `anchor`, `position` → `align` and `direction`, `allowInvalidPreload` → `keepOutOfRangeValue`, `ignoredFocusElements` → `keepOpenFor`, `disable` → `disabledDates`, `enable` → `enabledDates`, `altInput` and `altFormat` → `displayFormat`, `inline` → `inline`, `defaultDate` → `value` or `selectedDates`. | `flatpickrProps` is removed. |
| Replace `onDayCreate` with `dayDescription` or `dayClass`, and the other hooks with the component's events (`on:change`, `on:open`, `on:close`, `on:view`, `on:error`). | flatpickr's hooks are removed. |
| Replace flatpickr's range, monthSelect, and weekSelect plugins with `datePickerType`. | Those modes are built in. Other plugins are not supported. |
| Prefer a language tag such as `locale="de"` to an imported locale module. | Tags need no import; month and weekday names come from the browser's `Intl` data. A locale object still works when you need exact strings, so `locale={German}` behaves as before. |
| Pair the DatePicker with a [TimePicker](/components/TimePicker) to collect a time. | The calendar has no time picker. |
| Use `bind:calendar`'s `open()`, `close()`, `showMonth()`, `focusDate()`, `view`, and `selectedDates`; set dates with `bind:selectedDates`. | `bind:calendar` no longer hands out the engine. |
| Rename flatpickr classes in app CSS and tests (table below). | The calendar's markup uses `bx--date-picker__*` classes, with a modifier for each state. |
| Find the calendar by role in tests: `getByRole("dialog", { name: "Choose a date" })`, then `grid`, `row`, and `gridcell`. | The calendar is a dialog of month grids, not a `role="application"` labelled `calendar-container`. |

| flatpickr class | Carbon class |
| --- | --- |
| `flatpickr-calendar`, with `open`, `inline`, `static` | `bx--date-picker__calendar`, with `--open`, `--inline`, `--static` |
| `flatpickr-prev-month`, `flatpickr-next-month` | `bx--date-picker__nav-button--previous`, `--next` |
| `cur-month`, `cur-year` | `bx--date-picker__month-label`, `bx--date-picker__year-input` |
| `dayContainer` | `bx--date-picker__month-days`, with a `bx--date-picker__week` per row |
| `flatpickr-day`, with `selected`, `today`, `inRange`, `startRange`, `endRange`, `flatpickr-disabled` | `bx--date-picker__day`, with `--selected`, `--today`, `--in-range`, `--range-start`, `--range-end`, `--disabled` |
| `prevMonthDay`, `nextMonthDay` | `bx--date-picker__day--outside-month` |
| `flatpickr-monthSelect-month`, `flatpickr-yearSelect-year` | `bx--date-picker__grid-cell` |

The native mobile date input and the month dropdown are not available.

---

### Component API

#### `DatePicker` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `number \| string` | Specify the date picker input value.<br />Follows the inputs when the owning form resets. | `""` |
| `valueFrom` (Reactive) | `string` | Specify the date picker start date value (from).<br />Only works with the "range" date picker type.<br />Follows the inputs when the owning form resets. | `""` |
| `valueTo` (Reactive) | `string` | Specify the date picker end date value (to).<br />Only works with the "range" date picker type.<br />Follows the inputs when the owning form resets. | `""` |
| `calendar` (Reactive) | `import("./calendar-api.js").DatePickerCalendar \| null` | Bind to the calendar for programmatic control: `open()`, `close()`,<br />`showMonth(date)`, `focusDate(date)`, `isOpen`, and `selectedDates`.<br />Available for every `datePickerType` except `"simple"`, where it stays<br />`null`. | `null` |
| `selectedDates` (Reactive) | `ReadonlyArray<Date>` | Bind to the selected dates as `Date` objects, in the same order as<br />`calendar.selectedDates` (range: start, then end). Setting it selects<br />those dates and updates `value` (or `valueFrom`/`valueTo`). At mount, a<br />non-empty `value` takes precedence. Reassign the array to update; do not<br />mutate it.<br />Not supported with the "simple" date picker type. | `[]` |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the calendar. Updates when the user opens or<br />closes it. Setting it to `false` closes the calendar and dispatches<br />`close` with the `"programmatic"` trigger, as Modal does.<br />Ignored by the "simple" type and inline calendars. | `false` |
| `datePickerType` | `"simple" \| "single" \| "range" \| "month" \| "quarter" \| "year" \| "week" \| "multiple"` | Specify the date picker type.<br />Changing it after mount rebuilds the calendar.<br />`"week"` selects a whole week: a picked day becomes the first day of its<br />week, so `value` is that date in `dateFormat`. A `value` set from outside<br />is kept as given. | `"simple"` |
| `dateFormat` | `string` | Specify the date format.<br />Use `"F Y"` or `"m/Y"` with `datePickerType="month"`, and `"Y"` with<br />`datePickerType="year"`. | `"m/d/Y"` |
| `displayFormat` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a separate format for the text shown in the input, using the<br />same tokens as `dateFormat`. `value` and the submitted form field keep<br />using `dateFormat`.<br />Not supported with the "simple" and "range" date picker types. | _undefined_ |
| `maxDate` | `null \| string \| Date` | Specify the maximum date.<br />Changing it drops selected dates that fall outside, updating `value`<br />(or `valueFrom`/`valueTo`) and `selectedDates` without a `change` event. | `null` |
| `minDate` | `null \| string \| Date` | Specify the minimum date.<br />Changing it drops selected dates that fall outside, updating `value`<br />(or `valueFrom`/`valueTo`) and `selectedDates` without a `change` event. | `null` |
| `disabledDates` | `ReadonlyArray<DatePickerDateRule>` | Specify dates to disable in the calendar. A date matches a rule when it<br />equals a string or `Date`, falls within a `{ from, to }` range, or a<br />predicate function returns `true`. Strings follow `dateFormat`.<br />When `enabledDates` is also non-empty, `enabledDates` takes priority and<br />`disabledDates` is ignored, matching flatpickr.<br />Reassign the array to update an open calendar; mutating it in place<br />(`push`) is not reactive. If the currently selected date becomes<br />disabled by a rule change, it stays selected.<br />Only works with the "single", "range", and "multiple" date picker types. | `[]` |
| `enabledDates` | `ReadonlyArray<DatePickerDateRule>` | Specify the only dates to enable in the calendar; every other date is<br />disabled. Takes the same rule shapes as `disabledDates`. When both are<br />non-empty, `enabledDates` takes priority and `disabledDates` is ignored,<br />matching flatpickr.<br />Reassign the array to update an open calendar; mutating it in place<br />(`push`) is not reactive. If the currently selected date becomes<br />disabled by a rule change, it stays selected.<br />Only works with the "single", "range", and "multiple" date picker types. | `[]` |
| `minRangeDays` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the fewest days a range may span, counting both ends.<br />While the start is picked, days that would make a shorter range are<br />disabled. Typed and programmatic values are not checked.<br />Only works with the "range" date picker type. | _undefined_ |
| `maxRangeDays` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the most days a range may span, counting both ends.<br />While the start is picked, days that would make a longer range are<br />disabled. Typed and programmatic values are not checked.<br />Only works with the "range" date picker type. | _undefined_ |
| `initialMonth` | `null \| string \| Date` | Specify the month to show when the calendar opens with no date<br />selected. Only the month and year are used; the day is ignored.<br />Values may be a Date, or a string in the same format as `dateFormat`.<br />Clamped into `minDate` / `maxDate` when it falls outside them.<br />Ignored once a date is selected, until the selection is cleared.<br />Only works with the "single", "range", and "multiple" date picker<br />types. | `null` |
| `locale` | `string \| Partial<import("./calendar-dates.js").CalendarLocale>` | Specify the locale. | `"en"` |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | `undefined \| 0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | Specify the first day of the week, from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday).<br />Overrides the locale's own first day, which is used when unset. | _undefined_ |
| `weekNumbers` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to show each week's number beside it in the calendar.<br />Weeks are numbered per ISO 8601. The column is only shown with a<br />single month. | `false` |
| `allowInput` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to allow picking from the calendar only: the field<br />stays focusable but can't be typed into. | `true` |
| `closeOnSelect` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to keep the calendar open after a date is picked. | `true` |
| `parseDate` | `undefined \| ((text: string, format: string) => Date \| undefined)` | Parse typed text into a date. Receives the text and `dateFormat`;<br />return `undefined` for text that isn't a date. | _undefined_ |
| `formatDate` | `undefined \| ((date: Date, format: string) => string)` | Format a date for the field. Receives the date and the format in use. | _undefined_ |
| `months` | `1 \| 2` | Number of months the calendar shows side by side.<br />Not supported with the "week", "month", "quarter", and "year" types. | `1` |
| `conjunction` | `string` | Separator between dates in the field, with `datePickerType="multiple"`. | `", "` |
| `monthLabel` | `"long" \| "short"` | Show the month in the calendar header in full ("September") or short<br />("Sep"), from the active `locale`. | `"long"` |
| `direction` | `"auto" \| "bottom" \| "top"` | Where a portalled calendar opens relative to its field: below, above,<br />or whichever fits. | `"auto"` |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | How a portalled calendar lines up with its field. `"start"` and `"end"`<br />follow the writing direction: in RTL, `"start"` is the right edge. | `"start"` |
| `anchor` | `undefined \| HTMLElement` | Position a portalled calendar against this element instead of the field. | _undefined_ |
| `keepOutOfRangeValue` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to keep an initial value outside `minDate`/`maxDate` or<br />the enabled dates, instead of clearing it. | `false` |
| `dayDescription` | `undefined \| ((date: Date) => string \| undefined)` | Describe a day for screen readers, such as "2 events". The text is added<br />to the day's label, and the day gets a marker. | _undefined_ |
| `dayClass` | `undefined \| ((date: Date) => string \| undefined)` | Add a class to a day, such as for holidays. | _undefined_ |
| `animate` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to animate the calendar as it opens. | `false` |
| `keepOpenFor` | `ReadonlyArray<HTMLElement>` | Elements that count as part of the calendar: focusing or clicking them<br />doesn't close it, such as a "Today" button beside the field. | `[]` |
| `calendarLabelText` | `string \| undefined` | Accessible name of the calendar. Defaults to "Choose a date" (or a<br />month, quarter, or year, by `datePickerType`). | _undefined_ |
| `previousLabelText` | `string \| undefined` | Label of the button that shows the previous month. Defaults to<br />"Previous month" (or year, or decade, by `datePickerType`). | _undefined_ |
| `nextLabelText` | `string \| undefined` | Label of the button that shows the next month. Defaults to "Next month"<br />(or year, or decade, by `datePickerType`). | _undefined_ |
| `inline` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render the calendar permanently below the input<br />instead of in a popup. `open` and `close` events are not dispatched,<br />`portalMenu` is ignored, and the calendar stops accepting input while<br />the input is read-only or disabled.<br />Not supported with the "simple" date picker type. | `false` |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to show a button that clears the date. It appears while<br />there is a value, and not while the input is read-only or disabled.<br />In range mode it sits on the end input and clears both dates. | `false` |
| `clearButtonLabelText` | `string` | Specify the ARIA label for the clear button. | `"Clear date"` |
| `short` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for a narrower field, sized for a short format such as<br />`dateFormat="m/y"`; a full date like `mm/dd/yyyy` is cut off. Only<br />applies to the `"simple"` type; on other types it logs a warning. | `false` |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to fill the parent's width instead of the fixed input width.<br />A range splits the width between its two inputs. | `false` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`. | `false` |
| `portalMenu` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to always render the calendar in a portal, or `false` to<br />keep it in place. Left unset, the calendar opens in a portal inside a<br />`Modal`, or when a box around it (`overflow` other than `visible`, such<br />as a `DataTable`) would cut it off.<br /><br />When the date picker is inside a native `<dialog>` (opened with<br />`showModal()`) or an open `[popover]` element, the calendar auto-mounts<br />into that top-layer ancestor and uses `position: fixed` so it renders<br />above the backdrop instead of behind it. | _undefined_ |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the date picker element | `uniqueId()` |

#### `DatePicker` typedefs

```ts
type DatePickerDateRule =
  | string
  | Date
  | {
      from: string | Date;
      to: string | Date;
    }
  | ((date: Date) => boolean);
```

#### `DatePicker` dispatched events

## DescriptionList

### Layouts

#### Vertical

`DescriptionList` renders a native `<dl>`. Each `DescriptionListItem` wraps one `<dt>` term and its `<dd>` detail, so screen readers announce them as a description list rather than a table. Use [StructuredList](/components/StructuredList) instead when rows need selection or tabular columns.

By default, each term sits above its detail. Set the term with the `term` prop; slot the detail as children.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Name">postgres-prod-01</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Engine">PostgreSQL 16.2</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Region">us-east-1</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Created">March 14, 2026</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

#### Horizontal

Set `layout` to `"horizontal"` to place each term beside its detail.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList layout="horizontal">
  <DescriptionListItem term="Name">postgres-prod-01</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Engine">PostgreSQL 16.2</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Region">us-east-1</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Created">March 14, 2026</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

#### Summary

Set `layout` to `"summary"` for an order or price breakdown. Each detail sits at the right edge in tabular figures, so amounts line up, and a long term wraps without pushing it. Set `total` on the last item to rule it off with a larger detail.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList layout="summary" gap={3}>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Subtotal">$128.00</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Shipping">$9.00</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Estimated tax">$10.24</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Total" total>$147.24</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

#### Columns

Set `columns` to arrange items in an equal-width grid.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList columns={2}>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Name">postgres-prod-01</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Engine">PostgreSQL 16.2</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Region">us-east-1</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Created">March 14, 2026</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

### Rich terms

Use the `term` slot for more than plain text, such as a Toggletip that explains a charge or a link to change a plan. The slot overrides the `term` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
    Link,
    Toggletip,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList layout="summary" gap={3}>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Subtotal">$128.00</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem>
    <svelte:fragment slot="term">
      <Toggletip labelText="Estimated tax"
        >Based on your shipping address. The final amount is set at checkout.</Toggletip
      >
    </svelte:fragment>
    $10.24
  </DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem>
    <svelte:fragment slot="term">
      Pro plan, billed yearly · <Link size="sm" href="#">Change</Link>
    </svelte:fragment>
    $96.00
  </DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Total" total>$234.24</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

### Breakdowns

#### Sections

Set `divider` to rule an item off from the items above without enlarging it, such as to start a group of taxes and fees.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList layout="summary" gap={3}>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Two nights, Deluxe King"
    >$1,240.00</DescriptionListItem
  >
  <DescriptionListItem term="Breakfast for two">$64.00</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="City tax" divider>$18.00</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Service fee">$25.00</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Total" total>$1,347.00</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

#### Discounts and original prices

Write a discount with the minus sign (-, U+2212) and name it in the term. Screen readers don't announce strikethrough, so give a struck-through price visually hidden text.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList layout="summary" gap={3}>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Annual plan">
    <s><span class="bx--visually-hidden">Was </span>$160.00</s> $128.00
  </DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Promo SPRING10">-$12.80</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Total" total>$115.20</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

#### Live total

A total that changes as the user edits the order changes silently for screen reader users. Set `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"` on the total item, so the term and the new amount are read together.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
    NumberInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <NumberInput labelText="Nights" min={1} max={14} bind:value={nights} />
  <DescriptionList layout="summary" gap={3}>
    <DescriptionListItem term="{nights} nights at $620.00"
      >${(nights * 620).toLocaleString("en-US")}.00</DescriptionListItem
    >
    <DescriptionListItem term="Service fee">$25.00</DescriptionListItem>
    <DescriptionListItem
      term="Total"
      total
      aria-live="polite"
      aria-atomic="true"
      >${(nights * 620 + 25).toLocaleString("en-US")}.00</DescriptionListItem
    >
  </DescriptionList>
</Stack>
```

#### Loading

While amounts are calculated, put a SkeletonText with `noMargin` in each detail, and set `aria-busy="true"` on the list until they arrive.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
    SkeletonText,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList layout="summary" gap={3} aria-busy="true">
  <DescriptionListItem term="Subtotal"
    ><SkeletonText noMargin width="64px" /></DescriptionListItem
  >
  <DescriptionListItem term="Estimated tax"
    ><SkeletonText noMargin width="48px" /></DescriptionListItem
  >
  <DescriptionListItem term="Total" total
    ><SkeletonText noMargin width="96px" /></DescriptionListItem
  >
</DescriptionList>
```

#### Usage

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Use `layout="summary"` for amounts and other short values. | Each detail keeps at least its longest word on one line, so a long sentence-like detail wraps and loses the clean right edge. |
| Mark only the final line `total`, and use `divider` for sections above it. | A larger detail reads as the answer; two of them compete. |
| Name a discount in the term, not only by the sign of the amount. | The term carries the meaning even if the minus sign is missed. |
| Keep live regions to the total. | Announcing every line on each change repeats information the user just entered. |

### Gap

Use `gap` to pick a spacing step from 1-13 (the same scale as [Stack](/components/Stack)), or pass a custom value such as `"22px"`. The default is step 5 (16px).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList gap={7}>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Name">postgres-prod-01</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Engine">PostgreSQL 16.2</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Region">us-east-1</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

### Copyable value

To copy one value, put [CopyText](/components/CopyText) in an item's detail. It renders the value inline with a compact copy button beside it. The value is copied as rendered, or set `text` to copy something different from what is displayed.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    CopyText,
    DescriptionList,
    DescriptionListItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DescriptionList>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Name">postgres-prod-01</DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem term="Endpoint"
    ><CopyText>postgres-prod-01.acme.io:5432</CopyText></DescriptionListItem
  >
  <DescriptionListItem term="Webhook"
    ><CopyText text="https://api.acme.io/webhooks/incoming/f8a2c91d"
      >https://api.acme.io/.../f8a2c91d</CopyText
    ></DescriptionListItem
  >
  <DescriptionListItem term="Region">us-east-1</DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

---

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal" \| "summary"` | Specify whether each term/detail pair stacks (term above detail),<br />sits side by side (term beside detail), or is a summary line with the<br />detail right-aligned in tabular figures, as in an order total.
