### Submission

Fluid inputs submit exactly like their default variants: give each field a `name`, and read the values with `request.formData()` in a SvelteKit form action. See [Form](/components/Form#submitted-values) for what each component submits and [Form](/components/Form#form-actions) for a complete action.

#### Server-side validation

This example stands in for a form action in the browser. Fluid inputs do not show `helperText`, so put formatting hints in the `labelText` or `placeholder` and let the server's message appear through `invalidText`. The actions sit below the fluid form in a full-width [ActionSet](/components/ActionSet) and target it with `form`, the way a modal footer would.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    ActionSet,
    Button,
    Dropdown,
    FluidForm,
    InlineNotification,
    Stack,
    TextArea,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const regions = [
    { id: "us-east", text: "US East (Washington DC)" },
    { id: "eu-de", text: "EU Germany (Frankfurt)" },
  ];

  /**
   * Stand-in for a SvelteKit form action: reads FormData, validates on the
   * "server", and returns either the errors with the submitted values or a
   * success result.
   * @param {FormData} data
   */
  async function createAppAction(data) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 600));
    const name = String(data.get("name") ?? "").trim();
    const region = String(data.get("region") ?? "");
    const description = String(data.get("description") ?? "");

    /** @type {Record<string, string>} */
    const errors = {};
    if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,}$/.test(name)) {
      errors.name = "Use 3 or more lowercase letters, numbers, or dashes.";
    }
    if (region === "") errors.region = "Choose a deployment region.";

    if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) {
      return {
        type: "failure",
        data: { values: { name, region, description }, errors },
      };
    }
    return { type: "success", data: { created: name } };
  }

  /** The action result, like SvelteKit's `form` prop. */
  let form = null;
  /** Dropdown does not restore itself on reset, so track it and clear it in `on:reset`. */
  let region;
  let submitting = false;

  $: values = form?.type === "failure" ? form.data.values : {};
  $: errors = form?.type === "failure" ? form.data.errors : {};
</script>

<FluidForm
  id="fluid-form-server-validation"
  novalidate
  on:reset={() => (region = undefined)}
  on:submit={async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const formElement = /** @type {HTMLFormElement} */ (e.currentTarget);
    submitting = true;
    form = await createAppAction(new FormData(formElement));
    submitting = false;
    if (form.type === "success") formElement.reset();
  }}
>
  <TextInput
    name="name"
    labelText="Application name"
    placeholder="customer-portal"
    value={values.name ?? ""}
    invalid={!!errors.name}
    invalidText={errors.name}
  />
  <Dropdown
    name="region"
    labelText="Deployment region"
    label="Choose a region"
    items={regions}
    bind:selectedId={region}
    invalid={!!errors.region}
    invalidText={errors.region}
  />
  <TextArea
    name="description"
    labelText="Description (optional)"
    value={values.description ?? ""}
  />
</FluidForm>

<Stack gap={5}>
  {#if form?.type === "success"}
    <InlineNotification
      kind="success"
      title="Application created"
      subtitle={`${form.data.created} is being deployed.`}
      hideCloseButton
    />
  {/if}
  <ActionSet size="lg">
    <Button kind="secondary" type="reset" form="fluid-form-server-validation">
      Reset
    </Button>
    <Button
      type="submit"
      form="fluid-form-server-validation"
      loading={submitting}
      loadingDescription="Creating"
    >
      Create application
    </Button>
  </ActionSet>
</Stack>
```

`Dropdown` keeps its selection through a reset. To clear it after a successful submission, reset its bound value in `on:reset`, as `region` is here.

#### SvelteKit enhance

Set `actions` to apply SvelteKit's `enhance` (or any other action) to the underlying form element. See [Form](/components/Form#sveltekit-enhance) for usage details.

```svelte
<script>
  import { enhance } from "$app/forms";
  import { FluidForm, TextInput, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FluidForm method="POST" action="?/save" actions={[enhance]}>
  <TextInput name="name" labelText="Name" />
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</FluidForm>
```

A complete fluid form action, returning the submitted values and the errors on failure:

```svelte
<!-- src/routes/apps/new/+page.svelte -->
<script>
  import { enhance } from "$app/forms";
  import {
    Button,
    Dropdown,
    FluidForm,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  export let form;

  $: values = form?.values ?? {};
  $: errors = form?.errors ?? {};
</script>

<FluidForm method="POST" novalidate actions={[enhance]}>
  <TextInput
    name="name"
    labelText="Application name (lowercase, dashes)"
    value={values.name ?? ""}
    invalid={!!errors.name}
    invalidText={errors.name}
  />
  <Dropdown
    name="region"
    labelText="Deployment region"
    selectedId={values.region || undefined}
    items={[
      { id: "us-east", text: "US East (Washington DC)" },
      { id: "eu-de", text: "EU Germany (Frankfurt)" },
    ]}
    invalid={!!errors.region}
    invalidText={errors.region}
  />
  <Button type="submit">Create application</Button>
</FluidForm>
```

```js
// src/routes/apps/new/+page.server.js
import { fail } from "@sveltejs/kit";

export const actions = {
  default: async ({ request }) => {
    const data = await request.formData();
    const name = String(data.get("name") ?? "").trim();
    const region = String(data.get("region") ?? "");

    const errors = {};
    if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,}$/.test(name))
      errors.name = "Use 3 or more lowercase letters, numbers, or dashes.";
    if (region === "") errors.region = "Choose a deployment region.";

    if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) {
      return fail(400, { values: { name, region }, errors });
    }

    // Create the application here.
    return { created: name };
  },
};
```

### Best practices

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Follow the [Form best practices](/components/Form#best-practices) | Name every field, validate on the server, and return the submitted values with the errors. |
| Put hints in the label or placeholder | Fluid inputs hide `helperText`, so guidance placed there never reaches the user. |
| Show one clear `invalidText` per field | The fluid variant renders it inside the field's border, next to the value it describes. |
| Mirror the loaded form with the fluid skeletons | The layout does not shift when the initial values arrive. |
| Inside a modal, give the form an `id` and set the modal's `formId` | The modal's primary button then submits the form (see [Modal](/components/Modal#with-form-submission)). |

---

### Component API

#### `FluidForm` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLFormElement` | Obtain a reference to the form element. | `null` |
| `actions` | `ReadonlyArray<FormActionEntry>` | Apply Svelte actions to the underlying form element.<br />Each entry is an action or a `[action, parameter]` tuple.<br />Use this for SvelteKit's `enhance` and other form actions that<br />cannot target components with `use:`. | `[]` |

#### `FluidForm` typedefs

```ts
type FormAction = import("svelte/action").Action<HTMLFormElement, any>;

type FormActionEntry = FormAction | readonly [FormAction, any];
```

#### `FluidForm` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `FluidForm` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:keydown`    |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |
| `on:reset`      |
| `on:submit`     |

#### `FluidForm` $$restProps

`FluidForm` spreads `$$restProps` to the `form` element.


## Form

### Basic

Group related controls with `FormGroup`, and give every field a `name` so it submits. The placeholder option has an empty value and the select is `required`, so the browser asks for a plan before it submits.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Checkbox,
    Form,
    FormGroup,
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form on:submit={(e) => e.preventDefault()}>
  <FormGroup legendText="Security settings">
    <Checkbox name="sso" labelText="Enable single sign-on (SSO)" checked />
    <Checkbox name="mfa" labelText="Require multi-factor authentication" />
    <Checkbox name="audit" labelText="Enable audit logging" disabled />
  </FormGroup>
  <Stack gap={7}>
    <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Storage tier" name="tier" selected="standard">
      <RadioButton value="free" labelText="Free (1 GB)" />
      <RadioButton value="standard" labelText="Standard (10 GB)" />
      <RadioButton value="pro" labelText="Pro (128 GB)" disabled />
    </RadioButtonGroup>
    <Select name="plan" labelText="Account plan" required>
      <SelectItem disabled hidden value="" text="Choose a plan" />
      <SelectItem value="free" text="Free" />
      <SelectItem value="starter" text="Starter" />
      <SelectItem value="team" text="Team" />
    </Select>
    <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
  </Stack>
</Form>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` on `Form` to size every field inside it. Text inputs, number inputs, selects, dropdowns, date and time pickers, and their skeletons all inherit it. Buttons take the same height (`xs`, `small` for `sm`, and the 48px default for `xl`), unless inside an `ActionSet`. A field's or button's own `size` takes precedence.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Dropdown,
    Form,
    NumberInput,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form size="xs" on:submit={(e) => e.preventDefault()}>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <TextInput name="service" labelText="Service name" value="billing-api" />
    <NumberInput name="replicas" labelText="Replicas" value={3} />
    <Dropdown
      labelText="Region"
      selectedId="us-east-1"
      items={[
        { id: "us-east-1", text: "US East (N. Virginia)" },
        { id: "eu-west-1", text: "EU West (Ireland)" },
      ]}
    />
    <DatePicker datePickerType="single">
      <DatePickerInput
        labelText="Maintenance window"
        placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
      />
    </DatePicker>
    <TextInput
      size="sm"
      name="owner"
      labelText="Owner (small)"
      value="platform-team"
    />
    <Button type="submit">Deploy</Button>
  </Stack>
</Form>
```

### Form group

Use `FormGroup` to wrap related controls in a `fieldset`, with an optional `legend` rendered from `legendText`.

#### Disabled

Set `disabled` on FormGroup to disable every field inside it, with no `disabled` on the fields themselves. Each field, list boxes and sliders included, takes its disabled state and styles from the fieldset, and disabled controls are left out of the submission. A plain `<fieldset disabled>` works the same way.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Checkbox,
    Dropdown,
    Form,
    FormGroup,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form>
  <FormGroup legendText="Account details" disabled>
    <Stack gap={6}>
      <div>
        <Checkbox name="email" labelText="Email notifications" checked />
        <Checkbox name="sms" labelText="SMS notifications" />
      </div>
      <Select name="language" labelText="Preferred language">
        <SelectItem value="en" text="English" />
        <SelectItem value="es" text="Spanish" />
      </Select>
      <Dropdown
        name="team"
        labelText="Team"
        selectedId="design"
        items={[
          { id: "design", text: "Design" },
          { id: "engineering", text: "Engineering" },
        ]}
      />
    </Stack>
  </FormGroup>
</Form>
```

#### No margin

Set `noMargin` to `true` to remove the default bottom margin below a fieldset, useful when stacking form groups without extra spacing between them.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Checkbox, Form, FormGroup } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form>
  <FormGroup legendText="Default spacing">
    <Checkbox labelText="Show advanced settings" />
  </FormGroup>
  <FormGroup legendText="No margin" noMargin>
    <Checkbox labelText="Show advanced settings" />
  </FormGroup>
</Form>
```

#### Validation

Set `invalid` to `true` to mark the fieldset invalid via the `data-invalid` attribute. Set `message` to `true` with `messageText` to render a requirement below the fieldset's controls; when the group is invalid, the message shows as an error with a warning icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Checkbox, Form, FormGroup } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form>
  <FormGroup
    legendText="Contact preferences"
    invalid
    message
    messageText="Select at least one contact method"
  >
    <Checkbox name="contact" value="email" labelText="Email" />
    <Checkbox name="contact" value="sms" labelText="SMS" />
  </FormGroup>
</Form>
```

#### Helper text and messages

Place `FormHelperText` and `FormRequirement` directly in a `FormGroup` to describe the whole group. Their ids derive from the group's `id`, and the fieldset's `aria-describedby` lists them while they're mounted, so screen readers read them when focus enters the group. Render `FormRequirement` with `{#if}` while there is an error. Check a box to clear the error.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Checkbox,
    Form,
    FormGroup,
    FormHelperText,
    FormRequirement,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let email = false;
  let sms = false;

  $: empty = !email && !sms;
</script>

<Form>
  <FormGroup legendText="Contact preferences" invalid={empty}>
    <Checkbox
      name="contact"
      value="email"
      labelText="Email"
      bind:checked={email}
    />
    <Checkbox name="contact" value="sms" labelText="SMS" bind:checked={sms} />
    <FormHelperText>We only contact you about your account</FormHelperText>
    {#if empty}
      <FormRequirement>Select at least one contact method</FormRequirement>
    {/if}
  </FormGroup>
</Form>
```

### Custom controls

`FormLabel`, `FormHelperText`, and `FormRequirement` are the label, helper text, and invalid or warn message that fields like `TextInput` render. Use them to give a native or third-party control the same look.

#### Associate parts with a control

Wrap the parts in a `FormItem` and apply its `control` action to the control. The label's `for`, the control's `id`, and the ids its `aria-describedby` lists all derive from `controlId`, so no id is written by hand. Render a `FormRequirement` only while there is a message: while it's mounted, the control is described by it, and an invalid message sets `aria-invalid` and the `invalid` slot prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    FormHelperText,
    FormItem,
    FormLabel,
    FormRequirement,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let workEmail = "ada@example";

  $: workEmailError =
    workEmail && !/^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/.test(workEmail)
      ? "Enter an email address like name@example.com"
      : "";
  $: workEmailWarning = workEmail.endsWith("@gmail.com")
    ? "Use your work email if you have one"
    : "";
</script>

<FormItem controlId="custom-control-email" let:control let:invalid>
  <FormLabel>Work email</FormLabel>
  <input
    class="bx--text-input"
    type="email"
    data-invalid={invalid || undefined}
    bind:value={workEmail}
    use:control
  />
  <FormHelperText>We send the invite here</FormHelperText>
  {#if workEmailError}
    <FormRequirement>{workEmailError}</FormRequirement>
  {:else if workEmailWarning}
    <FormRequirement kind="warn">{workEmailWarning}</FormRequirement>
  {/if}
</FormItem>
```

#### Non-native controls

A `<label for>` only names native form elements. When the `control` action is applied to anything else, such as a `div` with `role="combobox"`, it also sets `aria-labelledby` to the `FormLabel`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    FormHelperText,
    FormItem,
    FormLabel,
    control,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FormItem let:control>
  <FormLabel>Assignee</FormLabel>
  <div
    role="combobox"
    tabindex="0"
    aria-expanded="false"
    aria-controls="assignee-menu"
    use:control
  >
    Choose a person
  </div>
  <FormHelperText>They are notified when assigned</FormHelperText>
</FormItem>
```

#### Component controls

An action can't be applied to a component. When the control is a component that forwards attributes to its focusable element, pass the slot props instead: `controlId`, `labelId`, `describedBy`, and `invalid`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    FormHelperText,
    FormItem,
    FormLabel,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import PersonPicker from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/PersonPicker.svelte";
  import controlId from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/controlId.svelte";
  import describedBy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/describedBy.svelte";
  import labelId from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/labelId.svelte";
</script>

<FormItem let:controlId let:labelId let:describedBy let:invalid>
  <FormLabel>Assignee</FormLabel>
  <PersonPicker
    id={controlId}
    aria-labelledby={labelId}
    aria-describedby={describedBy}
    aria-invalid={invalid || undefined}
  />
  <FormHelperText>They are notified when assigned</FormHelperText>
</FormItem>
```

#### Sizes and fluid forms

Inside a `Form` with `size`, the `size` slot prop holds that size, and inside a `FluidForm` the `fluid` slot prop is `true`. Use them to style the control like the fields around it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Form, FormItem, FormLabel, control } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form size="sm">
  <FormItem let:control let:size>
    <FormLabel>Work email</FormLabel>
    <input
      class="bx--text-input"
      class:bx--text-input--sm={size === "sm"}
      class:bx--text-input--xl={size === "xl"}
      use:control
    />
  </FormItem>
</Form>
```

#### Without FormItem

Each part also works on its own. Set `for` on the label and `id` on the helper text or message, then reference them from the control.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FormHelperText, FormLabel } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FormLabel for="nickname">Nickname</FormLabel>
<input
  id="nickname"
  class="bx--text-input"
  aria-describedby="nickname-helper"
/>
<FormHelperText id="nickname-helper">Shown on your profile</FormHelperText>
```

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Use `TextInput`, `Select`, and the other fields when they fit | They already pair their label, helper text, and messages with the control. |
| Render `FormRequirement` with `{#if}` instead of hiding it | Only a mounted message describes the control or marks it invalid. |
| Set the control's id through `controlId` on `FormItem` | The `control` action overwrites the control's `id` with `controlId`. |
| Also pass `id={controlId}` to the control when you server render | The `control` action runs only in the browser, so without it the label's `for` matches no id in the server HTML. |
| Style the control from the `invalid` and `warn` slot props | The parts only render text; the control's own invalid styles are up to you. |

### Submission

Handle form submission, including preventing the default browser behavior, reading what the form submits, and resetting it.

#### Prevent default behavior

Handle form submission by preventing the default browser behavior. Use `e.preventDefault()` to stop the native form submission and handle the event programmatically.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Checkbox, Form, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form
  on:submit={(e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    console.log("submit", e);
  }}
>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <Checkbox name="confirm" labelText="Send email confirmation" checked />
    <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
  </Stack>
</Form>
```

#### Submitted values

Every control that should reach the server needs a `name`. Submit this example to see the `FormData` entries the browser would send: a disabled field is left out, a read-only field is included, an unchecked checkbox is absent, and a multi-select sends one entry per selected item.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Checkbox,
    CodeSnippet,
    Dropdown,
    Form,
    FormGroup,
    MultiSelect,
    NumberInput,
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
    Toggle,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const teams = [
    { id: "design", text: "Design" },
    { id: "eng", text: "Engineering" },
    { id: "ops", text: "Operations" },
  ];

  /** @type {null | string} */
  let submitted = null;
</script>

<Stack gap={7}>
  <Form
    on:submit={(e) => {
      e.preventDefault();
      const form = /** @type {HTMLFormElement} */ (e.currentTarget);
      const entries = [...new FormData(form)];
      submitted = entries
        .map(([key, value]) => `${key} = ${JSON.stringify(value)}`)
        .join("\n");
    }}
  >
    <FormGroup legendText="Workspace">
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <TextInput name="workspace" labelText="Name" value="Acme" />
        <NumberInput name="seats" labelText="Seats" value={5} min={1} />
        <TextInput
          name="account"
          labelText="Account (read-only, submitted)"
          value="acct-042"
          readonly
        />
        <TextInput
          name="internal"
          labelText="Internal id (disabled, not submitted)"
          value="int-7"
          disabled
        />
      </Stack>
    </FormGroup>
    <FormGroup legendText="Plan">
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <RadioButtonGroup name="plan" selected="team">
          <RadioButton value="starter" labelText="Starter" />
          <RadioButton value="team" labelText="Team" />
        </RadioButtonGroup>
        <Select name="region" labelText="Region" selected="eu-de">
          <SelectItem value="us-east" text="US East" />
          <SelectItem value="eu-de" text="EU Germany" />
        </Select>
        <Dropdown
          name="channel"
          labelText="Alert channel"
          selectedId="email"
          items={[
            { id: "email", text: "Email" },
            { id: "slack", text: "Slack" },
          ]}
        />
        <MultiSelect
          name="teams"
          labelText="Teams"
          label="Select teams"
          selectedIds={["design", "eng"]}
          items={teams}
        />
      </Stack>
    </FormGroup>
    <FormGroup legendText="Consent">
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <div>
          <Checkbox name="terms" labelText="Accept the terms" checked />
          <Checkbox name="marketing" labelText="Send product updates" />
        </div>
        <Toggle
          name="digest"
          value="weekly"
          labelText="Weekly digest"
          toggled
        />
      </Stack>
    </FormGroup>
    <Button type="submit">Show submitted values</Button>
  </Form>

  {#if submitted}
    <CodeSnippet type="multi" code={submitted} />
  {/if}
</Stack>
```

What each control submits under its `name`:

| Component | Submitted value |
| --- | --- |
| `TextInput`, `PasswordInput`, `TextArea`, `Search` | The text, or `""` when empty. |
| `NumberInput` | The number as a string (`1234.5`), or `""` when empty, even when `locale` formats the display. |
| `Checkbox`, `Toggle` | `value` (`"on"` by default) while checked; nothing while unchecked. |
| `RadioButtonGroup`, `TileGroup` | The selected option's `value`; nothing when none is selected. |
| `SelectableTileGroup` | One entry per selected tile `value`; read them with `getAll`. |
| `Select` | The selected `SelectItem` value, as a string. |
| `Dropdown` | `selectedId`, as a string; `""` when nothing is selected. |
| `ComboBox` | The displayed text, not `selectedId`. |
| `MultiSelect` | One entry per selected item `id`; read them with `getAll`. |
| `DatePicker` | Each `DatePickerInput`'s text in `dateFormat`; a range picker's two inputs each take their own `name`. |
| `TimePicker`, `TimePickerSelect` | The time text and each select's value, under their own names. |
| `Slider` | The value as a string; `RangeSlider` uses `name` and `nameUpper`. |
| `PinCodeInput` | The assembled code. |
| `FileUploader` | `File` objects; the form needs `enctype="multipart/form-data"`. See [FileUploader](/components/FileUploader#form-submission). |

Disabled controls submit nothing, like native disabled inputs. Read-only controls still submit their value.

#### Tiles

Tile groups submit like the controls they wrap. A `TileGroup` is a radio group: set `name` on the group and the checked tile's `value` is sent under it. A `SelectableTileGroup` is a set of checkboxes that share the group's `name`, so each selected tile sends its own entry. Give every tile a `value` (a `SelectableTile` sends `"value"` when it has none).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    CodeSnippet,
    Form,
    RadioTile,
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
    Stack,
    TileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  /** @type {null | string} */
  let submitted = null;
</script>

<Stack gap={7}>
  <Form
    on:submit={(e) => {
      e.preventDefault();
      const form = /** @type {HTMLFormElement} */ (e.currentTarget);
      const data = new FormData(form);
      // One value per radio group, one entry per selected tile.
      submitted = JSON.stringify(
        { plan: data.get("plan"), addons: data.getAll("addons") },
        null,
        2,
      );
    }}
  >
    <Stack gap={6}>
      <TileGroup legendText="Plan" name="plan" selected="team" required>
        <RadioTile value="starter">
          Starter: 3 projects, community support
        </RadioTile>
        <RadioTile value="team">
          Team: unlimited projects, email support
        </RadioTile>
        <RadioTile value="enterprise">
          Enterprise: SSO, dedicated support
        </RadioTile>
      </TileGroup>
      <SelectableTileGroup
        legendText="Add-ons"
        name="addons"
        selected={["backups"]}
      >
        <SelectableTile value="backups">Daily backups</SelectableTile>
        <SelectableTile value="audit">Audit log</SelectableTile>
        <SelectableTile value="sandbox">Sandbox environment</SelectableTile>
      </SelectableTileGroup>
      <Button type="submit">Show submitted values</Button>
    </Stack>
  </Form>

  {#if submitted}
    <CodeSnippet type="multi" code={submitted} />
  {/if}
</Stack>
```

On the server, read the radio group with `get` and the selectable group with `getAll`:

```js
const data = await request.formData();
const plan = data.get("plan"); // "team"
const addons = data.getAll("addons"); // ["backups", "audit"]
```

#### Reset

A `<Button type="reset">`, `form.reset()`, or SvelteKit's `enhance` after a successful action resets the form. The browser restores each field to its markup default: empty or unchecked when the value was set on the client, and the server-rendered value when the page came from the server. Every component then updates its bound value to match what the field shows, without firing events, so `bind:value`, `bind:checked`, and `bind:selected` stay in step.

Controls that always hold a value keep it through a reset: `Select`, `Slider`, `RangeSlider`, `NumberInput` (unless `allowEmpty` is set), `Dropdown`, and `MultiSelect`. A read-only control keeps its value too.

In this example, the name clears, the region stays, and the checkbox unchecks.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    Checkbox,
    Form,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let name = "Acme";
  let notify = true;
  let region = "eu-de";
  let resets = 0;
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Form on:reset={() => (resets += 1)} on:submit={(e) => e.preventDefault()}>
    <Stack gap={5}>
      <TextInput bind:value={name} name="name" labelText="Workspace name" />
      <Select bind:selected={region} name="region" labelText="Region">
        <SelectItem value="us-east" text="US East" />
        <SelectItem value="eu-de" text="EU Germany" />
      </Select>
      <Checkbox bind:checked={notify} name="notify" labelText="Email me" />
      <ButtonSet>
        <Button kind="secondary" type="reset">Reset</Button>
        <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
      </ButtonSet>
    </Stack>
  </Form>

  <p>
    Bound values: {JSON.stringify({ name, region, notify })} · resets: {resets}
  </p>
</Stack>
```

#### Reset custom fields

Use the `formReset` action on a field you build yourself to run a callback after the form that owns it resets. A native reset restores field values without firing an `input` event, so state derived from the field goes stale unless the callback clears it.

The callback runs after the browser has restored the field values, so it reads the reset values. It does not run if a `reset` listener cancels the reset. Press the reset button to clear the preview along with the field.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Form, formReset } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let preview = "";
</script>

<Form>
  <label class="bx--label" for="project-slug">Project slug</label>
  <input
    id="project-slug"
    class="bx--text-input"
    placeholder="payments-api"
    on:input={(e) =>
      (preview = `https://acme-corp.com/${e.currentTarget.value}`)}
    use:formReset={() => (preview = "")}
  />
  <p>Preview: {preview || "Enter a slug"}</p>
  <Button type="reset" kind="secondary">Reset</Button>
</Form>
```

### SvelteKit

Forms work without JavaScript first: a `method="POST"` form posts its fields to a [form action](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/form-actions), and `enhance` then upgrades it to submit in place.

#### Form actions

Read the submission with `request.formData()`. Every value arrives as a string (or a `File`), so convert and validate on the server. Return `fail` with the submitted values and the errors so the page can show them.

```js
// src/routes/invite/+page.server.js
import { fail } from "@sveltejs/kit";

export const actions = {
  default: async ({ request }) => {
    const data = await request.formData();
    const email = String(data.get("email") ?? "").trim();
    const seats = Number(data.get("seats"));
    const teams = data.getAll("teams").map(String);
    const notify = data.has("notify");

    const errors = {};
    if (!email.includes("@")) errors.email = "Enter a valid email address.";
    if (!Number.isInteger(seats) || seats < 1)
      errors.seats = "Enter at least 1 seat.";

    if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) {
      return fail(400, { values: { email, seats: data.get("seats") }, errors });
    }

    // Save the invite here.
    return { invited: email };
  },
};
```

In the page, feed the returned values back into the fields and map each error to `invalid` and `invalidText`:

```svelte
<!-- src/routes/invite/+page.svelte -->
<script>
  import { enhance } from "$app/forms";
  import {
    Button,
    Checkbox,
    Form,
    MultiSelect,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  export let form;

  $: values = form?.values ?? {};
  $: errors = form?.errors ?? {};
</script>

<Form method="POST" actions={[enhance]}>
  <TextInput
    name="email"
    type="email"
    labelText="Email"
    value={values.email ?? ""}
    invalid={!!errors.email}
    invalidText={errors.email}
  />
  <TextInput
    name="seats"
    type="number"
    labelText="Seats"
    value={values.seats ?? "1"}
    invalid={!!errors.seats}
    invalidText={errors.seats}
  />
  <MultiSelect
    name="teams"
    labelText="Teams"
    items={[
      { id: "design", text: "Design" },
      { id: "eng", text: "Engineering" },
    ]}
  />
  <Checkbox name="notify" labelText="Email me a copy" />
  <Button type="submit">Send invite</Button>
</Form>

{#if form?.invited}
  <p>Invited {form.invited}.</p>
{/if}
```

#### SvelteKit enhance

Svelte's `use:` directive cannot target components. Set `actions` to apply SvelteKit's `enhance` (or any other action) to the underlying form element.

```svelte
<script>
  import { enhance } from "$app/forms";
  import { Form, TextInput, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form method="POST" action="?/save" actions={[enhance]}>
  <TextInput name="name" labelText="Name" />
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>
```

After a successful action, `enhance` resets the form (see [Reset](#reset)). A failed action leaves the fields as submitted.

Pass a submit callback as a `[action, parameter]` tuple. The submit callback returns the function that runs after the response; call `update` in it to keep the default handling, here without resetting the form:

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Form, TextInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form
  method="POST"
  action="?/save"
  actions={[
    [
      enhance,
      () =>
        async ({ update }) =>
          update({ reset: false }),
    ],
  ]}
>
  <TextInput name="name" labelText="Name" />
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>
```

#### Pending state

Use the submit callback to track the request and set `loading` on the submit button while it runs. A loading button can't be activated, so a second submit cannot send a duplicate request, and unlike a disabled button it keeps focus. Leave the fields enabled: a disabled field is left out of the submission.

```svelte
<script>
  import { enhance } from "$app/forms";
  import { Button, Form, TextInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let submitting = false;

  const trackSubmit = () => {
    submitting = true;
    return async ({ update }) => {
      await update();
      submitting = false;
    };
  };
</script>

<Form method="POST" actions={[[enhance, trackSubmit]]}>
  <TextInput name="email" labelText="Email" />
  <Button type="submit" loading={submitting} loadingDescription="Saving">
    Save
  </Button>
</Form>
```

#### Server-side validation

This example stands in for a form action in the browser. It validates on submit, shows the errors on the fields while keeping what was typed, and resets the form after a successful submission, the way `enhance` does. Set `novalidate` when the server owns validation, so the browser's own bubbles do not compete with `invalidText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Form,
    InlineNotification,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  /**
   * Stand-in for a SvelteKit form action: reads FormData, validates on the
   * "server", and returns either the errors with the submitted values or a
   * success result.
   * @param {FormData} data
   */
  async function inviteAction(data) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 600));
    const email = String(data.get("email") ?? "").trim();
    const seatsRaw = String(data.get("seats") ?? "");
    const seats = seatsRaw === "" ? Number.NaN : Number(seatsRaw);

    /** @type {Record<string, string>} */
    const errors = {};
    if (!/^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/.test(email)) {
      errors.email = "Enter an email address like name@example.com.";
    }
    if (!Number.isInteger(seats) || seats < 1 || seats > 50) {
      errors.seats = "Choose between 1 and 50 seats.";
    }

    if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) {
      return {
        type: "failure",
        data: { values: { email, seats: seatsRaw }, errors },
      };
    }
    return { type: "success", data: { invited: email } };
  }

  /** The action result, like SvelteKit's `form` prop. */
  let form = null;
  let submitting = false;

  $: values = form?.type === "failure" ? form.data.values : {};
  $: errors = form?.type === "failure" ? form.data.errors : {};
</script>

<Form
  novalidate
  on:submit={async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const formElement = /** @type {HTMLFormElement} */ (e.currentTarget);
    submitting = true;
    form = await inviteAction(new FormData(formElement));
    submitting = false;
    // Like `use:enhance`, reset only after a successful submission.
    if (form.type === "success") formElement.reset();
  }}
>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <TextInput
      name="email"
      type="email"
      labelText="Email"
      value={values.email ?? ""}
      invalid={!!errors.email}
      invalidText={errors.email}
    />
    <TextInput
      name="seats"
      type="number"
      labelText="Seats"
      placeholder="1-50"
      value={values.seats ?? ""}
      invalid={!!errors.seats}
      invalidText={errors.seats}
    />
    {#if form?.type === "success"}
      <InlineNotification
        kind="success"
        title="Invitation sent"
        subtitle={`We emailed ${form.data.invited}.`}
        hideCloseButton
      />
    {/if}
    <Button type="submit" loading={submitting} loadingDescription="Sending">
      Send invite
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</Form>
```

#### Multiple actions

One form can post to different named actions. Set `formaction` on each submit button; `Button` passes it to the native `<button>`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Form, TextInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form method="POST" actions={[enhance]}>
  <TextInput name="title" labelText="Title" />
  <Button type="submit" formaction="?/save">Save</Button>
  <Button kind="danger" type="submit" formaction="?/delete">Delete</Button>
</Form>
```

### Best practices

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Give every field a `name` | Only named, enabled controls are submitted. Keep ids for labels and tests. |
| Validate on the server | `required`, `type`, `min`, and `max` improve the form in the browser, but they are not a guarantee. |
| Treat every value as a string | Convert numbers with `Number()` and check for `NaN`. Read checkboxes and toggles with `data.has(name)`. |
| Read multi-value fields with `data.getAll(name)` | `MultiSelect` and checkboxes that share a `name` submit one entry per value. |
| Use `readonly`, not `disabled`, for values the server needs | Disabled fields are left out of the submission; read-only fields are included. |
| Return the submitted values with the errors | The user does not retype them, and `invalid` and `invalidText` can mark the field each error belongs to. |
| Set `enctype="multipart/form-data"` with a `FileUploader` | Without it, the browser sends only the file names. |
| Call `event.preventDefault()` in `on:reset` to reset to specific values | A reset restores the markup defaults; prevent it and set the bound values yourself instead. |
| Prefer `method="POST"` plus `enhance` over custom `fetch` code | The form keeps working before JavaScript loads. |

---

### Component API

#### `Form` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLFormElement` | Obtain a reference to the form element. | `null` |
| `actions` | `ReadonlyArray<FormActionEntry>` | Apply Svelte actions to the underlying form element.<br />Each entry is an action or a `[action, parameter]` tuple.<br />Use this for SvelteKit's `enhance` and other form actions that<br />cannot target components with `use:`. | `[]` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Set the size of every field in the form.<br />A field's own `size` takes precedence.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (the 40px default) and `"lg"` (`"xl"`). | _undefined_ |

#### `Form` typedefs

```ts
type FormAction = import("svelte/action").Action<HTMLFormElement, any>;

type FormActionEntry = FormAction | readonly [FormAction, any];
```

#### `Form` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Form` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:keydown`    |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |
| `on:reset`      |
| `on:submit`     |

#### `Form` $$restProps

`Form` spreads `$$restProps` to the `form` element.

#### `FormGroup` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `noMargin` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for to remove the bottom margin | `false` |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state.<br />With `message`, shows the message as an error with a warning icon. | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the fieldset and every field inside it,<br />including their labels, helper text and disabled styles. | `false` |
| `message` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render a form requirement | `false` |
| `messageText` | `string` | Specify the message text | `""` |
| `legendText` | `string` | Specify the legend text | `""` |
| `legendId` | `string` | Specify an id for the legend element | `""` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the fieldset element.<br />The message id derives from it as `{id}-message`. `FormHelperText`<br />and `FormRequirement` placed directly in the group derive theirs as<br />`helper-{id}`, `error-{id}`, and `warn-{id}`. | `uniqueId()` |

| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `FormGroup` $$restProps

`FormGroup` spreads `$$restProps` to the `fieldset` element.

#### `FormItem` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `controlId` | `string` | Set the id of the control in this form item.<br />Child `FormLabel`, `FormHelperText`, and `FormRequirement`<br />components derive their `for` and `id` attributes from it.<br />Apply it to the control with the `control` slot prop action. | `uniqueId()` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to style child labels and helper text as disabled | `false` |

#### `FormLabel` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |

| `id` | `string \| undefined` | Set the id of the control this label is for. | _undefined_ |
| `disabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to use disabled styles.<br />Inside a `FormItem`, defaults to the item's `disabled`. A disabled<br />fieldset around it applies either way. | _undefined_ |

| Event           |

#### `FormLabel` $$restProps

`FormLabel` spreads `$$restProps` to the `label` element.

#### `FormHelperText` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string \| undefined` | Set an id for the helper text element.<br />Inside a `FormItem`, defaults to `helper-{controlId}` (`-1`, `-2`,<br />and so on for later helper texts), and the item's control lists it<br />in `aria-describedby`. | _undefined_ |
| `disabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to use disabled styles.<br />Inside a `FormItem`, defaults to the item's `disabled`. A disabled<br />fieldset around it applies either way. | _undefined_ |

#### `FormHelperText` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `FormHelperText` $$restProps

`FormHelperText` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.

#### `FormRequirement` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"invalid" \| "warn"` | Specify the kind of message.<br />An `"invalid"` message is announced with `role="alert"`. | `"invalid"` |
| `id` | `string \| undefined` | Set an id for the message element.<br />Inside a `FormItem`, defaults to `error-{controlId}` or<br />`warn-{controlId}` (`-1`, `-2`, and so on for later messages of the<br />same kind), and the item's control lists it in `aria-describedby`.<br />An invalid message also sets the control's `aria-invalid` while it's<br />mounted. | _undefined_ |

#### `FormRequirement` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `FormRequirement` $$restProps

`FormRequirement` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## FullPageError

### Basic

Create a full-page error with `labelText`, `title`, and `description`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FullPageError } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FullPageError
  labelText="Error"
  title="Unable to load this workspace"
  description="We couldn't load this workspace right now. Try again in a few minutes, or contact your administrator if the problem persists."
/>
```

### 403

Set `kind` to `"403"` to display the forbidden access illustration.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FullPageError } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FullPageError
  kind="403"
  labelText="Error 403"
  title="Access denied"
  description="You don't have permission to view this workspace. Contact your workspace administrator to request access."
/>
```

### 404

Set `kind` to `"404"` to display the not found illustration.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FullPageError } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FullPageError
  kind="404"
  labelText="Error 404"
  title="Page not found"
  description="The dashboard you're looking for doesn't exist or has been moved."
/>
```

### With action

Use the default slot to add extra body content below the description, such as a button to navigate back home.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, FullPageError } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FullPageError
  labelText="Error"
  title="This service is temporarily unavailable"
  description="We're experiencing an unplanned outage. Our engineering team is investigating and will restore access as soon as possible."
>
  <Button>Go home</Button>
</FullPageError>
```

### Slottable label, title, and description

Use the `labelChildren`, `titleChildren`, and `descriptionChildren` slots to render custom markup instead of plain text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FullPageError, Link } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FullPageError>
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Error <code>500</code>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="titleChildren">Internal server error</svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="descriptionChildren">
    Try again, or <Link size="lg" href="#">contact support</Link> if the problem persists.
  </svelte:fragment>
</FullPageError>
```

### Custom illustration

Use the `illustration` slot to replace the default kind-based SVG. Pictograms from [carbon-pictograms-svelte](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-pictograms-svelte) work well here.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FullPageError } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Robot from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Robot.svelte";
</script>

<FullPageError labelText="Error" title="This automation is currently offline">
  <Robot slot="illustration" />
</FullPageError>
```

---

### Component API

#### `FullPageError` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"custom" \| "403" \| "404"` | Specify the kind of error page to be displayed. | `"custom"` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label describing the error that occurred. | `""` |
| `title` | `string` | Specify the main title of the error page. | `""` |
| `description` | `string` | Specify the description for the error. | `""` |

#### `FullPageError` slots

| Slot                  | Detail                  |
| --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`             | `Record<string, never>` |
| `descriptionChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `illustration`        | `Record<string, never>` |
| `labelChildren`       | `Record<string, never>` |
| `titleChildren`       | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `FullPageError` $$restProps

`FullPageError` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## Grid

### Basic

The [Carbon grid system](https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/2x-grid/overview/) uses a responsive column structure where the total number of columns changes based on screen size. Column spans are relative to the total columns at each breakpoint -- to create a full-width column, use `sm={4} md={8} lg={16}` instead of the same value across all breakpoints.

Create a basic grid layout with equal-width columns.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

| Breakpoint          | Viewport width   | Columns |
| ------------------- | ---------------- | ------- |
| **Small (`sm`)**    | 0-671px          | 4       |
| **Medium (`md`)**   | 672-1055px       | 8       |
| **Large (`lg`)**    | 1056-1311px      | 16      |
| **X-Large (`xlg`)** | 1312-1583px      | 16      |
| **Max (`max`)**     | 1584px and above | 16      |

### Variants

Adjust grid width and column spacing.

#### Full width

Use the full-width grid variant for layouts that span the entire viewport width. This removes the default max-width constraint.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid fullWidth>
  <Row>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Narrow

Create a more compact grid layout using the narrow variant. This reduces the spacing between columns.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid narrow>
  <Row>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Condensed

Use the condensed variant for even tighter spacing between columns. This is ideal for dense data displays.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid condensed>
  <Row>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
    <Column>Column</Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Per-row

`condensed`, `narrow`, `noGutter`, and `padding` are also available directly on `Row`, so you can mix densities within a single grid instead of applying a variant to every row.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row condensed>
    <Column>Condensed row</Column>
    <Column>Condensed row</Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column>Default row</Column>
    <Column>Default row</Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

### Columns

Build responsive layouts by setting a different column width per breakpoint. Each breakpoint has a different total column count, so scale spans proportionally.

#### Full width column

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Column sm={4} md={8} lg={16} />
```

#### Half width (50/50 split)

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8} />
<Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8} />
```

#### Two-thirds / one-third split

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Column sm={4} md={6} lg={11} />
<Column sm={4} md={2} lg={5} />
```

#### Extra-large and max breakpoints

`lg`, `xlg`, and `max` all share the same 16-column grid, but the viewport keeps growing past `lg`. Set `xlg` and `max` independently when a layout needs a different span on very wide screens instead of stretching the `lg` value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Column sm={4} md={8} lg={8} xlg={6} max={4} />
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={1} md={4} lg={8}>sm: 1, md: 4, lg: 8</Column>
    <Column sm={1} md={2} lg={2}>sm: 1, md: 2, lg: 2</Column>
    <Column sm={1} md={1} lg={1}>sm: 1, md: 1, lg: 1</Column>
    <Column sm={1} md={1} lg={1}>sm: 1, md: 1, lg: 1</Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Offset

Create space between columns using the offset feature for more flexible layouts without empty columns.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={{ span: 1, offset: 3 }}>Offset 3</Column>
    <Column sm={{ span: 2, offset: 2 }}>Offset 2</Column>
    <Column sm={{ span: 3, offset: 1 }}>Offset 1</Column>
    <Column sm={{ span: 4, offset: 0 }}>Offset 0</Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Aspect ratio

Maintain consistent column heights using aspect ratio columns. This ensures content alignment across different column widths.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column aspectRatio="2x1">2x1</Column>
    <Column aspectRatio="2x1">2x1</Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

### Alignment

`Row` stretches its columns to an equal height by default. Set `align` on `Row` to change how columns align along the cross axis (`start`, `center`, `end`, or `stretch`), or set `align` on an individual `Column` to override the row's alignment for that column alone.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row align="center" style="height: 8rem;" data-outline>
    <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>Centered</Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={4} align="end">Self-aligned end</Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Equal height columns

A stretched `Column` does not stretch the content inside it. Set `fullHeight` on `Tile` so a tile fills its column instead of sizing to its own content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={4} lg={8}>
      <Tile fullHeight>Requests per minute: 4,201</Tile>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={4} lg={8}>
      <Tile fullHeight
        >Error rate: 0.3% over the last hour, down from 0.8% yesterday</Tile
      >
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

### Spacing

Control vertical rhythm and horizontal gutters at the grid, row, or column level.

#### Padding

Add vertical padding (top/bottom) with `padding`. Apply it at the grid, row, or column level to control spacing between rows of content. This is useful for creating vertical rhythm without manually adding margins.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Column, Grid, Row, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Box padding={5}>
    Adding padding to Grid applies it to columns in all rows:
  </Box>

  <Grid padding>
    <Row>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
    </Row>
  </Grid>

  <Box padding={5}>Adding padding to a Row only applies to its columns:</Box>

  <Grid>
    <Row padding>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
    </Row>
    <Row>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
    </Row>
  </Grid>

  <Box padding={5}>
    Adding padding to a specific column only applies it to the column:
  </Box>

  <Grid>
    <Row>
      <Column padding>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
    </Row>
  </Grid>
</Stack>
```

#### Gutter

Remove the horizontal gutter with `noGutter`, or remove just one side with `noGutterLeft` / `noGutterRight`. These props are available on `Grid`, `Row`, and `Column`, so you can drop the gutter globally or flush a single column against an edge or divider.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Column, Grid, Row, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Box padding={5}>
    Adding noGutter to Grid removes the gutter from every column:
  </Box>

  <Grid noGutter>
    <Row>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
    </Row>
  </Grid>

  <Box padding={5}>
    Adding noGutterLeft or noGutterRight to individual columns removes only that
    side's gutter--useful for flushing a column against a page edge or divider:
  </Box>

  <Grid>
    <Row>
      <Column noGutterLeft>No left gutter</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column>Column</Column>
      <Column noGutterRight>No right gutter</Column>
    </Row>
  </Grid>
</Stack>
```

### Custom element

Set `as` to `true` on `Grid`, `Row`, or `Column` to render a semantic element instead of the default `<div>`. Props are destructured as `props` in the default slot and must be spread onto the custom element to keep the Carbon grid classes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid as let:props>
  <main {...props}>
    <Row as let:props>
      <section {...props}>
        <Column as let:props>
          <article {...props}>Content</article>
        </Column>
      </section>
    </Row>
  </main>
</Grid>
```

### GridOverlay

Draw the real breakpoint grid over the page to check content against the actual columns instead of eyeballing it. `GridOverlay` renders a fixed, `pointer-events: none` layer of 16 columns -- hidden or shown per breakpoint the same way a regular `Column`'s numeric span does -- so it lines up with `sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xlg`/`max` exactly.

`GridOverlay` never toggles its own visibility; the caller owns `open`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Column,
    Grid,
    GridOverlay,
    Row,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Grid padding>
  <Row>
    <Column>
      <Button on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
        {open ? "Hide" : "Show"}
        grid overlay
      </Button>
    </Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={8} lg={16}><Tile>Header</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={11}><Tile>Content</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={5}><Tile>Sidebar</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>

<GridOverlay {open} />
```

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Gate `open` behind a dev-only control, then remove it before shipping | The overlay has no built-in toggle or guard, so anything left wired to `open` renders in production |
| Match `condensed` / `narrow` / `fullWidth` to the `Grid` underneath | The overlay's columns only line up with a mismatched `Grid`'s columns by coincidence |

#### Gutters

Set `gutters` to shade each column's padding a step darker than its content area, so you can check that content sits inside the columns rather than in the gutters.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Column,
    Grid,
    GridOverlay,
    Row,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Grid padding>
  <Row>
    <Column>
      <Button on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
        {open ? "Hide" : "Show"}
        grid overlay with gutters
      </Button>
    </Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={8} lg={16}><Tile>Header</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={11}><Tile>Content</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={5}><Tile>Sidebar</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>

<GridOverlay {open} gutters />
```

#### Condensed

Set `condensed` to match a condensed `Grid`. The columns sit in the same place, but the gutters shrink to 1px (0.5px of padding on each side). This example also sets `gutters`: compared with the Gutters example, the 32px bands all but disappear.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Column,
    Grid,
    GridOverlay,
    Row,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Grid condensed>
  <Row>
    <Column>
      <Button on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
        {open ? "Hide" : "Show"}
        condensed grid overlay
      </Button>
    </Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={8} lg={16}><Tile>Header</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={11}><Tile>Content</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={5}><Tile>Sidebar</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>

<GridOverlay {open} condensed gutters />
```

#### Narrow

Set `narrow` to match a narrow `Grid`, where each column drops its 16px left padding so its content hangs into the gutter. This example also sets `gutters`, so only the right-hand 16px of each gutter is shaded.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Column,
    Grid,
    GridOverlay,
    Row,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

</script>

<Grid narrow padding>
  <Row>
    <Column>

        {open ? "Hide" : "Show"}
        narrow grid overlay
      </Button>
    </Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={8} lg={16}><Tile>Header</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={11}><Tile>Content</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={5}><Tile>Sidebar</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>

<GridOverlay {open} narrow gutters />
```

#### Full width

Set `fullWidth` to match a full-width `Grid`. It only differs from the default at the `max` breakpoint (1584px and above), where the default grid stops growing and the full-width grid keeps spanning the viewport.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Column,
    Grid,
    GridOverlay,
    Row,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

</script>

<Grid fullWidth padding>
  <Row>
    <Column>
      <Button on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
        {open ? "Hide" : "Show"}
        full-width grid overlay
      </Button>
    </Column>
  </Row>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={8} lg={16}><Tile>Header</Tile></Column>

    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
    <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><Tile>Card</Tile></Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>

<GridOverlay {open} fullWidth />
```

### Breakpoints reference

Understanding [breakpoints](/components/Breakpoint) is critical for creating responsive layouts. Each breakpoint has specific pixel ranges and column counts:

| Breakpoint          | Viewport width   | Columns | Typical use               |
| ------------------- | ---------------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| **Small (`sm`)**    | 0-671px          | 4       | Mobile phones             |
| **Medium (`md`)**   | 672-1055px       | 8       | Tablets, small laptops    |
| **Large (`lg`)**    | 1056-1311px      | 16      | Desktop monitors, laptops |
| **X-Large (`xlg`)** | 1312-1583px      | 16      | Large desktop monitors    |
| **Max (`max`)**     | 1584px and above | 16      | Extra-large displays      |

When designing responsive layouts, start with mobile (sm) and work your way up to ensure your content works well at all sizes.

---

### Component API

#### `Grid` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render a custom HTML element.<br />Props are destructured as `props` in the default slot. | `false` |
| `condensed` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the condensed variant | `false` |
| `narrow` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the narrow variant | `false` |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fullWidth variant | `false` |
| `noGutter` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the gutter | `false` |
| `noGutterLeft` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the left gutter | `false` |
| `noGutterRight` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the right gutter | `false` |
| `padding` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to add top and bottom padding to all columns | `false` |

#### `Grid` slots

| Slot | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | `{<br />  props: {<br />    class: string;<br />    [key: string]: any;<br />  };<br />}` |

#### `Grid` $$restProps

`Grid` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.

#### `Row` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render a custom HTML element.<br />Props are destructured as `props` in the default slot. | `false` |
| `condensed` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the condensed variant | `false` |
| `narrow` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the narrow variant | `false` |
| `noGutter` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the gutter | `false` |
| `noGutterLeft` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the left gutter | `false` |
| `noGutterRight` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the right gutter | `false` |
| `padding` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to add top and bottom padding to all columns | `false` |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" \| undefined` | Set the cross-axis alignment of the columns in the row. | _undefined_ |

#### `Row` slots

| Slot | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | `{<br />  props: {<br />    class: string;<br />    [key: string]: any;<br />  };<br />}` |

#### `Row` $$restProps

`Row` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.

#### `Column` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render a custom HTML element.<br />Props are destructured as `props` in the default slot. | `false` |
| `noGutter` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the gutter | `false` |
| `noGutterLeft` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the left gutter | `false` |
| `noGutterRight` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the right gutter | `false` |
| `padding` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to add top and bottom padding to the column | `false` |
| `aspectRatio` | `"2x1" \| "2x3" \| "16x9" \| "9x16" \| "1x2" \| "4x3" \| "3x4" \| "3x2" \| "1x1" \| undefined` | Specify the aspect ratio of the column. | _undefined_ |
| `sm` | `ColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the small breakpoint. | _undefined_ |
| `md` | `ColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the medium breakpoint. | _undefined_ |
| `lg` | `ColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the large breakpoint. | _undefined_ |
| `xlg` | `ColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the extra large breakpoint. | _undefined_ |
| `max` | `ColumnBreakpoint \| undefined` | Set the maximum breakpoint. | _undefined_ |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" \| undefined` | Set the cross-axis self-alignment of the column within its row. | _undefined_ |

#### `Column` typedefs

```ts
type ColumnSize = boolean | number;

type ColumnSizeDescriptor = {
  span?: ColumnSize;
  offset?: number;
};

type ColumnBreakpoint = ColumnSize | ColumnSizeDescriptor;
```

#### `Column` slots

| Slot | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | `{<br />  props: {<br />    class: string;<br />    [key: string]: any;<br />  };<br />}` |

#### `Column` $$restProps

`Column` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.

#### `GridOverlay` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to show the overlay. The caller controls this; GridOverlay never toggles its own visibility (no keyboard shortcut, no internal state). | `false` |
| `condensed` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to match a condensed Grid. | `false` |
| `narrow` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to match a narrow Grid. | `false` |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to match a fullWidth Grid. | `false` |
