## Kbd

### Basic

Set `shortcut` to the keys joined by `+`. `mod` is Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere, so one shortcut reads right on both. Here, `"mod+k"` shows <DocKbd shortcut="mod+k" />. Modifiers show in the platform's order, and screen readers hear the key names ("Command K"), not the symbols.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Kbd, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5} align="center">
  <Kbd shortcut="mod+k" />
  <Kbd shortcut="mod+shift+p" />
  <Kbd shortcut="alt+arrowleft" />
  <Kbd shortcut="escape" />
</Stack>
```

### Platform

The server can't tell the platform, so a `Kbd` renders both sets of keys in one place, as wide as the wider set, and shows the Windows and Linux keys until it mounts; on a Mac, every `Kbd` then switches to Apple's symbols together, without moving the layout. To show the right keys from the first paint, at their own width, inline `platformScript` as a script in `<head>`: it marks `<html>` with the platform before the page renders.

```js
import { platformScript } from "carbon-components-svelte";

const script = `<script>${platformScript()}</script>`;
```

A Content Security Policy that blocks inline scripts also blocks this one. Add a nonce to the tag and the policy, or allow the script's hash in `script-src`.

Set `apple` to choose the platform yourself, such as from the request's user agent on the server.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Kbd, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5} align="center">
  <Kbd shortcut="mod+shift+s" apple />
  <Kbd shortcut="mod+shift+s" apple={false} />
</Stack>
```

### One key

Without a `shortcut`, the default slot is shown as one key, for a key the shortcut syntax doesn't name.

<Kbd>Fn</Kbd>

### Sizes

Set `size` to control key height. The default is `"default"`, 24px tall. Use `"sm"`, 20px, for keys in a 32px or 40px control.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Kbd, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5} align="center">
  <Kbd shortcut="mod+k" size="sm" />
  <Kbd shortcut="mod+k" />
</Stack>
```

### Muted

Set `variant` to `"muted"` to run the keys together as secondary text, as a menu shows shortcuts. Here, `"mod+shift+s"` shows <DocKbd shortcut="mod+shift+s" variant="muted" />. Buttons show their `shortcut` this way.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Kbd, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5} align="center">
  <Kbd shortcut="mod+shift+s" variant="muted" apple />
  <Kbd shortcut="mod+shift+s" variant="muted" apple={false} />
</Stack>
```

### Translations

Override `translateWithId` to translate the words on the keys and the names screen readers hear for Apple's symbols, such as "Strg" for Ctrl on a German keyboard. A key it returns `undefined` for keeps its English name.

<Kbd shortcut="mod+shift+s" apple={false} translateWithId={(id) => ({ ctrl: "Strg", shift: "Umschalt" })[id]} />

To translate every key on the page, including the keys a Button, Search or menu item shows for its `shortcut`, call `setKbdTranslations` once near the root of the app with the names to replace. A key left out keeps its English name. A `Kbd`'s own `translateWithId` still wins, and a key it returns `undefined` for uses these names. It also takes a function of the id.

```svelte
<script>
  import { setKbdTranslations } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  setKbdTranslations({ ctrl: "Strg", shift: "Umschalt" });
</script>
```

### In a button

To show a shortcut in a button, set the button's own `shortcut`: it shows the keys, announces them with `aria-keyshortcuts`, and clicks the button when they're pressed. See [Button](/components/Button#keyboard-shortcut).

| Do | Why |
| :-- | :-- |
| Use `Kbd` for keys in UI chrome: a hint, a legend, a menu | It sizes to controls and reads the platform |
| Write keys in copy as `kbd` in `Prose` | Prose keeps them inline with the text's size and line height |
| Set `shortcut` on a Button rather than placing a `Kbd` in it | The button also announces and binds the keys |
| Draw keys with `Kbd`, and keep `formatShortcut` for plain strings such as a `title` | IBM Plex has no Apple modifier glyphs, so text on the page makes the browser download a 63 KB fallback font |

---

### Component API

#### `Kbd` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLElement` | Obtain a reference to the outer `kbd` element. | `null` |
| `shortcut` | `string` | Specify the shortcut to show, such as `"mod+k"` or `"shift+?"`. `mod`<br />shows Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. Leave it empty<br />to show the default slot as one key. | `""` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "default"` | Specify the size of the keys. | `"default"` |
| `variant` | `"keycap" \| "muted"` | Specify how the keys look: `"keycap"` boxes each key; `"muted"` runs<br />them together as secondary text, as menus show shortcuts: icons run<br />together on Apple platforms, Ctrl+Shift+P elsewhere. | `"keycap"` |
| `apple` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to show the keys as on an Apple platform, or `false` as<br />elsewhere. Unset, it follows the browser once mounted; the server renders<br />the keys for other platforms. | _undefined_ |
| `translationIds` | `{ ctrl: "ctrl"; control: "control"; alt: "alt"; option: "option"; shift: "shift"; meta: "meta"; command: "command"; enter: "enter"; return: "return"; escape: "escape"; escapeName: "escapeName"; tab: "tab"; backspace: "backspace"; delete: "delete"; forwardDelete: "forwardDelete"; del: "del"; forwardDel: "forwardDel"; space: "space"; arrowUp: "arrowUp"; arrowDown: "arrowDown"; arrowLeft: "arrowLeft"; arrowRight: "arrowRight"; pageUp: "pageUp"; pageDown: "pageDown"; home: "home"; end: "end" }` | Default translation ids | `{<br />  ctrl: "ctrl",<br />  control: "control",<br />  alt: "alt",<br />  option: "option",<br />  shift: "shift",<br />  meta: "meta",<br />  command: "command",<br />  enter: "enter",<br />  return: "return",<br />  escape: "escape",<br />  escapeName: "escapeName",<br />  tab: "tab",<br />  backspace: "backspace",<br />  delete: "delete",<br />  forwardDelete: "forwardDelete",<br />  del: "del",<br />  forwardDel: "forwardDel",<br />  space: "space",<br />  arrowUp: "arrowUp",<br />  arrowDown: "arrowDown",<br />  arrowLeft: "arrowLeft",<br />  arrowRight: "arrowRight",<br />  pageUp: "pageUp",<br />  pageDown: "pageDown",<br />  home: "home",<br />  end: "end",<br />}` |
| `translateWithId` | `(id: KbdTranslationId) => string \| undefined` | Override the default translations of the key names. Words such as<br />"Ctrl" are shown on the keys; names such as "Command" are read by<br />screen readers for the icons shown on Apple platforms. A key it<br />returns `undefined` for uses the nearest `setKbdTranslations`, then<br />English. | `(id) => shared?.(id) ?? KBD_TRANSLATIONS[id]` |

#### `Kbd` typedefs

```ts
type KbdTranslationId =
  | "ctrl"
  | "control"
  | "alt"
  | "option"
  | "shift"
  | "meta"
  | "command"
  | "enter"
  | "return"
  | "escape"
  | "escapeName"
  | "tab"
  | "backspace"
  | "delete"
  | "forwardDelete"
  | "del"
  | "forwardDel"
  | "space"
  | "arrowUp"
  | "arrowDown"
  | "arrowLeft"
  | "arrowRight"
  | "pageUp"
  | "pageDown"
  | "home"
  | "end";
```

#### `Kbd` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Kbd` $$restProps

`Kbd` spreads `$$restProps` to the `kbd` element.


## Layer

### Basic

Carbon stacks surfaces in up to three layers. Components read contextual tokens (`layer`, `field`, `border-subtle`, ...) instead of a fixed layer, and `Layer` re-points those tokens to the next level for everything inside it. Levels count from 0, the page surface. Level 0 uses the `-01` tokens, so a field inside a level 1 `Layer` takes `field-02` and still stands out.

`Layer` works with `all.css` and with the single-theme stylesheets.

Each nested `Layer` steps up one level. Set `withBackground` to paint the layer's surface.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, Stack, TextInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <TextInput labelText="Page (level 0)" placeholder="field-01" />
  <Layer withBackground>
    <Box padding={5}>
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <TextInput labelText="Level 1" placeholder="field-02" />
        <Layer withBackground>
          <Box padding={5}>
            <TextInput labelText="Level 2" placeholder="field-03" />
          </Box>
        </Layer>
      </Stack>
    </Box>
  </Layer>
</Stack>
```

### Tiles

A `Tile` paints the `layer` token, so a tile inside a `Layer` takes the next surface.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Layer, Stack, Text, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tile>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <Text>Tile at level 0</Text>
    <Layer>
      <Tile>
        <Stack gap={5}>
          <Text>Tile at level 1</Text>
          <Layer>
            <Tile>
              <Text>Tile at level 2</Text>
            </Tile>
          </Layer>
        </Stack>
      </Tile>
    </Layer>
  </Stack>
</Tile>
```

### Level

Set `level` to pick a level instead of counting from the parent: `0` is the page surface, `2` the highest. Nested layers continue from it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer level={2} withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <Search placeholder="Search at level 2" />
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Modals

[Modal](/components/Modal) and [ComposedModal](/components/ComposedModal) start their own layer at level `0`, wherever they render. The modal body sits on level `1`, so fields in it take `field-02`, and a `Layer` inside the body sits on level `2`.

### Slot props

The default slot receives the layer's `level`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, Text } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground let:level>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <Text>This layer is level {level}.</Text>
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Layer` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `LayerLevel \| undefined` | Set the layer level: `0` is the page surface, `2` the highest. By<br />default a layer sits one level above its parent `Layer`, so a<br />top-level layer is level 1. | _undefined_ |
| `withBackground` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to paint the layer's background | `false` |
| `tag` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` | Specify the tag name. | `"div"` |

#### `Layer` typedefs

```ts
type LayerLevel = 0 | 1 | 2;
```

#### `Layer` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `{ level: LayerLevel }` |

#### `Layer` $$restProps

`Layer` spreads `$$restProps` to the `svelte:element` element.


## LayoutDirection

### Basic

Set `dir` to `"rtl"` or `"ltr"`. `LayoutDirection` renders a `div` with that `dir`, and components inside it read the direction from context. Use `tag` to render another element, such as `section` or `form`. A plain `dir` attribute inside it wins for its part, for the arrow keys as for the styles.

It matches Carbon React's `LayoutDirection`. To set the direction for the whole page, set `dir` on `<html>` instead. See the [right-to-left guide](/right-to-left) to set up an app, and for what flips and what stays left to right.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    LayoutDirection,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar" tag="form">
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <TextInput labelText="اسم الخدمة" placeholder="api-gateway" />
    <TextInput
      labelText="البريد الإلكتروني للمالك"
      placeholder="ops@example.com"
    />
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5}>
      <Button>نشر</Button>
      <Button kind="secondary">إلغاء</Button>
    </Stack>
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Text fields

In RTL, a field's icons and buttons sit at its left end: the password toggle, the copy button, the number steppers, the clear button, the select chevron, the calendar icon, and the invalid, warning, and read-only icons. The text keeps clear of them.

`TagInput`'s tags sit at the right, so <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> at the start of the text moves to the last tag and <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> moves back. `PinCodeInput`'s first segment is the rightmost one, and <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> moves to the next segment.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    CopyInput,
    LayoutDirection,
    NumberInput,
    PasswordInput,
    Search,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <PasswordInput labelText="مفتاح الواجهة البرمجية" value="sk-live-4242" />
    <CopyInput
      labelText="رابط الإشعارات"
      value="https://hooks.example.com/42"
    />
    <NumberInput
      labelText="عدد النسخ"
      value={12}
      invalid
      invalidText="الحد الأقصى ١٠ نسخ"
    />
    <Search labelText="بحث في الحوادث" value="فشل النشر" />
    <Select labelText="المنطقة" invalid invalidText="المنطقة غير متاحة">
      <SelectItem value="us-east" text="شرق الولايات المتحدة" />
      <SelectItem value="eu-west" text="غرب أوروبا" />
    </Select>
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Buttons

In RTL, a button's label starts at its right edge and its icon sits at its left end. `ButtonSet`, `ComboButton` and `ActionSet` draw each divider on the right side of the button after it, and modal footers run from right to left.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    LayoutDirection,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Add from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Add.svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap="wrap" gap={5}>
      <Button icon={Add}>إضافة خدمة</Button>
      <Button kind="secondary" icon={Add}>إضافة خدمة</Button>
      <Button kind="tertiary" icon={Add}>إضافة خدمة</Button>
      <Button kind="ghost" icon={Add}>إضافة خدمة</Button>
      <Button kind="danger" icon={TrashCan}>حذف الخدمة</Button>
      <Button kind="danger-tertiary" icon={TrashCan}>حذف الخدمة</Button>
      <Button kind="danger-ghost" icon={TrashCan}>حذف الخدمة</Button>
    </Stack>
    <ButtonSet>
      <Button kind="secondary">إلغاء</Button>
      <Button>نشر</Button>
    </ButtonSet>
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Date picker

In RTL, the calendar runs from the right: the week starts at the right edge, and the previous month arrow sits on the right and points right. <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> moves to the next day, month, or year, and <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> to the previous one. <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> still go to the first and last day of the week. A calendar in a portal opens at the field's right edge. Set `locale` to name the months and weekdays and to start the week on the locale's first day, such as Saturday for `"ar"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    LayoutDirection,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <DatePicker datePickerType="range" locale="ar">
    <DatePickerInput labelText="بداية الفترة" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    <DatePickerInput labelText="نهاية الفترة" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Slider

In RTL, `Slider` and `RangeSlider` put `min` at the right end of the track. Dragging, clicking the track, marks, and the arrow keys follow it: <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> raises the value.

The thumbs, fill, and marks follow the nearest `dir` in the styles, in server-rendered markup and as it changes. A slider in a `LayoutDirection` reads its `dir` for the keys and the pointer as it changes. Outside one, it reads the page direction when it mounts, and again when the pointer or keyboard focus reaches it.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    LayoutDirection,
    RangeSlider,
    Slider,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Stack gap={7}>
    <Slider labelText="عدد النسخ" min={0} max={10} value={3} />
    <RangeSlider
      labelText="نطاق النسخ"
      min={0}
      max={10}
      value={2}
      valueUpper={6}
      marks={[
        { value: 0, label: "٠" },
        { value: 5, label: "٥" },
        { value: 10, label: "١٠" },
      ]}
    />
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Tabs

Tabs run from right to left. <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> moves to the next tab and <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> to the previous one. <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> still go to the first and last tab. Outside a `LayoutDirection`, the tabs read the page direction on each arrow key. When the list overflows, the first tab sits at the right end, and the scroll buttons and edge fades follow it. This also holds for the row layout of `TabsVertical`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    LayoutDirection,
    Tab,
    TabContent,
    Tabs,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Tabs>
    <Tab label="نظرة عامة" />
    <Tab label="السجلات" />
    <Tab label="الإعدادات" />
    <svelte:fragment slot="content">
      <TabContent>حالة الخدمة وآخر عملية نشر.</TabContent>
      <TabContent>سجلات آخر ٢٤ ساعة.</TabContent>
      <TabContent>المنطقة وحدود الموارد.</TabContent>
    </svelte:fragment>
  </Tabs>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### TreeView

In RTL, rows indent from the right and a collapsed caret points left. <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> expands a row or moves to its first child, and <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> collapses it or moves to its parent. Outside a `LayoutDirection`, the tree reads the page direction on each arrow key.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LayoutDirection, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <TreeView
    labelText="الخدمات"
    expandedIds={["analytics"]}
    nodes={[
      {
        id: "analytics",
        text: "التحليلات",
        nodes: [
          { id: "spark", text: "Apache Spark" },
          { id: "query", text: "استعلام SQL" },
        ],
      },
      {
        id: "storage",
        text: "التخزين",
        nodes: [{ id: "object-storage", text: "تخزين الكائنات" }],
      },
    ]}
  />
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Menus

In RTL, a menu opens from the trigger's right edge, and a submenu opens to the left. When there is no room on the left, the submenu opens to the right instead. <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> opens a submenu and <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> closes it. This covers `Menu`, `MenuButton`, `ComboButton`, `ContextMenu`, and `HeaderNavMenu`.

In `MenuButton` and `ComboButton`, `intrinsicAlign` values `"start"` and `"end"` mean the trigger's inline start and end. An `OverflowMenu` lines up with the button's right edge, and with its left edge when `flipped`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    LayoutDirection,
    MenuButton,
    MenuItem,
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5} align="center">
    <MenuButton labelText="إجراءات">
      <MenuItem labelText="نسخ" />
      <MenuItem labelText="تصدير بصيغة">
        <MenuItem labelText="PDF" />
        <MenuItem labelText="PNG" />
      </MenuItem>
    </MenuButton>
    <OverflowMenu iconDescription="خيارات">
      <OverflowMenuItem text="إعادة التشغيل" />
      <OverflowMenuItem text="إيقاف" />
    </OverflowMenu>
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Arrow keys

In RTL, <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> moves to the next item and <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> to the previous one in `ContentSwitcher`, `ToggleButtonGroup`, `ProgressIndicator`, `TagSet` with `navigation="roving"`, and the `HeaderNav` menubar. Outside a `LayoutDirection`, each reads the page direction when the key arrives.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    ContentSwitcher,
    LayoutDirection,
    Switch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <ContentSwitcher>
    <Switch text="الأحدث" />
    <Switch text="الأكثر رواجًا" />
    <Switch text="المحفوظة" />
  </ContentSwitcher>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Resizing

In RTL, a resizable `SideNav` has its handle on its left edge, and a horizontal `Splitter` puts its start pane on the right. Dragging the handle or separator left widens the side nav or the start pane, and so does <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd>.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, LayoutDirection, Splitter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Box height="10rem" border="subtle">
    <Splitter size={35} separatorLabel="تغيير حجم قائمة الملفات">
      <Box slot="start" padding={5}>الملفات</Box>
      <Box slot="end" padding={5}>deploy.yaml</Box>
    </Splitter>
  </Box>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Icons

In RTL, icons that point forward or back mirror: Pagination, PaginationNav, Carousel, Tabs and DatePicker month arrows, Stepper and InterstitialScreen buttons, the AILabel undo icon, submenu carets and the Card and ClickableTile icons. Icons without a direction stay as they are, such as check marks, the search icon and the Launch icon of an outbound link.

Add the `bx--icon--mirror-rtl` class to mirror your own forward or back icon, such as an arrow in a link's `icon` slot. A `dir="ltr"` region inside an RTL page turns the mirror off again.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Card,
    CardBody,
    CardHeader,
    CardTitle,
    ClickableTile,
    LayoutDirection,
    Link,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import ArrowRight from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/ArrowRight.svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <ClickableTile href="#" icon={ArrowRight}>إعدادات الفوترة</ClickableTile>
    <Card clickable href="#" aria-label="إعدادات المشروع">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>إعدادات المشروع</CardTitle>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>إدارة الأعضاء والصلاحيات والتكاملات.</CardBody>
    </Card>
    <Link href="#">
      عرض سجل النشر
      <ArrowRight slot="icon" class="bx--icon--mirror-rtl" />
    </Link>
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Copy input

`CopyInput` takes the direction of its value from the first letter of the value, so a URL or a token keeps its order in an RTL page, and Arabic or Hebrew text still reads right to left. Set `dir="ltr"` on a value that must read left to right whatever its first letter, such as a file path with Arabic folder names.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CopyInput, LayoutDirection, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <CopyInput
      labelText="رابط الخدمة"
      value="https://api.example.com/v1/deployments/"
    />
    <CopyInput labelText="اسم الخدمة" value="بوابة الدفع (الإنتاج)" />
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Tooltips and popovers

Above and below a trigger, `align="start"` and `align="end"` name inline sides, as in floating-ui, which Carbon React uses. In RTL they swap: a start-aligned tooltip lines up with the trigger's right edge, and its caret follows. `left`, `right`, and Popover's older names, such as `"top-left"`, name physical sides and stay put.

This covers Tooltip, TooltipIcon, TooltipDefinition, Toggletip, the AILabel explanation, Popover, and the tooltips of icon-only buttons, in place and in a portal. A Breadcrumb's overflow menu opens from the right edge of its trigger. Outside a `LayoutDirection`, each reads the page direction when it opens.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    LayoutDirection,
    Stack,
    Toggletip,
    TooltipIcon,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={10}>
    <Toggletip align="start" labelText="الخطة">
      تُحسب الرسوم في بداية كل شهر.
    </Toggletip>
    <TooltipIcon
      align="start"
      tooltipText="تُحسب الرسوم شهريًا"
      icon={Information}
    />
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Portalled menus

A menu or tooltip that renders in a portal leaves the subtree in the DOM, so it would lose the direction. `LayoutDirection` carries it to the portal. A plain `dir` nearer the trigger wins, as for the styles. This covers `portalMenu` on Dropdown, ComboBox, and MultiSelect, a portalled DatePicker calendar, and every component that portals a tooltip or menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown, LayoutDirection } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Dropdown
    portalMenu
    labelText="المنطقة"
    selectedId="0"
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "شرق الولايات المتحدة" },
      { id: "1", text: "غرب أوروبا" },
      { id: "2", text: "جنوب شرق آسيا" },
    ]}
  />
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Mixed directions

Nest a `LayoutDirection` to switch back for one part, such as English fields in an RTL form. The nearest direction wins, so the password toggle and the search icons sit where they do in an LTR page. A `CodeSnippet` needs no wrapper: its code always reads left to right. See [CodeSnippet](/components/CodeSnippet#right-to-left).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    LayoutDirection,
    PasswordInput,
    Search,
    Stack,
    Text,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <Text>أدخل بيانات الخادم باللغة الإنجليزية:</Text>
    <LayoutDirection dir="ltr" lang="en">
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <TextInput
          labelText="Server URL"
          placeholder="https://api.example.com"
        />
        <PasswordInput labelText="API key" value="sk-live-4f2a9c71" />
        <Search labelText="Search services" value="payments-api" />
      </Stack>
    </LayoutDirection>
    <Text>نستخدم هذا العنوان والمفتاح في كل طلب.</Text>
  </Stack>
</LayoutDirection>
```

### Reading the direction

Call `getLayoutDirection` during component initialization to read the nearest direction in your own components. It returns a store that holds `"ltr"`, `"rtl"`, or `undefined` outside a `LayoutDirection`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { getLayoutDirection } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const direction = getLayoutDirection();
</script>

<span>{$direction === "rtl" ? "←" : "→"}</span>
```

---

### Component API

#### `LayoutDirection` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` (Required) | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` | Specify the layout direction of the content. | _undefined_ |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLElementTagNameMap[Tag]` | Obtain a reference to the HTML element. | `null` |
| `tag` | `Tag` | Specify the tag name. | `"div"` |

#### `LayoutDirection` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `LayoutDirection` $$restProps

`LayoutDirection` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## LazyMount

### Basic

`LazyMount` renders its default slot once the wrapper comes within `rootMargin` (600px by default) of the viewport, so the content is ready before the reader scrolls to it. Until then it shows the `placeholder` slot and reserves `estimatedHeight`. Once mounted, content stays mounted.

Every instance shares one `IntersectionObserver` per `rootMargin`. Without `IntersectionObserver`, content renders right away.

Wrap a heavy widget, and set `estimatedHeight` close to its rendered height so the page doesn't shift when it mounts. A number is in pixels; any CSS length works.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable, LazyMount } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LazyMount estimatedHeight={400}>
  <DataTable {headers} {rows} />
</LazyMount>
```

### Placeholder

Fill the `placeholder` slot to show something while the content waits, such as a skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LazyMount, SkeletonText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LazyMount estimatedHeight="12rem">
  <SkeletonText slot="placeholder" paragraph lines={4} />
  <p>This paragraph rendered once it came near the viewport.</p>
</LazyMount>
```

### Idle

Set `when` to `"idle"` to mount the content once the browser is idle, or sooner if it comes near the viewport. Use it for content just below the fold that should be ready without waiting for a scroll. Several take turns, one each time the browser is idle, from the top of the page down. Content above the viewport waits until the reader scrolls near it, since mounting it would move what's on screen.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    LazyMount,
    SkeletonPlaceholder,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LazyMount when="idle" estimatedHeight={160}>
  <SkeletonPlaceholder slot="placeholder" width="100%" height={160} />
  <DataTable size="short" {headers} rows={rows.slice(0, 3)} />
</LazyMount>
```

### Mount event

`mount` is dispatched once, after the content first renders. Bind `mounted` to read whether it has.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LazyMount } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import mountedAt from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/mountedAt.svelte";
</script>

<LazyMount on:mount={() => (mountedAt = new Date().toLocaleTimeString())}>
  <p>Mounted at {mountedAt}.</p>
</LazyMount>
```

### Eager

Set `eager` to render the content right away, for example in tests, or for a page that must be complete when it loads. Content also mounts on `beforeprint`, so printing a page includes it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LazyMount } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LazyMount eager>
  <p>This content rendered on the first pass.</p>
</LazyMount>
```

### Usage

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Wrap live examples, charts, large tables, and other widgets that are costly to mount. | They cost the most to render, and nobody sees them until scrolling there. |
| Leave text, headings, and links unwrapped. | Content that hasn't mounted isn't in find in page, anchor links, the accessibility tree, or server-rendered HTML. |
| Set `estimatedHeight` close to the content's rendered height. | The page doesn't shift when the content mounts, and scroll anchors land in the right place. |
| Show a placeholder for content inside a scroll container, such as a modal body. | `rootMargin` grows the viewport only, so content there mounts as it scrolls into the container's view, with no head start. |
| Prefer CSS `content-visibility: auto` for static content that's costly to lay out. | The browser skips its rendering but keeps it in find in page and the accessibility tree. |

---

### Component API

#### `LazyMount` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mounted` (Reactive) | `boolean` | `true` once the content has mounted. Mounted content stays mounted. | `false` |
| `when` | `"visible" \| "idle"` | Specify when the content mounts.<br />`"visible"` mounts it once the wrapper comes within `rootMargin` of the viewport.<br />`"idle"` mounts it once the browser is idle, or sooner if it comes that close.<br />Idle mounts take turns, one an idle period, top to bottom, and skip<br />content above the viewport, which mounts as the reader scrolls near it. | `"visible"` |
| `rootMargin` | `string` | Specify how far outside the viewport counts as near, as a CSS margin.<br />Content mounts before it scrolls into view, so it is ready when it does. | `"600px"` |
| `estimatedHeight` | `number \| string \| undefined` | Specify the height to reserve until the content mounts, so the page<br />doesn't shift when it does. A number is in pixels. | _undefined_ |
| `eager` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render the content right away, for example in tests or<br />before printing. Content also mounts on `beforeprint`. | `false` |

#### `LazyMount` slots

| Slot          | Detail                  |
| ------------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`     | `Record<string, never>` |
| `placeholder` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `LazyMount` dispatched events

| Event      | Detail | Description                                       |
| ---------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `on:mount` | `null` | Dispatched once, after the content first renders. |

#### `LazyMount` $$restProps

`LazyMount` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## Link

### Basic

Create a basic link with the default styling.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Link href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/">API documentation</Link>
```

### Inline

Create links that flow naturally with surrounding text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Review the
  <Link inline href="/docs/rate-limits">rate limit policy</Link>
  before configuring retries.
</div>
```

### Muted

Set `muted` to `true` so the link inherits the surrounding text color instead of the link color. Pair it with `inline` for links that sit within body text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link, Text } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Text>
  Read the
  <Link inline muted href="/incidents/2451/postmortem">
    incident postmortem
  </Link>
  for root cause analysis and remediation steps.
</Text>
```

### Custom colors

Set `--cds-link-text-color` on a link, or on an element that holds links, to recolor it. `--cds-link-hover-text-color`, `--cds-link-visited-text-color` and `--cds-link-focus-text-color` set the hover color, the `visited` color and the focus ring. Each falls back to its theme token. `Toggletip` sets them to the inverse link colors on its content, so set them on an element inside the content to recolor its links.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Link
  href="/billing/invoices"
  style="--cds-link-text-color: var(--cds-text-secondary); --cds-link-hover-text-color: var(--cds-text-primary)"
>
  Billing invoices
</Link>
```

### External links

Use these patterns when linking to resources outside your app.

#### Opens in new tab

For external links that open in a new tab, the component automatically adds security attributes (rel="noopener noreferrer"). Override rel if needed.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Link href="https://cloud.ibm.com/status" target="_blank">Service status</Link>
```

#### Outbound link

Use `OutboundLink` as a convenient alternative for external links. Because it opens in a new tab (`target="_blank"`), it adds visually hidden text ("(opens in a new tab)") so screen readers announce the behavior.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OutboundLink } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OutboundLink href="https://cloud.ibm.com/apidocs">API reference</OutboundLink>
```

#### Custom assistive text

External links open in a new tab and append assistive text automatically for screen readers. Override `assistiveText` if needed, or set it to an empty string to opt out.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OutboundLink } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OutboundLink
  href="https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/terms-use"
  assistiveText="(opens in a new window)"
>
  Terms of service
</OutboundLink>
```

### Download link

Use `LinkDownload` to trigger a client-side file download instead of navigating to a URL. Set `data` to the content to download, a string or `Blob`, and `filename` for the downloaded file name.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LinkDownload } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LinkDownload
  data="id,name,region{'\n'}1,lb-east,us-east-1{'\n'}2,lb-west,us-west-2"
  filename="load-balancers.csv"
  type="text/csv;charset=utf-8"
>
  Download CSV
</LinkDownload>
```

#### Dynamic content

`data` is read at the moment the link is clicked, so downloaded content reflects filtering, sorting, or other state changes made before the click.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LinkDownload, Search, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const loadBalancers = [
    { id: "1", name: "lb-east", region: "us-east-1" },
    { id: "2", name: "lb-west", region: "us-west-2" },
    { id: "3", name: "lb-central", region: "us-central-1" },
  ];

  let value = "";

  $: filteredRows = loadBalancers.filter((row) =>
    row.name.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase()),
  );

  $: csv = [
    "id,name,region",
    ...filteredRows.map((row) => `${row.id},${row.name},${row.region}`),
  ].join("\n");
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Search
    bind:value
    labelText="Filter load balancers"
    placeholder="Filter by name..."
  />
  <ul>
    {#each filteredRows as row (row.id)}
      <li>{row.name} ({row.region})</li>
    {/each}
  </ul>
  <LinkDownload
    data={csv}
    filename="load-balancers.csv"
    type="text/csv;charset=utf-8"
  >
    Download CSV
  </LinkDownload>
</Stack>
```

#### Events

Listen for `download`, dispatched after the file downloads successfully, and `download:error`, dispatched if the download throws, with the error at `event.detail.error`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LinkDownload } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LinkDownload
  data="id,name,region{'\n'}1,lb-east,us-east-1{'\n'}2,lb-west,us-west-2"
  filename="load-balancers.csv"
  type="text/csv;charset=utf-8"
  on:download={() => console.log("downloaded")}
  on:download:error={(e) => console.log(e.detail.error)}
>
  Download CSV
</LinkDownload>
```

#### Custom download behavior

Override the default download behavior by passing a function to `download`. It receives `(data, filename, type)` and can return a promise; use it to upload the payload, show a confirmation step, or otherwise replace the built-in Blob download.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LinkDownload } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LinkDownload
  data="id,name,region{'\n'}1,lb-east,us-east-1{'\n'}2,lb-west,us-west-2"
  filename="load-balancers.csv"
  download={(data, filename, type) => console.log(data, filename, type)}
>
  Download CSV
</LinkDownload>
```

```

</script>

  Release notes

#### Small with icon

<Link size="sm" href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/release-notes" icon={Carbon}>
  Release notes
</Link>
```

### States

Reflect interaction and navigation history.

#### Disabled

Set `disabled` to `true` to disable the link. Native `<a>` elements have no `disabled` attribute, so the link instead renders with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`, and drops its `href`, remaining focusable and readable by assistive technology while looking and behaving like plain text. Clicks are also blocked outright--`event.preventDefault()` and `event.stopPropagation()` run before any forwarded `on:click` listener, so neither the link nor an ancestor element receives the click.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Link disabled href="/audit-logs">Audit logs</Link>
```

#### Disabled with icon

The icon still renders when the link is disabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
</script>

<Link disabled href="/audit-logs" icon={Carbon}>Audit logs</Link>
```

#### Visited

Show visited state styling with `visited`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Link visited href="/deployments/history">Deployment history</Link>
```

## Loading

### Basic

Display a loading indicator with a semi-transparent overlay that covers the entire viewport. While active, the overlay holds keyboard focus. Focus returns to the previous element when loading stops.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Loading } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Loading />
```

### No overlay

Show a loading indicator without the overlay, allowing interaction with the underlying content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Loading } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Loading withOverlay={false} />
```

### Small

Display a more compact loading indicator.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Loading } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Loading withOverlay={false} small />
```

### Description

Set `description` to name the spinner for screen readers. The overlay also uses it as the name of its dialog. Defaults to `"loading"`. The spinner is not a live region: the overlay is announced when its dialog takes focus, and a spinner inside a control, such as Button's, is read with that control.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Loading } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Loading description="Loading metrics..." withOverlay={false} />
```

### Delay

Set `delay` to wait a number of milliseconds after `active` becomes `true` before showing the spinner. Work that finishes within the delay shows no spinner. Once shown, the spinner stays for at least 500 ms so it does not flash.

While it waits, the spinner is in the page but hidden. The server HTML holds it too, and CSS shows it after the delay even before the page's script runs. This also covers a `Loading` that mounts when the work starts, as in `{#if loading}`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Loading, Stack, Text } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let active = false;

  async function simulateRequest(duration) {
    active = true;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, duration));
    active = false;
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5} align="center">
    <Button on:click={() => simulateRequest(150)}>Fast request (150 ms)</Button>
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => simulateRequest(400)}>
      Request (400 ms)
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={() => simulateRequest(2000)}>
      Slow request (2 s)
    </Button>
    <Loading withOverlay={false} small {active} delay={300} />
  </Stack>

  <Text type="helper-text-01">
    The fast request finishes before the 300 ms delay, so it shows no spinner.
    The 400 ms request shows the spinner at 300 ms and keeps it until 800 ms.
  </Text>
</Stack>
```

### Stop state

Set `active` to `false` to play the spinner's end-of-loading animation. Useful when transitioning out of a loading state before removing the component.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Loading } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Loading active={false} withOverlay={false} />
```

---

### Component API

#### `Loading` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `small` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the small variant | `false` |
| `active` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to disable the active state | `true` |
| `withOverlay` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to disable the overlay | `true` |
| `description` | `string` | Specify the description to describe the loading state | `"loading"` |
| `delay` | `number` | Wait this many milliseconds after `active` turns `true` before showing<br />the spinner. Once shown, the spinner stays for at least 500 ms, so fast<br />work shows nothing and slow work never flashes. While it waits, the<br />spinner is in the page but hidden, so server HTML already holds it.<br />Set to `0` to show the spinner at once. | `0` |

#### `Loading` $$restProps

`Loading` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## LocalStorage

### Basic

See how the component maintains state across page reloads. Toggle the switch and refresh the page to see the persisted state. Unlike [SessionStorage](/components/SessionStorage), data persists indefinitely and is shared across all tabs of the same origin.

The component listens for the [storage event](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/storage_event), so changes made in one browser tab are automatically synchronized to other tabs with the same key. Cross-tab updates dispatch `on:update` with a payload shaped like `{ prevValue, value }`. When another tab removes the key, the bound value resets to undefined so the next local write does not re-persist stale data.

The example below logs both `on:save` and `on:update` as they fire; see [Events](#events) for what each one means.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LocalStorage, Toggle } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let toggled = false;
  let events = [];

  // `document` is undefined during server-side rendering.
  $: if (typeof document !== "undefined") {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute("theme", toggled ? "g100" : "white");
  }
</script>

<LocalStorage
  key="dark-mode"
  bind:value={toggled}
  on:save={() => {
    events = [...events, { event: "on:save" }];
  }}
  on:update={({ detail }) => {
    events = [...events, { event: "on:update", detail }];
  }}
/>

<Toggle size="sm" labelText="Dark mode" bind:toggled />

<br />

<pre>{JSON.stringify(events, null, 2)}</pre>
```

### Persisting objects and arrays

The bound value can be any JSON-serializable data; objects and arrays are serialized with JSON.stringify. Strings are stored as is, except strings that look like JSON (such as `"123"` or `"true"`), which are JSON-encoded so they read back as strings rather than numbers or booleans. The component compares the serialized form to decide when to write, which has two consequences:

- Reassigning to a new object or array with **identical contents** does not trigger a redundant write.
- **In-place mutations** (for example, changing a nested theme property) persist only when you signal the change to Svelte. Reassign the value (`value = { ...value, theme: "light" }`) or use the self-assignment idiom (`value = value`); a bare mutation alone will not re-render and therefore will not persist.

In this example, the text inputs bind directly to nested properties and the button mutates the object in place. Edit a field and refresh the page to confirm the change is persisted.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    LocalStorage,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  // A nested object value. Editing a nested field -- either through a two-way
  // binding or an explicit in-place mutation signalled with `value = value` --
  // is persisted because the component compares the serialized form.
  let settings = {
    profile: { name: "Priya Nair", role: "Site Reliability Engineer" },
    sessionCount: 0,
  };
  let events = [];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <LocalStorage
    key="admin-user-profile"
    bind:value={settings}
    on:update={({ detail }) => {
      events = [...events, { event: "on:update", detail }];
    }}
  />

  <div>
    Edit the nested fields below, then refresh the page to confirm the changes
    survive. The two-way bindings mutate <code>settings</code> in place; the component
    still persists them.
  </div>

  <TextInput
    labelText="Name (binds to settings.profile.name)"
    bind:value={settings.profile.name}
  />

  <TextInput
    labelText="Role (binds to settings.profile.role)"
    bind:value={settings.profile.role}
  />

  <Button
    size="small"
    on:click={() => {
      settings.sessionCount += 1; // in-place mutation
      settings = settings; // signal the change to Svelte
    }}
  >
    Increment session count ({settings.sessionCount})
  </Button>

  <div>
    <strong>Current value:</strong>
    <pre>{JSON.stringify(settings, null, 2)}</pre>
  </div>

  <div>
    <strong>Updates (note prevValue is a true snapshot):</strong>
    <pre>{JSON.stringify(events, null, 2)}</pre>
  </div>
</Stack>
```

### Reactive key

The storage key is also reactive -- set `key` to switch between contexts, useful for per-user settings.

In this example, each user has their own theme preference stored under a separate key. When you switch users, the component automatically loads that user's saved preference.

Switching keys only hydrates the bound value from storage; it does not dispatch `on:update`. The event log below should stay empty when you change users and only record entries when you change the theme.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    LocalStorage,
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedUser = "morgan-lee";
  let theme = "white";
  let events = [];

  $: storageKey = `theme-preference-${selectedUser}`;
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    Try selecting different users and changing their theme preferences. Each
    user's preference is stored separately and persists across page reloads.
  </div>
  <LocalStorage
    key={storageKey}
    bind:value={theme}
    on:update={({ detail }) => {
      events = [...events, { event: "on:update", detail }];
    }}
  />
  <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Select user" bind:selected={selectedUser}>
    <RadioButton labelText="Morgan Lee" value="morgan-lee" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Priya Nair" value="priya-nair" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Sam Okafor" value="sam-okafor" />
  </RadioButtonGroup>
  <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Theme preference" bind:selected={theme}>
    <RadioButton labelText="White" value="white" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 10" value="g10" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 80" value="g80" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 90" value="g90" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 100" value="g100" />
  </RadioButtonGroup>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <div>
      <strong>Current key:</strong>
      {storageKey}
    </div>
    <div>
      <strong>Current theme:</strong>
      {theme}
    </div>
  </Stack>
  <strong> Updates: </strong>
  <pre>{JSON.stringify(events, null, 2)}</pre>
</Stack>
```

### Disabling cross-tab sync

With sync enabled by default, another tab writing the same key updates the bound value and fires `on:update`. Set `sync="off"` to ignore those writes. The component still loads storage on mount and saves your own changes.

Use sync off when each tab should keep separate state: drafts, forms in progress, or a second login tab that should not clobber the first. You can also turn sync off if the app resolves conflicts itself. Sync is reactive, so you can change it at runtime.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LocalStorage } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LocalStorage key="draft" bind:value sync="off" />
```

### Clear item, clear all

The component provides methods to manage stored data:

| Method      | Description                       |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| `clearItem` | Remove a specific key-value pair. |
| `clearAll`  | Remove all stored data.           |

Use `bind:this` to access these methods. Both also reset the bound value to `undefined` and dispatch [`update`](#update), so there is no need to reset it yourself. The key stays cleared until the value changes again. Other tabs with the same key reset their bound value when they receive the storage event.

In this example, try toggling the switch, refreshing the page, then clearing the storage.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, LocalStorage, Toggle } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let storage;
  let toggled = false;

  // `document` is undefined during server-side rendering.
  $: if (typeof document !== "undefined") {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute("theme", toggled ? "g100" : "white");
  }
</script>

<LocalStorage key="dark-mode" bind:this={storage} bind:value={toggled} />

<Toggle size="sm" labelText="Dark mode" bind:toggled />

<br />
<br />

<Button size="small" on:click={storage.clearAll}>Clear storage</Button>
```

### Events

The component dispatches three events: `save`, `update`, and `error`.

#### Update

Fires whenever the persisted value changes -- after your own `bind:value` write, after `clearItem` or `clearAll`, or when another tab or window writes the same key while `sync` is `"on"` (the default). The payload is `{ prevValue, value }`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LocalStorage } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LocalStorage
  key="dark-mode"
  bind:value
  on:update={({ detail }) => console.log(detail)} // { prevValue, value }
/>
```

#### Save

Fires once, when the component mounts, if the key does not already exist in storage -- this is the component's own first write to initialize that key. Switching to a different key afterward (see [Reactive key](#reactive-key)) does not dispatch `save`, even if the new key has no stored value yet.

#### Error

Fires when a write to storage fails, for example when the storage quota is exceeded or storage access is denied (such as private browsing modes that disable storage). The payload is `{ error }`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LocalStorage } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<LocalStorage
  key="workspace-settings"
  bind:value
  on:error={({ detail }) => console.error(detail.error)}
/>
```

---

### Component API

#### `LocalStorage` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `T` | Provide a value to persist. | `""` |
| `key` | `string` | Specify the local storage key. | `"local-storage-key"` |
| `sync` | `"on" \| "off"` | `"off"` ignores storage events from other tabs or windows on the same<br />origin. `"on"` (default) keeps the previous behavior. | `"on"` |
| `clearItem` | `() => void` | Remove the persisted key value from the browser's local storage.<br />Also resets the bound `value` to `undefined` and dispatches `update`. | _undefined_ |
| `clearAll` | `() => void` | Clear all key values from the browser's local storage.<br />Also resets the bound `value` to `undefined` and dispatches `update`. | _undefined_ |

#### `LocalStorage` forwarded events

| Event       |
| ----------- |
| `on:error`  |
| `on:save`   |
| `on:update` |


## Menu

### Basic

Menu positions its content relative to an `anchor` element and does not render a trigger of its own. Bind a reference to the element that opens the menu, then control `open` from that element's event handler. Use `MenuItem` for each action; set `disabled` to make an item non-interactive.

The root element has `role="menu"`. Set `labelText` or `aria-label` on Menu so assistive technologies get a meaningful name, since there is no visible text the menu is otherwise associated with.

Once open, arrow keys move focus between items without wrapping past the first or last item. <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> jump to the first and last item. Disabled items take focus so screen reader users can find them, but they do not run. Type a character to move focus to the next item whose label starts with it; type several characters quickly to match a longer prefix. <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes the menu and returns focus to the anchor. See [Events](#events) for the full set of ways the menu can close, and how to keep it open after selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem disabled>Delete</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

### Size

Set `size` to control each item's row height. The default is `"sm"`.

#### Extra small

`"xs"` is a compact row height for dense layouts.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} size="xs" bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Medium

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} size="md" bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Large

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} size="lg" bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

### Menu items

`MenuItem` takes an `icon`, `kind="danger"` for destructive rows, and nested children for submenus. Use `MenuDivider` between groups.

#### Icons

Pass a Carbon icon to `icon`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Cut from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Cut.svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem icon={Cut} on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem icon={Copy} on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Shortcuts

Set `shortcut` to show its keys on the right of the row, such as `"mod+x"`, which shows <DocKbd shortcut="mod+x" variant="muted" /> on your platform. The item announces them with `aria-keyshortcuts`. The menu only shows the keys, since it's usually closed when they're pressed: bind the command itself with `onShortcut`. For other content, use `shortcutText` or the `shortcutChildren` slot, which take precedence. A value that isn't a shortcut, such as `"CmdC"` from Carbon React's free-text `shortcut`, shows as written, with no `aria-keyshortcuts`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Cut from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Cut.svelte";
  import Paste from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Paste.svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem icon={Cut} shortcut="mod+x" on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>
    Cut
  </MenuItem>
  <MenuItem icon={Copy} shortcut="mod+c" on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>
    Copy
  </MenuItem>
  <MenuItem icon={Paste} shortcut="mod+v" on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>
    Paste
  </MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Danger

Set `kind="danger"` on `MenuItem` for a destructive action.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Menu,
    MenuDivider,
    MenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuDivider />
  <MenuItem
    icon={TrashCan}
    kind="danger"
    on:click={() => console.log("Delete")}
  >
    Delete
  </MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Dividers

Put a `MenuDivider` between groups.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Menu,
    MenuDivider,
    MenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
  <MenuDivider />
  <MenuItem kind="danger" on:click={() => console.log("Delete")}
    >Delete</MenuItem
  >
</Menu>
```

#### Selectable

Wrap items in `MenuItemGroup` to make them checkboxes that hold state, such as which table columns are visible. Set `labelText` on `MenuItemGroup` for the group's accessible name. Give every item an `id`, then bind `selectedIds` for the chosen ones. Set `selected` on an item to check it when the menu first opens, or set `selectable` on a single item outside a group for a standalone toggle. See [MenuButton selectable](/components/MenuButton#selectable) for how this interacts with keeping the menu open on selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Menu,
    MenuItem,
    MenuItemGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
  let selectedIds = ["name"];

  $: visibleColumns = selectedIds.join(", ") || "None";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>View</Button>

  <Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="View menu">
    <MenuItemGroup labelText="Columns" bind:selectedIds>
      <MenuItem id="name" labelText="Name" />
      <MenuItem id="size" labelText="Size" />
      <MenuItem id="modified" labelText="Last modified" />
    </MenuItemGroup>
  </Menu>

  <p>Visible columns: {visibleColumns}</p>
</Stack>
```

#### Radio group

Wrap items in `MenuItemRadioGroup` for a set where one choice is active at a time, such as row density. Set `labelText` on `MenuItemRadioGroup` for the group's accessible name. Bind `selectedId` for the active id; picking another item clears the previous one.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Menu,
    MenuDivider,
    MenuItem,
    MenuItemRadioGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
  let selectedId = "comfortable";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>View</Button>

  <Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="View menu">
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Reset")}>Reset</MenuItem>
    <MenuDivider />
    <MenuItemRadioGroup labelText="Density" bind:selectedId>
      <MenuItem id="compact" labelText="Compact" />
      <MenuItem id="comfortable" labelText="Comfortable" />
      <MenuItem id="spacious" labelText="Spacious" />
    </MenuItemRadioGroup>
  </Menu>

  <p>Density: {selectedId}</p>
</Stack>
```

#### Indent alignment

A selectable or radio item's checkmark and a `MenuItem`'s own `icon` sit in separate columns: the checkmark column reserves space for every item once any item in the menu is selectable or radio, and the icon column reserves space for every item once any item sets `icon`. This keeps every label in one column, whether or not that particular row has a checkmark, an icon, both, or neither.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Menu,
    MenuDivider,
    MenuItem,
    MenuItemGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Cut from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Cut.svelte";
  import Paste from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Paste.svelte";
  import TextBold from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TextBold.svelte";
  import TextItalic from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TextItalic.svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
  let selectedIds = ["bold"];
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Edit</Button>

<Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="Edit menu">
  <MenuItem icon={Cut} shortcut="mod+x" on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>
    Cut
  </MenuItem>
  <MenuItem icon={Copy} shortcut="mod+c" on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>
    Copy
  </MenuItem>
  <MenuItem icon={Paste} shortcut="mod+v" on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>
    Paste
  </MenuItem>
  <MenuDivider />
  <MenuItemGroup labelText="Style" bind:selectedIds>
    <MenuItem id="bold" icon={TextBold} shortcut="mod+b">Bold</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="italic" icon={TextItalic} shortcut="mod+i">Italic</MenuItem>
  </MenuItemGroup>
</Menu>
```

#### Nested

Set `labelText` on a `MenuItem` and nest child `MenuItem` rows to get a submenu. Use the `labelChildren` slot instead of plain text to customize the label's content; `labelText` is still used as the accessible name and title in that case. See [MenuButton menu items](/components/MenuButton#menu-items) for keyboard and hover behavior. Typing a character inside an open submenu searches only that submenu's items.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem labelText="Export as">
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("PDF")}>PDF</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("JPG")}>JPG</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("PNG")}>PNG</MenuItem>
  </MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Custom label content

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon, in place of `labelText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Menu,
    MenuItem,
    TooltipIcon,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem labelText="Deploy" on:click={() => console.log("Deploy")}>
    <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
      Deploy
      <TooltipIcon
        align="start"
        tooltipText="Deploys the latest build to production."
        icon={Information}
      />
    </svelte:fragment>
  </MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("View details")}>View details</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

### Scrollable

Set `maxHeight` to cap the menu height and scroll the remaining items. A number is treated as pixels; a string is used as any CSS length, such as `"20rem"`. Keyboard navigation scrolls the focused item into view.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;

  const actions = [
    "Assign to me",
    "Assign to team",
    "Change priority",
    "Change status",
    "Add label",
    "Remove label",
    "Add to sprint",
    "Remove from sprint",
    "Duplicate",
    "Convert to task",
    "Link related issue",
    "Move to project",
    "Watch",
    "Stop watching",
    "Export as CSV",
    "Export as JSON",
    "Print",
    "Archive",
    "Restore",
    "Delete",
  ];
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu {anchor} bind:open labelText="Actions menu" maxHeight={240}>
  {#each actions as action (action)}
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log(action)}>{action}</MenuItem>
  {/each}
</Menu>
```

### Placement

Menu forwards its placement props to [FloatingPortal](/components/FloatingPortal).

#### Direction

Set `direction` to `"top"`, `"bottom"` (default), `"left"`, or `"right"` to control which side of the anchor the menu opens toward. The menu flips to the opposite side automatically when there is not enough space.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Box marginTop="220px">
  <Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>
</Box>

<Menu {anchor} direction="top" bind:open labelText="Actions menu">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Intrinsic width

By default, the menu matches the anchor's width. Set `intrinsicWidth` to `true` to size the menu to its content instead, and set `intrinsicAlign` to `"start"` to keep it flush with the trigger's leading edge, the common menu pattern.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Box width="320px">
  <Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
    Actions on this wide button
  </Button>
</Box>

<Menu
  {anchor}
  bind:open
  intrinsicWidth
  intrinsicAlign="start"
  labelText="Actions menu"
>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Intrinsic alignment

When `intrinsicWidth` is `true`, set `intrinsicAlign` to `"start"`, `"center"` (default), or `"end"` to position the menu along the anchor.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Box width="320px">
  <Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
    Actions on this wide button
  </Button>
</Box>

<Menu
  {anchor}
  bind:open
  intrinsicWidth
  intrinsicAlign="end"
  labelText="Actions menu"
>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Gaps and offsets

Use `gapTop` and `gapBottom` to add vertical spacing when direction is `"top"` or `"bottom"`. Use `horizontalGapLeft` and `horizontalGapRight` to add horizontal spacing when direction is `"left"` or `"right"`, and `verticalAlignOffsetLeft` / `verticalAlignOffsetRight` to nudge that same content up or down. See [FloatingPortal gaps and offsets](/components/FloatingPortal#gaps-and-offsets) for the full prop reference.

#### Custom target

By default, the menu mounts into the anchor's nearest `<dialog>` or `[popover]` ancestor, falling back to `document.body`. Set `target` to mount it into a specific DOM element instead. See the [FloatingPortal custom target](/components/FloatingPortal#custom-target) documentation for typical use cases.

#### Z-index

Set `zIndex` to change the menu's stacking order. The default is `9200`.

### Events

Menu dispatches `open` once it finishes opening and focus moves to the first item, and `close` on every close attempt.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let anchor;
  let open = false;
</script>

<Button bind:ref={anchor} on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Actions</Button>

<Menu
  {anchor}
  bind:open
  labelText="Actions menu"
  on:open={(e) => console.log("open", e.detail)}
  on:close={(e) => console.log("close", e.detail.trigger)}
>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Open event

`open`'s detail is the `anchor` element.

#### Close event

Use `on:close` to respond to every close attempt, regardless of cause. The event detail's `trigger` is `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, or `"select"`. An item's `click` event is separately cancelable: call `event.preventDefault()` in a `MenuItem`'s `on:click` handler to keep the menu open after that particular selection. See [MenuButton keep open on selection](/components/MenuButton#keep-open-on-selection).

---

### Component API

#### `Menu` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the menu. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLUListElement` | Obtain a reference to the unordered list HTML element. | `null` |
| `anchor` | `null \| HTMLElement` | Required. Specify the anchor element to position the menu relative to. | `null` |
| `direction` | `"bottom" \| "top" \| "left" \| "right"` | Set the preferred direction of the menu.<br />The menu flips to the opposite direction if there is not enough space. | `"bottom"` |
| `labelText` | `string \| undefined` | Accessible name for the menu.<br />Prefer setting this (or `aria-label`) when there is no visible trigger<br />text for `aria-labelledby`. | _undefined_ |
| `gapTop` | `number` | Vertical gap in pixels when direction is top. | `0` |
| `gapBottom` | `number` | Vertical gap in pixels when direction is bottom. | `0` |
| `horizontalGapLeft` | `number` | Horizontal gap in pixels when direction is left. | `0` |
| `horizontalGapRight` | `number` | Horizontal gap in pixels when direction is right. | `0` |
| `verticalAlignOffsetLeft` | `number` | Vertical offset in pixels when direction is left. | `0` |
| `verticalAlignOffsetRight` | `number` | Vertical offset in pixels when direction is right. | `0` |
| `zIndex` | `number` | Specify the z-index of the menu. | `9200` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | Specify the size of the menu, which controls each item's row height.<br />`"xs"` has no Carbon v10 equivalent and is hand-authored (see `css/_menu-xs.scss`). | `"sm"` |
| `intrinsicWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the menu's intrinsic width instead of matching the anchor width. | `false` |
| `intrinsicAlign` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | When `intrinsicWidth` is true, align the menu to the anchor.<br />With `direction` set to `"top"` or `"bottom"`, `start` and `end` are the<br />anchor's inline start and end, which swap under `dir="rtl"`.<br />A menu that would run past a side of the window takes another<br />alignment for that open. | `"center"` |
| `maxHeight` | `number \| string \| undefined` | Specify the maximum height of the menu.<br />A number is treated as pixels; a string is used as a CSS length.<br />The menu scrolls once its items exceed the height. | _undefined_ |
| `target` | `HTMLElement \| null` | DOM node to mount the menu into.<br />When unset, uses the anchor's nearest `<dialog>` or `[popover]`, else the<br />fullscreen element holding the anchor, else `document.body`. | `null` |

#### `Menu` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Menu` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:keydown`    |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |

#### `Menu` dispatched events

| Event | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `on:close` | `{<br />  trigger:<br />    \| "escape-key"<br />    \| "outside-click"<br />    \| "select";<br />}` |
| `on:open` | `HTMLElement` |

#### `Menu` $$restProps

`Menu` spreads `$$restProps` to the `ul` element.

#### `MenuItem` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selected` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to select the item.<br />Only applies to a selectable item or one inside<br />`MenuItemGroup` or `MenuItemRadioGroup`. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLLIElement` | Obtain a reference to the list item HTML element. | `null` |
| `kind` | `"default" \| "danger"` | Specify the kind of item. | `"default"` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the item | `false` |
| `icon` | `Icon \| undefined` | Specify the icon to render.<br />Icon is rendered to the left of the label text. | _undefined_ |
| `labelText` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the label text.<br />Required to nest `MenuItem` children and create a submenu: once set,<br />the default slot holds the nested items instead of the label.<br />Alternatively, use the "labelChildren" slot for custom label content;<br />`labelText` is still used as the accessible name and title in that case. | _undefined_ |
| `shortcutText` | `string` | Specify the shortcut text.<br />Alternatively, use the "shortcutChildren" slot.<br />Display only; does not register a keybinding. | `""` |
| `shortcut` | `string` | Specify a keyboard shortcut to show, such as `"mod+s"`. `mod` is<br />Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. The keys show where<br />`shortcutText` goes, and the item gets `aria-keyshortcuts`. Display only:<br />bind the command itself with `onShortcut`, since the menu is usually<br />closed. `shortcutText` and its slot take precedence. A value that isn't<br />a shortcut, such as `"Ctrl C"`, shows as written. | `""` |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to make the item a standalone checkbox.<br />Automatically enabled when `selected` is `true` or when the item<br />is inside `MenuItemGroup`. | `false` |
| `id` | `string` | Specify the id.<br />It's recommended to provide an id as a value to bind to<br />within a selectable or radio menu group. | `uniqueId()` |

#### `MenuItem` slots

| Slot               | Detail                  |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- |
| `default`          | `Record<string, never>` |
| `labelChildren`    | `Record<string, never>` |
| `shortcutChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `shortcutText`     | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `MenuItem` forwarded events

| Event        |
| ------------ |
| `on:keydown` |

#### `MenuItem` dispatched events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on:click` | `MouseEvent` | Dispatched on selection. Cancelable: call `preventDefault()` to keep<br />the menu open. A selectable or radio item's selection still updates. |

#### `MenuItem` $$restProps

`MenuItem` spreads `$$restProps` to the `li` element.

#### `MenuItemGroup` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectedIds` (Reactive) | `ReadonlyArray<string>` | Specify the selected ids. | `[]` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |

#### `MenuItemGroup` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `MenuItemRadioGroup` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectedId` (Reactive) | `string` | Set the selected radio group id. | `""` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
