## MenuButton

### Basic

Wrap `MenuItem` components in `MenuButton` and set `labelText` for the trigger label. Use the `labelChildren` slot for custom trigger content. Unlike [Menu](/components/Menu), `MenuButton` includes the trigger; you don't pass an anchor. See [Events](#events) for the menu's `close` event.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem disabled>Delete</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

### Reactive example

Control the menu state programmatically by binding to `open`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    MenuButton,
    MenuItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Stack gap={6} align="start">
  <MenuButton labelText="Actions" bind:open>
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
  </MenuButton>
  <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
    {open ? "Close menu" : "Open menu"}
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

### Kind

Set `kind` to match the importance of the action.

#### Primary

The default kind is `"primary"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Tertiary

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" kind="tertiary">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Ghost

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" kind="ghost">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

### Size

Set `size` to scale the trigger button and each menu item's row height together. The default is `"md"`.

#### Extra small

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" size="xs">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Small

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" size="sm">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Large

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" size="lg">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

### Icon-only

Set `iconOnly` for an icon-only trigger. `labelText` is no longer rendered, but it remains the trigger's accessible name. Use this trigger for overflow menus that need submenus, which [OverflowMenu](/components/OverflowMenu) does not support.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuDivider, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton iconOnly labelText="Row actions">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Rename")}>Rename</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem labelText="Export as">
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("PDF")}>PDF</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("CSV")}>CSV</MenuItem>
  </MenuItem>
  <MenuDivider />
  <MenuItem
    icon={TrashCan}
    kind="danger"
    on:click={() => console.log("Delete")}
  >
    Delete
  </MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Custom icon

Pass `icon` to swap the glyph. The default is the overflow (kebab) icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton iconOnly labelText="Copy options" icon={Copy}>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy as reference")}
    >Copy as reference</MenuItem
  >
</MenuButton>
```

#### Icon description

The icon-only trigger needs its own accessible label, since it has no visible text. Override `iconDescription` to change it; the default is `labelText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton iconOnly labelText="Row actions" iconDescription="More row actions">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Rename")}>Rename</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem
    icon={TrashCan}
    kind="danger"
    on:click={() => console.log("Delete")}
  >
    Delete
  </MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

### Direction

Set `direction` to `"top"` or `"bottom"` (default) for which side of the trigger the menu opens on. The menu flips to the opposite side when there isn't room on the preferred side. See [Menu placement](/components/Menu#placement) for gap and offset props.

#### Top

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" direction="top">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Alignment

Set `intrinsicAlign` to `"start"` (default), `"center"`, or `"end"` to align the menu edge with the trigger.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" intrinsicAlign="end">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

### Scrollable

Set `maxHeight` to cap the menu height and scroll the remaining items. A number is treated as pixels; a string is used as any CSS length, such as `"20rem"`. Keyboard navigation scrolls the focused item into view.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const actions = [
    "Assign to me",
    "Assign to team",
    "Change priority",
    "Change status",
    "Add label",
    "Remove label",
    "Add to sprint",
    "Remove from sprint",
    "Duplicate",
    "Convert to task",
    "Link related issue",
    "Move to project",
    "Watch",
    "Stop watching",
    "Export as CSV",
    "Export as JSON",
    "Print",
    "Archive",
    "Restore",
    "Delete",
  ];
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" maxHeight={240}>
  {#each actions as action (action)}
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log(action)}>{action}</MenuItem>
  {/each}
</MenuButton>
```

### Disabled

Set `disabled` to `true` to disable the trigger button.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" disabled>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

### Menu items

`MenuItem` takes `disabled`, an `icon`, `kind="danger"` for destructive rows, and nested children for submenus. Use `MenuDivider` between groups.

#### Disabled

Set `disabled` on a `MenuItem` to make it non-interactive.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem disabled on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Icons

Pass a Carbon icon to `icon`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Cut from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Cut.svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions">
  <MenuItem icon={Cut} on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem icon={Copy} on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Shortcuts

Set `shortcut` to show its keys on the right of the row, such as `"mod+x"`, which shows <DocKbd shortcut="mod+x" variant="muted" /> on your platform. The item announces them with `aria-keyshortcuts`. The menu only shows the keys, since it's usually closed when they're pressed: bind the command itself with `onShortcut`. For other content, use `shortcutText` or the `shortcutChildren` slot, which take precedence.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Cut from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Cut.svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions">
  <MenuItem icon={Cut} shortcut="mod+x" on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}
    >Cut</MenuItem
  >
  <MenuItem icon={Copy} shortcut="mod+c" on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}
    >Copy</MenuItem
  >
  <MenuItem shortcut="mod+v" on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}
    >Paste</MenuItem
  >
</MenuButton>
```

#### Danger

Set `kind="danger"` on `MenuItem` for a destructive action.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuDivider, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuDivider />
  <MenuItem
    icon={TrashCan}
    kind="danger"
    on:click={() => console.log("Delete")}
  >
    Delete
  </MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Dividers

Put a `MenuDivider` between groups.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuDivider, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Paste")}>Paste</MenuItem>
  <MenuDivider />
  <MenuItem kind="danger" on:click={() => console.log("Delete")}
    >Delete</MenuItem
  >
</MenuButton>
```

#### Selectable

Wrap items in `MenuItemGroup` to make them checkboxes that hold state, such as which table columns are visible. Give every item an id, then bind `selectedIds` for the chosen ones. Set `selected` on an item to check it when the menu first opens, or set `selectable` on a single item outside a group for a standalone toggle.

Choosing an item closes the menu by default. See [Keep open on selection](#keep-open-on-selection) to change that.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    MenuButton,
    MenuItem,
    MenuItemGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedIds = ["name"];

  $: visibleColumns = selectedIds.join(", ") || "None";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <MenuButton labelText="View">
    <MenuItemGroup labelText="Columns" bind:selectedIds>
      <MenuItem id="name" labelText="Name" />
      <MenuItem id="size" labelText="Size" />
      <MenuItem id="modified" labelText="Last modified" />
    </MenuItemGroup>
  </MenuButton>

  <p>Visible columns: {visibleColumns}</p>
</Stack>
```

#### Radio group

Wrap items in `MenuItemRadioGroup` for a set where one choice is active at a time, such as row density. Bind `selectedId` for the active id; picking another item clears the previous one. Choosing an item closes the menu by default; see [Keep open on selection](#keep-open-on-selection) to change that.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    MenuButton,
    MenuDivider,
    MenuItem,
    MenuItemRadioGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedId = "comfortable";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <MenuButton labelText="View">
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Reset")}>Reset</MenuItem>
    <MenuDivider />
    <MenuItemRadioGroup labelText="Density" bind:selectedId>
      <MenuItem id="compact" labelText="Compact" />
      <MenuItem id="comfortable" labelText="Comfortable" />
      <MenuItem id="spacious" labelText="Spacious" />
    </MenuItemRadioGroup>
  </MenuButton>

  <p>Density: {selectedId}</p>
</Stack>
```

#### Nested

Set `labelText` on a `MenuItem` and nest child `MenuItem` rows to get a submenu. Open it with <kbd>→</kbd>, click, or hover (short delay). <kbd>←</kbd> closes it and refocuses the parent. Picking a nested item closes the whole menu, including open submenus. See [Keep open on selection](#keep-open-on-selection) to change that.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions">
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem labelText="Export as">
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("PDF")}>PDF</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("JPG")}>JPG</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("PNG")}>PNG</MenuItem>
  </MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

#### Keep open on selection

Choosing an item closes the menu by default, including any open submenus. Call `event.preventDefault()` in the item's `on:click` handler to keep the menu open. A selectable or radio item still updates its own state; only the close is canceled. Use this for multi-select, or for a radio choice in a submenu that should stay open after a pick.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    MenuButton,
    MenuDivider,
    MenuItem,
    MenuItemGroup,
    MenuItemRadioGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedIds = ["name"];
  let theme = "light";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <MenuButton labelText="View">
    <MenuItemGroup labelText="Columns" bind:selectedIds>
      <MenuItem
        id="name"
        labelText="Name"
        on:click={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
      />
      <MenuItem
        id="size"
        labelText="Size"
        on:click={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
      />
      <MenuItem
        id="modified"
        labelText="Last modified"
        on:click={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
      />
    </MenuItemGroup>
    <MenuDivider />
    <MenuItem labelText="Theme">
      <MenuItemRadioGroup bind:selectedId={theme}>
        <MenuItem
          id="light"
          labelText="Light"
          on:click={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
        />
        <MenuItem
          id="dark"
          labelText="Dark"
          on:click={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
        />
      </MenuItemRadioGroup>
    </MenuItem>
  </MenuButton>

  <p>Visible columns: {selectedIds.join(", ") || "None"}</p>
  <p>Theme: {theme}</p>
</Stack>
```

### Events

Respond to menu close attempts.

#### Close event

Use `on:close` to respond to every close attempt, regardless of cause. The event detail's `trigger` is `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, or `"select"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MenuButton, MenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MenuButton labelText="Actions" on:close={(e) => console.log(e.detail.trigger)}>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Cut")}>Cut</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem on:click={() => console.log("Copy")}>Copy</MenuItem>
</MenuButton>
```

---

### Component API

#### `MenuButton` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `labelText` (Required) | `string` | Required. Specify the trigger button text.<br />Alternatively, use the "labelChildren" slot for custom trigger content;<br />`labelText` is still used as the accessible name in that case.<br />When `iconOnly` is `true`, the text is not rendered but remains the<br />trigger's accessible name. | _undefined_ |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the menu. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLButtonElement` | Obtain a reference to the trigger button HTML element. | `null` |
| `iconOnly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render an icon-only trigger | `false` |
| `icon` | `Icon` | Specify the icon to render in the icon-only trigger. | `OverflowMenuVertical` |
| `iconDescription` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the ARIA label and title for the icon-only trigger's icon.<br />Defaults to `labelText`. | _undefined_ |
| `kind` | `"primary" \| "tertiary" \| "ghost"` | Specify the kind of button.<br />Does not apply when `iconOnly` is `true`; the icon-only trigger is<br />always ghost. | `"primary"` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | Specify the size of the trigger button and the menu's row height. | `"md"` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the trigger button | `false` |
| `direction` | `"top" \| "bottom"` | Set the preferred direction the menu opens toward.<br />The menu flips to the opposite direction if there is not enough space. | `"bottom"` |
| `intrinsicAlign` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | Align the menu to the trigger button.<br />`start` and `end` are the trigger's inline start and end, which swap<br />under `dir="rtl"`.<br />A menu that would run past a side of the window takes another<br />alignment for that open. | `"start"` |
| `maxHeight` | `number \| string \| undefined` | Specify the maximum height of the menu.<br />A number is treated as pixels; a string is used as a CSS length.<br />The menu scrolls once its items exceed the height. | _undefined_ |

#### `MenuButton` slots

| Slot            | Detail                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`       | `Record<string, never>` |
| `labelChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `MenuButton` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:blur`       |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:close`      |
| `on:focus`      |
| `on:mousedown`  |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `MenuButton` $$restProps

`MenuButton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `button` element.

#### `MenuItem` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selected` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to select the item.<br />Only applies to a selectable item or one inside<br />`MenuItemGroup` or `MenuItemRadioGroup`. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLLIElement` | Obtain a reference to the list item HTML element. | `null` |
| `kind` | `"default" \| "danger"` | Specify the kind of item. | `"default"` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the item | `false` |
| `icon` | `Icon \| undefined` | Specify the icon to render.<br />Icon is rendered to the left of the label text. | _undefined_ |
| `labelText` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the label text.<br />Required to nest `MenuItem` children and create a submenu: once set,<br />the default slot holds the nested items instead of the label.<br />Alternatively, use the "labelChildren" slot for custom label content;<br />`labelText` is still used as the accessible name and title in that case. | _undefined_ |
| `shortcutText` | `string` | Specify the shortcut text.<br />Alternatively, use the "shortcutChildren" slot.<br />Display only; does not register a keybinding. | `""` |
| `shortcut` | `string` | Specify a keyboard shortcut to show, such as `"mod+s"`. `mod` is<br />Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. The keys show where<br />`shortcutText` goes, and the item gets `aria-keyshortcuts`. Display only:<br />bind the command itself with `onShortcut`, since the menu is usually<br />closed. `shortcutText` and its slot take precedence. A value that isn't<br />a shortcut, such as `"Ctrl C"`, shows as written. | `""` |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to make the item a standalone checkbox.<br />Automatically enabled when `selected` is `true` or when the item<br />is inside `MenuItemGroup`. | `false` |
| `id` | `string` | Specify the id.<br />It's recommended to provide an id as a value to bind to<br />within a selectable or radio menu group. | `uniqueId()` |

#### `MenuItem` slots

| Slot               | Detail                  |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- |
| `default`          | `Record<string, never>` |
| `labelChildren`    | `Record<string, never>` |
| `shortcutChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `shortcutText`     | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `MenuItem` forwarded events

| Event        |
| ------------ |
| `on:keydown` |

#### `MenuItem` dispatched events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on:click` | `MouseEvent` | Dispatched on selection. Cancelable: call `preventDefault()` to keep<br />the menu open. A selectable or radio item's selection still updates. |

#### `MenuItem` $$restProps

`MenuItem` spreads `$$restProps` to the `li` element.

#### `MenuItemGroup` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectedIds` (Reactive) | `ReadonlyArray<string>` | Specify the selected ids. | `[]` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |

#### `MenuItemGroup` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `MenuItemRadioGroup` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectedId` (Reactive) | `string` | Set the selected radio group id. | `""` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |

#### `MenuItemRadioGroup` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |


## Meter

### Basic

Create a meter with `labelText`, `value`, and `max`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter labelText="Storage" value={420} max={1000} />
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to control the track height.

#### Medium

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter labelText="Storage" value={420} max={1000} size="md" />
```

#### Small

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter labelText="Storage" value={420} max={1000} size="sm" />
```

### Value text

Set `valueText` to render a right-aligned value in the label row. Format it yourself; `valueText` also becomes the meter's `aria-valuetext`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter labelText="Storage" value={812} max={1000} valueText="812 GB of 1 TB" />
```

Use the `valueChildren` slot to render custom value content instead of `valueText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter labelText="Storage" value={812} max={1000}>
  <strong slot="valueChildren">812 GB / 1 TB</strong>
</Meter>
```

When `valueText` is unset, `aria-valuetext` is generated automatically if the value is over capacity or the status is `"warning"` or `"error"`; otherwise it's omitted. Override the generated range (e.g., "420 of 1,000") with `valueRangeText`, and the status word with `warningText` or `errorText`.

Set `locale` to format the numbers in the generated `aria-valuetext` and threshold description for a specific language instead of the runtime default. A server often runs in a different locale than the browser, so without a fixed value the prerendered text differs from the one the client prints. Pass the same `locale` on both sides to keep them identical.

### Helper text

Set `helperText` to render supporting text below the track, linked to the meter through `aria-describedby`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter
  labelText="Storage"
  value={420}
  max={1000}
  helperText="420 GB used of 1 TB"
/>
```

### Thresholds

Set `thresholds` with `warning` and `error` values, in the same units as `value`, to color the bar as usage grows.

#### Warning

The bar switches to the warning color once `value` reaches `thresholds.warning`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter
  labelText="Storage"
  value={820}
  max={1000}
  thresholds={{ warning: 800, error: 950 }}
  helperText="Approaching capacity"
/>
```

#### Error

The bar switches to the error color once `value` reaches `thresholds.error`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter
  labelText="Storage"
  value={960}
  max={1000}
  thresholds={{ warning: 800, error: 950 }}
  helperText="Over capacity soon"
/>
```

#### Threshold markers

Set `showThresholds` to `true` to draw a tick at each defined threshold. This also adds a visually hidden sentence describing the threshold amounts to the meter's `aria-describedby`, since the ticks themselves are decorative. Override that sentence with `thresholdsText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter
  labelText="Storage"
  value={820}
  max={1000}
  thresholds={{ warning: 800, error: 950 }}
  showThresholds
/>
```

### Status

Set `status` to override the derived status. An explicit `status` wins over `thresholds`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Meter labelText="Default" value={420} max={1000} status="default" />
  <Meter labelText="Success" value={420} max={1000} status="success" />
  <Meter labelText="Warning" value={420} max={1000} status="warning" />
  <Meter labelText="Error" value={420} max={1000} status="error" />
</Stack>
```

#### Status announcements

A move into warning or error is announced to assistive technologies. Set `warningText` and `errorText` to localize or customize the announced text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter
  labelText="Storage"
  value={960}
  max={1000}
  thresholds={{ warning: 800, error: 950 }}
  errorText="Critique"
/>
```

### Over capacity

When `value` exceeds `max`, the meter caps the bar and label at full width and switches to the error status.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter
  labelText="Storage"
  value={1200}
  max={1000}
  helperText="1.2 TB used of 1 TB"
/>
```

### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Meter labelText="Storage" value={420} max={1000} hideLabel />
```

### Reactive

Drive a meter's `value` from a bound `Slider` to see the thresholds respond as usage changes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Meter, Slider, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = 420;
  const max = 1000;
  const thresholds = { warning: 800, error: 950 };

  $: helperText = `${value} GB used of ${max} GB`;
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <Meter labelText="Storage" {value} {max} {thresholds} {helperText} />
  <Slider labelText="Usage (GB)" bind:value min={0} max={1200} step={10} />
</Stack>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Meter` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | Specify the current amount, in the same units as `max`. | `0` |
| `max` | `number` | Specify the capacity. | `100` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text. | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text. The label remains available to screen readers. | `false` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text, rendered below the track. | `""` |
| `valueText` | `string` | Specify the value text, right-aligned in the label row and used for `aria-valuetext`.<br />Format it yourself, e.g. "812 GB of 1 TB". | `""` |
| `warningText` | `string` | Specify the text announced and described when the status is `"warning"`. | `"Warning"` |
| `errorText` | `string` | Specify the text announced and described when the status is `"error"`. | `"Error"` |
| `valueRangeText` | `(value: number, max: number, locale?: string) => string` | Override the value text generated for `aria-valuetext` when `valueText` is not set.<br />Used only when the value is over capacity or the status is `"warning"` or `"error"`.<br />Receives `locale` as the third argument. | _undefined_ |
| `thresholds` | `MeterThresholds \| undefined` | Specify the warning and error thresholds, in the same units as `value`. | _undefined_ |
| `status` | `"default" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "error" \| undefined` | Override the derived status. When unset, the status is derived from `thresholds`. | _undefined_ |
| `showThresholds` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to draw a tick at each defined threshold. | `false` |
| `thresholdsText` | `(thresholds: MeterThresholds, locale?: string) => string` | Override the visually hidden threshold description, used when `showThresholds` is `true`.<br />Return an empty string to omit it. Receives `locale` as the second argument. | _undefined_ |
| `locale` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the locale used to format the numbers in the generated `aria-valuetext`<br />and threshold description. Defaults to the runtime locale. | _undefined_ |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | Specify the size of the meter. | `"md"` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the meter element.<br />The helper text, thresholds, and status ids derive from it as<br />`{id}-helper`, `{id}-thresholds`, and `{id}-status`. | `uniqueId()` |

#### `Meter` typedefs

```ts
type MeterThresholds = {
  warning?: number;
  error?: number;
};
```

#### `Meter` slots

| Slot            | Detail                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `labelChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `valueChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Meter` $$restProps

`Meter` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## Modal

### Modal vs ComposedModal

The modal is an all-in-one component configured through props, making it ideal for standard modal dialogs. For more complex layouts or fine-grained control, use [ComposedModal](/components/ComposedModal) instead.

### Basic

Display a modal dialog with a header, content area, and footer. Use primary and secondary actions for confirmations or input. Neither button closes the modal automatically. Wire up `on:submit` and `on:click:button--secondary` to set `open` to `false` yourself; see [Events](#events).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Create database</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Create database"
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:open
  on:close
  on:submit
>
  <p>Create a new Cloudant database in the US South region.</p>
</Modal>
```

### Focus

Control how focus moves when the modal opens, and override the default target when needed.

#### Focus behavior

When the modal opens, focus is set using the following priority:

1. The element matching `selectorPrimaryFocus` (default: `[data-modal-primary-focus]`)
2. The first input, textarea, or select (for transactional modals with form fields)
3. The primary action button (for confirmation modals), or the cancel button (for destructive modals with `danger={true}`)
4. The close button (for passive modals or modals without a primary button)

After closing the modal, focus is returned to the element that triggered the modal.

The close button shows `iconDescription` in a tooltip on hover and focus. When the modal opens with focus on the close button, the tooltip stays closed until the next hover or focus. While the tooltip shows, <kbd>Escape</kbd> hides it first. The next <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes the modal.

#### Custom focus

Use `selectorPrimaryFocus` to override the default and target a specific element when the automatic first-input focus is not desired. Set `selectorPrimaryFocus` to `null` to skip initial focus when you move focus yourself, for example in `on:transitionend`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal, Stack, TextInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Create database</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Create database"
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  selectorPrimaryFocus="#advanced-options"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:open
  on:close
  on:submit
>
  <Stack gap={3}>
    <p>Create a new Cloudant database in the US South region.</p>
    <TextInput
      id="db-name"
      labelText="Database name"
      placeholder="Enter database name..."
    />
    <Button id="advanced-options" kind="ghost" size="small">
      Advanced options
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</Modal>
```

#### Custom overlays

`Modal` and `ComposedModal` already keep focus inside the dialog. For an overlay that does not build on them, call the `trapFocus` helper from a `keydown` handler. It is a helper, not an action: pass the `container` element and the keyboard `event`, and focus loops through the tabbable elements inside.

The helper always calls `event.preventDefault()`, so call it only when `event.key` is `"Tab"`. Calling it for other keys blocks their default behavior. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>Shift+Tab</kbd> in the dialog to see focus loop.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Button,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
    trapFocus,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let container;

  function handleKeydown(event) {
    if (event.key === "Tab") trapFocus({ container, event });
    if (event.key === "Escape") open = false;
  }
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Invite teammate</Button>

{#if open}
  <Box
    bind:ref={container}
    role="dialog"
    aria-label="Invite teammate"
    tabindex="-1"
    on:keydown={handleKeydown}
    marginTop={5}
    padding={5}
    maxWidth="20rem"
    fill="layer-01"
  >
    <Stack gap={5}>
      <TextInput labelText="Email" placeholder="ada@acme-corp.com" />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={3}>
        <Button size="small" on:click={() => (open = false)}>Send invite</Button
        >
        <Button size="small" kind="ghost" on:click={() => (open = false)}>
          Cancel
        </Button>
      </Stack>
    </Stack>
  </Box>
{/if}
```

### Alert mode

Set `alert` to `true` to mark the modal as time-sensitive or requiring immediate attention. This changes the ARIA `role` from `"dialog"` to `"alertdialog"` (or `"alert"` when combined with `passiveModal`), which prompts assistive technology to announce the modal as soon as it opens. When not `passiveModal`, the body content is also linked with `aria-describedby` so screen readers include it in the announcement.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button kind="danger" on:click={() => (open = true)}>Delete all</Button>

<Modal
  alert
  danger
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Delete all instances"
  primaryButtonText="Delete"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
>
  <p>This is a permanent action and cannot be undone.</p>
</Modal>
```

### Variants

Change the modal's tone and purpose.

#### Danger

Display critical actions or destructive operations with the danger variant. This style emphasizes the severity of the action.

By default, the cancel button receives focus instead of the critical button to prevent accidental destructive actions.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button kind="danger" on:click={() => (open = true)}>Delete all</Button>

<Modal
  danger
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Delete all instances"
  primaryButtonText="Delete"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:open
  on:close
  on:submit
>
  <p>This is a permanent action and cannot be undone.</p>
</Modal>
```

#### Passive

Create a non-interactive modal for displaying information. This variant lacks action buttons and focuses on content presentation. Since there is no primary button, the close button will receive focus when the modal opens. A passive modal closes on an outside click; see [Outside click](#outside-click).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button kind="tertiary" on:click={() => (open = true)}>Learn more</Button>

<Modal passiveModal bind:open modalHeading="IBM Cloudant" on:open on:close>
  <p>
    IBM Cloudant is a distributed, secure database with global availability and
    zero vendor lock-in used to build web and mobile apps at scale.
  </p>
</Modal>
```

### Content

Customize the modal's heading, label, and body content.

#### Build the content on first open

Set `lazy` to build the body and footer the first time the modal opens, then keep them. A closed modal is invisible but still laid out, so this matters on pages with several modals or heavy content: a closed modal holding a 20-field form drops from 131 nodes to 8. ComposedModal takes the same prop.

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Set `lazy` on modals most visitors never open. | Their content costs nothing until it's needed. |
| Leave it off when you bind to or read the content before the first open. | That content doesn't exist yet. |
| Leave it off when the content must be in server-rendered markup. | It isn't rendered until the modal opens. |

#### Custom heading and label

Override the plain-text `modalHeading` and `modalLabel` with the `heading` and `labelChildren` slots when you need richer markup, such as a status tag next to the title.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal, Tag } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Create database</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Cloudant <Tag type="green" size="sm">Beta</Tag>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="heading">Create database</svelte:fragment>
  <p>Create a new Cloudant database in the US South region.</p>
</Modal>
```

#### With form submission

Connect the modal's primary button to a form with `formId`. This enables native form submission even though the button is outside the form element. Clicking the primary button or pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> will trigger the form's submit event.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal, Stack, TextInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let name = "";
  let email = "";

  function handleSubmit() {
    console.log("Form submitted:", { name, email });
    open = false;
  }
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Create account</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Create account"
  primaryButtonText="Submit"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  hasForm
  formId="account-form"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
>
  <form id="account-form" on:submit|preventDefault={handleSubmit}>
    <Stack gap={5}>
      <TextInput bind:value={name} labelText="Name" placeholder="Enter name" />
      <TextInput
        bind:value={email}
        labelText="Email"
        type="email"
        placeholder="Enter email"
      />
    </Stack>
  </form>
</Modal>
```

#### Has scrolling content

Enable vertical scrolling for modals with lengthy content. This ensures all content remains accessible while maintaining a reasonable modal height.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Create database</Button>

<Modal bind:open passiveModal modalHeading="About Cloudant" hasScrollingContent>
  <p>
    Cloudant is a fully managed, distributed database optimized for heavy
    workloads and fast-growing web and mobile apps, IBM Cloudant is available as
    an IBM Cloud® service with a 99.99% SLA.
  </p>
  <br />
  <p>
    The database elastically scales throughput and storage, and its API and
    replication protocols are compatible with Apache CouchDB for hybrid or
    multicloud architectures.
  </p>
</Modal>
```

#### Scrolling form

When `hasScrollingContent` is set, a gradient overlays the bottom of the body while more content remains below. Tabbing to a field near that edge scrolls it into view so it isn't hidden under the gradient. Use <kbd>Tab</kbd> to move through the fields; the fade recedes once you reach the last field.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal, Stack, TextInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Provision resource</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  size="sm"
  modalHeading="Provision resource"
  primaryButtonText="Provision"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  hasForm
  hasScrollingContent
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <TextInput labelText="Name" placeholder="Enter name" />
    <TextInput labelText="Email" type="email" placeholder="Enter email" />
    <TextInput labelText="Organization" placeholder="Enter organization" />
    <TextInput labelText="Region" placeholder="Enter region" />
    <TextInput labelText="Project" placeholder="Enter project" />
    <TextInput labelText="Resource name" placeholder="Enter resource name" />
    <TextInput labelText="Capacity" placeholder="Enter capacity" />
    <TextInput labelText="Notes" placeholder="Enter notes" />
  </Stack>
</Modal>
```

#### Full width

Set `fullWidth` to remove the modal body padding so content spans edge to edge. Use it for content that supplies its own layout, such as a table or fluid form.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, DataTable, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>View database instances</Button>

<Modal
  fullWidth
  bind:open
  modalLabel="Cloudant"
  modalHeading="Database instances"
  primaryButtonText="Add instance"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  hasScrollingContent
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
>
  <DataTable
    headers={[
      { key: "resource", value: "Resource" },
      { key: "region", value: "Region" },
      { key: "status", value: "Status" },
    ]}
    rows={[
      {
        id: "1",
        resource: "prod-db-01",
        region: "us-south",
        status:
          "Provisioning replicas across three availability zones to meet the 99.99% SLA.",
      },
      {
        id: "2",
        resource: "staging-db-02",
        region: "eu-de",
        status: "Backup snapshot completed; 30-day retention policy applied.",
      },
    ]}
  />
</Modal>
```

### AI label

Put an `AILabel` in the `decorator` slot to mark the modal's content as AI-generated. The label sits beside the close button, and the modal shows the AI surface.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Review forecast</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Usage forecast"
  primaryButtonText="Apply budget"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:submit={() => (open = false)}
>
  <AILabel slot="decorator">
    <p>Generated from 90 days of billing data across your workspace.</p>
  </AILabel>
  <p>
    Spend is projected to grow 12% next month. Raise the monthly budget to
    $4,800 to avoid overage alerts.
  </p>
</Modal>
```

### Buttons

Configure the footer actions.

#### Multiple secondary buttons

Add up to two secondary actions with `secondaryButtons`, which replaces the single secondary button text option. Each entry needs display text; set `kind` and `disabled` per button when actions should differ in weight or availability.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Create database</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Create database"
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtons={[
    { text: "Cancel", kind: "ghost" },
    { text: "Save draft", kind: "secondary" },
  ]}
  on:click:button--secondary={({ detail }) => {
    if (detail.text === "Cancel") open = false;
    if (detail.text === "Save draft") console.log("Save draft");
  }}
  on:open
  on:close
  on:submit
>
  <p>Create a new Cloudant database in the US South region.</p>
</Modal>
```

#### Custom footer with ActionSet

Modal builds its footer from `primaryButtonText` and `secondaryButtons` and has no footer slot. For a custom footer composed from `Button`s, use [ActionSet](/components/ActionSet) in [ComposedModal](/components/ComposedModal#custom-footer-with-actionset)'s `ModalFooter`.

#### Button with icon

Enhance modal buttons with icons for better visual context and clarity.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Send from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Send.svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Invite teammate</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Invite teammate"
  primaryButtonText="Send invitation"
  primaryButtonIcon={Send}
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
>
  <p>An email invitation with a link to join the workspace will be sent.</p>
</Modal>
```

#### Primary button loading

Set `primaryButtonLoading` while an async submit is in progress. The primary button shows an [InlineLoading](/components/InlineLoading) spinner, becomes non-interactive, and suppresses `submit` until loading finishes. The modal stays open.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let saving = false;

  function onSave() {
    saving = true;
    setTimeout(() => {
      saving = false;
      open = false;
    }, 2000);
  }
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Save changes</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Save changes"
  primaryButtonText="Save"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  primaryButtonLoading={saving}
  primaryButtonLoadingDescription="Saving..."
  on:click:button--secondary={() => {
    if (!saving) open = false;
  }}
  on:submit={onSave}
>
  <p>Save your changes to the Cloudant database configuration.</p>
</Modal>
```

#### Loading status

Set `loadingStatus` to show the progress of the primary action in its button: `"active"` while the work runs, then `"finished"` or `"error"`. Any status other than `"inactive"` disables the footer buttons and suppresses `submit`. After `"finished"`, the modal dispatches `loading:success` when the [InlineLoading](/components/InlineLoading) success delay ends. Close the modal there.

`primaryButtonLoading` is the same as `"active"`, except that the secondary buttons stay enabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Checkbox, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let failSave = false;
  let loadingStatus = "inactive";

  $: loadingDescription =
    loadingStatus === "error"
      ? "Save failed"
      : loadingStatus === "finished"
        ? "Saved"
        : "Saving...";

  async function save() {
    loadingStatus = "active";
    // For demo purposes only: simulate a network request.
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1500));
    loadingStatus = failSave ? "error" : "finished";
    if (failSave) {
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
      loadingStatus = "inactive";
    }
  }
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Save changes</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Save changes"
  primaryButtonText="Save"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  {loadingStatus}
  primaryButtonLoadingDescription={loadingDescription}
  preventCloseOnClickOutside={loadingStatus !== "inactive"}
  on:submit={save}
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:loading:success={() => {
    open = false;
    loadingStatus = "inactive";
  }}
>
  <p>Save your changes to the Cloudant database configuration.</p>
  <Checkbox labelText="Simulate a failed save" bind:checked={failSave} />
</Modal>
```

#### Secondary button loading

Secondary buttons support their own, independent loading state, useful when a secondary action (such as "Save as draft") is itself async. For `secondaryButtons`, set `loading` (and optionally `loadingDescription`) on the entry; for `secondaryButtonText`, use `secondaryButtonLoading` and `secondaryButtonLoadingDescription`. A loading secondary button shows its own `InlineLoading` spinner and becomes non-interactive, independent of `primaryButtonLoading`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let savingDraft = false;

  function onSaveDraft() {
    savingDraft = true;
    setTimeout(() => {
      savingDraft = false;
    }, 2000);
  }
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Save changes</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Save changes"
  primaryButtonText="Save"
  secondaryButtons={[
    {
      text: "Save as draft",
      kind: "secondary",
      loading: savingDraft,
      loadingDescription: "Saving...",
    },
  ]}
  on:click:button--secondary={({ detail }) => {
    if (detail.text === "Save as draft") onSaveDraft();
  }}
  on:submit={() => (open = false)}
>
  <p>Save your changes to the Cloudant database configuration.</p>
</Modal>
```

### Stacking modals

Show more than one modal at a time.

#### Multiple modals

Stack multiple modals for complex workflows. Each modal maintains its own state and focus management.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let openCreate = false;
  let openDelete = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (openCreate = true)}>Create database</Button>
<Button kind="danger-tertiary" on:click={() => (openDelete = true)}>
  Delete database
</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open={openCreate}
  modalHeading="Create database"
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (openCreate = false)}
  on:open
  on:close
  on:submit
>
  <p>Create a new Cloudant database in the US South region.</p>
</Modal>

<Modal
  danger
  bind:open={openDelete}
  modalHeading="Delete database"
  primaryButtonText="Delete"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (openDelete = false)}
  on:open
  on:close
  on:submit
>
  <p>This is a permanent action and cannot be undone.</p>
</Modal>
```

#### Nested

Nest a modal inside another modal's content to stack a confirmation dialog on top of it. Each modal tracks its own `open` state, and <kbd>Escape</kbd> only closes the topmost (innermost) modal.

Wrap the nested modal in [Portal](/components/Portal) so it renders outside the outer modal's DOM. The outer modal's container has its own transform and `overflow: hidden`, so an unportaled nested modal would be sized and clipped to that container instead of covering the full screen.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal, Portal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let openConfirm = false;
</script>

<Button kind="danger-tertiary" on:click={() => (open = true)}>
  Delete database
</Button>

<Modal
  danger
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Delete database"
  primaryButtonText="Delete"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:submit={() => (openConfirm = true)}
>
  <p>This will permanently delete the database and all of its data.</p>

  <Portal>
    <Modal
      danger
      size="xs"
      bind:open={openConfirm}
      modalHeading="Are you absolutely sure?"
      primaryButtonText="Delete forever"
      secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
      on:click:button--secondary={() => (openConfirm = false)}
      on:submit={() => {
        openConfirm = false;
        open = false;
      }}
    >
      <p>This action cannot be undone.</p>
    </Modal>
  </Portal>
</Modal>
```

### Portal and dropdowns

Render the modal, or components inside it, outside normal DOM boundaries.

#### With portal

Wrap the modal in a portal to escape parent containers with `overflow: hidden` or z-index stacking contexts. This ensures the modal appears above all content and isn't clipped by parent boundaries.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Button, Modal, Portal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Box
  display="flex"
  direction="column"
  gap={5}
  overflow="hidden"
  position="relative"
  height="200px"
  border="subtle"
  borderStyle="dashed"
  padding={5}
>
  <p>
    This container hides overflowing content. Without a portal, the modal would
    be clipped.
  </p>
  <div>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Deploy build #4213</Button>
  </div>
  <Portal>
    <Modal
      bind:open
      modalHeading="Confirm deployment"
      primaryButtonText="Deploy"
      secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
      on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
    >
      <p>
        Deploying build #4213 to production cannot be undone. This modal is
        rendered in a portal, escaping the parent container's overflow
        constraints and ensuring it appears above all other content.
      </p>
    </Modal>
  </Portal>
</Box>
```

#### Modal with dropdowns

Components with menus, such as a combo box, dropdown, multi-select, date picker, or overflow menu, automatically render their menus in a floating portal when used inside a modal. The menus are positioned relative to their trigger and are not clipped by the modal's overflow or z-index stacking.

Set `portalMenu={false}` on these components to opt out. In this example, the modal itself is wrapped in a portal.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ComboBox,
    Dropdown,
    Modal,
    MultiSelect,
    Portal,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;

  const contactItems = [
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
    { id: "3", text: "Teams" },
    { id: "4", text: "Phone" },
  ];
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open modal</Button>

<Portal>
  <Modal
    bind:open
    size="sm"
    modalHeading="Add a contact"
    primaryButtonText="Add"
    secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
    on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  >
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <ComboBox
        labelText="Contact method"
        placeholder="Select contact method"
        items={contactItems}
      />
      <Dropdown
        labelText="Preferred channel"
        selectedId="0"
        items={contactItems}
      />
      <MultiSelect
        labelText="Notification methods"
        label="Select methods..."
        items={contactItems}
      />
    </Stack>
  </Modal>
</Portal>
```
