### Closing

Control how the modal can be dismissed.

#### Prevent default

The modal dispatches a cancelable `close` event. Call `e.preventDefault()` to keep the modal open. The event includes a `trigger` property indicating what triggered the close attempt: `"escape-key"` (<kbd>Escape</kbd>), `"outside-click"`, `"close-button"`, or `"programmatic"` (the `open` prop was set to `false` from outside the component, for example through `bind:open`, rather than through one of the modal's own dismiss controls).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, InlineNotification, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let hasUnsavedChanges = true;
  let showWarning = false;
</script>

<Button
  on:click={() => {
    open = true;
    hasUnsavedChanges = true;
    showWarning = false;
  }}
>
  Open modal with unsaved changes
</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Edit profile"
  primaryButtonText="Save"
  secondaryButtonText="Discard changes"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => {
    hasUnsavedChanges = false;
    open = false;
  }}
  on:close={(e) => {
    console.log("Close triggered by:", e.detail.trigger);
    if (hasUnsavedChanges) {
      e.preventDefault();
      showWarning = true;
    }
  }}
  on:submit={() => {
    hasUnsavedChanges = false;
    open = false;
  }}
>
  {#if showWarning}
    <InlineNotification
      kind="warning"
      title="Unsaved changes"
      subtitle="Please save or discard your changes before closing."
      hideCloseButton
    />
  {/if}
  <p>You have unsaved changes. Click "Save" to apply them.</p>
</Modal>
```

#### Outside click

A modal with actions stays open when the user clicks outside it, so the user has to choose an action. A passive modal closes. This matches Carbon v11.

Set `preventCloseOnClickOutside` to `true` to keep a passive modal open, for example while it shows a value the user must copy. Set it to `false` to close a modal with actions on an outside click. Carbon advises against this, since the user can lose their input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, CodeSnippet, Modal, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Create API key</Button>

<Modal
  passiveModal
  preventCloseOnClickOutside
  bind:open
  modalHeading="API key created"
  on:open
  on:close
>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <p>
      Copy this key now. You can't view it again after you close this dialog.
    </p>
    <CodeSnippet code="cld_live_8f3a2c91e4b7d605" />
  </Stack>
</Modal>
```

#### Hide close button

Set `hideCloseButton` to `true` to remove the header close button. Use this for forced-choice dialogs such as auth walls or terms acceptance. Always provide an alternative dismiss path, typically footer actions. A modal with actions already stays open on an outside click. <kbd>Escape</kbd> still closes the modal unless you cancel the `close` event.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Review terms</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  hideCloseButton
  modalHeading="Accept terms of use"
  primaryButtonText="Accept"
  secondaryButtonText="Decline"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:submit={() => (open = false)}
>
  <p>
    You must accept or decline the terms. The header close button is hidden, so
    use the footer actions to leave this dialog.
  </p>
</Modal>
```

### Events

Modal dispatches events for its lifecycle and button interactions. Only the close button, <kbd>Escape</kbd>, and an outside click on a passive modal close the modal automatically. See [Closing](#closing) above. Every other action leaves `open` untouched; handle the event and set `open` to `false` yourself when the action should dismiss the dialog.

#### Open

Listen for `on:open` to know when `open` becomes `true`. It fires before the modal is visible and before focus moves into it. To run code after focus has moved, listen for `on:transitionend` and check `event.detail.open`.

```svelte
<Modal bind:open on:open={() => console.log("opened")}>
```

#### Submit and button clicks

The primary button dispatches both `submit` and `click:button--primary` when clicked. Secondary buttons dispatch `click:button--secondary` with the button's `text`.

```svelte
<Modal
  bind:open
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:submit={() => (open = false)}
>
```

When `shouldSubmitOnEnter` is `true` (the default), pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> also dispatches `submit` and `click:button--primary`, unless focus is on a button, link, textarea, select, or contenteditable element. Set `shouldSubmitOnEnter` to `false` to disable this.

#### Transition end

Listen for `on:transitionend` to know when the modal's open or close animation finishes. `event.detail.open` reflects the modal's state at the end of the transition.

```svelte
<Modal
  bind:open
  on:transitionend={(e) => console.log("open:", e.detail.open)}
>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Modal` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the modal. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the top-level HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| undefined` | Set the size of the modal.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"`, the default width. | _undefined_ |
| `danger` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the danger variant | `false` |
| `alert` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable alert mode | `false` |
| `passiveModal` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the passive variant | `false` |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the modal body padding so content spans edge to edge | `false` |
| `modalHeading` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the modal heading. | _undefined_ |
| `modalLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the modal label.<br />Alternatively, use the "labelChildren" slot. | _undefined_ |
| `modalAriaLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the ARIA label for the modal. | _undefined_ |
| `iconDescription` | `string` | Specify the label of the close button.<br />It names the button and shows in its tooltip. | `"Close the modal"` |
| `hasForm` | `boolean` | Set to `true` if the modal contains form elements | `false` |
| `formId` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the ID of a form element to associate with the primary button.<br />This enables the primary button to submit the form from outside the form element. | _undefined_ |
| `hasScrollingContent` | `boolean` | Set to `true` if the modal contains scrolling content | `false` |
| `primaryButtonText` | `string` | Specify the primary button text | `""` |
| `primaryButtonDisabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the primary button | `false` |
| `primaryButtonLoading` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to show a loading state on the primary button.<br />While loading, the button is non-interactive and submit is suppressed.<br />Same as `loadingStatus="active"`, except that the secondary buttons<br />stay enabled. `loadingStatus` wins when it is not `"inactive"`. | `false` |
| `loadingStatus` | `"inactive" \| "active" \| "finished" \| "error"` | Set the loading status of the footer.<br />Any status other than `"inactive"` shows `InlineLoading` with that<br />status in the primary button, disables the footer buttons, and<br />suppresses submit. `"finished"` dispatches `loading:success` after the<br />success delay. | `"inactive"` |
| `primaryButtonLoadingDescription` | `string` | Specify the description for the primary button loading state.<br />Passed to `InlineLoading` as `description`. | `"Loading"` |
| `primaryButtonLoadingIconDescription` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the description for the primary button loading icon.<br />Passed to `InlineLoading` as `iconDescription`. | _undefined_ |
| `primaryButtonIcon` | `Icon \| undefined` | Specify the primary button icon. | _undefined_ |
| `shouldSubmitOnEnter` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the "submit" and "click:button--primary" events<br />to be dispatched when pressing "Enter". | `true` |
| `secondaryButtonText` | `string` | Specify the secondary button text | `""` |
| `secondaryButtonLoading` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to show a loading state on the secondary button.<br />Only applies to the `secondaryButtonText` path (not `secondaryButtons`).<br />While loading, the button is non-interactive. | `false` |
| `secondaryButtonLoadingDescription` | `string` | Specify the description for the secondary button loading state.<br />Passed to `InlineLoading` as `description`. | `"Loading"` |
| `secondaryButtons` | `ReadonlyArray<{ text: string; kind?: import("../Button/Button.svelte").ButtonProps["kind"]; disabled?: boolean; loading?: boolean; loadingDescription?: string }>` | One or two secondary buttons for the modal footer.<br />Supersedes `secondaryButtonText`. Each entry needs `text`; optional<br />`kind` (defaults to `"secondary"`), `disabled`, `loading`, and<br />`loadingDescription` (defaults to `"Loading"`) pass through to Button /<br />the loading state. With two entries plus a primary button, the footer<br />uses the three-button layout. | `[]` |
| `selectorPrimaryFocus` | `null \| string` | Specify a selector to be focused when opening the modal.<br />Set to `null` to skip initial focus and move focus yourself. | `"[data-modal-primary-focus]"` |
| `preventCloseOnClickOutside` | `boolean \| undefined` | Control whether clicking outside the modal closes it.<br />By default, a passive modal (`passiveModal`) closes and a modal with<br />actions stays open, as in Carbon v11.<br />Set to `true` to always keep the modal open on an outside click, or<br />`false` to always close it. | _undefined_ |
| `hideCloseButton` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to hide the header close button.<br />Provide an alternative dismiss path (footer actions or Escape). | `false` |
| `lazy` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to build the modal's content the first time it opens<br />instead of at mount, and keep it afterwards. A closed modal is still<br />laid out (it is only made invisible), so this saves its nodes on pages<br />that hold modals most visitors never open. Content is not in the DOM,<br />or in server-rendered markup, until then. | `false` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the top-level element | `uniqueId()` |

#### `Modal` slots

| Slot            | Detail                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`       | `Record<string, never>` |
| `decorator`     | `Record<string, never>` |
| `heading`       | `Record<string, never>` |
| `label`         | `Record<string, never>` |
| `labelChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Modal` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:keydown`    |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `Modal` dispatched events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on:click:button--primary` | `null` |  |
| `on:click:button--secondary` | `{<br />  text: string;<br />}` |  |
| `on:close` | `{<br />  trigger:<br />    \| "escape-key"<br />    \| "outside-click"<br />    \| "close-button"<br />    \| "programmatic";<br />}` |  |
| `on:loading:success` | `null` | Dispatched when `loadingStatus` is `"finished"`, after the `InlineLoading` success delay. |
| `on:open` | `null` |  |
| `on:submit` | `null` |  |
| `on:transitionend` | `{<br />  open: boolean;<br />}` |  |

#### `Modal` $$restProps

`Modal` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## MultiSelect

### Basic

Create a basic multi-select dropdown with three contact methods. Every item must have a unique id. By default, items are ordered alphabetically.

With the menu open, type a character to move the highlight to the next enabled item whose text starts with it; type several characters quickly to match a longer prefix. Typing highlights an item without selecting it. <kbd>PageUp</kbd> and <kbd>PageDown</kbd> move the highlight 10 items and stop at either end.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Content

Customize how items render and what supporting text appears around the field.

#### Custom slot

Override the default slot to customize item rendering. Use `let:item`, `let:index`, `let:selected`, and `let:highlighted` to access each item's data and its derived selected and highlighted state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  let:item
  let:index
  let:selected
  let:highlighted
>
  <div>
    <strong>{item.text}</strong>
  </div>
  <div>
    id: {item.id} - index: {index} - selected: {selected} - highlighted:
    {highlighted}
  </div>
</MultiSelect>

<style>
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item),
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item__option) {
    height: auto;
  }

  :global(.bx--checkbox-label-text) {
    display: block;
  }
</style>
```

#### Display text

Format the display text of items using the `itemToString` prop. This example appends the item ID in parentheses.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  itemToString={(item) => {
    return item.text + " (" + item.id + ")";
  }}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  sortItem={() => {}}
/>
```

#### Helper text

Add descriptive text below the multi-select using the `helperText` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  helperText="Select one or more contact methods"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  hideLabel
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Title attribute

Set `useTitleInItem` to `true` to add a native `title` attribute to each option, using the resolved `itemToString` text. This surfaces a browser tooltip when an item's label is truncated by the field width.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  useTitleInItem
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Checkbox values

`MultiSelect` mounts a hidden `<input>` for every selected item, derived from the current selection -- not from what's rendered in the dropdown. This keeps native form submission (`FormData`) working while the menu is closed, while filtering, and with `virtualize`.

By default, each hidden input uses `name={item.id}` and an empty `value`, matching the option checkbox's own defaults. Use `itemToInput` to override `name`/`value` per item, or set the `name` prop to submit every selected item's `id` under one shared name (`contact=0&contact=1`), unless `itemToInput` returns its own `name` or `value`. `name` is only used for the hidden inputs -- with `filterable`, the visible text input is a query box and is never included in `FormData`. A disabled multi-select is left out of the submission, like a disabled native control.

```js
itemToInput={(item) => {
  return {
    name: 'contact',
    value: item.id
  }
}}
```

The above function sets every hidden input's name to `contact` and its value to the respective item's id, so a submission looks like `contact=0&contact=1`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  itemToInput={(item) => ({ name: "contact", value: item.id })}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Form, MultiSelect, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form method="POST" action="?/subscribe">
  <MultiSelect
    name="contact"
    labelText="Contact"
    label="Select contact methods..."
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
    ]}
  />
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>
```

### Selection

Control which items start selected, how selections reorder the list, and how to read the resolved order.

#### Range selection

Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while clicking an item to select every item between it and the last item clicked. From the keyboard, hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> on the highlighted item. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> on macOS) with the menu open to select every enabled item, or to clear them if all are already selected. In a filterable multi-select, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> selects the filter text instead.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Regions"
  label="Select regions..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Frankfurt" },
    { id: "1", text: "London" },
    { id: "2", text: "Mumbai" },
    { id: "3", text: "Sydney" },
    { id: "4", text: "Tokyo" },
    { id: "5", text: "Toronto" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Initial selection

Pre-select items by passing an array of item IDs to `selectedIds`. This example pre-selects Slack and Email.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectedIds={["0", "1"]}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Selection feedback

Move selected items to the top of the list immediately after selection by setting `selectionFeedback` to `"top"`. The default behavior (top-after-reopen) only reorders items when the dropdown is reopened.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectionFeedback="top"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Maximum selection

Limit how many items a user can select by setting `maxSelectedItems`. Once the cap is reached, remaining unchecked items are disabled until a selection is cleared. Select-all is unavailable when a cap is set.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  maxSelectedItems={3}
  labelText="Preferences"
  label="Select preferences..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Email" },
    { id: "1", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "2", text: "SMS" },
    { id: "3", text: "Push" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Select all

Add a "select all" item by setting isSelectAll to true on an item. Clicking this item selects or deselects all non-disabled items. Disabled items are not affected by "select all".

The select-all option is styled differently from regular options (with a separator border) so it is visually distinct as a group toggle. Its checkbox supports an `indeterminate` state when only a subset of non-disabled items are selected; it shows checked when all are selected and unchecked when none are selected.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  labelText="Roles"
  placeholder="Filter roles..."
  items={[
    { id: "select-all", text: "All roles", isSelectAll: true },
    { id: "editor", text: "Editor" },
    { id: "owner", text: "Owner" },
    { id: "uploader", text: "Uploader" },
    { id: "reader", text: "Reader", disabled: true },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Sorted items

Bind to `sortedItems` to read the resolved list after sorting and selection feedback is applied. This avoids recomputing the order from items, selectedIds, and sortItem in consumer code.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let sortedItems = [];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectionFeedback="top"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  bind:sortedItems
/>

<pre>{JSON.stringify(sortedItems, null, 2)}</pre>
```

#### Locale

Set `locale` to a BCP 47 language tag to control how the default `sortItem` orders items. The default sort uses `Intl.Collator` with numeric-aware comparison, so locale affects the ordering of accented characters and numbers embedded in text. Only used when `sortItem` is left at its default -- a custom `sortItem` ignores `locale`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  locale="de-DE"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Öl" },
    { id: "1", text: "Apfel" },
    { id: "2", text: "Zebra" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### No alphabetical ordering

Set `sortItem` to `false` to keep items in their original `items` order, skipping the sort entirely. A no-op function (`sortItem="{() => {}}"`) still works the same way, but pays for a sort that changes nothing. Prefer `false`.

If `items` is already sorted the way you want (for example, sorted server-side), leaving `sortItem` at its default still works: sorting an already-sorted array costs about `n` comparisons rather than `n log n`, so it's nearly free.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  sortItem={false}
/>
```

#### Clear selection

Use `bind:this` to access the component instance and call `MultiSelect.clear()` to clear the selection. Pass `focus: false` in the options to prevent re-focusing the field.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let ref;
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  selectedIds={["0", "1"]}
  bind:this={ref}
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
<br />
<Button on:click={() => ref.clear()}>Clear</Button>
<Button on:click={() => ref.clear({ focus: false })}>Clear (no focus)</Button>
<Button on:click={() => ref.clear({ open: true })}>Clear (reopen menu)</Button>
```

#### Open on clear

By default, the menu stays as-is after clearing the selection (open if it was open, closed if it was closed).

Set `openOnClear` to `true` to open the menu after clearing the selection via the clear button or the Delete/Backspace shortcut. This lets users immediately browse all available items without needing to click the field again.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  openOnClear
  selectedIds={["0", "1"]}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Selected tags

Set `selectionDisplay` to `"tags"` to list each selected item as a tag below the field, so users can see and change the selection without opening the menu. Closing a tag deselects the item, the same as unchecking its option. The count in the field still clears everything at once.

The tags are a single tab stop after the field: the arrow keys move between them, and <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> removes the focused one. Tags follow the order of `items`, so they don't move as the menu re-sorts.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectionDisplay="tags"
  selectedIds={["us-east", "eu-de", "jp-tok"]}
  labelText="Regions"
  label="Select regions..."
  items={[
    { id: "us-east", text: "US East" },
    { id: "us-south", text: "US South" },
    { id: "eu-de", text: "EU Germany" },
    { id: "eu-gb", text: "EU United Kingdom" },
    { id: "jp-tok", text: "Tokyo" },
    { id: "au-syd", text: "Sydney" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Collapsed overflow

Tags wrap onto as many rows as they need. Set `tagOverflow` to `"collapse"` to keep them on one row, with the rest behind a "+N" button. The button opens the hidden tags in a popover, where they can still be removed.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box maxWidth="20rem">
  <MultiSelect
    selectionDisplay="tags"
    tagOverflow="collapse"
    selectedIds={["us-east", "us-south", "eu-de", "eu-gb", "jp-tok"]}
    labelText="Regions"
    label="Select regions..."
    items={[
      { id: "us-east", text: "US East" },
      { id: "us-south", text: "US South" },
      { id: "eu-de", text: "EU Germany" },
      { id: "eu-gb", text: "EU United Kingdom" },
      { id: "jp-tok", text: "Tokyo" },
      { id: "au-syd", text: "Sydney" },
    ]}
  />
</Box>
```

#### Custom tags

Use the `tag` slot to render each selected item's tag yourself, for example with a color `type` or an icon. Spread the slot's `props` onto the tag so closing it still deselects the item. Leave out `filter` to lock a tag in place.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Tag } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectionDisplay="tags"
  selectedIds={["critical", "low"]}
  labelText="Severity"
  label="Select severities..."
  items={[
    { id: "critical", text: "Critical" },
    { id: "high", text: "High" },
    { id: "low", text: "Low" },
  ]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="tag" let:item let:props>
    <Tag {...props} type={item.id === "critical" ? "red" : "gray"}
      >{item.text}</Tag
    >
  </svelte:fragment>
</MultiSelect>
```

In Svelte 5, pass a snippet instead: `{#snippet tag({ item, props })}`.

#### Your own tag set

For full control over where and how the selection shows, keep the default `selectionDisplay` and render a `TagSet` from the bound `selectedIds`. Closing a tag then needs its own handler to deselect the item.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack, Tag, TagSet } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    { id: "us-east", text: "US East" },
    { id: "us-south", text: "US South" },
    { id: "eu-de", text: "EU Germany" },
    { id: "jp-tok", text: "Tokyo" },
  ];

  let selectedIds = ["us-east", "eu-de"];

  $: selectedItems = items.filter((item) => selectedIds.includes(item.id));

  function handleTagClose({ detail }) {
    selectedIds = selectedIds.filter((id) => id !== detail.tag.value);
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <MultiSelect
    bind:selectedIds
    labelText="Regions"
    label="Select regions..."
    {items}
  />
  <TagSet navigation="roving" multiline on:close:tag={handleTagClose}>
    {#each selectedItems as item (item.id)}
      <Tag type="blue" value={item.id} filter>{item.text}</Tag>
    {/each}
  </TagSet>
</Stack>
```

### Groups

Set `group` on items to list them under a non-selectable header. Groups appear in the order they first occur in `items`, and sorting and selection feedback apply within each group. Items without a group are listed first, without a header.

Each group is exposed to screen readers as a group named by its label. The selection is still a flat list of ids.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Regions"
  label="Select regions..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Frankfurt", group: "Europe" },
    { id: "1", text: "Toronto", group: "Americas" },
    { id: "2", text: "London", group: "Europe" },
    { id: "3", text: "São Paulo", group: "Americas" },
    { id: "4", text: "Mumbai", group: "Asia Pacific" },
    { id: "5", text: "Tokyo", group: "Asia Pacific" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Custom header

Override the `group` slot to customize a header. Use `let:group` for the label and `let:items` for the group's items, each with a `checked` flag. The slot changes the visible header only; screen readers still announce the plain label.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: "Frankfurt", group: "Europe" },
    { id: "1", text: "Toronto", group: "Americas" },
    { id: "2", text: "London", group: "Europe" },
    { id: "3", text: "São Paulo", group: "Americas" },
    { id: "4", text: "Mumbai", group: "Asia Pacific" },
    { id: "5", text: "Tokyo", group: "Asia Pacific" },
  ];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Regions"
  label="Select regions..."
  {items}
  selectedIds={["0", "2", "5"]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="group" let:group let:items={groupItems}>
    {@const selectedCount = groupItems.filter((item) => item.checked).length}
    {group}
    ({selectedCount}/{groupItems.length})
  </svelte:fragment>
</MultiSelect>
```

#### Virtualized

Grouped lists virtualize like ungrouped ones, including automatically above 100 items. Headers scroll with the options and stay aligned across group boundaries. This example groups 3,000 nodes by region, and only the rows in view are rendered.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const regions = [
    "us-east-1",
    "us-west-2",
    "eu-west-1",
    "eu-central-1",
    "ap-northeast-1",
    "ap-southeast-2",
  ];

  const items = regions.flatMap((region) =>
    Array.from({ length: 500 }, (_, index) => ({
      id: `${region}-${index + 1}`,
      text: `${region}-node-${String(index + 1).padStart(3, "0")}`,
      group: region,
    })),
  );
</script>

<MultiSelect labelText="Nodes (3,000)" label="Select nodes..." {items} />
```

### Filterable

Enable filtering by setting `filterable` to `true`. This example includes a placeholder text for the filter input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  spellcheck="false"
  filterable
  labelText="Contact"
  placeholder="Filter contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Fuzzy filter

Provide a custom `filterItem` to override the default substring matching. This example reuses the built-in `fuzzyMatch` utility, exported from `carbon-components-svelte`, as the predicate. It matches items whose text contains the typed characters in order (for example, "pr" matches "Production" and "Preview"). Only the `matched` boolean is used here; the `score` and `indices` it also returns rank and highlight matches, as shown in [Highlight matches](#highlight-matches) below.

```svelte
<script>
  import { fuzzyMatch, MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  // Reuse the built-in fuzzy matcher as the filter predicate. Each typed
  // character must appear in order within the item text, so "pr" matches
  // "Production" and "Preview". Only the `matched` boolean is used here.
  const filterItem = (item, value) => fuzzyMatch(item.text, value).matched;
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  {filterItem}
  labelText="Environment"
  placeholder="Filter environments..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Production" },
    { id: "1", text: "Staging" },
    { id: "2", text: "Development" },
    { id: "3", text: "Sandbox" },
    { id: "4", text: "QA" },
    { id: "5", text: "Canary" },
    { id: "6", text: "Preview" },
    { id: "7", text: "Local" },
    { id: "8", text: "Demo" },
    { id: "9", text: "Integration" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Highlight matches

Besides `matched`, `fuzzyMatch` returns the `indices` of the characters that matched. Pass them to the `highlightSegments` utility (also exported from `carbon-components-svelte`) to split the item text into matched and unmatched runs, then bold the matched runs in the default slot. Bind `value` to read the filter text inside the slot.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    fuzzyMatch,
    highlightSegments,
    MultiSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: "Production" },
    { id: "1", text: "Staging" },
    { id: "2", text: "Development" },
    { id: "3", text: "Sandbox" },
    { id: "4", text: "QA" },
    { id: "5", text: "Canary" },
    { id: "6", text: "Preview" },
    { id: "7", text: "Local" },
    { id: "8", text: "Demo" },
    { id: "9", text: "Integration" },
  ];

  // One matcher drives filtering and highlighting. `filterItem` keeps the
  // items whose text fuzzy-matches the filter value; the default slot reuses
  // the same match and bolds the characters that matched. Bind `value` to read
  // the filter text inside the slot.
  const filterItem = (item, value) => fuzzyMatch(item.text, value).matched;
</script>

<MultiSelect
  bind:value
  filterable
  {filterItem}
  labelText="Environment"
  placeholder="Filter environments..."
  {items}
  let:item
>
  {#each highlightSegments(item.text, fuzzyMatch(item.text, value).indices) as segment}
    {#if segment.match}
      <strong>{segment.text}</strong>
    {:else}
      {segment.text}
    {/if}
  {/each}
</MultiSelect>
```

#### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to select the full filter value when the field receives focus. Only applies when `filterable` is `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectTextOnFocus
  filterable
  labelText="Contact"
  value="Slack"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Empty state

When the filter matches nothing, the menu shows "No results" in place of the options. Screen readers already hear the count from `filterResultsText`, so the message is hidden from them.

Set `emptyText` to change the message, or pass a function that builds it from the filter text. Set it to `""` to leave the menu empty instead.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  labelText="Contact"
  placeholder="Filter contact methods..."
  emptyText="No matching contact methods"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

Use the `empty` slot for richer content. `let:value` is the filter text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  labelText="Contact"
  placeholder="Filter contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="empty" let:value>
    No contact method named "{value}".
  </svelte:fragment>
</MultiSelect>
```

Without `filterable`, an empty `items` list shows "No options" instead, such as before async options arrive. `loading` holds the message back, and screen readers hear it through the multi-select's live region.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  emptyText="No contact methods yet"
  items={[]}
/>
```

#### Async

For async (for example, server-side) filtering, bind to `value` and replace `items` with the server's results. Set `filterItem` to return `true` so the menu shows every result as sent. This example simulates the request with a debounced value change.

Keep the selected options in `items`. An option missing from `items` has no tag.

Set `loading` to `true` while a request is in flight. The menu shows a loading row after the options, is marked busy for screen readers, and holds back the empty state until the results arrive.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import { onMount } from "svelte";

  let items = [];
  let selected = [];
  let loading = false;
  let timeoutId;
  let inputValue = "";

  // Simulate a server that filters by the query.
  async function fetchItems(query) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 300));

    const allItems = [
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "PagerDuty" },
      { id: "3", text: "Webhook" },
      { id: "4", text: "Microsoft Teams" },
      { id: "5", text: "SMS" },
      { id: "6", text: "Opsgenie" },
      { id: "7", text: "ServiceNow" },
      { id: "8", text: "VictorOps" },
      { id: "9", text: "Zoom" },
    ];

    return allItems.filter((item) =>
      item.text.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()),
    );
  }

  // Keep the selected options in `items`, so their tags survive a search.
  function withSelected(results) {
    const selectedIds = new Set(selected.map((item) => item.id));
    return [
      ...selected,
      ...results.filter((item) => !selectedIds.has(item.id)),
    ];
  }

  onMount(() => () => clearTimeout(timeoutId));

  $: {
    clearTimeout(timeoutId);
    // Debounce input value changes.
    timeoutId = setTimeout(async () => {
      const query = inputValue;
      loading = true;
      const results = await fetchItems(query);
      // A newer search has started; let it report instead.
      if (query !== inputValue) return;
      items = withSelected(results);
      loading = false;
    }, 150);
  }
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  filterItem={() => true}
  labelText="Alert channels"
  placeholder="Type to search..."
  bind:value={inputValue}
  {items}
  {loading}
  emptyText={(value) => `No channels match "${value}"`}
  on:select={(e) => (selected = e.detail.selected)}
/>
```

### Multiple multi-selects

Manage multiple dropdowns in a form with coordinated state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ];

  let multiselect1_selectedIds = ["0"];
  let multiselect2_selectedIds = ["1", "2"];

  const formatSelected = (i) =>
    i.length === 0
      ? "N/A"
      : i.map((id) => items.find((item) => item.id === id).text).join(", ");

  $: primary = formatSelected(multiselect1_selectedIds);
  $: secondary = formatSelected(multiselect2_selectedIds);
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <MultiSelect
    labelText="Primary contact"
    helperText="Primary: {primary}"
    bind:selectedIds={multiselect1_selectedIds}
    label="Select contact methods..."
    {items}
  />
  <MultiSelect
    labelText="Secondary contact"
    helperText="Secondary: {secondary}"
    bind:selectedIds={multiselect2_selectedIds}
    label="Select contact methods..."
    {items}
  />
</Stack>
```

### Events

Respond to selection, clearing, and the menu opening and closing.

#### Select

Use `on:select` to listen for selection changes. `event.detail` includes `selectedIds`, `selected` (the checked items), and `unselected` (the rest). A [select-all](#select-all) item is left out of all three. It fires when the user toggles an option, selects a [range](#range-selection) with <kbd>Shift</kbd>, selects all with the select-all item or <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd>, or clears the selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  on:select={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
/>
```

#### Clear

Use `on:clear` to listen for the clear ("x") button that appears once there is a selection, activated by click or by keyboard. `event.detail` is the originating `MouseEvent` or `KeyboardEvent`. Clearing with <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd>, or calling [`clear()`](#clear-selection), does not dispatch `clear`. All three still dispatch `select`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectedIds={["0", "1"]}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  on:clear={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
/>
```

#### Open

Use `on:open` to know when the menu opens and why. `event.detail.trigger` is `"click"`, `"keydown"`, `"input"` (typing a filter opened it), or `"programmatic"` when `open` is set from outside, such as through `bind:open`. It fires once per open, after the menu renders, and not for a multi-select rendered already open.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  on:open={(e) => console.log(e.detail.trigger)}
/>
```

#### Close

Use `on:close` to know when the menu is dismissed and why. `event.detail.trigger` is `"escape-key"` (<kbd>Escape</kbd>, or <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> on an open menu) or `"outside-click"` (a click or focus outside the multi-select and its menu). Selecting an option keeps the menu open. Clicking the field to collapse it, or pressing <kbd>Tab</kbd>, closes the menu without dispatching `close`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  on:close={(e) => console.log(e.detail.trigger)}
/>
```

### Loading

Set `loading` to `true` to show a loading row after the options, such as while fetching more items. The menu is marked busy for screen readers, the options stay selectable, and the [empty state](#empty-state) is held back.

Set `loadingText` to change the row's text.

Set `loadingDelay` to wait a number of milliseconds after `loading` becomes `true` before showing the loading row. Work that finishes within the delay shows no row. Once shown, the row stays for at least 500 ms so it does not flash. The menu is marked busy, and the empty state held back, as soon as `loading` is `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  loading
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Virtualization

Virtualization renders only the items currently visible in the viewport, improving performance for large lists. By default, the multi-select virtualizes lists with more than 100 items.

#### Large lists

In the example below, 10,000 items are provided to the multi-select but only 11 items (8 visible items + 3 overscan items) are rendered in the DOM.

Set `virtualize={false}` to explicitly disable virtualization, even for large lists. Or, customize the threshold at which virtualization activates. See [Custom threshold](#custom-threshold).

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Account ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedIds = [1000];
  $: selectedItems = items.filter((item) => selectedIds.includes(item.id));
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <MultiSelect
    filterable
    labelText="Customer accounts (10,000)"
    {items}
    bind:selectedIds
  />
  <div>
    <strong>Selected:</strong>
    {selectedItems.map((item) => item.text).join(", ")}
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Load more

`scrollend` fires when the menu is scrolled near the bottom so you can append the next page of `items`. Same pattern as [ComboBox load more](/components/ComboBox#load-more): handle `on:scrollend`, keep prior items visible while loading, and set `loading` while the next page is in flight to show a loading row after them. The event is a near-bottom load-more signal, not the browser's native `scrollend`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const PAGE_SIZE = 40;
  const TOTAL = 200;

  let items = [];
  let loading = false;
  let hasMore = true;

  function makePage(offset) {
    return Array.from({ length: PAGE_SIZE }, (_, i) => {
      const n = offset + i;
      return { id: String(n), text: `Contact #${n + 1}` };
    }).filter((item) => Number(item.id) < TOTAL);
  }

  async function loadMore() {
    if (loading || !hasMore) return;
    loading = true;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 400));
    const next = makePage(items.length);
    items = [...items, ...next];
    hasMore = items.length < TOTAL;
    loading = false;
  }

  loadMore();
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <MultiSelect
    labelText="Load more on scroll"
    placeholder="Open and scroll to the bottom..."
    {items}
    virtualize={{ containerHeight: 240, threshold: 1 }}
    {loading}
    loadingText="Loading more..."
    on:scrollend={loadMore}
  />
  {#if !hasMore}
    <p>Loaded all {TOTAL} items.</p>
  {:else}
    <p>
      {items.length}
      of {TOTAL} loaded. Scroll the menu to fetch the next page.
    </p>
  {/if}
</Stack>
```

#### Custom overscan

Overscanning is the process of rendering extra items above and below the viewport to ensure smooth scrolling. The default overscan value is 3.

Specify a custom value for `overscan` to control how many extra items are rendered above/below the viewport for smoother scrolling.

During very fast scrolling, higher overscan values may cause more flickering due to increased DOM updates. For fast-scrolling scenarios, use a lower overscan value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `SKU-${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedIds = [1000];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  virtualize={{ overscan: 100 }}
  filterable
  labelText="High overscan (10,000 items, overscan: 100)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedIds
/>
```

#### Fast scrolling

During a scroll faster than the menu can render, such as a quick drag of the scrollbar, the options can briefly disappear. Set `optimizeFastScroll: true` to keep the options already rendered in view until the new ones arrive.

The options then follow the scroll a frame behind, and pause while the page is busy running scripts. Leave it off when the menu sits on a page that often does heavy work.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `SKU-${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedIds = [1000];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  virtualize={{ optimizeFastScroll: true }}
  filterable
  labelText="Optimized for fast scrolling (10,000 items)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedIds
/>
```

#### Custom threshold

The threshold is the minimum number of items required before virtualization activates. The default threshold value is 100, meaning lists with fewer than 100 items will not be virtualized and all items will be rendered normally.

Specify a custom value for `threshold` to control when virtualization activates. Below the threshold, all items are rendered normally without virtualization.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 100 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Team ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedIds = [50];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  virtualize={{ threshold: 200 }}
  filterable
  labelText="Custom threshold (threshold: 200)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedIds
/>
```

#### Custom item height

By default, item height matches the menu row for each size: 24px (xs), 32px (sm), 40px (md), 48px (lg, xl). Set `itemHeight` when custom slots change row height.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Permission scope ${i + 1}`,
    description: `Grants access to resource group ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedIds = [1000];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  virtualize={{ itemHeight: 60 }}
  filterable
  labelText="Custom item height (60px)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedIds
  let:item
>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <strong>{item.text}</strong>
    <span>{item.description}</span>
  </Stack>
</MultiSelect>

<style>
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item),
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item__option) {
    height: auto;
  }

  :global(.bx--checkbox-label-text) {
    display: block;
  }
</style>
```

### Wrapped options

Option labels are truncated to one line. At a 320px viewport, that hides text and can leave two options looking identical, a WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow failure.

Set `wrapOptions` to let a label take as many lines as it needs. Lines break between words, and mid-word only when a word is too long to fit a line by itself. Default slot markup wraps with the label: a [highlighted match](#highlight-matches) stays marked across the break it is split by.

It defaults to `false` because wrapping changes option heights.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const roles = [
    "Chief Accessibility Officer for Regional Operations and Strategic Partnerships",
    "Deputy Director of Interdepartmental Communications and Outreach",
  ];

  const items = [
    { id: "all", text: "Select every role listed below", isSelectAll: true },
    { id: "0", text: roles[0] },
    { id: "1", text: roles[1] },
    { id: "2", text: "Analyst" },
  ];

  // Past the count at which a list is windowed, so only the options on screen
  // are rendered. `wrapOptions` turns on measured row heights by itself, so
  // offsets follow the heights the wrapped options actually take.
  const manyItems = Array.from({ length: 300 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: String(i),
    text: `${i + 1}. ${roles[i % 2]}`,
  }));

  // Input order, so the "select all" row stays in front of the roles it
  // toggles rather than sorting into the middle of them.
  const sortItem = () => 0;
</script>

<Box display="flex" direction="column" gap={6} maxWidth="20rem">
  <MultiSelect
    labelText="Truncated (default)"
    selectedIds={["2"]}
    {sortItem}
    {items}
  />
  <MultiSelect
    wrapOptions
    labelText="Wrapped"
    selectedIds={["2"]}
    {sortItem}
    {items}
  />
  <MultiSelect
    wrapOptions
    filterable
    labelText="Wrapped (windowed, 300 items)"
    placeholder="Filter..."
    {sortItem}
    items={manyItems}
  />
</Box>
```

### Portal menu

A dropdown menu that a container would cut off, such as a box with `overflow: hidden` or a scroll area, opens in a floating portal. The container in the example below hides its overflow, so the menu moves to a portal when it opens. Inside a [Modal](/components/Modal#modal-with-dropdowns), the menu always opens in a portal.

Set `portalMenu` to `true` to always render the menu in a portal, for example to escape a z-index stacking context. Set it to `false` to keep the menu in place. A portalled menu leaves its container in the DOM, so CSS that targets the menu as a descendant of the container does not match it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box
  display="flex"
  direction="column"
  gap={4}
  overflow="hidden"
  border="subtle"
  borderStyle="dashed"
  padding={5}
  maxHeight="120px"
>
  <div>
    This container has hidden overflow. The menu would not fit, so it opens in a
    portal.
  </div>
  <MultiSelect
    labelText="Notification methods"
    label="Select methods..."
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
    ]}
  />
</Box>
```

### States

#### Invalid

Indicate an invalid selection by setting `invalid` to `true`. This example shows a required field error.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  invalid
  invalidText="A contact method is required"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Invalid (filterable)

Combine `filterable` and `invalid` to show validation errors on a filterable multi-select.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  invalid
  invalidText="A contact method is required"
  labelText="Contact"
  placeholder="Filter contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Invalid (filterable with selection)

The invalid outline wraps the whole field, selection tag included.

<script>

<MultiSelect

  invalid
  invalidText="Choose at least two contact methods"
  labelText="Contact"

  ]}
/>

#### Read-only

Set `readonly` to `true` to display non-editable values. The menu can still be opened and navigated to review the selected values, but the selection cannot be changed or cleared.

```svelte

</script>

<MultiSelect
  readonly
  selectedIds={["0", "1"]}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Required

Set `required` to keep a surrounding form from submitting until at least one item is selected. Disabled items do not count, as they are left out of the submission. The field is marked required for screen readers.

When a submit is blocked, the field shows its invalid state instead of the browser's error bubble, and the first invalid field takes focus. Calling `checkValidity()` from code shows nothing. The state clears once the field has a value or the form resets.

Set `requiredInvalidText` to change the message, which defaults to "Select at least one item". Your own `invalid` and `invalidText` take precedence.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Form, MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let submitted = false;
</script>

<Form
  on:submit={(e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    submitted = true;
  }}
>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <MultiSelect
      required
      labelText="Contact"
      label="Select contact methods"
      items={[
        { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
        { id: "1", text: "Email" },
        { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
      ]}
      on:select={() => (submitted = false)}
    />
    <div>
      <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
    </div>
    {#if submitted}
      <p>Submitted.</p>
    {/if}
  </Stack>
</Form>
```

### Skeleton

Show a loading state with `MultiSelectSkeleton`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelectSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";

<MultiSelectSkeleton />

Virtualization renders only the items currently visible in the viewport, improving performance for large lists.<br /><br />By default, virtualization is automatically enabled for lists with more than 100 items.<br /><br />Set `virtualize={false}` to explicitly disable virtualization, even for large lists.<br /><br />Set `virtualize={true}` to explicitly enable virtualization with default settings.<br /><br />Provide an object to customize virtualization behavior:<br />- `itemHeight` (default: size-based, or 64px for fluid unless `condensed`): Height of each item in pixels. Override when custom slots change row height. Under `wrapOptions`, heights are measured from the rendered options and this serves as the starting estimate for ones not yet measured.<br />- `containerHeight` (default: 300): The maximum height in pixels of the dropdown container.<br />- `overscan` (default: 3): The number of extra items to render above and below the viewport for smoother scrolling. Higher values may cause more flickering during very fast scrolling.<br />- `threshold` (default: 100): The minimum number of items required before virtualization activates. Lists with fewer items will render all items normally without virtualization.<br />- `maxItems` (default: undefined): The maximum number of items to render. When undefined, all visible items are rendered.<br />- `optimizeFastScroll` (default: false): Keep the rendered options in view during very fast scrolling, such as a scrollbar drag, instead of showing blank space until new options render. | `loadingText` | `string` | Specify the text of the loading row | `"Loading..."` |
| `loadingDelay` | `number` | Wait this many milliseconds after `loading` turns `true` before showing<br />the loading row. The menu sets `aria-busy` and<br />holds back the empty state as soon as `loading` is `true`.<br />Set to `0` to show it at once. | `0` |
| `wrapOptions` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to let an option's label wrap onto as many lines as it needs<br />instead of being truncated with an ellipsis. | `false` |
| `portalMenu` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to always render the menu in a portal, or `false` to<br />keep it in place. Left unset, the menu moves to a portal inside a<br />Modal, or when a box around it (`overflow` other than `visible`)<br />would cut it off. | _undefined_ |

#### `MultiSelect` typedefs

```ts
type MultiSelectItemText = string;

type MultiSelectItem<Id = any> = {
  id: Id;
  text: MultiSelectItemText;
  /** Whether the item is disabled */
  disabled?: boolean;
  /** Whether this item acts as a "select all" toggle */
  isSelectAll?: boolean;
  /** Group label. Items sharing a label render together under a non-selectable header, groups in order of first appearance and `sortItem` sorting within each group. */
  group?: string;
};
```
