## NotificationQueue

### Basic

Use `bind:this` to get a queue reference, then call `add()` to show notifications. The queue uses underlying [ToastNotification](ToastNotification) components, manages positioning, and removes notifications when they time out or are closed.

While the pointer or focus is in the queue, every toast's timer pauses, so users can finish reading. Each timer then resumes with the time it had left.

The toasts also stay in place while the pointer is in the queue. A closed toast leaves an empty space, so the next close button does not slide under the pointer. A new toast appears at the end away from the screen edge, and a full queue drops its oldest toast only when the pointer and focus leave.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "success",
        title: "Deployment succeeded",
        subtitle: "Build #482 deployed to production.",
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Show success
  </Button>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "error",
        title: "API rate limit exceeded",
        subtitle: "Requests are being throttled. Try again in 60 seconds.",
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Show error
  </Button>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Scheduled maintenance",
        subtitle: "Maintenance window begins tonight at 10:00 PM UTC.",
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Show info
  </Button>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "warning",
        title: "Certificate expiring soon",
        subtitle: "TLS certificate for api.example.com expires in 7 days.",
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Show warning
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

### Positioning

Configure where the queue and its notifications render on screen.

#### Screen position

Configure queue position with the `position` prop. Supported values are `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right` (default), `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, and `bottom-right`.

The top-right position assumes usage of the [UIShell](/components/UIShell) component. Use left or center placements when a side panel would otherwise cover toasts. Customize placement with [offset props](#custom-offsets).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let topRightQueue;
  let topCenterQueue;
  let topLeftQueue;
  let bottomRightQueue;
  let bottomCenterQueue;
  let bottomLeftQueue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={topRightQueue} position="top-right" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={topCenterQueue} position="top-center" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={topLeftQueue} position="top-left" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={bottomRightQueue} position="bottom-right" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={bottomCenterQueue} position="bottom-center" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={bottomLeftQueue} position="bottom-left" />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      topLeftQueue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Top left",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add top left
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      topCenterQueue.add({
        kind: "success",
        title: "Top center",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add top center
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      topRightQueue.add({
        kind: "success",
        title: "Top right",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add top right
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
<br />
<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      bottomLeftQueue.add({
        kind: "warning",
        title: "Bottom left",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add bottom left
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      bottomCenterQueue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Bottom center",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add bottom center
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      bottomRightQueue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Bottom right",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add bottom right
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

#### Custom offsets

Customize queue placement with `offsetTop`, `offsetBottom`, `offsetLeft`, and `offsetRight`. Useful for positioning notifications below headers or adjusting spacing.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, NotificationQueue } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue
  bind:this={queue}
  position="top-right"
  offsetTop="5rem"
  offsetRight="2rem"
/>

<Button
  on:click={() => {
    queue.add({
      kind: "success",
      title: "Custom offset",
    });
  }}
>
  Add notification
</Button>
```

#### Z-index

Specify the stacking order of the queue with `zIndex`. Defaults to `9000`, matching the z-index used by [Modal](/components/Modal), so notifications render above dialog content by default.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NotificationQueue } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NotificationQueue zIndex={2000} />
```

Lower the value if the queue should render behind other fixed UI instead.

### Managing notifications

The queue tracks notifications by id, so `add`, `update`, `remove`, and the `maxNotifications` limit all key off the same identifier.

Since each queued notification renders as a [ToastNotification](/components/ToastNotification), `add` also accepts that component's `pauseOnHover`, `role`, `fullWidth`, `statusIconDescription`, and `actionable` props.

#### Deduplication

By default, id is optional; a unique id is generated for each notification. The queue [keys](https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/each#Keyed-each-blocks) notifications by id for performance.

Notifications are deduplicated by id. Adding a notification with an id that already exists in the queue is ignored. To change an existing notification in place, use [update](#update).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
  let count = 0;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        id: "id",
        kind: "warning",
        title: "Duplicate notification",
        subtitle:
          "This notification has the same id. Click the button multiple times.",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add duplicate
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        id: `id-${count++}`,
        kind: "info",
        title: "Unique notification",
        subtitle: "This has a unique id, so it will always appear.",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add unique
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

#### Update

Use `update(id, patch)` to change an existing notification in place. The patch merges into the matching notification, useful for reflecting progress (for example, transitioning a loading toast to success without removing and re-adding it).

`update` returns true if a notification with the given id was found, false otherwise.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, NotificationQueue } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<Button
  on:click={() => {
    const id = queue.add({
      id: "upload",
      kind: "info",
      title: "Uploading...",
      subtitle: "0%",
      hideCloseButton: true,
    });

    let progress = 0;
    const interval = setInterval(() => {
      progress += 25;
      if (progress < 100) {
        queue.update(id, { subtitle: `${progress}%` });
      } else {
        clearInterval(interval);
        queue.update(id, {
          kind: "success",
          title: "Upload complete",
          subtitle: "All files have been uploaded.",
          hideCloseButton: false,
          timeout: 3000,
        });
      }
    }, 600);
  }}
>
  Start upload
</Button>
```

#### Max notifications

By default, the queue displays a maximum of 3 notifications. When the limit is exceeded, the oldest notification is removed automatically. While the pointer or focus is in the queue, the removal waits until both leave.

Customize the limit with `maxNotifications`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, NotificationQueue } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
  let count = 0;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} maxNotifications={5} />

<Button
  on:click={() => {
    count++;
    queue.add({
      kind: "success",
      title: `Backup job ${count} completed`,
    });
  }}
>
  Add notification
</Button>
```

#### Remove and clear

Use `remove(id)` to programmatically remove a specific notification, or `clear()` to remove all notifications at once.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
  let notificationIds = [];
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      const id = queue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Removable notification",
        subtitle: "This notification can be removed programmatically.",
        timeout: 0,
      });
      notificationIds = [...notificationIds, id];
    }}
  >
    Add notification
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      if (notificationIds.length > 0) {
        const id = notificationIds[notificationIds.length - 1];
        queue.remove(id);
        notificationIds = notificationIds.slice(0, -1);
      }
    }}
  >
    Remove last
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.clear();
      notificationIds = [];
    }}
  >
    Clear all
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

### Actions

Pass `action` to add one action, such as an undo or a retry, with a label and an `onClick` handler. Set `href` to render the action as a link. The toast closes after the handler runs. Call `event.preventDefault()` in the handler to keep it open, for example to show progress with [update](#update).

A toast with an action does not time out, since a timer could remove it before a keyboard or screen reader user reaches it. It stays until the user acts or closes it, or the app removes it. When the queue is full, toasts without an action are removed first.

The toast does not take focus when it opens, so focus stays where the user is working. The queue is a landmark named "Notifications" (set `labelText` to rename it). Press <kbd>F6</kbd> to move focus to the newest toast, and <kbd>F6</kbd> or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F6</kbd> to return.

Set `actionable` to `true` only when the toast answers something the user just did and needs a response. The toast then becomes an `alertdialog` and takes focus, as in [ToastNotification](/components/ToastNotification#actionable).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "success",
        title: "Report deleted",
        subtitle: "Q3 revenue summary moved to trash.",
        action: {
          label: "Undo",
          onClick: () => {
            queue.add({
              kind: "info",
              title: "Report restored",
              subtitle: "Q3 revenue summary is back in Reports.",
              timeout: 3000,
            });
          },
        },
      });
    }}
  >
    Delete report
  </Button>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    on:click={() => {
      const id = queue.add({
        kind: "error",
        title: "Upload failed",
        subtitle:
          "The connection timed out before quarterly-report.pdf finished.",
        action: {
          label: "Retry",
          onClick: (event) => {
            // Keep the toast open and show progress in place.
            event.preventDefault();
            queue.update(id, {
              kind: "info",
              title: "Retrying upload",
              subtitle: "Uploading quarterly-report.pdf.",
              action: undefined,
              hideCloseButton: true,
            });
            setTimeout(() => {
              queue.update(id, {
                kind: "success",
                title: "Upload complete",
                subtitle: "quarterly-report.pdf is in Reports.",
                hideCloseButton: false,
                timeout: 3000,
              });
            }, 1500);
          },
        },
      });
    }}
  >
    Upload file
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

### Persistent

Create persistent notifications that do not auto-dismiss by omitting timeout and hiding the close button with `hideCloseButton`.

These notifications remain visible until programmatically removed.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "warning",
        title: "Persistent notification",
        subtitle:
          "This notification has no close button and will not auto-dismiss.",
        hideCloseButton: true,
      });
    }}
  >
    Add persistent
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Auto-dismiss notification",
        subtitle:
          "This notification has no close button but will auto-dismiss after 3 seconds.",
        hideCloseButton: true,
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Add auto-dismiss
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.clear();
    }}
  >
    Clear all
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

---

### Component API

#### `NotificationQueue` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `"top-left" \| "top-center" \| "top-right" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-center" \| "bottom-right"` | Specify the position of the notification queue. | `"top-right"` |
| `offsetTop` | `string` | Specify the top offset (CSS value) | `"3rem"` |
| `offsetBottom` | `string` | Specify the bottom offset (CSS value) | `"1rem"` |
| `offsetLeft` | `string` | Specify the left offset (CSS value) | `"1rem"` |
| `offsetRight` | `string` | Specify the right offset (CSS value) | `"1rem"` |
| `zIndex` | `number` | Specify the z-index of the notification queue.<br />By default, this matches the z-index of modals. | `9000` |
| `maxNotifications` | `number` | Specify the maximum number of notifications to display.<br />When this limit is exceeded, the oldest notification is automatically removed.<br />Notifications without an `action` or `actionable` go first. | `3` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the accessible name of the notifications landmark | `"Notifications"` |
| `add` | `(notification: NotificationData) => string` | Add a notification to the queue.<br />If a notification with the same id already exists, the call is ignored.<br />To change an existing notification in place, use `update`.<br />Returns the notification id (either the provided id or a generated one). | _undefined_ |
| `update` | `(id: string, patch: Partial<NotificationData>) => boolean` | Update an existing notification by id, merging `patch` into it.<br />The id of the notification cannot be changed.<br />Returns true if the notification was found and updated, false otherwise. | _undefined_ |
| `remove` | `(id: string) => boolean` | Remove a notification by id.<br />Returns true if the notification was found and removed, false otherwise. | _undefined_ |
| `clear` | `() => void` | Clear all notifications. | _undefined_ |

#### `NotificationQueue` typedefs

```ts
type NotificationAction = {
  /** The action button text */
  label: string;
  /** Called when the action is clicked. The toast then closes, unless the handler calls `event.preventDefault()`. */
  onClick?: (event: MouseEvent) => void;
  /** Render the action as a link */
  href?: string;
};

type NotificationData = {
  /** Optional id for deduplication */
  id?: string;
  kind?:
    "error" | "info" | "info-square" | "success" | "warning" | "warning-alt";
  title?: string;
  subtitle?: string;
  caption?: string;
  /** Ignored when the notification has an `action` or is `actionable` */
  timeout?: number;
  lowContrast?: boolean;
  closeButtonDescription?: string;
  statusIconDescription?: string;
  hideCloseButton?: boolean;
  pauseOnHover?: boolean;
  role?: "alert" | "log" | "status";
  fullWidth?: boolean;
  /** Render as an `alertdialog` that takes focus and closes on Escape */
  actionable?: boolean;
  focusOnOpen?: boolean;
  closeOnEscape?: boolean;
  /** Add an action button. The toast keeps focus where it is and does not time out. */
  action?: NotificationAction;
};

type QueuedNotification = NotificationData & {
  id: string;
  placeholder?: undefined;
};

interface Placeholder {
  id?: undefined;
  placeholder: { height: number };
}
```


## NumberInput

### Basic

Create a basic number input with increment and decrement controls. The input accepts numerical values and provides visual feedback.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### No value

Allow empty values by setting `allowEmpty` to `true` and `value` to `null`. Both are required: allowEmpty enables the empty state, and null represents no value.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NumberInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = null;
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <NumberInput
    labelText="Clusters"
    allowEmpty
    bind:value
    helperText="Value: {value}"
  />
  <ButtonSet>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (value = null)}>
      Set to null
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (value = 0)}>
      Set to 0
    </Button>
  </ButtonSet>
</Stack>
```

### Helper text

Add descriptive text below the input with `helperText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={0}
  helperText="Clusters provisioned in your region"
/>
```

### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput hideLabel labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to provide custom label content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput labelText="" value={0}>
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Clusters</strong>
</NumberInput>
```

### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to select the full value when the field receives focus.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput selectTextOnFocus labelText="Clusters" value={12} />
```

### Range and steps

Control the allowed values and increment.

#### Min and max

Constrain input values with `min` and `max`. Stepper buttons stop at the range limits. Typed values outside the range show an invalid state rather than silently clamping. Add `invalidText` for an error message.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  min={4}
  max={20}
  value={4}
  invalidText="Number must be between 4 and 20."
  helperText="Clusters provisioned in your region"
  labelText="Clusters (4 min, 20 max)"
/>
```

#### Step

Control increment and decrement step size with `step`. This example uses a step of 0.1.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  value={1}
  helperText="Step of 0.1"
  step={0.1}
  labelText="CPU cores allocated"
/>
```

#### Keyboard stepping

With the input focused, <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> and <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> step by `step`. <kbd>PageUp</kbd> and <kbd>PageDown</kbd> step by 10 × `step`, clamped to `min`/`max`.

A stepper button held for 400 ms steps, then steps every 50 ms until release or `min`/`max`. A shorter press steps once, on release.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  value={50}
  step={1}
  min={0}
  max={100}
  helperText="Press PageUp or PageDown to step by 10"
  labelText="Clusters"
/>
```

#### Scrub by dragging the label

Set `scrubbable` to `true` to change the value by dragging the label left or right: every 4 pixels of travel moves one `step`, and holding <kbd>Shift</kbd> moves 10 steps. Dragging right raises the value, and in a right-to-left layout dragging left does. The pointer shows a horizontal resize cursor over the label. `on:input` fires while dragging and `on:change` once on release. Clicking the label still focuses the input, and typing, arrow keys, and the steppers work as usual, so scrubbing is a pointer shortcut rather than the only way to set a value. It suits dense settings panels where many numeric fields sit together.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput scrubbable value={40} min={0} max={100} labelText="Opacity (%)" />
```

#### Step start

Configure a starting point for stepping when the input is empty or zero with `stepStartValue`. When the user clicks increment or decrement, the value jumps to stepStartValue instead of stepping from zero.

This is useful when zero is outside the min/max range, or when a more sensible default exists (for example, the current year). Combined with allowEmpty, it ensures the user interacts with the input before submitting a value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  stepStartValue={2026}
  allowEmpty
  min={2026}
  max={2100}
  labelText="Year"
/>
```

### Formatting

Control how the value is parsed and displayed.

#### Preserve decimals

Preserve decimal input formatting like `"1.0"`, `"2.00"`, or `"3."` by setting `allowDecimal` to `true`. The input uses text mode with decimal input instead of a native number field, so trailing zeros and decimal points stay intact while typing. Useful for financial data or precise decimal entry.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NumberInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = 1.5;
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <NumberInput
    allowDecimal
    allowEmpty
    bind:value
    step={0.01}
    labelText="Amount"
  />

  <ButtonSet>
    <Button on:click={() => (value = null)}>Set to null</Button>
    <Button on:click={() => (value = 0)}>Set to 0</Button>
    <Button on:click={() => (value = 1.23)}>Set to 1.23</Button>
  </ButtonSet>

  <div>
    <strong>Value:</strong>
    {value}
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Locale

Format numbers according to a locale with `locale` and a BCP 47 language tag. The display value is formatted on blur using Intl.NumberFormat. When locale is set, the input uses text mode with decimal input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput locale="de-DE" value={1234.5} labelText="Amount (German)" />
```

#### Locale options

Combine `locale` with `formatOptions` for additional formatting control such as decimal precision.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  locale="en-US"
  formatOptions={{ minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }}
  value={1234.5}
  labelText="Price"
/>
```

### Custom validation

Use `validate` for custom validation logic. The function receives the raw input string and optional locale. Return `false` to mark invalid, `true` to force valid (overriding auto bounds checks), or `undefined` to use built-in validation.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  validate={(raw) => {
    const num = Number(raw);
    return Number.isNaN(num) ? undefined : num % 2 === 0;
  }}
  invalidText="Must be an even number"
  labelText="Even number"
  value={0}
/>
```

### Stepper controls

Control the stepper buttons and scroll-wheel interaction.

#### Hidden steppers

Hide the increment and decrement controls by setting `hideSteppers` to `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput hideSteppers labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Disable wheel

Prevent the scroll wheel from changing the input value by setting `disableWheel` to `true`. This is useful in forms where accidental scroll changes are undesirable.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput disableWheel labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### Events

Respond to value changes and stepper interactions.

#### Value change

Use `on:input` to listen for every keystroke, and `on:change` to listen for committed changes--on blur, or immediately after a stepper click or arrow key press. Both events dispatch the parsed value directly as `event.detail`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  on:input={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // number | null
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // number | null
/>
```

#### Blur

Use `on:blur` to listen for when the input loses focus. The event detail includes the current parsed value and the original FocusEvent.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  on:blur={(e) => {
    console.log(e.detail.value); // number | null
    console.log(e.detail.event); // FocusEvent
  }}
/>
```

#### Stepper click

Use `on:click:stepper` to listen for stepper button clicks. The event detail includes the updated value and direction (`"up"` or `"down"`). This event only fires on button clicks, not arrow key presses. A held button fires it once, on release, with the final value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  on:click:stepper={(e) => {
    console.log(e.detail.value); // number
    console.log(e.detail.direction); // "up" | "down"
  }}
/>
```

#### Stepper blur

Use `on:blur:stepper` to listen for when a stepper button loses focus. The event detail includes the current value, direction, and original FocusEvent.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  on:blur:stepper={(e) => {
    console.log(e.detail.value); // number | null
    console.log(e.detail.direction); // "up" | "down"
    console.log(e.detail.event); // FocusEvent
  }}
/>
```

#### Stepper

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = 0;
  let clickStepperEvents = [];
  let blurEvents = [];
  let blurStepperEvents = [];
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <NumberInput
    bind:value
    labelText="Clusters"
    on:click:stepper={(e) => {
      clickStepperEvents = [
        ...clickStepperEvents,
        `value: ${e.detail.value}, direction: ${e.detail.direction}`,
      ];
    }}
    on:blur={(e) => {
      blurEvents = [...blurEvents, `value: ${e.detail.value}`];
    }}
    on:blur:stepper={(e) => {
      blurStepperEvents = [
        ...blurStepperEvents,
        `value: ${e.detail.value}, direction: ${e.detail.direction}`,
      ];
    }}
  />
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <strong>click:stepper events:</strong>
      <pre>{clickStepperEvents.join("\n") || "(none)"}</pre>
    </Stack>
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <strong>blur events:</strong>
      <pre>{blurEvents.join("\n") || "(none)"}</pre>
    </Stack>
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <strong>blur:stepper events:</strong>
      <pre>{blurStepperEvents.join("\n") || "(none)"}</pre>
    </Stack>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### AI label

Put an `AILabel` in the `decorator` slot to mark the value as AI-generated. The field shows the AI gradient. See [AI label](/components/AILabel#fields) for the revert flow.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput labelText="Clusters" value={3}>
  <AILabel slot="decorator">
    <p>Recommended from last month's peak traffic.</p>
  </AILabel>
</NumberInput>
```

### Sizes

`size` sets the input height. The default is `"md"`.

#### Extra-large

Use the extra-large size for prominent inputs by setting `size` to `"xl"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput size="xl" labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Small

Use the small size for compact layouts by setting `size` to `"sm"`. This is ideal for secondary inputs.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput size="sm" labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Extra-small

Use the extra-small size for dense layouts, such as toolbars and table rows, by setting `size` to `"xs"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput size="xs" labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <NumberInput labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to `true` to use the fluid variant, which embeds the label inside the field. Fluid number inputs can be used standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), where the fluid variant is applied automatically.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput fluid labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Hidden steppers

The fluid variant works with `hideSteppers` to remove the increment and decrement controls.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput fluid hideSteppers labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput fluid value={0}>
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Clusters
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="The number of clusters provisioned in your region."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</NumberInput>
```

#### Invalid

Fluid number inputs display the error message inside the field boundary. Long messages wrap to multiple lines.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  fluid
  invalid
  invalidText="The number of clusters must be between 4 and 20 to provision a highly available cluster in this region."
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={0}
/>
```

#### Warning

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  fluid
  warn
  warnText="Increasing the cluster count will incur additional charges."
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={0}
/>
```

#### Disabled

Invalid and warning states are not displayed while the input is disabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  fluid
  disabled
  invalid
  invalidText="The number of clusters is invalid."
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={0}
/>
```

#### Read-only

Invalid and warning states are not displayed while the input is read-only.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput fluid readonly labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Skeleton

Display a loading skeleton for the fluid number input variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FluidNumberInputSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FluidNumberInputSkeleton />
```

### States

Reflect validation and interaction states.

#### Invalid

Indicate an invalid value by setting `invalid` to `true`. This example shows a validation error.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  invalid
  invalidText="Enter a valid cluster count"
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={0}
/>
```

#### Warning

Indicate a warning state by setting `warn` to `true`. This example shows a warning about the input value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  warn
  warnText="A high number may impact initial rollout"
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={25}
/>
```

#### Disabled

Disable the input by setting `disabled` to `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput disabled labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Read-only

Make the input read-only by setting `readonly` to `true`. This allows viewing but prevents editing.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput readonly labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### Skeleton

Show a loading state with the number input skeleton. This is useful while data is being fetched.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInputSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInputSkeleton />
```

#### Sizes

Set `size` to match the field the skeleton stands in for.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInputSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInputSkeleton size="xs" />
```

#### Without label

Show a loading state without a label by setting `hideLabel` to `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInputSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInputSkeleton hideLabel />
```

### Component API

#### `NumberInput` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `null \| number` | Specify the input value.<br />Use `null` to denote "no value".<br />Kept when the owning form resets; with `allowEmpty`, follows the field<br />instead. | `null` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Set the size of the input.<br />Inherits the parent `Form` size when unset.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (the 40px default, which overrides a<br />`Form` size) and `"lg"` (`"xl"`). | _undefined_ |
| `step` | `number` | Specify the step increment | `1` |
| `max` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the maximum value. | _undefined_ |
| `min` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the minimum value. | _undefined_ |
| `stepStartValue` | `number \| undefined` | Provide the value stepping should begin at when the input is empty. | _undefined_ |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the input to be read-only | `false` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`. | `false` |
| `allowEmpty` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to allow for an empty value | `false` |
| `allowDecimal` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to preserve decimal input formatting.<br />When enabled, uses type="text" with inputmode="decimal" instead of type="number". | `false` |
| `locale` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a BCP 47 locale for number formatting.<br />When set, forces type="text" with inputmode="decimal"<br />and formats the display value using Intl.NumberFormat. | _undefined_ |
| `formatOptions` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| undefined` | Specify Intl.NumberFormat options when `locale` is set. | _undefined_ |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the input | `false` |
| `hideSteppers` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to hide the input stepper buttons | `false` |
| `disableWheel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to prevent the scroll wheel from changing the input value | `false` |
| `scrubbable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to change the value by dragging the label left or right.<br />Dragging toward the inline end raises the value: right, or left under<br />`dir="rtl"`. Every 4 pixels of travel moves one `step`; hold Shift to<br />move 10 steps.<br />Typing, arrow keys, and the steppers work as usual. | `false` |
| `selectTextOnFocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to select the input's text when it receives focus | `false` |
| `validate` | `((value: string, locale: string \| undefined) => boolean \| undefined) \| undefined` | Custom validation function.<br />Receives the current raw input string and locale.<br />Return `true` to force valid, `false` to force invalid,<br />or `undefined` to defer to built-in validation. | _undefined_ |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `translateWithId` | `(id: NumberInputTranslationId) => string` | Override the default translation ids. | `(id) => defaultTranslations[id]` |
| `translationIds` | `{ increment: "increment"; decrement: "decrement" }` | Default translation ids. | `{<br />  increment: "increment",<br />  decrement: "decrement",<br />}` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the input element | `uniqueId()` |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a name attribute for the input.<br />With `locale` or `allowDecimal`, the form submits the numeric value<br />(for example `1234.5`), not the formatted display text. | _undefined_ |

## OrderedList

### Basic

Create a basic ordered list by wrapping list item components within the ordered list. For tree-structured data, consider [RecursiveList](/components/RecursiveList#ordered).

```svelte
<script>
  import { ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList>
  <ListItem>Submit the change request for approval</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Run the automated test suite in the CI pipeline</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Deploy the build to the production environment</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

### With links

Add interactive elements like link components within list items.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link, ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList>
  <ListItem>
    <Link href="#">Review the architecture decision record</Link>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>
    <Link href="#">Review the security sign-off checklist</Link>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>
    <Link href="#">Review the on-call runbook</Link>
  </ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

### Nested lists

Create hierarchical lists with support for the browser's native numbering style.

#### Standard

Set `nested` on a child ordered list for proper indentation and numbering.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList>
  <ListItem>
    Triage the incident
    <OrderedList nested>
      <ListItem>Acknowledge the PagerDuty alert</ListItem>
      <ListItem>
        Assess the blast radius
        <OrderedList nested>
          <ListItem>Check the service health dashboard</ListItem>
          <ListItem>Identify affected customer tenants</ListItem>
        </OrderedList>
      </ListItem>
    </OrderedList>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>Mitigate the incident</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Publish the postmortem</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

#### Native styles

Set `native` to `true` to use the browser's native list styles. Useful for large lists where the list number may overlap with the list item text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList native>
  <ListItem>
    Triage the incident
    <OrderedList nested>
      <ListItem>Acknowledge the PagerDuty alert</ListItem>
      <ListItem>
        Assess the blast radius
        <OrderedList nested>
          <ListItem>Check the service health dashboard</ListItem>
          <ListItem>Identify affected customer tenants</ListItem>
        </OrderedList>
      </ListItem>
    </OrderedList>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>Mitigate the incident</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Publish the postmortem</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

### Expressive styles

Use Carbon's expressive typesetting with `expressive`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link, ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList expressive>
  <ListItem
    ><Link size="lg" href="#">Complete the security training module</Link
    ></ListItem
  >
  <ListItem>Set up multi-factor authentication</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Request access to the production VPN</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

### Virtualization

Render thousands of items with [VirtualList](/components/VirtualList). Set `spacerTag` to `"li"` so it renders only the items in view, straight into the list. Only those items are in the DOM, so set `native` and pass `value={index + 1}` to each `ListItem` to keep the numbering. Wrap the list in a [ScrollGradient](/components/ScrollGradient) and pass its `scrollElementRef` as `scrollElement`. Set `measured` if items can wrap.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    ListItem,
    OrderedList,
    ScrollGradient,
    VirtualList,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const databases = ["billing", "orders", "inventory", "audit", "sessions"];

  const steps = Array.from({ length: 2000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    label: `Back up the ${databases[i % databases.length]} database`,
  }));

  let scrollElementRef = null;
</script>

<ScrollGradient height="240px" bind:scrollElementRef>
  <Box paddingY={4} paddingX={5}>
    <OrderedList native>
      <VirtualList
        items={steps}
        itemHeight={20}
        containerHeight={240}
        scrollElement={scrollElementRef}
        spacerTag="li"
        measured
        getKey={(item) => item.id}
        let:item
        let:index
      >
        <ListItem value={index + 1}>{item.label}</ListItem>
      </VirtualList>
    </OrderedList>
  </Box>
</ScrollGradient>
```

---

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `expressive` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use Carbon's expressive typesetting | `false` |

| Event           |
| --------------- |
