| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `ListItem` $$restProps

`ListItem` spreads `$$restProps` to the `li` element.


## OverflowMenu

### Basic

Create a basic overflow menu by wrapping overflow menu item components within the overflow menu. For menus that need submenus, use [MenuButton](/components/MenuButton#icon-only) instead.

Once open, arrow keys move focus between items without wrapping past the first or last item. <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> jump to the first and last enabled item, skipping disabled ones. Type a character to move focus to the next enabled item whose text starts with it; type several characters quickly to match a longer prefix.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

### Reactive example

Control the menu state programmatically by binding to `open`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Stack gap={6} align="start">
  <OverflowMenu bind:open>
    <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
    <OverflowMenuItem
      href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
      target="_blank"
      text="API documentation"
    />
    <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
  </OverflowMenu>
  <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
    {open ? "Close menu" : "Open menu"}
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

### Positioning

Control where and how the menu opens.

#### Portal

A menu that a container would cut off, such as a box with `overflow: hidden` or a scroll area, opens in a floating portal. The container in the example below hides its overflow, so the menu moves to a portal when it opens. Inside a [Modal](/components/Modal#modal-with-dropdowns), the menu always opens in a portal.

Set `portalMenu` to `true` to always render the menu in a portal, for example to escape a z-index stacking context. Set it to `false` to keep the menu in place. A portalled menu leaves its container in the DOM, so CSS that targets the menu as a descendant of the container does not match it.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box
  display="flex"
  direction="column"
  gap={4}
  overflow="hidden"
  border="subtle"
  borderStyle="dashed"
  padding={5}
  maxHeight="120px"
>
  <div>
    This container has hidden overflow. The menu would not fit, so it opens in a
    portal.
  </div>
  <OverflowMenu>
    <OverflowMenuItem text="Edit" />
    <OverflowMenuItem text="Duplicate" />
    <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete" />
  </OverflowMenu>
</Box>
```

#### Flipped

Set `flipped` to `true` to align the menu with the button's inline end: its right edge, or its left edge in a right-to-left layout.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu flipped>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Direction

Set `direction` to `"top"` to position the menu above the button.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu flipped direction="top">
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Layer,
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <OverflowMenu>
      <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
      <OverflowMenuItem
        href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
        target="_blank"
        text="API documentation"
      />
      <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
    </OverflowMenu>
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to control trigger and item height. The default is `md`.

#### Extra-large

Set `size` to `"xl"` for an extra-large overflow menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu size="xl">
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Small

Set `size` to `"sm"` for a small overflow menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu size="sm">
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Extra-small

Set `size` to `"xs"` for an extra-small overflow menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu size="xs">
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

### Scrollable

Set `maxHeight` to cap the menu height and scroll the remaining items. A number is treated as pixels; a string is used as any CSS length, such as `"20rem"`. Keyboard navigation scrolls the focused item into view.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const workspaces = [
    "Platform API",
    "Billing Service",
    "Customer Portal",
    "Admin Console",
    "Data Pipeline",
    "Analytics Warehouse",
    "Notification Service",
    "Identity & Access",
    "Payments Gateway",
    "Support Desk",
    "Audit & Compliance",
    "Mobile Backend",
    "Search Service",
    "Reporting Engine",
    "Webhook Relay",
    "File Storage",
    "Message Queue",
    "Feature Flags",
    "Monitoring Stack",
    "Incident Response",
  ];
</script>

<OverflowMenu maxHeight={240}>
  {#each workspaces as workspace (workspace)}
    <OverflowMenuItem text={workspace} />
  {/each}
  <OverflowMenuItem hasDivider danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

### Trigger

Customize the menu trigger button.

#### Icon

Replace the default vertical overflow menu icon with a custom icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Add from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Add.svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu icon={Add}>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Slot

Use the `menu` slot to customize the trigger button content. The trigger grows to fit custom content, and never shrinks below the default icon trigger's size.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu>
  <Box slot="menu" paddingX={5}>Custom trigger</Box>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Accessible label

The trigger takes its accessible name and tooltip from `iconDescription`, which defaults to `"Options"`. The menu takes the same name. Set it to describe the actions.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu iconDescription="Service actions">
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

Set `aria-label` to give the trigger and the menu a longer name than the tooltip shows. Start it with the tooltip text, so voice control users can say what they see.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu
  iconDescription="Actions"
  aria-label="Actions for API Gateway service"
>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Tooltip position

Set `tooltipAlign` to place the trigger's tooltip, with Popover's `align` names. The default is `"top"`. It replaces `tooltipPosition` and `tooltipAlignment`, which still work and are deprecated. The tooltip shows on hover and focus, hides while the menu is open, and flips to the opposite side when there is not enough space. It stays closed when the menu returns focus to the trigger.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu tooltipAlign="bottom-start">
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Disabled

Set `disabled` to `true` to disable the trigger button.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu disabled>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

### Items

Customize individual menu items.

#### Icons

Set `icon` for an icon at the start or `iconEnd` for one at the end; the label fills the space between them. Use the matching slots for custom markup. Item icons are not intended for `sm` or `xs` sizes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Document from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Document.svelte";
  import Edit from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Edit.svelte";
  import Launch from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Launch.svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu>
  <OverflowMenuItem icon={Edit} text="Rename" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    icon={Document}
    iconEnd={Launch}
    text="Open docs"
    href="https://www.ibm.com/docs"
    target="_blank"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem hasDivider danger icon={TrashCan} text="Delete" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Keyboard shortcuts

Set `shortcut` to show an item's keys at the end of the row, such as `"mod+d"`, which shows <DocKbd shortcut="mod+d" variant="muted" /> on your platform. The item announces them with `aria-keyshortcuts`, and the menu widens, up to 20rem, so the keys don't squeeze the labels. The menu only shows the keys: bind the command itself with `onShortcut`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Edit" shortcut="mod+e" />
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Duplicate" shortcut="mod+d" />
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Delete" shortcut="mod+backspace" danger hasDivider />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Primary focus

Set `primaryFocus` to `true` on a menu item to focus it when opening the dropdown.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem primaryFocus danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Disabled

Disable individual menu items with `disabled`. Use a divider to add visual separation between items.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Create key" />
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Import key" />
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Revoke key" disabled />
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Duplicate key" disabled />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    hasDivider
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem hasDivider danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Danger

Set `danger` on an item to indicate a critical or destructive action, such as deleting a resource. The item renders in red with a matching focus outline.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem hasDivider danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

### Events

Respond to menu close attempts and individual item clicks.

#### Close event

Use `on:close` to respond to every close attempt, regardless of cause. The event detail includes `trigger` (`"toggle"`, `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, or `"item-select"`); when triggered by a selection, `index` and `text` identify the selected item.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu
  on:close={(e) => {
    console.log(e.detail.trigger); // "toggle" | "escape-key" | "outside-click" | "item-select"
    console.log(e.detail.index); // number | undefined
    console.log(e.detail.text); // string | undefined
  }}
>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Prevent item close

Use `e.preventDefault()` on an individual overflow menu item click event to prevent the menu from closing when that item is clicked. Use this to keep the menu open after performing an action.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let copying = false;
  let copied = false;

  async function copyToClipboard() {
    if (copying) return;
    copying = true;
    copied = false;
    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(
      "https://api.example.com/webhooks/incoming/8f2b41c9",
    );
    copied = true;
    setTimeout(() => {
      copied = false;
    }, 2000);

    copying = false;
  }
</script>

<OverflowMenu>
  <OverflowMenuItem
    text={copied ? "Copied!" : "Copy webhook URL"}
    disabled={copying}
    on:click={(e) => {
      // Prevent menu from closing for this item.
      e.preventDefault();
      copyToClipboard();
    }}
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Close menu" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Cancel close event

The `close` event is cancelable. Call `e.preventDefault()` on it to keep the menu open when it would otherwise close from the trigger, <kbd>Escape</kbd>, or an outside click. The example below guards against accidentally dismissing unsaved changes: toggle a setting, then try to close the menu without saving.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let emailEnabled = false;
  let smsEnabled = false;
  let saved = true;

  function toggle(setter) {
    return (e) => {
      // Keep the menu open while editing settings.
      e.preventDefault();
      setter();
      saved = false;
    };
  }
</script>

<OverflowMenu
  on:close={(e) => {
    // Guard against accidentally dismissing unsaved changes.
    if (!saved && !window.confirm("Discard unsaved notification settings?")) {
      e.preventDefault();
    }
  }}
>
  <OverflowMenuItem
    text="Email alerts: {emailEnabled ? 'On' : 'Off'}"
    on:click={toggle(() => (emailEnabled = !emailEnabled))}
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    text="SMS alerts: {smsEnabled ? 'On' : 'Off'}"
    on:click={toggle(() => (smsEnabled = !smsEnabled))}
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    hasDivider
    text="Save changes"
    on:click={() => {
      // Allow the menu to close after saving.
      saved = true;
    }}
  />
</OverflowMenu>
```

---

### Component API

#### `OverflowMenu` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the menu. | `false` |
| `icon` (Reactive) | `Icon` | Specify the icon to render. | `OverflowMenuVertical` |
| `buttonRef` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLButtonElement` | Obtain a reference to the trigger button element. | `null` |
| `menuRef` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLUListElement` | Obtain a reference to the overflow menu element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Specify the size of the overflow menu.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (the 40px default) and `"lg"` (`"xl"`). | _undefined_ |
| `direction` | `"top" \| "bottom"` | Specify the direction of the overflow menu relative to the button. | `"bottom"` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the trigger button | `false` |
| `flipped` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to align the menu with the button's inline end instead of<br />its start. Under `dir="rtl"` the default menu aligns with the button's<br />right edge, and a flipped one with its left. | `false` |
| `maxHeight` | `number \| string \| undefined` | Specify the maximum height of the menu.<br />A number is treated as pixels; a string is used as a CSS length.<br />The menu scrolls once its items exceed the height. | _undefined_ |
| `menuOptionsClass` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the menu options class. | _undefined_ |
| `iconClass` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the icon class. | _undefined_ |
| `iconDescription` | `string` | Specify the trigger's accessible name and tooltip text.<br />An `aria-label` on the component overrides the name, not the tooltip.<br />A custom trigger in the `menu` slot is named by its content and has no<br />tooltip. | `"Options"` |
| `tooltipAlign` | `"top" \| "top-start" \| "top-end" \| "bottom" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-end" \| "left" \| "left-start" \| "left-end" \| "right" \| "right-start" \| "right-end" \| undefined` | Set the tooltip placement in floating-ui form: the side, then `start`<br />or `end` along it, as Popover's `align` takes. Above and below,<br />`start` and `end` name inline sides, so they swap under `dir="rtl"`.<br />When set, takes precedence over `tooltipPosition` and `tooltipAlignment`. | _undefined_ |
| `tooltipPosition` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | Set the position of the trigger's tooltip.<br />The tooltip flips to the opposite side when there is not enough space. | `"top"` |
| `tooltipAlignment` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | Set the alignment of the trigger's tooltip. | `"center"` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the button element | `uniqueId()` |
| `portalMenu` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to always render the menu in a portal, or `false` to<br />keep it in place. Left unset, the menu moves to a portal inside a<br />Modal, or when a box around it (`overflow` other than `visible`)<br />would cut it off. | _undefined_ |

#### `OverflowMenu` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `menu`    | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `OverflowMenu` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:keydown`    |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `OverflowMenu` dispatched events

| Event | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `on:close` | `{<br />  trigger:<br />    \| "escape-key"<br />    \| "outside-click"<br />    \| "toggle"<br />    \| "item-select";<br />  /** only present when an item is selected */<br />  index?: number;<br />  /** only present when an item is selected */<br />  text?: string;<br />}` |

#### `OverflowMenu` $$restProps

`OverflowMenu` spreads `$$restProps` to the `button` element.

#### `OverflowMenuItem` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLAnchorElement \| HTMLButtonElement` | Obtain a reference to the HTML element. | `null` |
| `text` | `string` | Specify the item text.<br />Alternatively, use the default slot. | `"Provide text"` |
| `icon` | `Icon \| undefined` | Specify an icon to render to the left of the item text.<br />Alternatively, use the "icon" slot. | _undefined_ |
| `iconEnd` | `Icon \| undefined` | Specify an icon to render at the end of the item.<br />Alternatively, use the "iconEnd" slot. | _undefined_ |
| `iconRight` | `Icon \| undefined` | Specify an icon to render at the end of the item. | _undefined_ |
| `href` | `string` | Specify the `href` attribute if the item is a link | `""` |
| `target` | `import("svelte/elements").SvelteHTMLElements["a"]["target"]` | Specify the `target` attribute if the item is a link | `""` |
| `rel` | `import("svelte/elements").SvelteHTMLElements["a"]["rel"] \| undefined` | Specify the `rel` attribute if the item is a link.<br />By default, `noopener noreferrer` is added if<br />`target="_blank"` unless `rel` is specified. | _undefined_ |
| `primaryFocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` if the item should be focused when opening the menu | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the item | `false` |
| `hasDivider` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to include a divider | `false` |
| `shortcut` | `string` | Specify a keyboard shortcut to show, such as `"mod+d"`. `mod` is<br />Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. The keys show at the end<br />of the item, and it gets `aria-keyshortcuts`. Display only: bind the<br />command itself with `onShortcut`, since the menu is usually closed. A<br />value that isn't a shortcut, such as `"Ctrl D"`, shows as written. | `""` |
| `danger` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the danger variant | `false` |
| `requireTitle` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to omit the button `title` attribute | `true` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the top-level element | `uniqueId()` |

#### `OverflowMenuItem` slots

| Slot        | Detail                  |
| ----------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`   | `Record<string, never>` |
| `icon`      | `Record<string, never>` |
| `iconEnd`   | `Record<string, never>` |
| `iconRight` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `OverflowMenuItem` forwarded events

| Event        |
| ------------ |
| `on:keydown` |

#### `OverflowMenuItem` dispatched events

| Event      | Detail       |
| ---------- | ------------ |
| `on:click` | `MouseEvent` |

#### `OverflowMenuItem` $$restProps

`OverflowMenuItem` spreads `$$restProps` to the `li` element.


## PageHeader

### Basic

Set `title` and `subtitle`. The title renders as a `Heading`, so its level follows the nearest `Section` (an `h1` by default).

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" subtitle="Manage your database instances" />
```

### Breadcrumb

Place a `Breadcrumb` in the `breadcrumb` slot to render it above the title.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Breadcrumb,
    BreadcrumbItem,
    PageHeader,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" subtitle="Manage your database instances">
  <svelte:fragment slot="breadcrumb">
    <Breadcrumb noTrailingSlash>
      <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Resources</BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbItem href="/" isCurrentPage>Databases</BreadcrumbItem>
    </Breadcrumb>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Breadcrumb actions

Use the `breadcrumbEnd` slot for small, page-wide actions such as share or favorite. They sit at the end of the breadcrumb row, away from the main page actions.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Breadcrumb,
    BreadcrumbItem,
    Button,
    PageHeader,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Share from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Share.svelte";
  import Star from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Star.svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="db-prod-01" subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south">
  <svelte:fragment slot="breadcrumb">
    <Breadcrumb noTrailingSlash>
      <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Databases</BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbItem href="/" isCurrentPage>db-prod-01</BreadcrumbItem>
    </Breadcrumb>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="breadcrumbEnd">
    <Button kind="ghost" size="small" icon={Share} iconDescription="Share" />
    <Button
      kind="ghost"
      size="small"
      icon={Star}
      iconDescription="Add to favorites"
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

### Tabs and panels

#### Tabs

Place a `Tabs` in the `tabs` slot to render page-level navigation along the header's bottom edge.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader, Tab, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" subtitle="Manage your database instances">
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
    <Tabs>
      <Tab label="Overview" />
      <Tab label="Backups" />
      <Tab label="Settings" />
    </Tabs>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Tab panels

Content in the default slot renders after the header, outside the `<header>` element. Place one `TabContent` per tab there to pair each panel with its tab in the `tabs` slot, as you would in the `Tabs` `content` slot. Panels stay out of the header, so a `sticky` header does not pin them.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader, Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" subtitle="Manage your database instances">
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
    <Tabs>
      <Tab label="Overview" />
      <Tab label="Backups" />
      <Tab label="Settings" />
    </Tabs>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <TabContent>Overview: 4 instances, 2 regions.</TabContent>
  <TabContent>Backups: nightly, kept for 30 days.</TabContent>
  <TabContent>Settings: maintenance window Sunday 02:00 UTC.</TabContent>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Tabs end

Use the `tabsEnd` slot for controls that apply to every tab, such as a time range. They sit at the end of the tabs row, lined up with the actions. A ghost `MenuButton` matches the tab height, and `intrinsicAlign="end"` opens its menu toward the page.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    MenuButton,
    MenuItem,
    MenuItemRadioGroup,
    PageHeader,
    Tab,
    Tabs,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import timeRangeLabel from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/timeRangeLabel.svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="db-prod-01" subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south">
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
    <Tabs>
      <Tab label="Overview" />
      <Tab label="Metrics" />
      <Tab label="Logs" />
    </Tabs>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabsEnd">
    <MenuButton kind="ghost" intrinsicAlign="end" labelText={timeRangeLabel}>
      <MenuItemRadioGroup labelText="Time range" bind:selectedId={timeRange}>
        {#each timeRanges as range (range.id)}
          <MenuItem id={range.id} labelText={range.text} />
        {/each}
      </MenuItemRadioGroup>
    </MenuButton>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Container tabs

Set `type="container"` on the slotted `Tabs` to use container tabs. The header drops its divider, and panels in the default slot take the `"layer-01"` surface of the selected tab.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader, Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" subtitle="Manage your database instances">
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
    <Tabs type="container">
      <Tab label="Overview" />
      <Tab label="Backups" />
      <Tab label="Settings" />
    </Tabs>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <TabContent>Overview: 4 instances, 2 regions.</TabContent>
  <TabContent>Backups: nightly, kept for 30 days.</TabContent>
  <TabContent>Settings: maintenance window Sunday 02:00 UTC.</TabContent>
</PageHeader>
```

On a layered header (`fill="layer-01"`), the selected tab and its panel switch to the page `"background"` instead, so they still stand apart from the header.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader, Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader
  fill="layer-01"
  title="Databases"
  subtitle="Manage your database instances"
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
    <Tabs type="container">
      <Tab label="Overview" />
      <Tab label="Backups" />
      <Tab label="Settings" />
    </Tabs>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <TabContent>Overview: 4 instances, 2 regions.</TabContent>
  <TabContent>Backups: nightly, kept for 30 days.</TabContent>
  <TabContent>Settings: maintenance window Sunday 02:00 UTC.</TabContent>
</PageHeader>
```

### Actions

The `actions` slot aligns page actions with the title and wraps them below it on narrow screens. Children sit side by side with no gap, like a `ButtonSet`, so wrap them in a `Stack` or `Box` when they need space between them. Match control heights, for example `size="lg"` on `ComboButton` and `MenuButton` and `size="xl"` on `OverflowMenu`, to line up with default-size buttons.

#### Single action

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Add from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Add.svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" subtitle="Manage your database instances">
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button icon={Add}>Create database</Button>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Button set

Place a `ButtonSet` or `ActionSet` in the slot for a secondary and a primary action. Each button sizes to its label.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ButtonSet, PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Add from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Add.svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" subtitle="Manage your database instances">
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <ButtonSet>
      <Button kind="secondary">Import</Button>
      <Button icon={Add}>Create database</Button>
    </ButtonSet>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Icon buttons

Pair ghost icon-only buttons with the primary action for frequent secondary tasks.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Add from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Add.svelte";
  import Download from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Download.svelte";
  import Renew from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Renew.svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" subtitle="Manage your database instances">
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button
      kind="ghost"
      icon={Renew}
      iconDescription="Refresh"
      tooltipPosition="bottom"
    />
    <Button
      kind="ghost"
      icon={Download}
      iconDescription="Export"
      tooltipPosition="bottom"
    />
    <Button icon={Add}>Create database</Button>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Overflow menu

Move less frequent actions into an `OverflowMenu` beside the primary action. Set `flipped` so the menu opens toward the page, not off its edge.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
    PageHeader,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="db-prod-01" subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south">
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <ButtonSet>
      <Button kind="secondary">Restart</Button>
      <Button>Connect</Button>
    </ButtonSet>
    <OverflowMenu size="xl" flipped iconDescription="More actions">
      <OverflowMenuItem text="Rename" />
      <OverflowMenuItem text="Clone" />
      <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete" />
    </OverflowMenu>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Combo button

Use a `ComboButton` when one action is most common and related variants belong in its menu. Set `tooltipAlignment="end"` so the trigger's tooltip stays on screen at the page's right edge.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    ComboButton,
    MenuDivider,
    MenuItem,
    PageHeader,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Deployments" subtitle="Release builds to your environments">
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <ComboButton
      size="lg"
      labelText="Deploy"
      iconDescription="More deploy options"
      tooltipAlignment="end"
    >
      <MenuItem>Deploy to staging</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem>Deploy to production</MenuItem>
      <MenuDivider />
      <MenuItem>Schedule deploy</MenuItem>
    </ComboButton>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Menu button

Use a `MenuButton` to group several actions of equal weight behind one trigger. Set `intrinsicAlign="end"` so the menu opens aligned to the trigger's right edge, toward the page.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    MenuButton,
    MenuDivider,
    MenuItem,
    PageHeader,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="db-prod-01" subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south">
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <MenuButton
      size="lg"
      kind="tertiary"
      labelText="Actions"
      intrinsicAlign="end"
    >
      <MenuItem>Restart</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem>Create backup</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem>Scale</MenuItem>
      <MenuDivider />
      <MenuItem kind="danger">Delete</MenuItem>
    </MenuButton>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Filter

Place a `Search` in the slot to filter the content below the header in place. Wrap it in a `Box` with a fixed `width`, since a `Search` otherwise shrinks to its placeholder in the actions row.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    ContainedList,
    ContainedListItem,
    PageHeader,
    Search,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import databaseFilter from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/databaseFilter.svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader
  title="Databases"
  subtitle="{filteredDatabases.length} of {databases.length} instances"
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Box width="20rem">
      <Search
        labelText="Filter databases"
        placeholder="Filter by name, engine, or region"
        bind:value={databaseFilter}
      />
    </Box>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <ContainedList labelText="Instances" hideLabel>
    {#each filteredDatabases as db (db.name)}
      <ContainedListItem
        >{db.name} · {db.engine} · {db.region}</ContainedListItem
      >
    {:else}
      <ContainedListItem
        >No databases match "{databaseFilter}".</ContainedListItem
      >
    {/each}
  </ContainedList>
</PageHeader>
```

### Title content

#### Title only

Omit `subtitle` for a title-only header.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" />
```

#### Custom title

Use the `titleChildren` slot for rich title content. It renders inside the heading and overrides `title`. Place a `Text` with `tag="span"` in the slot to give the title a different type style.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader, Text } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader subtitle="Manage your database instances">
  <svelte:fragment slot="titleChildren">
    <Text tag="span" type="heading-03">Databases</Text>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Title icon

Use the `titleStart` slot to place an icon before the title.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import DataBase from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/DataBase.svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases" subtitle="Manage your database instances">
  <svelte:fragment slot="titleStart">
    <DataBase size={24} aria-hidden="true" />
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Eyebrow

Set `eyebrow` for short text above the title, such as the parent section or resource type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader
  eyebrow="Resources"
  title="Databases"
  subtitle="Manage your database instances"
/>
```

#### Eyebrow with icon

Set `eyebrowIcon` to place an icon before the eyebrow text. The icon always renders at 16px, whatever size the icon component is given.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Folder from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Folder.svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader
  eyebrow="Resources"
  eyebrowIcon={Folder}
  title="Databases"
  subtitle="Manage your database instances"
/>
```

#### Avatar

Place a `UserAvatar` in the `titleStart` slot for a person or account page.

```svelte
<script>

</script>

<PageHeader
  title="Richard Hendricks"
  subtitle="Administrator · richard.hendricks@example.com"
>

      imageDescription="Richard Hendricks"
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Status

Use the `titleEnd` slot for a status `Tag` or `IconIndicator` beside the title.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader, Tag } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="db-prod-01" subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south">
  <svelte:fragment slot="titleEnd">
```

```svelte
<script>

  <svelte:fragment slot="titleEnd">
    <IconIndicator kind="in-progress" label="Running" />
  </svelte:fragment>

```

#### Contextual actions

Use the `titleEnd` slot for small ghost icon buttons that act on the title itself, such as rename or copy. Keep page-wide actions in the `actions` slot.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Edit from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Edit.svelte";

<PageHeader title="db-prod-01" subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south">

    <Button kind="ghost" size="small" icon={Copy} iconDescription="Copy name" />
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Description

Use the `description` slot for longer rich text, such as a link to more help, in place of a one-line `subtitle`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link, PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader title="Databases">
  <svelte:fragment slot="description">

      >Learn about backups</Link
    >
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

### Appearance

#### Fill

Set `fill` to `"layer-01"` or `"layer-02"` to set the header apart from the page body. The default is `"background"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Breadcrumb,
    BreadcrumbItem,
    Button,
    PageHeader,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Add from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Add.svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader
  fill="layer-01"
  title="Databases"
  subtitle="Manage your database instances"
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="breadcrumb">
    <Breadcrumb noTrailingSlash>
      <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbItem href="/" isCurrentPage>Databases</BreadcrumbItem>
    </Breadcrumb>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button icon={Add}>Create database</Button>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Small

Set `size` to `"sm"` for a compact header on nested or detail pages. It uses a smaller title and tighter vertical spacing, and keeps the same inline padding so the title stays aligned.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader size="sm" title="Edit rule" subtitle="Alert rules / CPU above 90%">
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button kind="secondary" size="field">Cancel</Button>
    <Button size="field">Save</Button>
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Hidden divider

Set `hideDivider` to `true` to hide the border below the header, such as when the content below already starts with its own edge.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeader } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader
  hideDivider
  title="Databases"
  subtitle="Manage your database instances"
/>
```

### Skeleton

Use `PageHeaderSkeleton` while the page's data loads. It renders a title and subtitle placeholder by default; set `breadcrumb`, `actions`, and `tabs` (a count) to match the header it stands in for, and set `grid`, `fill`, and `hideDivider` the same way so it swaps in without shifting the layout.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeaderSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeaderSkeleton />
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { PageHeaderSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeaderSkeleton breadcrumb actions tabs={3} />
```

### Grid alignment

Set `grid` to line the header up with a `Grid`. The header content and the page body in the default slot both become grid containers, with a `Grid`'s max width, centering, and breakpoint padding, so the title lines up with each `Column`'s content. Place `Row`s in the body directly, without another `Grid`. Set `grid` to `"full-width"` to match `Grid fullWidth`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    BigNumber,
    Column,
    PageHeader,
    Row,
    Tab,
    TabContent,
    Tabs,
    Text,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PageHeader grid title="db-prod-01" subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south">
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
    <Tabs>
      <Tab label="Overview" />
      <Tab label="Metrics" />
    </Tabs>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <TabContent>
    <Row>
      <Column
        ><Tile><BigNumber labelText="Connections" value={128} /></Tile></Column
      >
      <Column
        ><Tile><BigNumber labelText="Queries per second" value={2400} /></Tile
        ></Column
      >
      <Column><Tile><BigNumber labelText="Replicas" value={3} /></Tile></Column>
    </Row>
  </TabContent>
  <TabContent>
    <Row>
      <Column><Text>Metrics charts go here.</Text></Column>
    </Row>
  </TabContent>
</PageHeader>
```

In grid mode, default-tab panels drop their inline padding so a `Row` in them lines up with the title. Container-tab panels keep it and line up with the container tab labels instead.

### Sticky

Set `sticky` to `true` to pin the header to the top of its nearest scroll container while the content below it scrolls.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Breadcrumb,
    BreadcrumbItem,
    PageHeader,
    Tab,
    TabContent,
    Tabs,
    Text,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box height="20rem" border="subtle" overflow="auto">
  <PageHeader
    sticky
    title="Databases"
    subtitle="Manage your database instances"
  >
    <svelte:fragment slot="breadcrumb">
      <Breadcrumb noTrailingSlash>
        <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbItem href="/" isCurrentPage>Databases</BreadcrumbItem>
      </Breadcrumb>
    </svelte:fragment>
    <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
      <Tabs>
        <Tab label="Overview" />
        <Tab label="Backups" />
      </Tabs>
    </svelte:fragment>
    <TabContent>
      <Box height="40rem">
        <Text
          >Scroll this area; the header and its tabs stay pinned to the top.</Text
        >
      </Box>
    </TabContent>
    <TabContent>
      <Box height="40rem">
        <Text>Backups panel. The header stays pinned here too.</Text>
      </Box>
    </TabContent>
  </PageHeader>
</Box>
```

#### Sticky offset

Set `stickyOffset` to stick the header below other fixed chrome, such as `"3rem"` to clear a UI Shell `Header`. Numbers `0`-`13` use the shared layout scale; strings accept any CSS length. Scroll the frame below: the page header stays under the app header. The example removes `Content`'s padding so the header spans the page.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Column,
    ContainedList,
    ContainedListItem,
    Content,
    Header,
    HeaderNav,
    HeaderNavItem,
    PageHeader,
    Row,
    Tab,
    TabContent,
    Tabs,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const events = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, index) => ({
    id: index,
    text: `Backup ${24 - index} completed`,
  }));
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud">
  <HeaderNav>
    <HeaderNavItem href="/" text="Resources" />
    <HeaderNavItem href="/" text="Billing" />
  </HeaderNav>
</Header>

<Content style="padding: 0">
  <PageHeader
    sticky
    stickyOffset="3rem"
    grid
    title="db-prod-01"
    subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south"
  >
    <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
      <Tabs>
        <Tab label="Activity" />
        <Tab label="Settings" />
      </Tabs>
    </svelte:fragment>
    <TabContent>
      <Row>
        <Column>
          <ContainedList labelText="Recent activity" hideLabel>
            {#each events as event (event.id)}
              <ContainedListItem>{event.text}</ContainedListItem>
            {/each}
          </ContainedList>
        </Column>
      </Row>
    </TabContent>
    <TabContent>
      <Row>
        <Column>Settings</Column>
      </Row>
    </TabContent>
  </PageHeader>
</Content>
```

#### List page

#### Dashboard

A layered header (`fill="layer-01"`) with a time range in `tabsEnd` that applies to every tab.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    BigNumber,
    Column,
    MenuButton,
    MenuItem,
    MenuItemRadioGroup,
    PageHeader,
    Row,
    Tab,
    TabContent,
    Tabs,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const timeRanges = [
    { id: "24h", text: "Last 24 hours" },
    { id: "7d", text: "Last 7 days" },
    { id: "30d", text: "Last 30 days" },
  ];

  let timeRange = "7d";

  $: timeRangeLabel = timeRanges.find((range) => range.id === timeRange)?.text;

  const metrics = [
    { label: "Requests", value: 1284000 },
    { label: "Error rate", value: 0.4, percentage: true },
    { label: "p95 latency (ms)", value: 182 },
    { label: "Active users", value: 9312 },
  ];
</script>

<PageHeader grid fill="layer-01" title="Usage" subtitle="All services">
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
    <Tabs>
      <Tab label="Overview" />
      <Tab label="By service" />
    </Tabs>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabsEnd">
    <MenuButton kind="ghost" intrinsicAlign="end" labelText={timeRangeLabel}>
      <MenuItemRadioGroup labelText="Time range" bind:selectedId={timeRange}>
        {#each timeRanges as range (range.id)}
          <MenuItem id={range.id} labelText={range.text} />
        {/each}
      </MenuItemRadioGroup>
    </MenuButton>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <TabContent>
    <Row padding>
      {#each metrics as metric (metric.label)}
        <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={4}>
          <Tile>
            <BigNumber
              labelText={metric.label}
              value={metric.value}
              percentage={metric.percentage}
            />
          </Tile>
        </Column>
      {/each}
    </Row>
  </TabContent>
  <TabContent>
    <Row padding>
      <Column>Per-service breakdown.</Column>
    </Row>
  </TabContent>
</PageHeader>
```

### Patterns

#### Responsive actions

Use `Breakpoint` to swap a `ButtonSet` for an `OverflowMenu` on small screens. Narrow the window to see the actions collapse below the `lg` breakpoint.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Breakpoint,
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
    PageHeader,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let size;

  $: compact = size === "sm" || size === "md";
</script>

<Breakpoint bind:size />

<PageHeader title="db-prod-01" subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south">
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    {#if compact}
      <OverflowMenu size="xl" flipped iconDescription="Actions">
        <OverflowMenuItem text="Restart" />
        <OverflowMenuItem text="Create backup" />
        <OverflowMenuItem text="Connect" />
      </OverflowMenu>
    {:else}
      <ButtonSet>
        <Button kind="tertiary">Restart</Button>
        <Button kind="secondary">Create backup</Button>
        <Button>Connect</Button>
      </ButtonSet>
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</PageHeader>
```

#### Tabs in the URL

Bind the header's `Tabs` to `queryParam` so the selected tab survives a reload and can be linked to. The body panels follow the selection as usual.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Column,
    PageHeader,
    queryParam,
    Row,
    Tab,
    TabContent,
    Tabs,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const tabs = [
    { id: "overview", label: "Overview" },
    { id: "backups", label: "Backups" },
    { id: "settings", label: "Settings" },
  ];

  const selectedTab = queryParam("tab", {
    defaultValue: tabs[0].id,
    parse: (id) => (tabs.some((tab) => tab.id === id) ? id : undefined),
  });
</script>

<PageHeader grid title="db-prod-01" subtitle="PostgreSQL 16 · us-south">
  <svelte:fragment slot="tabs">
    <Tabs bind:selectedId={$selectedTab}>
      {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
        <Tab id={tab.id} label={tab.label} />
      {/each}
    </Tabs>
  </svelte:fragment>
  {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
    <TabContent>
      <Row padding>
        <Column>{tab.label} content</Column>
      </Row>
    </TabContent>
  {/each}
</PageHeader>
```

---

| `subtitle` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the page subtitle. | _undefined_ |

Reuses<br />`Box`'s own `position="sticky"` and `top` -- see `Box.svelte`. There is<br />no collapse-on-scroll animation in this version. | `false` |

Numbers `0`-`13`<br />use the shared layout scale; strings accept any CSS length. | `0` |

| `size` | `"default" \| "sm"` | Specify the header size. `"sm"` uses a smaller title and tighter<br />vertical spacing, for nested or detail pages. | `"default"` |

## Pagination

### Basic

Create a basic pagination component with default page size options. The default size is medium.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to control the height. The default is medium.

#### Extra-small

Set `size` to `"xs"` to pair pagination with a compact data table.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination size="xs" totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />
```

#### Small

Set `size` to `"sm"` for a small pagination.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination size="sm" totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />
```

#### Large

Set `size` to `"lg"` for a large pagination.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination size="lg" totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />
```

### Page and page size

Configure the current page, and the available and default page sizes.

#### Current page

Set the current page with `page`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={102} page={4} />
```

#### Query string

Keep the page and page size in the URL so a reload or shared link lands on the same page. `queryParam` returns a store mirrored to a query parameter; bind `page` and `pageSize` to one each. Changes replace the current history entry, and other query parameters are preserved. `Pagination` clamps pages above the last one but not below 1, so `parse` rejects those. Default values remove their parameter. In an app with a router, pass the router's navigation API as `replace`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination, queryParam } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const pageSizes = [10, 15, 20];

  const page = queryParam("page", {
    defaultValue: 1,
    parse: (raw) => {
      const value = Number(raw);
      return Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 1 ? value : undefined;
    },
  });

  const pageSize = queryParam("size", {
    defaultValue: pageSizes[0],
    parse: (raw) => pageSizes.find((size) => size === Number(raw)),
  });
</script>

<Pagination
  totalItems={102}
  {pageSizes}
  bind:page={$page}
  bind:pageSize={$pageSize}
/>
```

#### Custom sizes

Specify custom page sizes and set a default page size. When the user picks a new size, `page` is recalculated so the first item that was visible stays on screen.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={102} pageSizes={[16, 36, 99]} pageSize={36} />
```

#### Dynamic sizes

Set `dynamicPageSizes` to hide page sizes larger than needed to display all items on one page.

For example, with 9 total items and page sizes of `[5, 10, 15]`, only 5 and 10 appear because 10 already exceeds the total.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={9} pageSizes={[5, 10, 15]} dynamicPageSizes />
```

#### Remember the page size

`pageSize` holds no state of its own between page loads. Bind it to [`LocalStorage`](/components/LocalStorage) so a size the user picks--say, showing 50 rows instead of 10--survives a refresh. Include the stored value in `pageSizes`, or it won't appear in the select.

```svelte
<script>
  import { LocalStorage, Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let pageSize = 10;
</script>

<LocalStorage key="pagination-page-size" bind:value={pageSize} />

<Pagination totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 20, 50]} bind:pageSize />
```

### Unknown pages

Set `pagesUnknown` when the total page count is unknown, such as with cursor-based APIs. The item range renders without a total, and the forward button is not constrained by totalItems.

Because the component cannot detect the last page, bind to `page` and toggle `forwardButtonDisabled` when there is no more data to load. The back button is disabled automatically once `page` reaches `1`; override `backButtonDisabled` the same way if the consumer needs equivalent manual control over the back button.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  // Simulate a cursor-based API where the total is unknown.
  const LAST_PAGE = 5;

  let page = 1;
  let pageSize = 10;

  $: forwardButtonDisabled = page >= LAST_PAGE;
</script>

<Pagination pagesUnknown bind:page bind:pageSize {forwardButtonDisabled} />
```

#### Custom item and page text

Because the total is unknown, this mode falls back to `itemText` and `pageText` instead of `itemRangeText` and `pageRangeText`, since there's no total to describe. Override either to change the wording.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination
  pagesUnknown
  itemText={(min, max) => `Showing ${min}-${max}`}
  pageText={(page) => `Page ${page}`}
/>
```

### Page window

The page-number dropdown uses native `<option>` elements, derived from `totalItems`. For large datasets, use `pageWindow` to cap how many options are rendered (default 1000).

This example also overrides `itemRangeText` and `pageRangeText` to format the item and page counts compactly (for example, `100k` instead of `100,000`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const formatNumber = (value) => {
    return Intl.NumberFormat("en", { notation: "compact" })
      .format(value)
      .toLowerCase();
  };
</script>

<Pagination
  totalItems={100_000}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  itemRangeText={(min, max, total) =>
    `${formatNumber(min)}-${formatNumber(max)} of ${formatNumber(total)} items`}
  pageRangeText={(_current, total) => `of ${formatNumber(total)} pages`}
/>
```

### Page number input

Set `pageInputType` to `"input"` to replace the page select with a number input. Use this for large page counts so users can jump to any page, including ones outside the windowed select options. It has no effect with `pagesUnknown`, which shows no page control.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination
  totalItems={100_000}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  pageInputType="input"
/>
```

### Custom page select

Use the `pageSelect` slot to replace the default page-number `Select` with your own control. The slot exposes `currentPage`, `totalPages`, `currentPageSize`, and `selectLabelText` for display; bind `page` on `Pagination` itself and set it from within the slot to navigate.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput, Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let page = 1;
</script>

<Pagination bind:page totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}>
  <svelte:fragment slot="pageSelect" let:totalPages let:selectLabelText>
    <NumberInput
      size="sm"
      hideLabel
      hideSteppers
      labelText={selectLabelText}
      min={1}
      max={totalPages}
      bind:value={page}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</Pagination>
```

### Simple

Set `simple` for a compact previous/next control with page status text. Useful in toolbars and cards.

The example below also overrides `pageText` to show only the page number, omitting the default `"page "` prefix.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Pagination,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Toolbar size="sm">
  <ToolbarContent>
    <Pagination
      simple
      size="sm"
      totalItems={102}
      pageText={(page) => `${page.toLocaleString()}`}
    />
  </ToolbarContent>
</Toolbar>
```

### Custom text

Override the button tooltips and items-per-page label independently of the total and item text overrides above.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination
  totalItems={102}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  forwardText="Next"
  backwardText="Previous"
  itemsPerPageText="Rows per page:"
/>
```

### Hidden controls

Hide individual pagination controls.

#### Page input

Disable the page input with `pageInputDisabled`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={102} pageInputDisabled />
```

#### Page size

Disable the page size selector with `pageSizeInputDisabled`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={102} pageSizeInputDisabled />
```

### Disabled

Set `disabled` to `true` to disable the entire pagination, including the nav buttons and both selects.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination disabled totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />
```

### Events

Respond to page and page-size changes.

#### Change

Use `on:change` to listen for direct user interaction--the previous/next buttons, or the page and page-size selects. The event detail includes whichever value changed; a page-size change includes both `pageSize` and the recalculated `page`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination
  totalItems={102}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // { page: number } | { pageSize: number, page: number }
/>
```

#### Update

Use `on:update` to listen for every change to `page` or `pageSize`, including programmatic updates from outside the component (for example, through `bind:page`). Unlike `change`, this fires regardless of whether the update came from user interaction, and the detail always includes both values.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination
  totalItems={102}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  on:update={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // { page: number, pageSize: number }
/>
```

#### Button clicks

Use `on:click:button--previous` and `on:click:button--next` to listen specifically for previous and next button clicks, separate from the page and page-size selects. Both dispatch the resulting page number.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination
  totalItems={102}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  on:click:button--previous={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // { page: number }
  on:click:button--next={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // { page: number }
/>
```

```svelte
<PaginationSkeleton />
```

```svelte
<PaginationSkeleton size="xs" />
```

### Component API

#### `Pagination` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` (Reactive) | `number` | Specify the current page index. | `1` |
| `pageSize` (Reactive) | `number` | Specify the number of items to display in a page. | `10` |
| `totalItems` | `number` | Specify the total number of items | `0` |
| `pageWindow` | `number` | If `totalItems` is a large number, it can affect the<br />rendering performance of this component since its value<br />is used to calculate the number of pages in the native<br />select dropdown. This value creates a small window of<br />pages rendered around the current page. By default,<br />a maximum of 1000 page `<option>` elements are rendered. | `1000` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the pagination | `false` |
| `forwardText` | `string` | Specify the forward button text | `"Next page"` |
| `forwardTextTooltipPosition` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | Specify the tooltip position for the forward button. | `"top"` |
| `backwardText` | `string` | Specify the backward button text | `"Previous page"` |
| `backwardTextTooltipPosition` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | Specify the tooltip position for the backward button. | `"top"` |
| `itemsPerPageText` | `string` | Specify the items per page text | `"Items per page:"` |
| `itemText` | `(min: number, max: number) => string` | Override the item text. | `(min, max) => `${min.toLocaleString()}-${max.toLocaleString()} item${max === 1 ? "" : "s"}`` |
| `itemRangeText` | `(min: number, max: number, total: number) => string` | Override the item range text.<br />If overridden, the custom function must handle `total <= 0` itself. | _undefined_ |
| `pageInputDisabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the page input | `false` |
| `pageInputType` | `"select" \| "input"` | Specify how the page number is entered.<br />Use `"input"` for large page counts so users can jump to pages<br />outside the windowed select options from `pageWindow`.<br />Has no effect when `pagesUnknown` is `true`, which shows no page control. | `"select"` |
| `pageSizeInputDisabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the page size input | `false` |
| `simple` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for a compact prev/next control with page status text.<br />Hides the page size and page selects. Suited to toolbars and cards. | `false` |
| `pageSizes` | `ReadonlyArray<number>` | Specify the available page sizes. | `[10]` |
| `dynamicPageSizes` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to dynamically filter page sizes based on total items.<br />Page sizes larger than needed to display all items on a single page are hidden. | `false` |
| `pagesUnknown` | `boolean` | Set to `true` if the number of pages is unknown | `false` |
| `forwardButtonDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Override the disabled state of the forward (next page) button.<br />Intended for use with `pagesUnknown` (controlled), where the consumer<br />knows when there is no more data to load. | _undefined_ |
| `backButtonDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Override the disabled state of the backward (previous page) button.<br />Intended for use with `pagesUnknown` (controlled), where the consumer<br />manages page bounds. | _undefined_ |
| `pageText` | `(page: number) => string` | Override the page text. | `(page) => `page ${page.toLocaleString()}`` |
| `pageRangeText` | `(current: number, total: number) => string` | Override the page range text. | `(_current, total) => `of ${total.toLocaleString()} page${total === 1 ? "" : "s"}`` |
| `pageSelectLabelText` | `(total: number) => string` | Override the accessible label for the page number select.<br />The default reads "Page number, of 1 page" or "Page number, of N pages". | `(total) => `Page number, of ${total} page${total === 1 ? "" : "s"}`` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the top-level element | `uniqueId()` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | Specify the size of the pagination. | `"md"` |

#### `Pagination` slots

| Slot | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `pageSelect` | `{<br />  currentPage: number;<br />  totalPages: number;<br />  currentPageSize: number;<br />  selectLabelText: string;<br />}` |

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

A page-size change may include both `page` and<br />`pageSize` together, since the current page is recalculated to keep<br />the same items in view. |
| `on:click:button--next` | `{<br />  page: number;<br />}` | Dispatched when the user clicks the next page button. |
| `on:click:button--previous` | `{<br />  page: number;<br />}` | Dispatched when the user clicks the previous page button. |
| `on:update` | `{<br />  pageSize: number;<br />  page: number;<br />}` | Dispatched reactively whenever the page or page size changes. |

## PaginationNav

### Basic

Create a basic pagination navigation with default settings.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PaginationNav />
```

### Reactive

Bind to `page` for the current page number.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, PaginationNav, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let page = 2;
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <PaginationNav bind:page />
  <Stack gap={4} orientation="horizontal" align="center">
    <Button
      kind="tertiary"
      size="small"
      on:click={() => (page = 1)}
      disabled={page === 0}
    >
      Set page to 1
    </Button>
    <div>
      <strong>Current page:</strong>
      {page}
    </div>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Query string

Keep the current page in the URL so it survives a reload and can be shared. `queryParam` returns a store mirrored to a query parameter; bind `page` to it. `PaginationNav` does not clamp `page`, so `parse` rejects values below 1 or above `total`. Page 1 removes the parameter. In an app with a router, pass the router's navigation API as `replace`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav, queryParam } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const total = 10;

  const page = queryParam("page", {
    defaultValue: 1,
    parse: (raw) => {
      const value = Number(raw);
      return Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 1 && value <= total
        ? value
        : undefined;
    },
  });
</script>

<PaginationNav {total} bind:page={$page} />
```

### Page count

#### Total pages

Specify the total number of pages with `total`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PaginationNav total={3} />
```

#### Visible pages

Control the number of visible page numbers with `shown`. Pages that don't fit collapse into an overflow menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PaginationNav total={100} shown={5} />
```

### Navigation buttons

The forward and backward navigation buttons can be customized independently of the page numbers.

#### Loop

Enable circular navigation between pages with `loop`. When enabled, clicking "Next" from the last page wraps to the first page, and clicking "Previous" from the first page wraps to the last page.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PaginationNav total={3} loop />
```

#### Custom text

Customize navigation button text with `forwardText` and `backwardText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PaginationNav forwardText="Next" backwardText="Previous" />
```

#### Tooltip position

Set tooltip position relative to the navigation buttons with `tooltipPosition`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PaginationNav tooltipPosition="outside" total={3} loop />
```

### Translations

Set `pageText` to name each page and `pageSelectLabelText` to name the overflow select. When the user changes the page, screen readers hear the page text followed by `pageRangeText`, as in "Page 3 of 20". Only the nav the user acted on announces it, so two navs bound to one `page` (above and below a table) announce once. A `page` set by your code is not announced. These props work like the Pagination props of the same names.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PaginationNav
  total={20}
  forwardText="Página siguiente"
  backwardText="Página anterior"
  pageText={(page) => `Página ${page}`}
  pageRangeText={(_current, total) => `de ${total}`}
  pageSelectLabelText={() => "Seleccionar página"}
/>
```

### Events

Respond to page changes and button clicks.

#### Change

Use `on:change` to listen for every user interaction--clicking a page number, an overflow menu item, or the previous/next buttons. The event detail includes the resulting page.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PaginationNav
  total={5}
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // { page: number }
/>
```

#### Button clicks

Use `on:click:button--previous` and `on:click:button--next` to listen specifically for previous and next button clicks, separate from the page numbers and overflow menu. Both dispatch the resulting page number.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PaginationNav } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PaginationNav
  total={5}
  on:click:button--previous={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // { page: number }
  on:click:button--next={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // { page: number }
/>
```

---

### Component API

#### `PaginationNav` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` (Reactive) | `number` | Specify the current page index. | `1` |
| `total` | `number` | Specify the total number of pages | `10` |
| `shown` | `number` | Specify the total number of pages to show | `10` |
| `loop` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to loop the navigation | `false` |
| `forwardText` | `string` | Specify the forward button text | `"Next page"` |
| `backwardText` | `string` | Specify the backward button text | `"Previous page"` |
| `tooltipPosition` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "outside" \| "inside"` | Set the position of the tooltip relative to the pagination buttons. | `"bottom"` |
| `pageText` | `(page: number) => string` | Override the page text, which names each page button. | `(page) => `Page ${page}`` |
| `pageRangeText` | `(current: number, total: number) => string` | Override the page range text. It follows the page text in the<br />announcement made when the page changes ("Page 3 of 10"). | `(_current, total) => `of ${total}`` |
| `pageSelectLabelText` | `(total: number) => string` | Override the accessible label for the overflow page select. | `(_total) => "Select page number"` |

#### `PaginationNav` dispatched events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on:change` | `{<br />  page: number;<br />}` | Fires after every user interaction |
| `on:click:button--next` | `{<br />  page: number;<br />}` |  |
| `on:click:button--previous` | `{<br />  page: number;<br />}` |  |

#### `PaginationNav` $$restProps

`PaginationNav` spreads `$$restProps` to the `nav` element.


## PasswordInput

### Basic

Create a basic password input with a label and placeholder.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput labelText="Password" placeholder="Enter password..." />
```

### Visibility toggle

Control the show/hide password toggle button and its tooltip. Press <kbd>Escape</kbd> to hide the tooltip without moving the pointer or focus. It shows again on the next hover or focus.

#### Value shown as text

Set `type` to `"text"` to show the password in plain text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput
  labelText="Password"
  type="text"
  placeholder="Enter password..."
  value="correct horse battery staple"
/>
```

#### Custom tooltip alignment

Place the visibility toggle's tooltip with `tooltipAlign`, which takes Popover's `align` names. It replaces `tooltipPosition` and `tooltipAlignment`, which still work and are deprecated.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput
  tooltipAlign="left-start"
  labelText="Password"
  placeholder="Enter password..."
/>
```

#### Toggle labels

Customize the toggle button's tooltip and ARIA label text with `showPasswordLabel` and `hidePasswordLabel`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput
  labelText="Password"
  placeholder="Enter password..."
  showPasswordLabel="Reveal password"
  hidePasswordLabel="Conceal password"
/>
```

#### Tooltip group

Wrap related password fields in a [TooltipGroup](/components/TooltipGroup) so their toggle tooltips hand off. Moving from one toggle to the next swaps the tooltip without a fade-in, and only one shows at a time.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput, Stack, TooltipGroup } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipGroup>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <PasswordInput
      labelText="New password"
      placeholder="Enter new password..."
    />
    <PasswordInput
      labelText="Confirm password"
      placeholder="Re-enter new password..."
    />
  </Stack>
</TooltipGroup>
```

### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to select the full value when the field receives focus.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput
  selectTextOnFocus
  labelText="Password"
  value="correct horse battery staple"
/>
```

### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput hideLabel labelText="Password" placeholder="Enter password..." />
```

### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to provide custom label content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput labelText="" placeholder="Enter password...">
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Password</strong>
</PasswordInput>
```

### Helper text

Add helper text to provide additional context or instructions.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput
  helperText="Must be at least 12 characters and include a number and symbol."
  labelText="New password"
  placeholder="Enter new password..."
/>
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <PasswordInput labelText="Password" placeholder="Enter password..." />
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to embed the label inside the field. Fluid password inputs work standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), which applies the variant automatically. The fluid variant cannot be combined with the inline variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput fluid labelText="Password" placeholder="Enter password..." />
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput
  fluid
  labelText="New password"
  placeholder="Enter new password..."
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    New password
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="Must be at least 12 characters and include a number and symbol."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</PasswordInput>
```

#### Invalid

Fluid password inputs display the error message inside the field boundary. Long messages wrap to multiple lines.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PasswordInput
  fluid
  invalid
  invalidText="Incorrect user name or password. Please verify your credentials and try again, or use the reset password link if you have forgotten your password."
  labelText="Password"
  placeholder="Enter password..."
/>
```

#### Warning

```svelte

<PasswordInput

  labelText="Password"
```


### Inside a modal

When used inside a Modal, the visibility toggle tooltip is automatically portalled to prevent clipping. Elsewhere, it opens in a portal when a container would cut it off, such as a box with `overflow: hidden`, a scroll area or a [DataTable](/components/DataTable). Set `portalTooltip` to `true` to always portal it, or to `false` to keep it in place.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal, PasswordInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Reset password</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Reset password"
  primaryButtonText="Reset password"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
>
  <PasswordInput
    labelText="New password"
    placeholder="Enter new password..."
    helperText="Must be at least 12 characters and include a number and symbol."
  />
</Modal>
```
