## PinCodeInput

### Basic

By default, four numeric segments are rendered. Typing a digit advances focus to the next segment; <kbd>Backspace</kbd> moves to the previous segment, <kbd>Delete</kbd> clears the focused segment, and <kbd>←</kbd> / <kbd>→</kbd> move between segments.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput labelText="Verification code" />
```

### Helper text

Add helper text below the input to provide additional context or instructions.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput
  labelText="Verification code"
  helperText="Enter the 4-digit code sent to your device"
/>
```

### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput hideLabel labelText="Verification code" />
```

### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link, PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput labelText="Verification code">
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Verification code (<Link href="/">resend</Link>)
  </svelte:fragment>
</PinCodeInput>
```

### Segment labels

Screen readers announce each segment as "Verification code digit 1 of 4" by default, or "character" when `type` is `"alphanumeric"`. Use `segmentLabelText` to override the label, for example to translate it. The function receives the 1-based position, the segment count, `labelText`, and `type`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput
  labelText="Código de verificación"
  segmentLabelText={(position, count) => `Dígito ${position} de ${count}`}
/>
```

### Input rules

Control how many segments render and which characters are accepted.

#### Custom length

Use `count` to set the number of segments. For example, six is common for SMS, email, and authenticator OTP flows.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput count={6} labelText="Verification code" />
```

#### Alphanumeric

The default input mode is `"numeric"`. Set `type` to `"alphanumeric"` to allow letters and digits.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput type="alphanumeric" labelText="Invite code" />
```

#### Custom pattern

Use `pattern` to override the per-character test used for typing and paste. Pass a `RegExp` or a string compiled with `new RegExp(...)`. The pattern is matched against each individual character, not the full assembled value. When `pattern` is unset, `type` selects the numeric or alphanumeric preset. `type` still sets the on-screen keyboard, so set `type="alphanumeric"` when the pattern accepts letters, as below.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput
  count={6}
  pattern={/^[0-9a-fA-F]$/}
  type="alphanumeric"
  uppercase
  labelText="Serial number"
  helperText="Enter the 6-character hex serial"
/>
```

#### Uppercase display

Set `uppercase` to `true` to display characters in uppercase. The bound value and code retain the original casing.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput type="alphanumeric" uppercase labelText="Invite code" />
```

### Masked

Set `mask` to `true` to obscure the entered characters. Each segment is masked while it is not focused and reveals its character when focused.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput mask labelText="Security code" />
```

### Placeholder

Non-fluid pin code inputs do not show a placeholder by default. Set `placeholder` to hint at empty segments and indicate expected length.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput placeholder="0" labelText="Verification code" />
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to control the segment height. The default is `md`.

#### Extra-small

Set `size` to `"xs"` to render extra-small segments.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput size="xs" labelText="Verification code" />
```

#### Small

Set `size` to `"sm"` to render small segments.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput size="sm" labelText="Verification code" />
```

#### Extra-large

Set `size` to `"xl"` to render extra-large segments.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput size="xl" labelText="Verification code" />
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <PinCodeInput labelText="Verification code" />
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to `true` to select a segment's value when it receives focus. Without this prop, browsers typically select the value only when the segment receives keyboard focus (for example, via <kbd>Tab</kbd>), not on click.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput selectTextOnFocus labelText="Verification code" />
```

### Events

Respond to edits, completion, clearing, and paste or autofill.

#### Edits, completion, and clearing

The component emits the following events:

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| `on:change` | Any edit (type, paste, delete). |
| `on:complete` | All segments become filled. This does not fire on mount with a prefilled value, but fires after user interaction fills every segment. |
| `on:clear` | All segments are emptied. |

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput
  labelText="Verification code"
  on:complete={(e) => console.log("complete", e.detail)}
  on:change={(e) => console.log("change", e.detail)}
  on:clear={() => console.log("clear")}
/>
```

#### Paste and autofill

Paste a full code into any segment to fill all segments at once. A partial paste fills from the focused segment forward. Non-matching characters are ignored. The `on:paste` event fires with the clipboard value (whitespace stripped) before segments are updated.

OS and password-manager autofill that inserts the whole code into one segment is distributed the same way. The first segment also sets `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, which lets browsers and mobile OSes offer a one-time-code autofill suggestion (for example, from an incoming SMS) for it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput
  labelText="Verification code"
  on:paste={(e) => console.log("paste", e.detail)}
/>
```

### Form name

Set `name` so the assembled code participates in native form submission (for example SvelteKit form actions and `FormData`). A hidden input mirrors `value`. `required` stays on each segment, so the browser blocks submission until every segment is filled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Form, PinCodeInput, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form method="POST" action="?/verify">
  <PinCodeInput name="code" required count={6} labelText="Verification code" />
  <Button type="submit">Verify</Button>
</Form>
```

### States

Reflect validation and interaction states.

#### Invalid

Set `invalid` to `true` and provide `invalidText` to describe the error. Invalid takes precedence over the [warning state](#warning) when both are set.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput
  invalid
  value="018"
  invalidText="The code you entered is incorrect"
  labelText="Verification code"
/>
```

#### Warning

Set `warn` to `true` and provide `warnText` to surface a non-blocking warning.

```svelte
<script>

</script>

  warn
  value="018"
  warnText="This code is about to expire"
  labelText="Verification code"
/>
```

#### Disabled

Set `disabled` to `true` to disable every segment.

```svelte
<script>

```

#### Read-only

Set `readonly` to `true` to display a code that cannot be edited.

```svelte
</script>

<PinCodeInputSkeleton hideLabel />
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to `true` to use the fluid variant, which embeds the label inside the field. Fluid pin code inputs can be used standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), where the fluid variant is applied automatically. Because fluid segments use an underline affordance rather than boxed fields, empty segments show a placeholder by default so the expected length remains visible. Set `placeholder=""` to remove it, or pass any other string to override the default in either variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput fluid labelText="Verification code" />
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput fluid labelText="Verification code">
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Verification code
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="Enter the code sent to your device."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</PinCodeInput>
```

#### Invalid

Fluid pin code inputs display the error message inside the field boundary. Long messages wrap to multiple lines. Invalid takes precedence over the [warning state](#warning) when both are set.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<PinCodeInput
  fluid
  invalid
  value="018"
  invalidText="The code you entered is incorrect. Please check the message we sent to your device and try again, or request a new code if it has expired."
  labelText="Verification code"
/>
```

Fluid pin code inputs display the warning message inside the field boundary. Long messages wrap to multiple lines.

```svelte
  fluid
```

### Bindable value

Bind to `value` for the concatenated code, to `complete` when every segment is filled, or to `code` for per-segment characters. Useful for controlled UI state; for OTP submission, prefer the dispatched change and complete payloads instead of branching on bound values locally.

```svelte
<script>
  import { PinCodeInput, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
  let complete = false;
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <PinCodeInput
    count={4}
    bind:value
    bind:complete
    labelText="Verification code"
  />
  <div>value: {JSON.stringify(value)}</div>
  <div>complete: {complete}</div>
</Stack>
```

### Programmatic usage

Use `bind:this` to obtain a reference to the component instance and call its accessor methods.

| Method | Description | Signature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `focusFirstInput` | Focus the first segment. | `(options?: { selectTextOnFocus?: boolean }) => void` |
| `focusLastInput` | Focus the last segment. | `(options?: { selectTextOnFocus?: boolean }) => void` |
| `focusNextEmptyInput` | Focus the first empty segment, or the last if all are filled. | `(options?: { selectTextOnFocus?: boolean }) => void` |
| `focusNext` | Focus the next segment from the active or last focused one; does not wrap at the last segment. Uses the last focused segment when focus has moved elsewhere (for example, a submit button). | `(options?: { selectTextOnFocus?: boolean }) => void` |
| `clear` | Clear all segments. Focus is not moved by default; pass `{ focus: true }` to focus the first segment afterward. | `(options?: { focus?: boolean }) => void` |

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    PinCodeInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let pinCodeInput;
  let value = "018";
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <PinCodeInput
    bind:this={pinCodeInput}
    bind:value
    labelText="Verification code"
  />
  <div>value: {JSON.stringify(value)}</div>
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <ButtonSet>
      <Button
        kind="tertiary"
        size="small"
        on:click={() => pinCodeInput?.focusFirstInput()}
      >
        Focus first
      </Button>
      <Button
        kind="tertiary"
        size="small"
        on:click={() => pinCodeInput?.focusLastInput()}
      >
        Focus last
      </Button>
      <Button
        kind="tertiary"
        size="small"
        on:click={() => pinCodeInput?.focusNextEmptyInput()}
      >
        Focus next empty
      </Button>
      <Button
        kind="tertiary"
        size="small"
        on:click={() => pinCodeInput?.focusNext()}
      >
        Focus next
      </Button>
      <Button
        kind="tertiary"
        size="small"
        on:click={() =>
          pinCodeInput?.focusFirstInput({ selectTextOnFocus: true })}
      >
        Focus first (select)
      </Button>
    </ButtonSet>
    <ButtonSet>
      <Button
        kind="tertiary"
        size="small"
        on:click={() => pinCodeInput?.clear()}
      >
        Clear
      </Button>
      <Button
        kind="tertiary"
        size="small"
        on:click={() => pinCodeInput?.clear({ focus: true })}
      >
        Clear (focus)
      </Button>
    </ButtonSet>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### UX example

End-to-end flow using the complete event: normalize the payload, simulate an async verification request, then set invalid / invalidText or show success from the response.

The hardcoded expected code is for demo purposes only. In production, POST the submitted value to your verification API and derive UI state from the server response.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    InlineLoading,
    InlineNotification,
    PinCodeInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import { onMount } from "svelte";

  // For demo purposes only: NEVER perform local verification of OTP codes.
  const EXPECTED_CODE = "A1B2";
  const VERIFY_DELAY_MS = 400;

  function normalize(value) {
    return value.toUpperCase().replace(/\s/g, "");
  }

  let pinCodeInput;
  let verifyTimeout;
  let loading = $state(false);
  let invalid = $state(false);
  let invalidText = $state("");
  let verified = $state(false);

  function clearVerificationState() {
    if (verifyTimeout) clearTimeout(verifyTimeout);
    loading = false;
    invalid = false;
    invalidText = "";
    verified = false;
  }

  function handleComplete(event) {
    clearVerificationState();
    loading = true;

    verifyTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
      loading = false;

      if (normalize(event.detail.value) === normalize(EXPECTED_CODE)) {
        verified = true;
      } else {
        invalid = true;
        invalidText = "The code you entered is incorrect";
      }
    }, VERIFY_DELAY_MS);
  }

  function resetVerification() {
    clearVerificationState();
    pinCodeInput?.clear({ focus: true });
  }

  function handleChange() {
    if (loading) return;
    if (!invalid && !verified) return;
    invalid = false;
    invalidText = "";
    verified = false;
  }

  onMount(() => {
    return () => {
      if (verifyTimeout) clearTimeout(verifyTimeout);
    };
  });
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <PinCodeInput
    bind:this={pinCodeInput}
    type="alphanumeric"
    uppercase
    count={EXPECTED_CODE.length}
    labelText="Invite code"
    helperText="Enter the code sent to your email (try {EXPECTED_CODE})"
    disabled={loading}
    {invalid}
    {invalidText}
    on:complete={handleComplete}
    on:change={handleChange}
    on:clear={clearVerificationState}
  />

  {#if loading}
    <InlineLoading status="active" description="Verifying code..." />
  {:else if verified}
    <InlineNotification
      kind="success"
      title="Code verified"
      subtitle="Your invite code was accepted."
      hideCloseButton
      lowContrast
    />
  {/if}

  <ButtonSet>
    <Button
      kind="tertiary"
      disabled={!verified && !invalid}
      on:click={resetVerification}
    >
      Reset
    </Button>
  </ButtonSet>
</Stack>
```

---

### Component API

#### `PinCodeInput` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `string` | The concatenated code value.<br /><br />Derived from `code` (i.e. `code.join("")`); bind to read the assembled<br />value. When `complete` is `true`, its length equals `count`. Each<br />character matches `pattern` when set, otherwise the active `type`:<br />`0-9` for `"numeric"`, `a-zA-Z0-9` for `"alphanumeric"`. Original casing<br />is preserved regardless of `uppercase`, which only affects the visual<br />rendering. | `""` |
| `code` (Reactive) | `string[]` | The individual segment characters.<br /><br />`code` is the source of truth; its length tracks `count`. Each element is<br />either an empty string (unfilled segment) or a single character matching<br />`pattern` when set, otherwise the active `type`: `0-9` for `"numeric"`,<br />`a-zA-Z0-9` for `"alphanumeric"`.<br />Follows the segments when the owning form resets. | `[]` |
| `complete` (Reactive) | `boolean` | `true` when every segment is filled. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the outer element. | `null` |
| `count` | `number` | Specify the number of input segments to render | `4` |
| `type` | `"numeric" \| "alphanumeric"` | Specify the type of allowed characters.<br /><br />`"numeric"` allows `0-9`; `"alphanumeric"` allows `a-z`, `A-Z`, `0-9`.<br />When `pattern` is set, `pattern` decides which characters are accepted,<br />and `type` still sets each segment's `inputmode` (`"numeric"` shows a<br />numeric keypad on touch devices). | `"numeric"` |
| `pattern` | `RegExp \| string \| undefined` | Override the per-character validation used for typing and paste.<br /><br />Accepts a `RegExp` or a string compiled with `new RegExp(...)`. The<br />pattern is tested against each individual character, not the full<br />assembled value. When unset, `type` selects the preset (`"numeric"` or<br />`"alphanumeric"`). Set `type` to `"alphanumeric"` when the pattern<br />accepts letters, so touch keyboards offer them. | _undefined_ |
| `uppercase` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually display the characters in uppercase<br />while retaining the original casing of `value` and `code`.<br /><br />Only affects letters, so it is most useful with `type="alphanumeric"`. | `false` |
| `mask` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to mask the segments.<br /><br />Each segment is masked when it is not focused, revealing its character<br />only while focused. | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the input | `false` |
| `size` | `"default" \| "xs" \| "sm" \| "xl" \| "md" \| "lg" \| undefined` | Set the size of the input.<br />Inherits the parent `Form` size when unset, otherwise `"default"`.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (`"default"`) and `"lg"` (`"xl"`). | `"default"` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `placeholder` | `string \| undefined` | Placeholder shown in empty segments.<br /><br />Defaults to a placeholder in the fluid variant; non-fluid segments have no<br />placeholder unless this prop is set. | _undefined_ |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `required` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to mark the field as required | `false` |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a name attribute for native form participation.<br /><br />When set, a hidden input mirrors the assembled `value` so the code is<br />included in FormData / form submissions. `required` stays on each<br />segment, since hidden inputs take no part in constraint validation. | _undefined_ |
| `form` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the id of a form element outside the component to associate the<br />segments and the hidden `name` input with. | _undefined_ |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the read-only variant | `false` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`. | `false` |
| `selectTextOnFocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to select a segment's value when it receives focus,<br />including on click. Without this prop, browsers typically select the<br />value only on keyboard focus (for example, via Tab). | `false` |
| `segmentLabelText` | `(position: number, count: number, labelText: string, type: "numeric" \| "alphanumeric") => string` | Override the accessible label of each segment.<br /><br />`position` is 1-based. The default returns, for example,<br />`"Verification code digit 1 of 4"`, using `"Pin code"` when `labelText`<br />is empty and `"character"` instead of `"digit"` when `type` is<br />`"alphanumeric"`. | `(<br />  position,<br />  count,<br />  labelText,<br />  type,<br />) =><br />  `${labelText \|\| "Pin code"} ${type === "numeric" ? "digit" : "character"} ${position} of ${count}`` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the input group | `uniqueId()` |
| `focusFirstInput` | `(options?: { selectTextOnFocus?: boolean }) => void` | Focus the first input segment. | _undefined_ |
| `focusLastInput` | `(options?: { selectTextOnFocus?: boolean }) => void` | Focus the last input segment. | _undefined_ |
| `focusNextEmptyInput` | `(options?: { selectTextOnFocus?: boolean }) => void` | Focus the first empty input segment, or the last if all are filled. | _undefined_ |
| `focusNext` | `(options?: { selectTextOnFocus?: boolean }) => void` | Focus the next input segment from the currently focused segment.<br />Does not wrap when the last segment is focused. | _undefined_ |
| `clear` | `(options?: { focus?: boolean }) => void` | Clear all segments programmatically.<br />By default, focus is not moved. Set `options.focus` to `true` to focus the first segment after clearing. | _undefined_ |

## Popover

### Basic

Create a basic popover with absolute positioning.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover open>Content</Popover>
</div>
```

### Placement

Position the popover relative to its trigger.

#### Relative position

Position the popover relative to its parent with `relative`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover relative open>Content</Popover>
</div>
```

#### Alignment

Customize popover alignment with `align`. Valid values include `"top"`, `"top-start"`, `"top-end"`, `"bottom"`, `"bottom-start"`, `"bottom-end"`, `"left"`, `"left-start"`, `"left-end"`, `"right"`, `"right-start"`, and `"right-end"`.

The default is top. These are the Carbon v11 names. The older names (`"top-left"`, `"left-bottom"`, and so on) still work and give the same placement. In RTL, `start` and `end` on the top and bottom swap sides, as in floating-ui, while the older names keep their physical side. See [LayoutDirection](/components/LayoutDirection#tooltips-and-popovers).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={10}>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="top-start">top-start</Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="top-end">top-end</Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="bottom">bottom</Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="bottom-start">bottom-start</Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="bottom-end">
      <div>bottom-end</div>
    </Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="left">left</Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="left-end">left-end</Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="left-start">left-start</Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="right">right</Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="right-end">right-end</Popover>
  </div>
  <div>
    Parent
    <Popover open align="right-start">right-start</Popover>
  </div>
</Stack>
```

### Caret

Add a caret indicator with `caret`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover caret open>Content</Popover>
</div>
```

#### Custom alignment

By default, the caret aligns to top. See [Alignment](#alignment) for all valid values.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover caret align="top-start" open>Content</Popover>
</div>
```

#### Stay in view

An open popover that would run past the window takes the other side, or the other start or end alignment, when it fits better there. One that a container would cut off, such as a box with `overflow: hidden` or a scroll area, opens in a portal for that open.

Set `portalPopover` to `true` to always render the popover in a portal, or to `false` to keep it in place. A portalled popover leaves its container in the DOM, so CSS that targets it as a descendant of the container does not match it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box padding={5} border="subtle" maxWidth="12rem" overflow="hidden">
  <Box position="relative">
    Parent
    <Popover open caret align="bottom-start">
      Content that the box would cut off
    </Popover>
  </Box>
</Box>
```

### Variants

Appearance variants for different backgrounds.

#### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <div>
      Parent
      <Popover open>Content</Popover>
    </div>
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

#### Without a drop shadow

The popover casts a drop shadow by default. Set `dropShadow` to `false` to remove it, for example on a surface that already separates it from the page.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover caret dropShadow={false} open>Content</Popover>
</div>
```

#### Border

Set `border` to `true` to draw a 1px border around the popover and its caret.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover caret border open>Content</Popover>
</div>
```

#### High contrast

Enable the high contrast variant for improved visibility.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover highContrast open>Content</Popover>
</div>
```

### Dismissal

Close the popover automatically, and listen for outside-click interactions.

#### Close on outside click

Close the popover when clicking outside with `closeOnOutsideClick`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover
    open
    closeOnOutsideClick
    on:click:outside={() => {
      console.log("on:click:outside");
    }}
  >
    Content
  </Popover>
</div>
```

#### Close on Escape

Close the popover when pressing <kbd>Escape</kbd> with `closeOnEscape`. The listener is attached to the window, so <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes the popover even when focus is on the trigger rather than inside the popover content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover
    open
    closeOnEscape
    on:close={() => {
      console.log("on:close");
    }}
  >
    Content
  </Popover>
</div>
```

#### Events

`on:click:outside` fires whenever a click lands outside the popover, with `event.detail.target` set to the clicked element, regardless of whether `closeOnOutsideClick` is set. `on:close` fires when the popover closes itself in response to `closeOnOutsideClick` or `closeOnEscape`, with `event.detail.trigger` set to `"outside-click"` or `"escape-key"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  Parent
  <Popover
    open
    closeOnOutsideClick
    closeOnEscape
    on:click:outside={(e) => console.log("on:click:outside", e.detail)}
    on:close={(e) => console.log("on:close", e.detail)}
  >
    Content
  </Popover>
</div>
```

#### Custom panels

Use the `dismiss` action on a panel you build yourself to close it when the user clicks outside. Set `enabled` to the open state so the action adds the `window` listener only while the panel is open, and a closed panel costs nothing. Pass `type: "click"` with a `handler` that closes the panel when the click lands outside it.

The panel's own trigger is also outside the panel, so the handler ignores clicks on the trigger and lets the trigger toggle the state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Button, dismiss, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let trigger;
  let panel;

  function handleOutsideClick(event) {
    if (
      panel &&
      !panel.contains(event.target) &&
      !trigger.contains(event.target)
    ) {
      open = false;
    }
  }
</script>

<Box bind:ref={trigger} display="inline-flex">
  <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
    Filter by region
  </Button>
</Box>

{#if open}
  <Box marginTop={3} maxWidth="20rem">
    <div
      bind:this={panel}
      use:dismiss={{
        enabled: open,
        type: "click",
        handler: handleOutsideClick,
      }}
    >
      <Tile>
        <p>US East (N. Virginia)</p>
        <p>EU West (Frankfurt)</p>
        <p>Asia Pacific (Tokyo)</p>
      </Tile>
    </div>
  </Box>
{/if}
```

Pass `listeners` to attach more than one listener, each with its own `type` and `handler`. Combine a `keydown` listener with a `click` listener to close the panel on <kbd>Escape</kbd> and on an outside click. Listeners with the same `type` and options share one `window` listener across every control on the page.

The action registers its listeners after a macrotask, not synchronously. Enabling it inside a click, such as a button that sets `open` to `true`, therefore never dismisses the panel with the same click that opened it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Button, dismiss, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let trigger;
  let panel;

  function handleKeydown(event) {
    if (event.key === "Escape") open = false;
  }

  function handleClick(event) {
    if (
      panel &&
      !panel.contains(event.target) &&
      !trigger.contains(event.target)
    ) {
      open = false;
    }
  }
</script>

<Box bind:ref={trigger} display="inline-flex">
  <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
    Open notifications
  </Button>
</Box>

{#if open}
  <Box marginTop={3} maxWidth="20rem">
    <div
      bind:this={panel}
      use:dismiss={{
        enabled: open,
        listeners: [
          { type: "keydown", handler: handleKeydown },
          { type: "click", handler: handleClick },
        ],
      }}
    >
      <Tile>
        <p>Build 4821 passed on main.</p>
        <p>Deployment to staging is waiting for approval.</p>
      </Tile>
    </div>
  </Box>
{/if}
```

### External element

Manage open state with an external element, like a button, using `open`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Button, Popover } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
  let ref = null;
</script>

<Box bind:ref position="relative">
  <Button on:click={() => (open = !open)}>Quick settings</Button>
  <Popover
    bind:open
    align="bottom-left"
    on:click:outside={({ detail }) => {
      console.log("on:click:outside");
      open = ref.contains(detail.target);
    }}
  >
    Adjust table density and default sort order for this workspace.
  </Popover>
</Box>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Popover` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to display the popover. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the popover element.<br />In a portal, this is the portalled element. | `null` |
| `closeOnOutsideClick` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to close the popover on an outside click | `false` |
| `closeOnEscape` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to close the popover on the Escape key | `false` |
| `caret` | `boolean` | Set to `true` render a caret | `false` |
| `align` | `"top" \| "top-start" \| "top-end" \| "bottom" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-end" \| "left" \| "left-start" \| "left-end" \| "right" \| "right-start" \| "right-end" \| "top-left" \| "top-right" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-right" \| "left-bottom" \| "left-top" \| "right-bottom" \| "right-top"` | Specify the alignment of the caret.<br />Prefer the Carbon v11 names (`"top-start"`, `"left-end"`, and so on).<br />On the top and bottom, `start` and `end` name inline sides, so they swap<br />under `dir="rtl"`. The older names (`"top-left"`, `"left-bottom"`, and so<br />on) still work and name physical sides, so they keep their place in RTL. | `"top"` |
| `dropShadow` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to remove the drop shadow | `true` |
| `border` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to draw a 1px border around the popover and its caret | `false` |
| `highContrast` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the high contrast variant | `false` |
| `relative` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use a relative position | `false` |
| `portalPopover` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to always render the popover in a portal, or `false` to<br />keep it in place. Left unset, it renders in place and moves to a portal<br />for an open when a box around it (`overflow` other than `visible`) would<br />cut it off. A `relative` popover stays in place. | _undefined_ |

#### `Popover` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Popover` dispatched events

| Event | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `on:click:outside` | `{<br />  target: HTMLElement;<br />}` |
| `on:close` | `{<br />  trigger:<br />    "outside-click" \| "escape-key";<br />}` |

#### `Popover` $$restProps

`Popover` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## Portal

### Basic

Render content in a portal -- useful for modals, tooltips, and menus that need to escape parent containers. For anchored, positioned content (dropdowns, popovers, overflow menus), use [FloatingPortal](/components/FloatingPortal) instead.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Portal } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div>
  <div>Rendered inside the dashboard panel</div>
  <br />
  <Portal>Rendered outside the panel, directly in document.body</Portal>
</div>
```

### Multiple portals

Each portal instance is independent, creating its own element in document.body, and is automatically cleaned up when removed.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ButtonSet, Portal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let showPortal1 = false;
  let showPortal2 = false;
</script>

<ButtonSet>
  <Button on:click={() => (showPortal1 = !showPortal1)}>
    {showPortal1 ? "Hide system alert" : "Show system alert"}
  </Button>
  <Button on:click={() => (showPortal2 = !showPortal2)}>
    {showPortal2 ? "Hide maintenance notice" : "Show maintenance notice"}
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>

{#if showPortal1}
  <Portal>System alert: API latency is elevated</Portal>
{/if}

{#if showPortal2}
  <Portal>Maintenance notice: scheduled downtime at 2:00 AM UTC</Portal>
{/if}
```

### Custom tag

The portal renders a div by default. Set `tag` to specify a custom HTML element.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Portal } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Portal tag="section">
  Rendered as a section element for the incident banner.
</Portal>
```

### Modal with portal

Wrap the modal in a portal to escape parent containers with overflow hidden or z-index stacking contexts. This ensures the modal appears above all content and is not clipped by parent boundaries.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Button, Modal, Portal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Box
  display="flex"
  direction="column"
  gap={5}
  overflow="hidden"
  position="relative"
  height="200px"
  border="subtle"
  borderStyle="dashed"
  padding={5}
>
  <p>
    This container hides overflowing content. Without a portal, the modal would
    be clipped.
  </p>
  <div>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Deploy build #4213</Button>
  </div>
  <Portal>
    <Modal
      bind:open
      modalHeading="Confirm deployment"
      primaryButtonText="Deploy"
      secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
      on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
    >
      <p>
        Deploying build #4213 to production cannot be undone. This modal is
        rendered in a portal, escaping the parent container's overflow
        constraints and ensuring it appears above all other content.
      </p>
    </Modal>
  </Portal>
</Box>
```

### Custom target

Mount the portal into a specific DOM element instead of document.body with `target`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Portal, Stack, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let target = null;
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <Tile>
    <div>Widget declared in the sidebar.</div>
    <Portal {target}><strong>3 incidents open</strong></Portal>
  </Tile>
  <Tile>
    <div bind:this={target}>
      But mounted into the dashboard's main panel via <code>target</code>.
    </div>
  </Tile>
</Stack>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Portal` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLElement` | Obtain a reference to the portal element. | `null` |
| `tag` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` | Specify the tag name. | `"div"` |
| `target` | `Element \| null` | Specify the DOM element to mount the portal into.<br />Defaults to `document.body`. | `null` |

#### `Portal` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Portal` $$restProps

`Portal` spreads `$$restProps` to the `svelte:element` element.


## ProgressBar

### Basic

Create an indeterminate progress bar that continuously animates. A progress bar is indeterminate when `value` is left `undefined` while `status` is `"active"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar helperText="Checking for updates..." />
```

### Value

#### Percentage

Display progress as a percentage with `value`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar
  value={40}
  labelText="Upload status"
  helperText="40 MB of 100 MB"
/>
```

#### Custom max value

Set a custom maximum value for the progress bar.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar
  value={40}
  max={200}
  labelText="Storage used"
  helperText="40 GB of 200 GB"
/>
```

#### Value text

Set `valueText` to render a right-aligned value in the label row. Format it yourself; `valueText` also becomes the progress bar's `aria-valuetext`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar value={40} labelText="Upload status" valueText="40 MB of 100 MB" />
```

Use the `valueChildren` slot to render custom value content. Also provide `valueText` as its plain-text equivalent for assistive technologies.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar value={40} labelText="Upload status" valueText="40 MB of 100 MB">
  <strong slot="valueChildren">40 MB / 100 MB</strong>
</ProgressBar>
```

### Label

#### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar
  hideLabel
  value={40}
  labelText="Upload status"
  helperText="40 MB of 100 MB"
/>
```

#### Custom label content

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar value={40} helperText="40 MB of 100 MB">
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Upload status
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="Files are scanned before upload completes."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</ProgressBar>
```

### Size

Use the small size variant for compact layouts.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar size="sm" helperText="Refreshing table data..." />
```

### Status

Reflect operation outcome with `status`.

#### Finished

Show completion status with a checkmark icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar
  value={100}
  status="finished"
  labelText="Upload file"
  helperText="Upload complete"
/>
```

#### Error

Indicate errors with an error icon and red styling.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar
  value={0}
  status="error"
  labelText="Upload file"
  helperText="Invalid file format"
/>
```

#### Status announcements

Status changes are announced to assistive technologies. Set `errorText` and `finishedText` to localize or customize the status text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar
  value={100}
  status="finished"
  labelText="Upload file"
  finishedText="Terminé"
/>
```

### Variants

Change layout with `kind`.

#### Inline

Use the inline variant to display progress without helper text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar
  kind="inline"
  value={40}
  labelText="Sync progress"
  helperText="40 of 100 records synced"
/>
```

#### Indented

Use the indented variant for a more compact layout.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar
  kind="indented"
  value={40}
  labelText="Provision resources"
  helperText="40 of 100 nodes provisioned"
/>
```

#### Indented (status)

Combine the indented variant with status indicators.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressBar } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressBar
  kind="indented"
  status="finished"
  value={40}
  labelText="Provision resources"
  helperText="Provisioning complete"
/>
```

### UX example

Demonstrate a complete upload flow with start and end states.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    ProgressBar,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const max = 328;
  let value = 0;
  let status = "active";

  $: helperText =
    value > 0 ? `${value.toFixed(0)}MB of ${max}MB` : "Press start";
  $: if (value === max) {
    helperText = "Done";
    status = "finished";
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={8}>
  <ProgressBar labelText="Upload status" {value} {max} {helperText} {status} />
  <ButtonSet>
    <Button
      disabled={value > 0}
      on:click={() => {
        const interval = setInterval(() => {
          const delta = Math.random() * 10;

          if (value + delta < max) {
            value += delta;
          } else {
            value = max;
            clearInterval(interval);
          }
        }, 30);
      }}
    >
      Start
    </Button>
    <Button
      kind="tertiary"
      disabled={value !== max}
      on:click={() => {
        value = 0;
        status = "active";
      }}
    >
      Reset
    </Button>
  </ButtonSet>
</Stack>
```

---

### Component API

#### `ProgressBar` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the current value. | _undefined_ |
| `max` | `number` | Specify the maximum value | `100` |
| `kind` | `"default" \| "inline" \| "indented"` | Specify the kind of progress bar. | `"default"` |
| `status` | `"active" \| "finished" \| "error"` | Specify the status. | `"active"` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "small" \| "big"` | Specify the size.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"small"` (`"sm"`) and `"big"` (`"md"`). | `"md"` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `valueText` | `string` | Specify the value text, at the end of the label row and used for `aria-valuetext`.<br />Format it yourself, e.g. "40 MB of 100 MB". | `""` |
| `errorText` | `string` | Specify the text announced and described when the status is `"error"`. | `"Error"` |
| `finishedText` | `string` | Specify the text announced and described when the status is `"finished"`. | `"Complete"` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the progress bar element.<br />The helper text and status ids derive from it as `{id}-helper` and<br />`{id}-status`. | `uniqueId()` |

#### `ProgressBar` slots

| Slot            | Detail                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `labelChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `valueChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `ProgressBar` $$restProps

`ProgressBar` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## ProgressIndicator

### Basic

Create a horizontal progress indicator with four steps. It shows progress only; for a flow the user fills in step by step, with Back and Continue, validation and a final submit, use [Stepper](/components/Stepper), which draws this indicator.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator currentIndex={2}>
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Build"
    description="Build completed successfully"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Test"
    description="Automated test suite passed"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    label="Stage"
    description="Deploying to the staging environment"
  />
  <ProgressStep label="Deploy" description="Waiting to release to production" />
</ProgressIndicator>
```

### Step selection

Control which step is active, and how clicking a step affects that selection.

#### Selected by id

For dynamic step sets, bind `selectedId` and give each `ProgressStep` a stable `id`. Selection stays on the same logical step when steps before it are added or removed. When set, `selectedId` takes precedence over `currentIndex`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Checkbox,
    ProgressIndicator,
    ProgressStep,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedId = "step-b";
  let showStepA = true;
  let showStepB = true;
  let showStepC = true;
  let showStepD = true;

  $: visibleSteps = [
    { id: "step-a", label: "Build", show: showStepA },
    { id: "step-b", label: "Test", show: showStepB },
    { id: "step-c", label: "Stage", show: showStepC },
    { id: "step-d", label: "Deploy", show: showStepD },
  ].filter((s) => s.show);
</script>

<Stack gap={3}>
  <div>
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showStepA} labelText="Show Build step" />
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showStepB} labelText="Show Test step" />
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showStepC} labelText="Show Stage step" />
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showStepD} labelText="Show Deploy step" />
  </div>
  <Stack gap={4} orientation="horizontal" align="center">
    <Button
      kind="tertiary"
      size="small"
      on:click={() => (selectedId = "step-c")}
    >
      Select the Stage step by id
    </Button>
    <div><strong>selectedId:</strong> {selectedId}</div>
  </Stack>
  <ProgressIndicator bind:selectedId>
    {#each visibleSteps as step (step.id)}
      <ProgressStep id={step.id} label={step.label} complete />
    {/each}
  </ProgressIndicator>
</Stack>
```

#### Programmatic usage

Update the current step programmatically while maintaining step completion rules. Bind to a step's `current` prop to read whether it's the active step.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ProgressIndicator,
    ProgressStep,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let currentIndex = 1;
  let thirdStepCurrent = false;
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <ProgressIndicator bind:currentIndex>
    <ProgressStep
      complete
      label="Build"
      description="Build completed successfully"
    />
    <ProgressStep
      complete
      label="Test"
      description="Automated test suite passed"
    />
    <ProgressStep
      complete
      bind:current={thirdStepCurrent}
      label="Stage"
      description="Deploying to the staging environment"
    />
    <ProgressStep
      label="Deploy"
      description="Waiting to release to production"
    />
  </ProgressIndicator>
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <div>
      <Button
        kind={currentIndex === 2 ? "secondary" : "primary"}
        size="small"
        on:click={() => {
          currentIndex = currentIndex === 2 ? 0 : 2;
        }}
      >
        Set currentIndex to
        {currentIndex === 2 ? 0 : 2}
      </Button>
    </div>
    <div>
      <strong>Current index:</strong>
      {currentIndex}
    </div>
    <div>
      <strong>Is the third step currently selected?</strong>
      {thirdStepCurrent}
    </div>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

#### Prevent change on click

Disable automatic step selection when clicking completed steps. Incomplete steps are never clickable; only completed steps respond, and `preventChangeOnClick` turns those off too.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator preventChangeOnClick currentIndex={2}>
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Build"
    description="Build completed successfully"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Test"
    description="Automated test suite passed"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    label="Stage"
    description="Deploying to the staging environment"
  />
  <ProgressStep label="Deploy" description="Waiting to release to production" />
</ProgressIndicator>
```

### Keyboard navigation

<kbd>Tab</kbd> reaches every enabled step. <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> and <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> (or <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> and <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> when vertical) move focus between steps. <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> jump to the first and last enabled step. <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> selects a completed step.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator currentIndex={2}>
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Build"
    description="Build completed successfully"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Test"
    description="Automated test suite passed"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    label="Stage"
    description="Deploying to the staging environment"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    disabled
    label="Deploy"
    description="Blocked until the stage step completes"
  />
</ProgressIndicator>
```

### Step states

#### Invalid step

Mark a step as invalid to indicate an error state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator>
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Build"
    description="Build completed successfully"
  />
  <ProgressStep invalid label="Test" description="Automated tests failed" />
  <ProgressStep label="Deploy" description="Blocked until tests pass" />
</ProgressIndicator>
```

#### Disabled steps

Disable specific steps to prevent user interaction.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator>
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Build"
    description="Build completed successfully"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    disabled
    label="Test"
    description="Blocked until the build step completes"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    disabled
    label="Deploy"
    description="Blocked until testing completes"
  />
</ProgressIndicator>
```

### Step content

Customize what renders inside a step, beyond the default label and icon.

#### Icon (slot)

Override the default step icon using the `icon` named slot. The slot exposes complete, current, invalid, and description so the override can mirror the step state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import CheckmarkFilled from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/CheckmarkFilled.svelte";
  import Circle from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Circle.svelte";
  import InProgress from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/InProgress.svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator currentIndex={1}>
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Build"
    description="Build completed successfully"
  >
    <CheckmarkFilled slot="icon" />
  </ProgressStep>
  <ProgressStep label="Test" description="Currently running the test suite">
    <InProgress slot="icon" />
  </ProgressStep>
  <ProgressStep label="Deploy" description="Waiting to deploy">
    <Circle slot="icon" />
  </ProgressStep>
</ProgressIndicator>
```

#### Label (slot)

Override the default label using the default slot instead of `label`. The slot exposes `props`, which includes the `class` needed to keep the label styled correctly.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator currentIndex={1}>
  <ProgressStep complete let:props description="Build completed successfully">
    <strong class={props.class}>Build</strong>
  </ProgressStep>
  <ProgressStep let:props description="Currently running the test suite">
    <strong class={props.class}>Test</strong>
  </ProgressStep>
  <ProgressStep let:props description="Waiting to deploy">
    <strong class={props.class}>Deploy</strong>
  </ProgressStep>
</ProgressIndicator>
```

#### Secondary label

Set `secondaryLabel` to display supplementary text after the label, such as marking a step as optional.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator currentIndex={1}>
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Create account"
    description="Account created successfully"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    label="Add payment method"
    description="Add a payment method now, or skip and add one later"
    secondaryLabel="Optional"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    label="Invite team"
    description="Invite teammates to your workspace"
  />
</ProgressIndicator>
```

### Layout

Adjust the orientation and step spacing. By default each step is 128px wide and shrinks to no less than 112px, so a row of steps can be wider than a narrow container: four steps need at least 448px. In a narrow column or sidebar, use `spaceEqually`, whose steps share the space and truncate long labels, or `vertical`, which stacks them.

#### Spaced-equally

Distribute steps evenly across the available space. Steps shrink to fit a narrow container, truncating long labels.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator spaceEqually>
  <ProgressStep
    label="Provision infrastructure resources"
    description="Allocate compute, storage, and networking capacity"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    label="Run integration test suite"
    description="Verify service-to-service contracts before release"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    label="Deploy to production environment"
    description="Roll out the release to all regions"
  />
</ProgressIndicator>
```

#### Vertical

Display steps in a vertical layout, for a narrow column or sidebar.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator vertical>
  <ProgressStep
    label="Provision infrastructure resources"
    description="Allocate compute, storage, and networking capacity"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    label="Run integration test suite"
    description="Verify service-to-service contracts before release"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    label="Deploy to production environment"
    description="Roll out the release to all regions"
  />
</ProgressIndicator>
```

### Events

Respond to step selection changes.

Use `on:change` to listen for the step becoming active. `change` dispatches when the user selects a completed step by click, <kbd>Enter</kbd>, or <kbd>Space</kbd>, with the new index as `event.detail`; updating `currentIndex` or `selectedId` from code does not dispatch it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicator, ProgressStep } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicator
  currentIndex={0}
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // number
>
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Build"
    description="Build completed successfully"
  />
  <ProgressStep
    complete
    label="Test"
    description="Automated test suite passed"
  />
  <ProgressStep label="Deploy" description="Waiting to release to production" />
</ProgressIndicator>
```

### Skeleton

Show a loading state with the specified number of steps.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicatorSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicatorSkeleton />
```

#### Vertical

Show a vertical loading state with the specified number of steps.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicatorSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicatorSkeleton vertical />
```

#### Spaced-equally

Show a loading state with steps distributed evenly across the available space.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicatorSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicatorSkeleton spaceEqually />
```

#### Step count

Set `count` to change the number of skeleton steps rendered. Defaults to `4`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ProgressIndicatorSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ProgressIndicatorSkeleton count={6} />
```
