## RecursiveList

### Basic

Create a hierarchical list using the `nodes` prop. Each node can contain text, links, nested children, and HTML content via `html`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RecursiveList } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const nodes = [
    {
      text: "Infrastructure",
      nodes: [
        {
          text: "Deployment runbooks",
          nodes: [{ html: "<h5>Last updated: Q3 2026</h5>" }],
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: "Incident response",
      nodes: [
        {
          href: "https://status.example.com/incidents",
        },
        {
          href: "https://status.example.com/incidents",
          text: "View incident history",
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: "Billing",
    },
  ];
</script>

<RecursiveList {nodes} />
```

### Trusted content

A node's `html` renders with `{@html}`, unsanitized, and its `href` goes straight to the link. Both run as written, so keep them to content you control.

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Use `text` for anything a user or a third party wrote | Text is escaped, so markup in it shows as written |
| Sanitize `html` that isn't yours, such as with DOMPurify, before passing it | `{@html}` runs event handlers and scripts in the markup |
| Check that an `href` from outside starts with `https:`, `http:` or `mailto:` | A `javascript:` URL runs when the link is followed |

### Link attributes

Set `target` on a node to control where a link opens. When `target` is `"_blank"`, `rel` defaults to `"noopener noreferrer"`; supply `rel` explicitly to override it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RecursiveList } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const nodes = [
    {
      text: "Status page",
      href: "https://status.example.com/",
      target: "_blank",
    },
    {
      text: "Internal wiki",
      href: "https://wiki.example.com/",
      rel: "nofollow",
    },
  ];
</script>

<RecursiveList {nodes} />
```

### Ordered

Set `type` to `"ordered"` for numbered lists with proper indentation.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RecursiveList } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const nodes = [
    {
      text: "Infrastructure",
      nodes: [
        {
          text: "Deployment runbooks",
          nodes: [{ html: "<h5>Last updated: Q3 2026</h5>" }],
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: "Incident response",
      nodes: [
        {
          href: "https://status.example.com/incidents",
        },
        {
          href: "https://status.example.com/incidents",
          text: "View incident history",
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: "Billing",
    },
  ];
</script>

<RecursiveList type="ordered" {nodes} />
```

#### Native styles

Set `type` to `"ordered-native"` for browser-native numbering styles.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RecursiveList } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const nodes = [
    {
      text: "Infrastructure",
      nodes: [
        {
          text: "Deployment runbooks",
          nodes: [{ html: "<h5>Last updated: Q3 2026</h5>" }],
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: "Incident response",
      nodes: [
        {
          href: "https://status.example.com/incidents",
        },
        {
          href: "https://status.example.com/incidents",
          text: "View incident history",
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: "Billing",
    },
  ];
</script>

<RecursiveList type="ordered-native" {nodes} />
```

### Expressive styles

Use Carbon's expressive typesetting with `expressive`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RecursiveList } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const nodes = [
    {
      text: "Engineering",
      nodes: [
        {
          text: "Platform team",
          nodes: [{ text: "On-call lead" }],
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: "Product",
      nodes: [{ text: "Design" }],
    },
    { text: "Customer support" },
  ];
</script>

<RecursiveList expressive {nodes} />
```

### Flat data

Convert flat data to hierarchical arrays with the `toHierarchy` utility.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RecursiveList, toHierarchy } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const nodesFlat = [
    { id: 1, text: "Infrastructure" },
    { id: 2, text: "Deployment runbooks", pid: 1 },
    { id: 3, html: "<h5>Last updated: Q3 2026</h5>", pid: 2 },
    { id: 4, text: "Incident response" },
    { id: 5, href: "https://status.example.com/incidents", pid: 4 },
    {
      id: 6,
      href: "https://status.example.com/incidents",
      text: "View incident history",
      pid: 4,
    },
    { id: 7, text: "Billing" },
  ];
</script>

<RecursiveList nodes={toHierarchy(nodesFlat, (node) => node.pid)} />
```

### Stable keys

Each node accepts an optional id (string or number) used as the each-block key. Supply an id when text or href values can repeat, so reordering or filtering preserves DOM identity.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RecursiveList } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const nodes = [
    { id: "overview", text: "Overview" },
    {
      id: "admin-guide",
      text: "Admin guide",
      nodes: [{ id: "admin-guide-sso", text: "Configure SSO" }],
    },
    { id: "api", text: "API reference" },
  ];
</script>

<RecursiveList {nodes} />
```

### Virtualization

A recursive list renders every node. For thousands of top-level nodes, window the top level with [VirtualList](/components/VirtualList): render each node as a `ListItem` with a `nested` `RecursiveList` of its children. Set `spacerTag` to `"li"` and `measured`, since each item is as tall as its subtree. Wrap the list in a [ScrollGradient](/components/ScrollGradient) and pass its `scrollElementRef` as `scrollElement`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    ListItem,
    RecursiveList,
    ScrollGradient,
    UnorderedList,
    VirtualList,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const environments = ["production", "staging", "preview"];

  const services = Array.from({ length: 1000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `service-${String(i + 1).padStart(4, "0")}`,
    nodes: environments.slice(0, (i % 3) + 1).map((environment) => ({
      text: environment,
      href: `#service-${i + 1}-${environment}`,
    })),
  }));

  let scrollElementRef = null;
</script>

<ScrollGradient height="240px" bind:scrollElementRef>
  <Box paddingY={4} paddingX={5}>
    <UnorderedList>
      <VirtualList
        items={services}
        itemHeight={60}
        containerHeight={240}
        scrollElement={scrollElementRef}
        spacerTag="li"
        measured
        getKey={(item) => item.id}
        let:item
      >
        <ListItem>
          {item.text}
          <RecursiveList nodes={item.nodes} nested />
        </ListItem>
      </VirtualList>
    </UnorderedList>
  </Box>
</ScrollGradient>
```

---

### Component API

#### `RecursiveList` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `ReadonlyArray<Node>` | Specify the nodes to render. | `[]` |
| `type` | `"unordered" \| "ordered" \| "ordered-native"` | Specify the type of list to render. | `"unordered"` |
| `expressive` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use Carbon's expressive typesetting | `false` |
| `nested` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the nested variant, as for a list inside a list item | `false` |

#### `RecursiveList` typedefs

```ts
type RecursiveListNode = {
  /** Unique node identifier; used as the each-block key when provided */
  id?: string | number;
  /** Node text content */
  text?: string;
  /** Node link URL */
  href?: string;
  /** Node HTML content, rendered unsanitized with `@html`; pass only trusted or sanitized markup */
  html?: string;
  /** Node link target */
  target?: import("svelte/elements").SvelteHTMLElements["a"]["target"];
  /** Node link rel */
  rel?: import("svelte/elements").SvelteHTMLElements["a"]["rel"];
  /** Child nodes */
  nodes?: RecursiveListNode[];
};
```

#### `RecursiveList` $$restProps

`RecursiveList` spreads `$$restProps` to the `ul | ol` element.


## RelativeTime

### Basic

Render a `date` relative to the current time.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RelativeTime date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000} {now} />
```

### Reference time

Set `now` to a fixed reference instant instead of the live clock, for deterministic output. `date` can be in the past or the future.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <RelativeTime date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000} {now} />
  <RelativeTime date={now + 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000} {now} />
</Stack>
```

### Numeric

Set `numeric` to control whether a unit phrase like "yesterday" is preferred over a numeric count.

#### Auto

The default `numeric="auto"` renders unit phrases such as "yesterday" when one exists.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RelativeTime date={now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000} {now} numeric="auto" />
```

#### Always

Set `numeric="always"` to force a numeric count for every unit.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RelativeTime date={now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000} {now} numeric="always" />
```

### Styles

Set `style` to control the verbosity of the formatted output.

#### Long

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RelativeTime date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000} {now} style="long" />
```

#### Short

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RelativeTime date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000} {now} style="short" />
```

#### Narrow

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RelativeTime date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000} {now} style="narrow" />
```

### Locale

Set `locale` to format the output for a specific language instead of the runtime default.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <RelativeTime date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000} {now} locale="fr" />
  <RelativeTime date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000} {now} locale="ja" />
</Stack>
```

### Custom content

Use the default slot with `let:formatted` to render custom content around the formatted string.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RelativeTime date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000} {now} let:formatted>
  Updated {formatted}
</RelativeTime>
```

### Absolute time

Hover over the rendered text to see the absolute time, sourced from the `title` attribute. Set `titleFormatOptions` to control its format. The underlying `datetime` attribute always holds the full ISO instant for assistive technology.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RelativeTime
  date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000}
  {now}
  titleFormatOptions={{ dateStyle: "full", timeStyle: "long" }}
/>
```

Set `timeZone` to an IANA time zone to format the `title` in that zone instead of the runtime default. A server often runs in UTC while the browser runs in the viewer's zone, so without a fixed value the prerendered `title` differs from the one the client prints. Pass the same `timeZone` on both sides to keep them identical.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RelativeTime
  date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000}
  {now}
  locale="en-US"
  timeZone="Asia/Tokyo"
/>
```

### Chat timestamps

Set `minUnit="minute"` to show the locale's word for the present, such as "now", for any time under a minute instead of counting seconds. Set `absoluteAfter` to a duration in milliseconds to show the clock time once `date` is that far in the past. Set `absoluteFormatOptions` to change its format. The default is the short time, such as "9:00 AM".

```svelte
<script>
  import { RelativeTime, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <RelativeTime
    date={now - 20 * 1000}
    {now}
    minUnit="minute"
    absoluteAfter={60 * 60 * 1000}
    timeZone="UTC"
  />
  <RelativeTime
    date={now - 5 * 60 * 1000}
    {now}
    minUnit="minute"
    absoluteAfter={60 * 60 * 1000}
    timeZone="UTC"
  />
  <RelativeTime
    date={now - 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000}
    {now}
    minUnit="minute"
    absoluteAfter={60 * 60 * 1000}
    timeZone="UTC"
  />
</Stack>
```

### Live

Leave `live` at its default of `true` to keep the output refreshing on an adaptive timer as time passes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, RelativeTime, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let savedAt = Date.now();

  function handleSave() {
    savedAt = Date.now();
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Button on:click={handleSave}>Save</Button>
  <RelativeTime date={savedAt} let:formatted>Saved {formatted}</RelativeTime>
</Stack>
```

---

### Component API

#### `RelativeTime` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string \| undefined` | Target instant. Invalid or missing renders an empty `<time>` with no `datetime`. | _undefined_ |
| `now` | `Date \| number \| undefined` | Fixed reference instant. When set, live updates are off (deterministic docs and tests). | _undefined_ |
| `locale` | `string \| undefined` | Runtime locale when unset. | _undefined_ |
| `timeZone` | `string \| undefined` | IANA time zone for the absolute time in `title`. Runtime time zone when<br />unset. Set a fixed value so the server and the client print the same<br />`title`. Equivalent to `titleFormatOptions={{ timeZone }}`, and overrides<br />`titleFormatOptions.timeZone` when both are set. | _undefined_ |
| `numeric` | `"always" \| "auto"` |  | `"auto"` |
| `style` | `"long" \| "short" \| "narrow"` |  | `"long"` |
| `minUnit` | `"second" \| "minute"` | Set the smallest unit shown. `"minute"` shows the locale's word for<br />the present, such as "now", for any time under a minute, then counts<br />minutes. `"second"` counts seconds. | `"second"` |
| `absoluteAfter` | `number \| undefined` | Show the absolute time once `date` is at least this many milliseconds<br />in the past, such as `3_600_000` for one hour. The timer then stops.<br />Leave unset to always show relative time. | _undefined_ |
| `absoluteFormatOptions` | `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` | Format for the absolute time shown after `absoluteAfter`. Honors<br />`timeZone` the same way `titleFormatOptions` does. | `{ timeStyle: "short" }` |
| `live` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to disable the adaptive refresh timer. | `true` |
| `titleFormatOptions` | `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` | Absolute time shown in `title`. | `{ dateStyle: "medium", timeStyle: "short" }` |

#### `RelativeTime` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `{ formatted: string }` |

#### `RelativeTime` $$restProps

`RelativeTime` spreads `$$restProps` to the `time` element.


## ScrollGradient

### Basic

Wrap scrollable content in `ScrollGradient`. Set `height` so the content overflows vertically -- it accepts any CSS length, with autocomplete for common presets like `"100%"` and `"100vh"`. The top gradient appears once the content is scrolled past its start, and the bottom gradient hides once it's scrolled to the end.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ScrollGradient } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ScrollGradient height="12rem">
  {#each auditLogEntries as entry}
    <p>{entry}</p>
  {/each}
</ScrollGradient>
```

### Horizontal

Gradients appear independently for each axis. Set a width to overflow horizontally.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, ScrollGradient, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ScrollGradient height="6rem">
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5}>
    {#each Array(20) as _, i}
      <Box
        display="flex"
        align="center"
        justify="center"
        width="6rem"
        height="4rem"
        fill="layer-accent"
      >
        {i + 1}
      </Box>
    {/each}
  </Stack>
</ScrollGradient>
```

### Colors

Set `color` to retint the gradient and `background` to repaint the content area. Both default to the `layer` token, which follows the enclosing [Layer](/components/Layer).

#### Theme tokens

Set either to a [Box fill](/components/Box#fill) token name, such as `"background"` or `"layer-02"`, so the fade matches the surface it sits on in every theme.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, ScrollGradient } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box fill="layer-02" padding={3}>
  <ScrollGradient color="layer-02" background="layer-02" height="12rem">
    {#each auditLogEntries as entry}
      <p>{entry}</p>
    {/each}
  </ScrollGradient>
</Box>
```

#### Custom color

Set `color` to any CSS color.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ScrollGradient } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ScrollGradient color="cornflowerblue" height="12rem">
  {#each auditLogEntries as entry}
    <p>{entry}</p>
  {/each}
</ScrollGradient>
```

#### Transparent background

Set `background` to `"transparent"` to let the parent's own background show through instead of repainting it. `color` still sets the fade.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ScrollGradient } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ScrollGradient background="transparent" height="12rem">
  {#each auditLogEntries as entry}
    <p>{entry}</p>
  {/each}
</ScrollGradient>
```

### Reactive example

Toggling content demonstrates that the gradients update as the container's overflow changes.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Checkbox,
    ScrollGradient,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let itemCount = 3;
  let hideStartGradient = false;
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Button size="small" kind="tertiary" on:click={() => (itemCount += 1)}>
      Add item
    </Button>
    <Button
      size="small"
      kind="tertiary"
      disabled={itemCount === 0}
      on:click={() => (itemCount = Math.max(0, itemCount - 1))}
    >
      Remove item
    </Button>
  </Stack>
  <Checkbox labelText="Hide start gradient" bind:checked={hideStartGradient} />
  <ScrollGradient {hideStartGradient} height="8rem">
    {#each Array(itemCount) as _, i}
      <p>Export job #{i + 1}</p>
    {/each}
  </ScrollGradient>
</Stack>
```

---

### Component API

#### `ScrollGradient` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scrollElementRef` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the inner scrollable element. | `null` |
| `color` | `"background" \| "layer-01" \| "layer-02" \| "layer-03" \| "layer-accent" \| "field" \| "inverse" \| "brand" \| (string & {}) \| undefined` | Specify the gradient color: a fill token name, the same set as Box<br />`fill`, or any CSS color. Defaults to the `layer` token, which follows<br />the enclosing Layer. | _undefined_ |
| `background` | `"background" \| "layer-01" \| "layer-02" \| "layer-03" \| "layer-accent" \| "field" \| "inverse" \| "brand" \| (string & {}) \| undefined` | Specify the background color of the scrollable content area: a fill<br />token name, the same set as Box `fill`, or any CSS color. Defaults to<br />the `layer` token, which follows the enclosing Layer. Does not affect<br />the gradient color; use `color` for that. | _undefined_ |
| `height` | `"100%" \| "100vh" \| (string & {}) \| undefined` | Specify the height of the component. Set a height so the content<br />can overflow vertically. | _undefined_ |
| `hideStartGradient` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to suppress the top and left gradients,<br />even when their edge is scrollable. | `false` |
| `scrollElementClassName` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a class for the inner scrollable element. | _undefined_ |

#### `ScrollGradient` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `ScrollGradient` forwarded events

| Event       |
| ----------- |
| `on:scroll` |

#### `ScrollGradient` $$restProps

`ScrollGradient` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## Search

### Basic

The search input is 40px tall by default, like other fields. Set `size` to choose another variant -- see [extra-large](#extra-large), [small](#small), and [extra-small](#extra-small). The input clears on <kbd>Escape</kbd> or the clear button.

To build a search typeahead with a results menu -- suggestions, grouped results, and recent searches -- use [SearchMenu](/components/SearchMenu), which composes `Search`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search />
```

### Helper text

Provide context below the input with `helperText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search
  labelText="Search catalog"
  helperText="Searches every connected data catalog"
/>
```

### Initial value

Set an initial value with `value`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search placeholder="Search catalog..." value="Cloud functions" />
```

### Reactive example

Bind to `value` for reactive updates.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ButtonSet, Search, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Search bind:value />
  <div>
    <ButtonSet>
      <Button
        size="small"
        disabled={value === "Cloud functions"}
        on:click={() => (value = "Cloud functions")}
      >
        Set value
      </Button>
      <Button
        kind="ghost"
        size="small"
        disabled={value.length === 0}
        on:click={() => (value = "")}
      >
        Clear value
      </Button>
    </ButtonSet>
  </div>
  <div>Value: {value}</div>
</Stack>
```

### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to select the full value when the field receives focus.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search
  selectTextOnFocus
  placeholder="Search catalog..."
  value="Cloud functions"
/>
```

### Clear event

The `clear` event fires when clicking the clear button or pressing <kbd>Escape</kbd>.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search value="Cloud functions" on:clear={() => console.log("clear")} />
```

### Search event

The `search` event fires when pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd>, with `value` as the event detail. Set `debounce` (milliseconds) to also dispatch `search` after typing pauses, without delaying the `value` binding itself. The default `debounce` of `0` does not dispatch on input -- only <kbd>Enter</kbd> does.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search debounce={300} on:search={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} />
```

### Custom labels

Customize the ARIA labels used for accessibility.

#### Landmark label

The outer element has `role="search"`, and its accessible name comes from `labelText` via `aria-labelledby`, not a static `aria-label`. The label is visually hidden by default -- see [Fluid](#fluid) for the variant with a visible label. Always set a descriptive `labelText`, especially when a page has more than one search region, so screen reader users can distinguish each landmark by name.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search labelText="Search catalog" />
```

#### Close button label

Set `closeButtonLabelText` to customize the accessible label of the clear button (default `"Clear search input"`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search value="Cloud functions" closeButtonLabelText="Clear catalog search" />
```

### Keyboard shortcut

Set `shortcut` to focus the field from anywhere on the page, such as `"/"` or `"mod+k"`, which shows <DocKbd shortcut="mod+k" /> on your platform. The keys show at the end of the empty field until it's focused, and the input announces them with `aria-keyshortcuts`. A key without a modifier, such as `/`, doesn't fire while typing in another field. An expandable search expands first, and its search button announces the keys while it's collapsed. To do something else, handle `on:shortcut` and call `preventDefault()`.

This site already uses <kbd>/</kbd> and <DocKbd shortcut="mod+k" /> for its own search, so the example uses `"mod+shift+f"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search shortcut="mod+shift+f" placeholder="Search components" />
```

Let users turn off a single-key shortcut such as `/`, or add a modifier to it. Speech input and stray key presses fire it by accident, and WCAG 2.1.4 asks for a way to turn it off or remap it.

### Expandable

Enable the expandable variant to show a compact search icon that expands on focus. While collapsed, the input is marked `inert` and removed from the tab order, hiding it from assistive technology until it expands -- only the search icon button is reachable. That icon renders as a `<button>`, so pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> opens the field without a pointer. Pressing <kbd>Escape</kbd> clears a non-empty value first, then collapses the field on the next press.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let expanded = false;
</script>

<Search expandable bind:expanded on:expand on:collapse />

<br />

<strong>Expanded:</strong>
{expanded}
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <Search />
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to embed a visible label inside the field. Fluid search inputs work standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), which applies the variant automatically. The fluid variant has a fixed height and cannot be combined with the expandable variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search fluid labelText="Search catalog" placeholder="Search services..." />
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<Search fluid labelText="Search catalog" placeholder="Search services...">
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Search catalog
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="Search applies to services in the selected region only."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</Search>
```

#### Disabled

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search
  fluid
  disabled
  labelText="Search catalog"
  placeholder="Search services..."
/>
```

#### Skeleton

Display a loading skeleton for the fluid search variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FluidSearchSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FluidSearchSkeleton />
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to control the input height. The default is `"lg"`, 40px.

Carbon v11's `"md"` also works and renders the default 40px `"lg"` size. Carbon v11's 48px `lg` is `"xl"` here.

#### Extra-large

Set `size` to `"xl"` for a 48px search input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search size="xl" />
```

#### Small

Set `size` to `"sm"` for a small search input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search size="sm" />
```

#### Extra-small

Set `size` to `"xs"` for an extra-small search input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search size="xs" />
```

### States

Reflect validation and interaction states.

#### Invalid

Indicate an invalid state with an error message by setting `invalid` and providing `invalidText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search
  invalid
  invalidText="Enter at least 3 characters to search the catalog."
  labelText="Search catalog"
  value="db"
/>
```

#### Warning

Indicate a warning state with a message by setting `warn` and providing `warnText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search
  warn
  warnText="Results may be up to 5 minutes behind the primary index."
  labelText="Search catalog"
  value="billing-api"
/>
```

#### Disabled

Set `disabled` to `true` to prevent user interaction.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search disabled />
```

#### Read-only

Set `readonly` to show a value that cannot be edited or cleared. The clear button is hidden and <kbd>Escape</kbd> leaves the value in place. A read-only search still submits its value with the form.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search readonly value="Carbon" />
```

### Custom icon

Replace the default search icon with a custom one.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Query from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Query.svelte";
</script>

<Search icon={Query} />
```

### Loading

Set `loading` to show a small spinner in place of the search icon while results are loading. The input stays editable and gets `aria-busy="true"`.

Set `loadingDelay` to wait a number of milliseconds after `loading` becomes `true` before showing the spinner. Work that finishes within the delay shows no spinner. Once shown, the spinner stays for at least 500 ms so it does not flash. The input gets `aria-busy` as soon as `loading` is `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search loading value="Cloud functions" />
```

### Skeleton

Show a loading state with the skeleton variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search skeleton />
```

#### Extra-large

Show a loading state for the extra-large search variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search size="xl" skeleton />
```

#### Small

Show a loading state for the small search variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search size="sm" skeleton />
```

#### Extra-small

Show a loading state for the extra-small search variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search size="xs" skeleton />
```

### Component API

#### `Search` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `T` | Specify the value of the search input.<br />Follows the field when the owning form resets. | `""` |
| `expanded` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true to expand the search input. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Specify the size of the search input.<br />Inherits the parent `Form` size when unset, otherwise `"lg"` (40px),<br />as in Carbon v11. Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (`"lg"`, 40px).<br />Carbon v11's 48px `lg` is `"xl"` here. | `"lg"` |
| `searchClass` | `string` | Specify the class name passed to the outer div element | `""` |
| `skeleton` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to display the skeleton state | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the search input | `false` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the read-only variant.<br />The value cannot be edited or cleared, and still submits with the form. | `false` |
| `expandable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the expandable variant | `false` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`.<br />Cannot be combined with the expandable variant. | `false` |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Specify the `placeholder` attribute of the search input | `"Search..."` |
| `autocomplete` | `"on" \| "off"` | Specify the `autocomplete` attribute. | `"off"` |
| `autofocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to auto focus the search element | `false` |
| `closeButtonLabelText` | `string` | Specify the close button label text | `"Clear search input"` |
| `shortcut` | `string` | Specify a keyboard shortcut that focuses the field, such as `"/"` or<br />`"mod+k"`. `mod` is Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. The<br />keys show at the end of the empty field until it's focused, and the<br />input gets `aria-keyshortcuts`. A shortcut without a modifier, such as<br />`"/"`, doesn't fire while typing in another field. | `""` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `icon` | `Icon` | Specify the icon to render. | `IconSearch` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the input element | `uniqueId()` |
| `selectTextOnFocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to select the input's text when it receives focus | `false` |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Set to `true` while results are loading. Shows a small spinner in place<br />of the search icon and sets `aria-busy` on the input. The field stays<br />editable. | `false` |
| `loadingDescription` | `string` | Specify the assistive text for the spinner shown while `loading` | `"Searching"` |
| `loadingDelay` | `number` | Wait this many milliseconds after `loading` turns `true` before showing<br />the spinner. Once shown, it stays for at least 500 ms, so fast work shows<br />nothing and slow work never flashes. The input sets `aria-busy` as soon as<br />`loading` is `true`.<br />Set to `0` to show it at once. | `0` |
| `debounce` | `number` | Milliseconds to wait after the last input before dispatching `search`.<br />0 (default) does not dispatch on input; Enter still dispatches<br />immediately. When greater than 0, `search` also fires after the pause.<br />`value` updates immediately either way. | `0` |
| `focusWithoutSelect` | `() => void` | Focus the input without selecting text, even when `selectTextOnFocus` is set. | _undefined_ |

| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `SearchSkeleton` $$restProps

`SearchSkeleton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.

#### `FluidSearchSkeleton` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `FluidSearchSkeleton` $$restProps

`FluidSearchSkeleton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## SearchMenu

### Basic

Render `SearchMenuItem` children to display suggestions. Each item highlights the portion of its `text` that matches the search value. Result text is flush-left with the input placeholder. The menu opens on focus. Use the arrow keys to move between results, <kbd>Enter</kbd> to select the active result, and <kbd>Escape</kbd> to close the menu. The menu also closes on an outside click.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "Data";

  const resources = [
    { id: "svc-db-testsql", name: "Databases for TestSQL" },
    { id: "svc-att-iot", name: "AT&T IoT Data Plans" },
    { id: "svc-memcache", name: "Data Store for Memcache" },
    { id: "svc-hazardhub", name: "HazardHub Property Risk Data API" },
    { id: "svc-financial", name: "Managed Financial Data API" },
  ];
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  {#each resources as resource (resource.id)}
    <SearchMenuItem
      text={resource.name}
      value={resource.id}
      on:select={(e) => console.log("select", e.detail)}
    />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to control the search input height, matching the [Search](/components/Search) input sizing. The default is extra-large (`"xl"`). By default the results menu adjusts to match the input: row height, text inset, and the leading-icon gutter all align with the input for the chosen size.

#### Recent searches

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Link,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuGroup,
    SearchMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Time from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Time.svelte";

    { id: "recent-vsi", query: "virtual servers" },

  bind:ref={searchRef}
  labelText="Search"
  placeholder="Search..."
>
```

### Layout

#### Leading dropdown

Use the `before` slot to render content to the left of the input within a joined bar, for example a [Dropdown](/components/Dropdown) that scopes the search. Bind to the dropdown selection to update the placeholder and filter results. Compose a [Stack](/components/Stack) with a 1px separator between the dropdown and the search input. The results menu matches the search input width, and opening the dropdown closes the search menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Dropdown,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
  let scopeId = "all";

  const scopeItems = [
    { id: "all", text: "All" },
    { id: "networks", text: "Networks" },
    { id: "devices", text: "Devices" },
  ];

  const scopeConfig = {
    all: {
      placeholder: "Search networks and devices",
      types: ["network", "device"],
    },
    networks: {
      placeholder: "Search private networks",
      types: ["network"],
    },
    devices: {
      placeholder: "Search edge gateways",
      types: ["device"],
    },
  };

  const resources = [
    { id: "gw-01", name: "Edge gateway 01", type: "device" },
    { id: "gw-02", name: "Edge gateway 02", type: "device" },
    { id: "gw-lab", name: "Edge gateway lab", type: "device" },
    { id: "net-us-south", name: "Private network us-south", type: "network" },
    { id: "net-eu-de", name: "Private network eu-de", type: "network" },
    { id: "net-ap-tokyo", name: "Private network ap-tokyo", type: "network" },
  ];

  $: config = scopeConfig[scopeId] ?? scopeConfig.all;
  $: placeholder = config.placeholder;
  $: results = resources.filter((item) => config.types.includes(item.type));
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value {placeholder} labelText="Search">
  <Stack slot="before" orientation="horizontal" align="stretch" gap={0}>
    <Box width="12rem">
      <Dropdown
        hideLabel
        size="xl"
        labelText="Scope"
        bind:selectedId={scopeId}
        items={scopeItems}
        on:select={() => (value = "")}
      />
    </Box>
    <Box aria-hidden="true" width={1} fill="layer-03" />
  </Stack>

  {#each results as item (item.id)}
    <SearchMenuItem text={item.name} value={item.id} />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

### Matching

As the user types, each `SearchMenuItem` is matched against the search value to decide whether it is shown and which characters of its `text` are highlighted. The `match` prop controls this. It receives the item `text` and the current search value and returns `{ matched, indices }`: `matched` filters the item out when `false`, and `indices` are the character positions highlighted in the text. The default is fuzzy matching.

#### Built-in fuzzy matching

Fuzzy matching prefers a contiguous substring, ranking a prefix above a word boundary above a mid-word occurrence, and falls back to a subsequence match so that "dsm" matches "**D**ata **S**tore for **M**emcache". Matching is case-insensitive. No configuration is required.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu labelText="Search" placeholder="Search..." value="dsm">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Data Store for Memcache" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="AT&T IoT Data Plans" />
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Custom fuzzy options

Import `fuzzyMatch` from `carbon-components-svelte` to reuse the built-in matcher with custom options. Pass an options object as the third argument to tune sensitivity: set `threshold` to a value between `0` and `1` to require a minimum match quality (`0`, the default, accepts any match; `0.5` requires a contiguous substring; `0.7` a word-boundary substring; and `0.9` a prefix). Set `caseSensitive` to `true` to match the exact case. Pass it to the `match` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    fuzzyMatch,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "Data";

  const resources = [
    "Data Table",
    "Data Store for Memcache",
    "Databases for TestSQL",
    "AT&T IoT Data Plans",
  ];

  // Reuse the built-in matcher, but raise the sensitivity threshold. A
  // `threshold` of 0.5 requires a contiguous substring, so a scattered
  // subsequence like "dt" (which the default fuzzy matching accepts for
  // "Data Table") no longer matches.
  const match = (text, query) => fuzzyMatch(text, query, { threshold: 0.5 });
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value {match} labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  {#each resources as text (text)}
    <SearchMenuItem {text} />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Custom filtering

Provide your own `match` function for full control over the matching logic. The example below matches items by a case-insensitive prefix. Return `matched: false` to filter an item out. Pass a no-op such as `match={() => ({ matched: true })}` to keep every item and disable highlighting entirely.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "data";

  const resources = [
    "Databases for TestSQL",
    "AT&T IoT Data Plans",
    "Data Store for Memcache",
    "HazardHub Property Risk Data API",
    "Managed Financial Data API",
  ];

  // Custom prefix matcher: only items whose text starts with the query match.
  // `matched` filters items out; `indices` are the characters to highlight.
  function match(text, query) {
    const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (q === "") return { matched: true, indices: [] };
    const matched = text.toLowerCase().startsWith(q);
    return {
      matched,
      indices: matched ? Array.from({ length: q.length }, (_, i) => i) : [],
    };
  }
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value {match} labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  {#each resources as text (text)}
    <SearchMenuItem {text} />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Custom filtering with character highlighting

To customize how matched characters render, use the default slot with `let:segments`. Each segment is `{ text, match }`, computed from your `match` function's `indices`, so you can wrap matched runs in your own markup -- no `{@html}` required. The example below applies a yellow highlight. Keep the `{#each}` compact so adjacent segments are not split by whitespace.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "data";

  const resources = [
    "Databases for TestSQL",
    "AT&T IoT Data Plans",
    "Data Store for Memcache",
    "HazardHub Property Risk Data API",
    "Managed Financial Data API",
  ];

  // Custom matcher: a case-insensitive substring match.
  function match(text, query) {
    const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (q === "") return { matched: true, indices: [] };
    const start = text.toLowerCase().indexOf(q);
    if (start === -1) return { matched: false, indices: [] };
    return {
      matched: true,
      indices: Array.from({ length: q.length }, (_, i) => start + i),
    };
  }
</script>

<!--
  Use the default slot with `let:segments` to render the label yourself. Each
  segment is `{ text, match }`, so no `{@html}` is needed -- wrap matched runs
  in your own markup. Keep the `{#each}` compact so adjacent segments are not
  split by whitespace.
-->
<SearchMenu bind:value {match} labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  {#each resources as text (text)}
    <SearchMenuItem {text} let:segments
      >{#each segments as segment}
        {#if segment.match}
          <mark>{segment.text}</mark>
        {:else}
          {segment.text}
        {/if}
      {/each}</SearchMenuItem
    >
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>

<style>
  mark {
    background: #f1c21b;
    color: #161616;
  }
</style>
```

### Filtering

The `shouldFilter` prop toggles client-side filtering. Client-side matching (the default) and server-side filtering can each be used on their own or combined. Unmatched items stay mounted and are hidden, so later keystrokes only punch visibility and update highlight marks.

#### Server-side results

Set `shouldFilter` to `false` to render results exactly as provided, for example results already filtered by a server. The default matcher still highlights the query within each result; pass a no-op `match={() => ({ matched: true })}` to disable client-side highlighting entirely.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu shouldFilter={false} labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Result rendered as-is" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Another server result" />
</SearchMenu>
```

#### No results

Provide a `noResults` slot to render an empty state when the search value matches no items.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu labelText="Search" placeholder="Search..." value="no match">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Data Store for Memcache" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="noResults">No results found</svelte:fragment>
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Async results

Combine an async data source with client-side highlighting. Set `debounce` (in milliseconds) to fetch on `search` after typing pauses, instead of on every keystroke. `value` and the fuzzy-match highlighting stay immediate; only `search` waits, and the default `debounce` of `0` never dispatches it. `shouldFilter={false}` defers filtering to the server, so the menu shows exactly what it returns while the client still highlights the query. Set `loading` to render a skeleton menu while fetching (customize the rows with `skeletonCount` or the `loading` slot), and use the `noResults` slot for the empty state.

Selecting an item or pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> with no active item cancels a pending `search` instead of also firing it, since `select` and `submit` already cover those cases. Clearing with the clear icon is instant and also cancels a pending `search`. <kbd>Escape</kbd> only closes the menu here; it does not clear `value`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
  let results = [];
  let loading = false;

  const database = [
    "Databases for PostgreSQL",
    "Databases for MongoDB",
    "Databases for Redis",
    "Db2 on Cloud",
    "Data Store for Memcache",
    "Cloud Object Storage",
    "Watson Machine Learning",
    "Key Protect",
  ];

  // Simulate a server endpoint. Swap the body for a real `fetch()`.
  function fetchResults(query) {
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      setTimeout(() => {
        const q = query.toLowerCase();
        resolve(database.filter((record) => record.toLowerCase().includes(q)));
      }, 600);
    });
  }

  function resetResults() {
    results = [];
    loading = false;
  }

  // Fires immediately, before the debounce pause. Reset right away on an
  // empty value instead of waiting for the debounced `search`, so stale
  // results don't linger. Otherwise show loading as soon as typing starts.
  function handleInput(event) {
    if (event.target.value.trim() === "") {
      resetResults();
    } else {
      loading = true;
    }
  }

  // `search` fires only after typing pauses. `shouldFilter={false}` defers
  // filtering to the server; the client still highlights the query in
  // each result.
  async function handleSearch(query) {
    const trimmed = query.trim();
    if (trimmed === "") return;
    results = await fetchResults(trimmed);
    loading = false;
  }
</script>

<SearchMenu
  bind:value
  {loading}
  debounce={300}
  shouldFilter={false}
  labelText="Search"
  placeholder="Search..."
  on:input={handleInput}
  on:search={(e) => handleSearch(e.detail)}
  on:clear={resetResults}
>
  {#each results as result (result)}
    <SearchMenuItem text={result} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="noResults">No results for "{value}"</svelte:fragment>
</SearchMenu>
```

### Events

The `select` event fires when an item is activated, carrying the `value`, the `item`, and the originating `event`. The `submit` event fires when pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> without an active item, carrying the current `value`. The `search` event fires after the `debounce` pause (see [Async results](#async-results)), carrying the current `value`. The `close` event fires when the menu closes, with a `trigger` of `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, `"select"`, or `"blur"`.

#### Load more

`scrollend` fires when the results menu is scrolled near the bottom. Use it to append the next page of `SearchMenuItem`s to the slot.

This is a library load-more signal, not the browser's native `scrollend` (scroll stopped). It fires once per approach to the bottom, re-arming after the user scrolls away and when more items are slotted.

While the menu already has results, set `loading` to append a loading row below them. `loading` only swaps in the full skeleton menu when there are no results yet.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const PAGE_SIZE = 6;
  const TOTAL = 36;

  let results = [];
  let loading = false;
  let hasMore = true;

  function makePage(offset) {
    return Array.from(
      { length: Math.min(PAGE_SIZE, TOTAL - offset) },
      (_, i) => `INC-${4201 + offset + i}: API gateway latency above threshold`,
    );
  }

  async function loadMore() {
    if (loading || !hasMore) return;
    loading = true;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 400));
    results = [...results, ...makePage(results.length)];
    hasMore = results.length < TOTAL;
    loading = false;
  }

  loadMore();
</script>

<SearchMenu
  labelText="Search incidents"
  placeholder="Open and scroll to the bottom..."
  shouldFilter={false}
  menuMaxHeight={200}
  {loading}
  on:scrollend={loadMore}
>
  {#each results as result (result)}
    <SearchMenuItem text={result} />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

```svelte
<SearchMenu labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">

    text="Carbon Components Svelte"
```


### States

Reflect interaction states.

#### Disabled

Disable the entire search input with `disabled`. The menu does not open.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu disabled labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Disabled items

Set `disabled` on an individual `SearchMenuItem` to keep it visible but non-interactive. Disabled items are skipped during keyboard navigation and cannot be selected.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "Data";

  const resources = [
    { id: "svc-db-testsql", name: "Databases for TestSQL", disabled: false },
    { id: "svc-memcache", name: "Data Store for Memcache", disabled: true },
    {
      id: "svc-financial",
      name: "Managed Financial Data API",
      disabled: false,
    },
    {
      id: "svc-hazardhub",
      name: "HazardHub Property Risk Data API",
      disabled: true,
    },
  ];
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  {#each resources as resource (resource.id)}
    <SearchMenuItem
      text={resource.name}
      value={resource.id}
      disabled={resource.disabled}
    />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Read-only

Set `readonly` to prevent opening the results menu or selecting a value. The current value stays visible and still submits with the form.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu
  readonly
  labelText="Search"
  placeholder="Search..."
  value="Cloud functions"
>
  <SearchMenuItem text="Cloud functions" />
</SearchMenu>
```

### Loading

Set `searchLoading` to show a spinner in the search input while results are loading, independent of `loading`, which controls the skeleton menu (see [Async results](#async-results)). Combine both props when the menu is also loading.

Set `loadingDelay` to wait a number of milliseconds after `loading` or `searchLoading` becomes `true` before showing the skeleton menu, the loading row or the spinner. Work that finishes within the delay shows none of them. Once shown, they stay for at least 500 ms so they do not flash. The menu is marked busy as soon as `loading` is `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu searchLoading labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Data Store for Memcache" />
</SearchMenu>
```

### Skeleton

#### Search input

Render only the input skeleton with the [Search](/components/Search) `skeleton` prop, for example before the menu is ready.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Search skeleton labelText="Search" placeholder="Search..." />
```

#### Search input and menu

Grey out both the input and the menu by composing [Search](/components/Search) with the `skeleton` prop and `SearchMenuSkeleton` for the results menu. Place `SearchMenuSkeleton` inside a `bx--search-menu__search` wrapper so the menu aligns with the input. For a loading state on an interactive menu, prefer the `loading` prop shown in [Async results](#async-results).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Search, SearchMenuSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<div class="bx--search-menu">
  <div class="bx--search-menu__search">
    <Search skeleton labelText="Search" placeholder="Search..." />
    <SearchMenuSkeleton />
  </div>
</div>
```

### Component API

#### `SearchMenu` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `T` | Specify the value of the search input. | `""` |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Whether the results menu is visible. Driven by focus and available content. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `menuRef` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the menu HTML element. | `null` |
| `shouldFilter` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to filter items by the search value using fuzzy matching.<br />Unmatched items stay mounted and are hidden so later keystrokes do not<br />recreate option nodes. | `true` |
| `match` | `(text: string, query: string) => { matched: boolean; indices?: number[] }` | Override how the search value is matched against each item's `text`.<br />Receives the item `text` and the current search value, and returns whether<br />the item `matched` along with the `indices` of characters to highlight.<br />Defaults to fuzzy matching. Supply your own function for custom filtering<br />and highlighting, or pass a no-op like `() => ({ matched: true })` to keep<br />every item and disable highlighting. | `fuzzyMatch` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | Specify the size of the search input.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (`"lg"`, 40px). `"lg"` keeps this<br />library's 40px; Carbon v11's 48px `lg` is `"xl"` here. | `"xl"` |
| `menuSize` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Specify the size of the results menu, independent of the input `size`.<br />Defaults to the input `size`.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (`"lg"`, 40px). `"lg"` keeps this<br />library's 40px; Carbon v11's 48px `lg` is `"xl"` here. | _undefined_ |
| `menuMaxHeight` | `number \| string \| undefined` | Override the results menu's max height. Numbers are pixels; strings<br />accept any CSS length (for example `"50vh"`). Defaults to 360px. | _undefined_ |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the search input | `false` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the read-only variant.<br />Blocks opening the results menu and selecting or submitting a value;<br />the current value still submits with the form. | `false` |
| `readonlyText` | `string` | Specify the assistive text announced to screen readers when read-only.<br />Exposed because VoiceOver does not announce `aria-readonly`. | `"Read-only"` |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render a skeleton menu while results are loading, for<br />example while fetching server-side results. Override the placeholder rows<br />with the `loading` slot. When results are already rendered, a single<br />loading row is appended below them instead. | `false` |
| `skeletonCount` | `number` | Specify the number of skeleton rows rendered while `loading` | `4` |
| `loadingDelay` | `number` | Wait this many milliseconds after `loading` turns `true` before showing<br />the skeleton menu or loading row, and the `searchLoading` spinner. Once<br />shown, it stays for at least 500 ms, so fast work shows nothing and slow<br />work never flashes. The menu sets `aria-busy` and holds back the<br />no-results state as soon as `loading` is `true`.<br />Set to `0` to show it at once. | `0` |
| `searchLoading` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to show a spinner in the search input while results are<br />loading. Independent of `loading`, which controls the skeleton menu --<br />combine both to show the spinner while the menu is also loading. | `false` |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Specify the placeholder text | `"Search..."` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `closeButtonLabelText` | `string` | Specify the close button label text | `"Clear search input"` |
| `icon` | `Icon \| undefined` | Specify the icon to render. | _undefined_ |
| `direction` | `"bottom" \| "top"` | Specify the direction of the results menu. | `"bottom"` |
| `portal` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render the menu in a portal to escape `overflow: hidden` containers | `true` |
| `searchClass` | `string` | Specify a class passed to the inner Search element | `""` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the search input | `uniqueId()` |
| `selectTextOnFocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to select the input's text when it receives focus | `false` |
| `debounce` | `number` | Milliseconds to wait after the last input before dispatching `search`.<br />0 (default) does not dispatch `search`. `value`, the fuzzy-match<br />highlighting, and clearing all stay immediate regardless of this delay<br />-- only the `search` event waits. Selecting an item or submitting with<br /><kbd>Enter</kbd> cancels a pending `search` instead of also firing it. | `0` |

## Select

### Basic

Create a basic select menu with select item components. The first item's value is used as the default if selected is not set.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select
  labelText="Account plan"
  on:change={(e) => console.log("value", e.target.value)}
>
  <SelectItem value="free" />
  <SelectItem value="starter" />
  <SelectItem value="team" />
  <SelectItem value="business" />
  <SelectItem value="enterprise" />
</Select>
```

### Reactive

Bind to `selected` for reactive updates, or listen for the `update` event directly--Select dispatches it whenever the selected value changes, which is what powers the two-way binding.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Select, SelectItem, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selected = "starter";
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <Select
    labelText="Account plan"
    helperText="Selected: {selected}"
    bind:selected
  >
    <SelectItem value="free" text="Free" />
    <SelectItem value="starter" text="Starter" />
    <SelectItem value="team" text="Team" />
    <SelectItem value="business" text="Business" />
    <SelectItem value="enterprise" text="Enterprise" />
  </Select>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    size="small"
    disabled={selected === "business"}
    on:click={() => (selected = "business")}
  >
    Set to "business"
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to provide custom label content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select labelText="">
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Account plan</strong>
  <SelectItem value="free" text="Free" />
  <SelectItem value="starter" text="Starter" />
  <SelectItem value="team" text="Team" />
  <SelectItem value="business" text="Business" />
  <SelectItem value="enterprise" text="Enterprise" />
</Select>
```

#### Remove label

Set `noLabel` to `true` to omit the label element entirely. Unlike `hideLabel`, which keeps the label available to screen readers, `noLabel` removes it from the DOM. Provide an accessible name some other way, such as `aria-label` (forwarded through to the select element), when using `noLabel`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select
  noLabel
  labelText="Account plan"
  selected="starter"
  aria-label="Account plan"
>
  <SelectItem value="free" text="Free" />
  <SelectItem value="starter" text="Starter" />
  <SelectItem value="team" text="Team" />
  <SelectItem value="business" text="Business" />
  <SelectItem value="enterprise" text="Enterprise" />
</Select>
```

#### Item groups

Group related options using select item group components. The example below also combines `disabled` and `hidden` on the first `SelectItem` to create a non-selectable placeholder that appears as the initial value but is absent from the open option list.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    SelectItemGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select labelText="Account plan" selected="0">
  <SelectItem value="0" text="Select a plan" disabled hidden />
  <SelectItemGroup label="Individual plans">
    <SelectItem value="free" text="Free" />
    <SelectItem value="starter" text="Starter" />
  </SelectItemGroup>
  <SelectItemGroup label="Team plans">
    <SelectItem value="team" text="Team" />
    <SelectItem value="business" text="Business" />
    <SelectItem value="enterprise" text="Enterprise" />
  </SelectItemGroup>
</Select>
```

#### Disabled group

Set `disabled` on `SelectItemGroup` to disable every item within a group.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    SelectItemGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select labelText="Account plan" selected="free">
  <SelectItemGroup label="Individual plans">
    <SelectItem value="free" text="Free" />
    <SelectItem value="starter" text="Starter" />
  </SelectItemGroup>
  <SelectItemGroup label="Team plans" disabled>
    <SelectItem value="team" text="Team" />
    <SelectItem value="business" text="Business" />
    <SelectItem value="enterprise" text="Enterprise" />
  </SelectItemGroup>
</Select>
```

Set `fluid` to embed the label inside the field. Fluid selects work standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), which applies the variant automatically. The fluid variant cannot be combined with the inline variant.

### Component API

#### `Select` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selected` (Reactive) | `Value \| undefined` | Specify the selected item value. | _undefined_ |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLSelectElement` | Obtain a reference to the select HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Set the size of the select input.<br />Inherits the parent `Form` size when unset.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (the 40px default, which overrides a<br />`Form` size) and `"lg"` (`"xl"`). | _undefined_ |
| `inline` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the inline variant | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the select element | `false` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the select element | `uniqueId()` |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a name attribute for the select element. | _undefined_ |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `noLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to not render a label | `false` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `required` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to mark the field as required | `false` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the select to be read-only | `false` |
| `readonlyText` | `string` | Specify the assistive text announced to screen readers when read-only.<br />Exposed because VoiceOver does not announce `aria-readonly`. | `"Read-only"` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`.<br />Cannot be combined with the inline variant. | `false` |

#### `Select` slots

| Slot            | Detail                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`       | `Record<string, never>` |
| `decorator`     | `Record<string, never>` |
| `labelChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |

## SelectableTile

### Basic

Group multiple selectable tiles together for multi-selection scenarios. Each tile shows a checkbox in its top-right corner: empty until the tile is selected, then checked.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  legendText="Deployment regions"
  name="options"
  selected={["us-east-1", "us-west-2"]}
>
  <SelectableTile value="us-east-1">US East (N. Virginia)</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="us-west-2">US West (Oregon)</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="eu-central-1">EU Central (Frankfurt)</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

### Values

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Give every tile a unique `value` | Tiles that share a value, including tiles that leave out `value`, select together. The group logs a warning when it finds a shared value. |
| Remove a value from `selected` yourself when its tile goes away | Unmounting a tile, for example while filtering a list, keeps its value in `selected`, so the choice survives the filter. |

### Selection

Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while clicking a tile, or while pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> on a focused tile, to apply its new checked state to every tile between it and the last tile toggled. Disabled tiles are skipped.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup legendText="Deployment regions" name="options-range">
  <SelectableTile value="us-east-1">US East (N. Virginia)</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="us-west-2">US West (Oregon)</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="eu-central-1">EU Central (Frankfurt)</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="ap-south-1">Asia Pacific (Mumbai)</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

### Reactive

#### One-way binding

Pass `selected` to `SelectableTileGroup` and update it from the `change` event, which fires once per toggle or range with every selected value. For per-tile reactions, `select` and `deselect` fire once for each tile that changes, including every tile in a range.

Inside a group, the group's `selected` is the source of truth. A tile's own `selected` prop only sets its initial state, so update the group's array rather than each tile.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const values = ["Lite plan", "Standard plan", "Plus plan"];

  let selected = [values[0], values[1]];
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <SelectableTileGroup
    legendText="Service pricing tiers"
    name="plan"
    {selected}
    on:change={({ detail }) => (selected = detail)}
  >
    {#each values as value}
      <SelectableTile {value}>{value}</SelectableTile>
    {/each}
  </SelectableTileGroup>
  <div>Selected: <strong>{selected.join(", ") || "None"}</strong></div>
  <Button
    size="small"
    kind="tertiary"
    disabled={selected.length === 0}
    on:click={() => (selected = [])}
  >
    Clear selection
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

#### Two-way binding

Bind to `selected` for simpler state management.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const values = ["Lite plan", "Standard plan", "Plus plan"];

  let selected = [values[0], values[1]];
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <SelectableTileGroup
    legendText="Service pricing tiers"
    name="plan"
    bind:selected
  >
    {#each values as value}
      <SelectableTile {value}>{value}</SelectableTile>
    {/each}
  </SelectableTileGroup>
  <div>Selected: <strong>{selected.join(", ") || "None"}</strong></div>
  <Button
    size="small"
    disabled={selected.length === 1 && selected[0] === values[1]}
    on:click={() => (selected = [values[1]])}
  >
    Set to "{values[1]}" only
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

### Legend

#### Custom content

Use the `legendChildren` slot on `SelectableTileGroup` to provide custom legend content instead of `legendText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  name="options-legend-slot"
  selected={["us-east-1", "us-west-2"]}
>
  <strong slot="legendChildren">Deployment regions</strong>
  <SelectableTile value="us-east-1">US East (N. Virginia)</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="us-west-2">US West (Oregon)</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="eu-central-1">EU Central (Frankfurt)</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

#### Hidden

Hide the legend visually by setting `hideLegend` to `true`. The legend remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  hideLegend
  legendText="Deployment regions"
  name="options-hidden-legend"
  selected={["us-east-1"]}
>
  <SelectableTile value="us-east-1">US East (N. Virginia)</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="us-west-2">US West (Oregon)</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="eu-central-1">EU Central (Frankfurt)</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

### AI label

Put an `AILabel` in the `decorator` slot to mark the tile's content as AI-generated. The tile shows the AI surface, and the label sits in the top-right corner, beside the checkbox at the `"xs"` size.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, SelectableTile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTile>
  Recommended plan: Team
  <AILabel slot="decorator">
    <p>Recommended for a workspace with 8 to 20 active members.</p>
  </AILabel>
</SelectableTile>
```

#### Rounded corners

Set `rounded` to `true` to round the corners of a tile with a decorator. Carbon reserves rounded tiles for AI content, so a tile without a decorator stays square.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, SelectableTile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTile rounded>
  Recommended plan: Team
  <AILabel slot="decorator">
    <p>Recommended for a workspace with 8 to 20 active members.</p>
  </AILabel>
</SelectableTile>
```

### Small size

Set `size="sm"` on the SelectableTileGroup for compact tiles, such as rows in a list of choices: less padding, no minimum height, and the checkbox pulled in. A tile's own `size` overrides the group's.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  legendText="Extras"
  name="extras"
  selected={["breakfast"]}
  size="sm"
>
  <SelectableTile value="breakfast">Breakfast</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="parking">Parking</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="late-checkout">Late checkout</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Layer,
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <SelectableTileGroup
      legendText="Deployment regions"
      name="options-layer"
      selected={["us-east-1", "us-west-2"]}
    >
      <SelectableTile value="us-east-1">US East (N. Virginia)</SelectableTile>
      <SelectableTile value="us-west-2">US West (Oregon)</SelectableTile>
      <SelectableTile value="eu-central-1">
        EU Central (Frankfurt)
      </SelectableTile>
    </SelectableTileGroup>
  </Box>
</Layer>
```
