## SessionStorage

### Basic

See how the component maintains state within a session. Toggle the switch and refresh the page to see the persisted state. State is cleared when the tab is closed. Unlike [LocalStorage](/components/LocalStorage), data is isolated per tab.

The component listens for the [storage event](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/storage_event) so updates from another same-origin document in the same tab (for example, an iframe) stay in sync. Session storage is isolated per tab, so this event does not propagate across tabs or windows. When the key is removed from a shared session context, the bound value resets to undefined so the next local write does not re-persist stale data.

This example logs the `save` and `update` events as they fire -- see [Events](#events) for what each one means and its payload shape.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SessionStorage, Toggle } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let toggled = false;
  let events = [];

  // `document` is undefined during server-side rendering.
  $: if (typeof document !== "undefined") {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute("theme", toggled ? "g100" : "white");
  }
</script>

<SessionStorage
  key="dark-mode-session"
  bind:value={toggled}
  on:save={() => {
    events = [...events, { event: "on:save" }];
  }}
  on:update={({ detail }) => {
    events = [...events, { event: "on:update", detail }];
  }}
/>

<Toggle size="sm" labelText="Dark mode" bind:toggled />

<br />

<pre>{JSON.stringify(events, null, 2)}</pre>
```

### Persisting objects and arrays

The bound value can be any JSON-serializable data; objects and arrays are serialized with JSON.stringify. Strings are stored as is, except strings that look like JSON (such as `"123"` or `"true"`), which are JSON-encoded so they read back as strings rather than numbers or booleans. The component compares the serialized form to decide when to write, which has two consequences:

- Reassigning to a new object or array with **identical contents** does not trigger a redundant write.
- **In-place mutations** (for example, changing a nested theme property) persist only when you signal the change to Svelte. Reassign the value (`value = { ...value, theme: "light" }`) or use the self-assignment idiom (`value = value`); a bare mutation alone will not re-render and therefore will not persist.

In this example, the text inputs bind directly to nested properties and the button mutates the object in place. Edit a field and refresh the page to confirm the change is persisted within the session.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    SessionStorage,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  // A nested object value. Editing a nested field -- either through a two-way
  // binding or an explicit in-place mutation signalled with `value = value` --
  // is persisted because the component compares the serialized form.
  let settings = { profile: { name: "Ada", role: "Engineer" }, visits: 0 };
  let events = [];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <SessionStorage
    key="user-profile-draft"
    bind:value={settings}
    on:update={({ detail }) => {
      events = [...events, { event: "on:update", detail }];
    }}
  />

  <div>
    Edit the nested fields below, then refresh the page to confirm the changes
    survive within the session. The two-way bindings mutate
    <code>settings</code>
    in place; the component still persists them.
  </div>

  <TextInput
    labelText="Name (binds to settings.profile.name)"
    bind:value={settings.profile.name}
  />

  <TextInput
    labelText="Role (binds to settings.profile.role)"
    bind:value={settings.profile.role}
  />

  <Button
    size="small"
    on:click={() => {
      settings.visits += 1; // in-place mutation
      settings = settings; // signal the change to Svelte
    }}
  >
    Increment visits ({settings.visits})
  </Button>

  <div>
    <strong>Current value:</strong>
    <pre>{JSON.stringify(settings, null, 2)}</pre>
  </div>

  <div>
    <strong>Updates (note prevValue is a true snapshot):</strong>
    <pre>{JSON.stringify(events, null, 2)}</pre>
  </div>
</Stack>
```

### Reactive key

The storage key is also reactive -- set `key` to switch between contexts, useful for per-user settings.

In this example, each user has their own theme preference stored under a separate key. When you switch users, the component automatically loads that user's saved preference.

Switching keys only hydrates the bound value from storage; it does not dispatch [`update`](#update). The event log below should stay empty when you change users and only record entries when you change the theme.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    SessionStorage,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedUser = "user-1";
  let theme = "white";
  let events = [];

  $: storageKey = `theme-preference-${selectedUser}`;
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    Try selecting different users and changing their theme preferences. Each
    user's preference is stored separately and persists within the session.
  </div>
  <SessionStorage
    key={storageKey}
    bind:value={theme}
    on:update={({ detail }) => {
      events = [...events, { event: "on:update", detail }];
    }}
  />
  <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Select user" bind:selected={selectedUser}>
    <RadioButton labelText="User 1" value="user-1" />
    <RadioButton labelText="User 2" value="user-2" />
    <RadioButton labelText="User 3" value="user-3" />
  </RadioButtonGroup>
  <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Theme preference" bind:selected={theme}>
    <RadioButton labelText="White" value="white" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 10" value="g10" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 80" value="g80" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 90" value="g90" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 100" value="g100" />
  </RadioButtonGroup>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <div>
      <strong>Current key:</strong>
      {storageKey}
    </div>
    <div>
      <strong>Current theme:</strong>
      {theme}
    </div>
  </Stack>
  <strong> Updates: </strong>
  <pre>{JSON.stringify(events, null, 2)}</pre>
</Stack>
```

### Disabling sync

With sync enabled by default, the component listens for storage events and updates the bound value when another same-origin document in this tab writes the same key, such as an iframe. Set `sync="off"` to ignore those writes. The component still loads storage on mount and saves your own changes.

Session storage is already per tab, so this matters mainly when an iframe shares the session. Turn sync off when the host page should not follow iframe writes, or when the app handles conflicts itself. Sync is reactive, so you can change it at runtime.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SessionStorage } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SessionStorage key="draft-form-data" bind:value sync="off" />
```

### Clear item, clear all

The component provides methods to manage stored data:

| Method      | Description                       |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| `clearItem` | Remove a specific key-value pair. |
| `clearAll`  | Remove all stored data.           |

Use `bind:this` to access these methods. Both also reset the bound value to `undefined` and dispatch [`update`](#update), so there is no need to reset it yourself. The key stays cleared until the value changes again.

In this example, toggle the switch and refresh the page to confirm the value persists, then try either button to clear storage.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    SessionStorage,
    Stack,
    Toggle,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let storage;
  let toggled = false;

  // `document` is undefined during server-side rendering.
  $: if (typeof document !== "undefined") {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute("theme", toggled ? "g100" : "white");
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <SessionStorage
    key="dark-mode-session"
    bind:this={storage}
    bind:value={toggled}
  />

  <Toggle size="sm" labelText="Dark mode" bind:toggled />

  <div>
    Toggle the switch, then refresh the page to confirm the value persists.
    <code>clearItem</code>
    removes just this key; <code>clearAll</code> removes every key in session storage.
    Either way, the toggle resets.
  </div>

  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Button size="small" on:click={() => storage.clearItem()}>
      Clear item
    </Button>
    <Button size="small" kind="danger" on:click={() => storage.clearAll()}>
      Clear all
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Events

Respond to storage writes, cross-document updates, and write failures.

#### Save

Dispatched once on mount, when `key` is not already present in storage -- right after the component seeds storage with the current `value`. The payload is always `null`.

This fires the first time a key is used in the current session, and again after storage is cleared and the page is refreshed (see [Clear item, clear all](#clear-item-clear-all)). The [Basic](#basic) example above logs this event.

#### Update

Dispatched whenever the stored value changes: after a local bound-value write, after `clearItem` or `clearAll`, or after `sync` picks up a matching write from another same-origin document in this tab (see [Disabling sync](#disabling-sync)). The payload is `{ prevValue, value }`; `prevValue` is a snapshot taken before the change, not a live reference to the current value.

Switching `key` hydrates the bound value from storage but does not dispatch this event (see [Reactive key](#reactive-key)).

The [Basic](#basic), [Persisting objects and arrays](#persisting-objects-and-arrays), and [Reactive key](#reactive-key) examples above all log this event.

#### Error

Dispatched when a write to session storage fails -- for example, when storage quota is exceeded, or access is denied such as in a private browsing mode that blocks Web Storage. The payload is `{ error }`, where `error` is the value thrown by the underlying `sessionStorage.setItem` call.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SessionStorage } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SessionStorage
  key="draft-form-data"
  bind:value
  on:error={({ detail }) => console.error("Failed to persist:", detail.error)}
/>
```

---

### Component API

#### `SessionStorage` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `T` | Provide a value to persist. | `""` |
| `key` | `string` | Specify the session storage key. | `"session-storage-key"` |
| `sync` | `"on" \| "off"` | `"off"` ignores storage events from other documents in this tab (e.g. an<br />iframe). `"on"` (default) keeps the previous behavior. | `"on"` |
| `clearItem` | `() => void` | Remove the persisted key value from the browser's session storage.<br />Also resets the bound `value` to `undefined` and dispatches `update`. | _undefined_ |
| `clearAll` | `() => void` | Clear all key values from the browser's session storage.<br />Also resets the bound `value` to `undefined` and dispatches `update`. | _undefined_ |

#### `SessionStorage` forwarded events

| Event       |
| ----------- |
| `on:error`  |
| `on:save`   |
| `on:update` |


## ShapeIndicator

### Basic

Create a shape indicator with `kind` and `label`. For a version that pairs a status icon with more visual weight instead of a shape, see [IconIndicator](/components/IconIndicator).

```svelte
<script>
  import { ShapeIndicator } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ShapeIndicator kind="stable" label="Stable" />
```

### Kinds

Set `kind` to match the status being communicated.

Each kind reads a Carbon v11 `status-*` theme token, such as `status-orange` for `medium`, so it follows the theme. In light themes, the `medium`, `low` and `cautious` shapes have a darker edge.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ShapeIndicator, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack gap={3}>
  <ShapeIndicator kind="failed" label="Failed" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="critical" label="Critical" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="high" label="High" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="medium" label="Medium" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="low" label="Low" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="cautious" label="Cautious" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="undefined" label="Undefined" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="stable" label="Stable" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="informative" label="Informative" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="incomplete" label="Incomplete" />
  <ShapeIndicator kind="draft" label="Draft" />
</Stack>
```

### Sizes

Set `textSize` to control the label text size.

#### 12px (default)

```svelte
<script>
  import { ShapeIndicator } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ShapeIndicator kind="stable" label="Stable" />
```

#### 14px

```svelte
<script>
  import { ShapeIndicator } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ShapeIndicator kind="stable" label="Stable" textSize={14} />
```

### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot for custom label content instead of `label`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ShapeIndicator } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ShapeIndicator kind="stable" label="Stable">
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Custom label</strong>
</ShapeIndicator>
```

### Component API

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` (Required) | `"failed" \| "critical" \| "high" \| "medium" \| "low" \| "cautious" \| "undefined" \| "stable" \| "informative" \| "incomplete" \| "draft"` | Specify the kind of the shape indicator. | _undefined_ |
| `label` (Required) | `string` | Specify the label displayed next to the shape. | _undefined_ |
| `textSize` | `12 \| 14` | Specify the text size of the shape indicator. | `12` |

## SidePanel

### Basic

Bind `open` to show the panel. It docks under the UI Shell header and closes from its close button or <kbd>Escape</kbd>. Put footer buttons in the `actions` slot. The panel lays them out in an [ActionSet](/components/ActionSet) sized to the panel. Set `condensedActions` to `true` for 48px buttons in place of 64px.

Use a side panel for work that relates to the page under it, such as editing a row or filtering a list. For a task that needs the user's full attention, use a [Modal](/components/Modal). For global tools such as notifications or a switcher, use a [UI Shell](/components/UIShell) `HeaderPanel`.

`titleText` names the panel for screen readers. A panel without a title needs an `aria-label`. A long title wraps onto more lines. It is never cut off.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    SidePanel,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Edit deployment</Button>
</Content>

<SidePanel
  bind:open
  labelText="checkout-api"
  titleText="Edit deployment"
  subtitleText="Changes apply on the next deploy."
>
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <TextInput labelText="Service name" value="checkout-api" />
    <Select labelText="Region" selected="us-east">
      <SelectItem value="us-east" text="US East" />
      <SelectItem value="eu-central" text="EU Central" />
      <SelectItem value="ap-south" text="AP South" />
    </Select>
    <TextInput labelText="Start command" value="node server.js" />
  </Stack>
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => (open = false)}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = false)}>Save</Button>
  </svelte:fragment>
</SidePanel>
```

### Focus

When the panel opens, focus moves to the first match:

1. The element that matches `selectorPrimaryFocus` (default: `[data-modal-primary-focus]`)
2. The first input, textarea or select
3. The close button

When the panel closes, focus goes back to the element that opened it. A panel already open when the page loads leaves focus where it is, unless it's modal. Set `selectorPrimaryFocus` to `null` to move focus yourself.

### Closing

The panel dispatches a cancelable `close` event. Call `e.preventDefault()` to keep it open, for example while a form has unsaved changes. `e.detail.trigger` tells you what closed it: `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, `"close-button"` or `"programmatic"`. The last one means your code set `open` to `false`.

Set `hideCloseButton` to `true` to remove the close button. Give the user another way out, such as a Cancel button.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    InlineNotification,
    SidePanel,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
  let name = "checkout-api";
  let saved = name;
  let showWarning = false;

  $: dirty = name !== saved;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      showWarning = false;
      open = true;
    }}
  >
    Rename service
  </Button>
</Content>

<SidePanel
  bind:open
  titleText="Rename service"
  on:close={(e) => {
    if (dirty && e.detail.trigger !== "programmatic") {
      e.preventDefault();
      showWarning = true;
    }
  }}
>
  <Stack gap={6}>
    {#if showWarning}
      <InlineNotification
        kind="warning"
        title="Unsaved changes"
        subtitle="Save or discard your changes to close the panel."
        hideCloseButton
      />
    {/if}
    <TextInput labelText="Service name" bind:value={name} />
  </Stack>
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button
      kind="secondary"
      on:click={() => {
        name = saved;
        open = false;
      }}
    >
      Discard
    </Button>
    <Button
      on:click={() => {
        saved = name;
        open = false;
      }}
    >
      Save
    </Button>
  </svelte:fragment>
</SidePanel>
```

### Without a header

The panel docks under the UI Shell `Header` when one is on the page, and spans the full height without one. To dock it under another fixed bar, set the `--ccs-side-panel-top` custom property to the bar's height. Set it on `:root` for all panels, or as a prop on one: `<SidePanel --ccs-side-panel-top="4rem">`. A server render places the panel under the header until the page loads.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, SidePanel } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>View service</Button>

<SidePanel bind:open titleText="checkout-api">
  <p>Node.js web service in US East, on the Standard plan.</p>
</SidePanel>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to control the panel width. The default is `"md"`, 480px. A panel never takes more than 75% of the window.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    SidePanel,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const sizes = ["xs", "sm", "md", "lg", "xl", "2xl"];

  let open = true;
  let size = "md";
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Size" bind:selected={size}>
      {#each sizes as value (value)}
        <RadioButton labelText={value} {value} />
      {/each}
    </RadioButtonGroup>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>View service</Button>
  </Stack>
</Content>

<SidePanel bind:open {size} titleText="checkout-api">
  <p>Node.js web service in US East, on the Standard plan.</p>
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => (open = false)}>Close</Button>
    <Button>Open dashboard</Button>
  </svelte:fragment>
</SidePanel>
```

### Placement

Set `placement` to `"start"` or `"end"` to choose the edge the panel docks to. The default is `"end"`, the right edge in a left-to-right layout and the left edge in a right-to-left one. Carbon React's `"left"` and `"right"` map to `"start"` and `"end"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    SidePanel,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
  let placement = "start";
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Placement" bind:selected={placement}>
      <RadioButton labelText="Start" value="start" />
      <RadioButton labelText="End" value="end" />
    </RadioButtonGroup>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Filter services</Button>
  </Stack>
</Content>

<SidePanel bind:open {placement} size="sm" titleText="Filters">
  <p>Show services by runtime, region and plan.</p>
</SidePanel>
```

### Overlay

Set `includeOverlay` to `true` to dim the page behind the panel. The panel is then modal: it keeps focus inside and stops the page from scrolling. Clicking the overlay closes a panel without actions. A panel with actions stays open, so a stray click can't discard a form. Set `preventCloseOnClickOutside` to change either.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    SidePanel,
    Stack,
    TextArea,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Report an incident</Button>
</Content>

<SidePanel bind:open includeOverlay titleText="Report an incident">
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <TextInput labelText="Summary" value="Checkout latency above 2s" />
    <TextArea
      labelText="Details"
      value="p95 latency on checkout-api rose after the 14:05 deploy."
    />
  </Stack>
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => (open = false)}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = false)}>Submit</Button>
  </svelte:fragment>
</SidePanel>
```

### Slide-in

Set `slideIn` to `true` to push the page content aside so the panel doesn't cover it. Set `selectorPageContent` to the element to push, such as the UI Shell `Content`. A slide-in panel is part of the page: it leaves focus where it is and does not close on <kbd>Escape</kbd>.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    SidePanel,
    Stack,
    StructuredList,
    StructuredListBody,
    StructuredListCell,
    StructuredListRow,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const events = [
    { time: "14:05", text: "Deploy started" },
    { time: "14:07", text: "Build succeeded" },
    { time: "14:08", text: "Deploy live" },
  ];

  let open = true;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <p>
      checkout-api serves 1.2k requests per minute across three instances in US
      East. The panel pushes this content aside instead of covering it.
    </p>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
      {open ? "Hide activity" : "Show activity"}
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</Content>

<SidePanel
  bind:open
  slideIn
  selectorPageContent="#main-content"
  size="sm"
  titleText="Activity"
>
  <StructuredList condensed>
    <StructuredListBody>
      {#each events as event (event.time)}
        <StructuredListRow>
          <StructuredListCell>{event.time}</StructuredListCell>
          <StructuredListCell>{event.text}</StructuredListCell>
        </StructuredListRow>
      {/each}
    </StructuredListBody>
  </StructuredList>
</SidePanel>
```

### Resizable

Set `resizable` to `true` to let users drag the panel's free edge, or move it with the arrow keys once it has focus. <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> jump to the narrowest and widest widths, and a double click restores `size`. Bind `width` to read or save the width. The `resize` event fires once per gesture. The handle hides on narrow screens.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    SidePanel,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
  let width;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>View logs</Button>
    <p>Width: {width ?? "md"}</p>
  </Stack>
</Content>

<SidePanel bind:open bind:width resizable titleText="Logs">
  <p>14:08:12 GET /health 200 3ms</p>
  <p>14:08:15 POST /orders 201 48ms</p>
  <p>14:08:19 GET /orders/1042 200 12ms</p>
</SidePanel>
```

### Multi-step

Set `currentStep` to show a back button from the second step on. Listen for `back` to go to the previous step. If the button that has focus goes away when the step changes, focus moves to the first field of the new step.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    SidePanel,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const steps = ["Create service", "Choose a plan"];

  let open = true;
  let currentStep = 0;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      currentStep = 0;
      open = true;
    }}
  >
    Create service
  </Button>
</Content>

<SidePanel
  bind:open
  {currentStep}
  titleText={steps[currentStep]}
  on:back={() => (currentStep -= 1)}
>
  {#if currentStep === 0}
    <Stack gap={6}>
      <TextInput labelText="Service name" value="checkout-api" />
      <TextInput labelText="Repository" value="acme/checkout" />
    </Stack>
  {:else}
    <Select labelText="Plan" selected="standard">
      <SelectItem value="starter" text="Starter" />
      <SelectItem value="standard" text="Standard" />
      <SelectItem value="pro" text="Pro" />
    </Select>
  {/if}
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => (open = false)}>Cancel</Button>
    {#if currentStep === 0}
      <Button on:click={() => (currentStep = 1)}>Next</Button>
    {:else}
      <Button on:click={() => (open = false)}>Create</Button>
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</SidePanel>
```

### Action toolbar

Put buttons for the panel's content in the `toolbar` slot, below the title.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Content, Header, SidePanel } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Download from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Download.svelte";
  import Renew from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Renew.svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>View environment</Button>
</Content>

<SidePanel
  bind:open
  titleText="Environment"
  subtitleText="Variables for checkout-api in production."
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="toolbar">
    <Button kind="ghost" size="small" icon={Renew}>Sync</Button>
    <Button kind="ghost" size="small" icon={Copy} iconDescription="Copy" />
    <Button
      kind="ghost"
      size="small"
      icon={Download}
      iconDescription="Download"
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
  <p>DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL and 12 more.</p>
</SidePanel>
```

### AI label

Put an [AILabel](/components/AILabel) in the `decorator` slot to mark AI-generated content. The panel takes the AI surface.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    AILabel,
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    SidePanel,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Explain incident</Button>
</Content>

<SidePanel
  bind:open
  titleText="Incident summary"
  subtitleText="Generated from the last hour of logs."
>
  <AILabel slot="decorator">
    <p>Summarized by a language model. Check it against the logs.</p>
  </AILabel>
  <p>
    p95 latency on checkout-api rose to 2.4s after the 14:05 deploy. The new
    build opens a database connection per request.
  </p>
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => (open = false)}>Dismiss</Button>
    <Button>Roll back</Button>
  </svelte:fragment>
</SidePanel>
```

### Layering

The panel starts a [Layer](/components/Layer) wherever it renders, like a modal. Its body sits one level up, so fields and tiles in it contrast with the panel, and a `Layer` inside steps up again.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    Layer,
    SidePanel,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
<Content>
  <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Edit scaling</Button>
</Content>

<SidePanel bind:open titleText="Scaling">
  <Stack gap={6}>
    <TextInput labelText="Minimum instances" value="2" />
    <Tile>
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <p>Autoscaling</p>
        <Layer>
          <TextInput labelText="Target CPU (%)" value="70" />
        </Layer>
      </Stack>
    </Tile>
  </Stack>
</SidePanel>
```

### Right-to-left

Inside a `dir="rtl"` page or a [LayoutDirection](/components/LayoutDirection), the panel mirrors: an end panel docks to the left, and the close and back buttons swap corners. The resize handle and its arrow keys follow the edge. To render the panel outside a transformed container, wrap it in a [Portal](/components/Portal), which keeps the direction and the [ThemeZone](/components/ThemeZone) theme.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Content,
    Header,
    LayoutDirection,
    SidePanel,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<LayoutDirection dir="rtl">
  <Header companyName="IBM" platformName="Cloud" />
  <Content>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>تعديل الخدمة</Button>
  </Content>

  <SidePanel bind:open resizable currentStep={1} titleText="تعديل الخدمة">
    <TextInput labelText="اسم الخدمة" value="checkout-api" />
    <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
      <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => (open = false)}>إلغاء</Button>
      <Button on:click={() => (open = false)}>حفظ</Button>
    </svelte:fragment>
  </SidePanel>
</LayoutDirection>
```

---

### Component API

#### `SidePanel` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the panel. Opening it moves focus into it; a<br />panel already open when it mounts leaves focus where it is, unless it<br />is modal. | `false` |
| `width` (Reactive) | `number \| undefined` | The width in pixels the user resized the panel to, or `undefined` to<br />follow `size`. Rendered clamped between the `xs` width and 75% of the<br />window. Has no effect unless `resizable` is `true`. | _undefined_ |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLElement` | Obtain a reference to the panel element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "2xl"` | Set the panel width. | `"md"` |
| `placement` | `"start" \| "end" \| "left" \| "right"` | Set the edge the panel docks to. `"end"` is the right edge in a<br />left-to-right layout and the left edge in a right-to-left one.<br />Also accepts Carbon React's `"right"` and `"left"`, which map to<br />`"end"` and `"start"`. | `"end"` |
| `slideIn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to push the page content aside instead of covering it.<br />Set `selectorPageContent` to the element to push. A slide-in panel<br />does not move focus, trap it, or close on Escape. | `false` |
| `selectorPageContent` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a CSS selector for the page content that a `slideIn` panel<br />pushes aside. Without a match, the panel covers the content. | _undefined_ |
| `includeOverlay` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to dim the page behind the panel. The panel is then<br />modal: it traps focus and locks page scroll. Has no effect when<br />`slideIn` is `true`. | `false` |
| `preventCloseOnClickOutside` | `boolean \| undefined` | Control whether clicking the overlay closes the panel.<br />By default, a panel without `actions` closes and a panel with<br />`actions` stays open, as modals do in Carbon v11.<br />Set to `true` to always keep the panel open, or `false` to always<br />close it. | _undefined_ |
| `titleText` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the title. It names the panel. A `title` attribute passes<br />through to the panel element. | _undefined_ |
| `subtitleText` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the subtitle. It describes the panel. | _undefined_ |
| `labelText` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a label above the title. Renders only with a `titleText`. | _undefined_ |
| `hideCloseButton` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to hide the close button | `false` |
| `closeIconDescription` | `string` | Specify the close button's accessible name | `"Close"` |
| `currentStep` | `number` | Specify the step of a multi-step panel. A step greater than `0`<br />shows a back button, which fires `back`. | `0` |
| `navigationBackIconDescription` | `string` | Specify the back button's accessible name | `"Back"` |
| `condensedActions` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for 48px footer buttons instead of 64px | `false` |
| `resizable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to let the user resize the panel by dragging its free<br />edge, or with the arrow keys once the edge has focus. The handle<br />hides below the `md` breakpoint. | `false` |
| `resizeHandleLabel` | `string` | Specify the ARIA label for the resize handle | `"Resize side panel"` |
| `resizeEnterDelayMs` | `number` | Specify the delay in milliseconds before hovering the resize handle<br />highlights it and shows the resize cursor. | `150` |
| `selectorPrimaryFocus` | `null \| string` | Specify a selector for the element to focus when the panel opens.<br />Without a match, focus goes to the first form field, then the close<br />button. Set to `null` to leave focus where it is. A `slideIn` panel<br />focuses only a match. | `"[data-modal-primary-focus]"` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the panel.<br />The title and subtitle ids derive from it as `{id}-title` and<br />`{id}-subtitle`. | `uniqueId()` |

#### `SidePanel` slots

| Slot               | Detail                  |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- |
| `default`          | `Record<string, never>` |
| `actions`          | `Record<string, never>` |
| `decorator`        | `Record<string, never>` |
| `subtitleChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `toolbar`          | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `SidePanel` forwarded events

| Event        |
| ------------ |
| `on:keydown` |

#### `SidePanel` dispatched events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on:back` | `null` | Fires when the back button is clicked. It shows while `currentStep` is greater than `0`. |
| `on:close` | `{<br />  trigger:<br />    \| "escape-key"<br />    \| "outside-click"<br />    \| "close-button"<br />    \| "programmatic";<br />}` |  |
| `on:open` | `null` |  |
| `on:resize` | `{<br />  width: number \| undefined;<br />}` | Fires once the user finishes resizing (drag release, key press or double click) and the width changed. `width` is `undefined` after a double click restores the `size` width. |

#### `SidePanel` $$restProps

`SidePanel` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div | aside` element.


## SkeletonIcon

### Sizes

SkeletonIcon wraps [SkeletonPlaceholder](/components/SkeletonPlaceholder) for icon-sized areas. Carbon icons use a 16/20/24/32 pixel scale, but you can set any pixel value with `size`.

#### 16px (default)

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonIcon />
```

#### 20px

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonIcon size={20} />
```

#### 24px

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonIcon size={24} />
```

#### 32px

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonIcon size={32} />
```

### Custom width and height

SkeletonIcon also accepts `width` and `height`, forwarded to the underlying [SkeletonPlaceholder](/components/SkeletonPlaceholder), for a non-square placeholder instead of `size`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonIcon width="2rem" height="1rem" />
```

### AI

Set `ai` to `true` for an icon that AI is generating. The skeleton turns blue, and a gradient sweeps across it. The sweep stops when the user prefers reduced motion.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonIcon, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5}>
  <SkeletonIcon ai />
  <SkeletonIcon ai size={20} />
  <SkeletonIcon ai size={24} />
  <SkeletonIcon ai size={32} />
</Stack>
```

---

### Component API

#### `SkeletonIcon` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `(16 \| 20 \| 24 \| 32 \| (number & {}))` | Specify the icon size.<br />Carbon icons use a 16/20/24/32 scale, but any number (pixels) can be used. | `16` |
| `ai` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the AI variant, a blue shimmer for content that<br />AI is generating | `false` |

#### `SkeletonIcon` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |


## SkeletonPlaceholder

### Basic

Create a basic skeleton placeholder with default styling.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonPlaceholder } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonPlaceholder />
```

### Custom size

Set both width and height with `size`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonPlaceholder } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonPlaceholder size="8rem" />
```

#### Number value

Number values default to pixels.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonPlaceholder } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonPlaceholder size={128} />
```

### Custom width and height

Use `width` and `height` for different dimensions.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonPlaceholder } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonPlaceholder width="20rem" height="10rem" />
```

#### Number values

Number values default to pixels.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonPlaceholder } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonPlaceholder width={320} height={160} />
```

#### Override a single dimension

`width` and `height` each take precedence over `size` independently, so you can set `size` as a base and override just one dimension.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonPlaceholder } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonPlaceholder size="4rem" height="10rem" />
```

### AI

Set `ai` to `true` for content that AI is generating, such as an image or a chart. The placeholder turns blue, and a gradient sweeps across it. The sweep stops when the user prefers reduced motion.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonPlaceholder } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonPlaceholder ai />
```

---

### Component API

#### `SkeletonPlaceholder` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `number \| string \| undefined` | Shorthand size that sets both width and height.<br />Accepts a number (px) or string (e.g., "12rem"). | _undefined_ |
| `width` | `number \| string \| undefined` | Width of the placeholder.<br />Accepts a number (px) or string (e.g., "12rem"). | _undefined_ |
| `height` | `number \| string \| undefined` | Height of the placeholder.<br />Accepts a number (px) or string (e.g., "12rem"). | _undefined_ |
| `ai` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the AI variant, a blue shimmer for content that<br />AI is generating | `false` |

#### `SkeletonPlaceholder` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `SkeletonPlaceholder` $$restProps

`SkeletonPlaceholder` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## SkeletonText

### Basic

Create a basic skeleton text with default styling.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonText />
```

### Heading

Use the heading variant for larger text placeholders.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonText heading />
```

### Paragraph

Use the paragraph variant for multi-line text placeholders.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonText paragraph />
```

#### Custom line count

Specify the number of lines with `lines`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonText paragraph lines={8} />
```

### Width

Set a custom width with `width`, as a percentage or pixel value. This works with any variant, not just paragraph.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonText width="50%" />
```

#### Paragraph

In paragraph mode, each line's width varies around the `width` value instead of using it uniformly, for a more natural look.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonText paragraph width="50%" />
```

### No margin

Set `noMargin` to `true` to remove the bottom margin, for placeholders in a flex or grid layout that sets its own gap.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonText, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={5}>
  <SkeletonText noMargin width="40%" />
  <SkeletonText noMargin width="20%" />
</Stack>
```

### AI

Set `ai` to `true` for text that AI is generating. The skeleton turns blue, and a gradient sweeps across it. The sweep stops when the user prefers reduced motion.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonText ai />
```

#### Paragraph

`ai` works with every variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SkeletonText } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SkeletonText ai paragraph />
```

---

### Component API

#### `SkeletonText` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | `number` | Specify the number of lines to render | `3` |
| `heading` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the heading size variant | `false` |
| `paragraph` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the paragraph size variant | `false` |
| `width` | `string` | Specify the width of the text (% or px) | `"100%"` |
| `noMargin` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the bottom margin, such as for a placeholder<br />in a flex or grid row that sets its own spacing. In a paragraph, only<br />the last line loses its margin, so the lines keep their gaps. | `false` |
| `ai` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the AI variant, a blue shimmer for content that<br />AI is generating | `false` |

#### `SkeletonText` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `SkeletonText` $$restProps

`SkeletonText` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## Slider

### Basic

Create a basic slider with a label and the default range from 0 to 100.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Instances" value={0} />
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to `"xs"` for a 24px number input. Inside a `Form` with `size="xs"`, sliders inherit it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider, Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider size="xs" labelText="Instances" value={4} max={10} />
<RangeSlider
  size="xs"
  labelText="Maintenance window (hours)"
  value={2}
  valueUpper={6}
  max={24}
/>
```

### Helper text

Add helper text below the slider to provide additional context or instructions.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Instances"
  helperText="Applies to new deployments only"
  value={4}
/>
```

### Labels and layout

Control how the slider label, text input, and width render.

#### Full width

Set `fullWidth` to `true` for the slider to span the full width of its container.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Instances" fullWidth value={0} />
```

#### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Instances" hideLabel value={0} />
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to provide custom label content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="" value={0}>
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Instances</strong>
</Slider>
```

#### Hidden text input

Set `hideTextInput` to `true` to hide the numeric input while keeping the slider.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Instances" hideTextInput value={0} />
```

#### Hidden range labels

Set `hideRangeLabels` to `true` to hide the min and max labels beside the track, as when a readout elsewhere already shows the range.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Rollout" hideRangeLabels fullWidth value={35} />
```

#### Input type

Set `inputType` to change the native `type` attribute of the text input--for example, `"text"` to avoid the browser's built-in number spinner controls. The bound `value` stays numeric regardless of `inputType`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider inputType="text" labelText="Instances" value={0} />
```

#### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to select the full value in the number input when it receives focus.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider selectTextOnFocus labelText="Instances" value={4} />
```

### Range and steps

Control the allowed values and increment.

#### Custom range

Set `min`, `max`, `minLabel`, and `maxLabel` to customize the range.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
/>
```

#### Custom step

Set `step` to control increment size.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
  step={10}
/>
```

#### Step multiplier

Set `stepMultiplier` to control how far <kbd>Shift</kbd> + Arrow key presses, or <kbd>PageUp</kbd>/<kbd>PageDown</kbd>, move the value. Holding Shift while pressing an arrow key, or pressing <kbd>PageUp</kbd>/<kbd>PageDown</kbd> alone, moves the value by `(max - min) / stepMultiplier`, rounded to the nearest `step`, instead of a single step. Defaults to `4`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
  step={10}
  stepMultiplier={2}
/>
```

### Formatting

Control how range labels and `aria-valuetext` are displayed.

#### Formatted values

Use `formatValue` to format range labels and `aria-valuetext` (for example currency or percent). The text input and bound `value` stay numeric.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Budget"
  value={50}
  formatValue={(v) =>
    new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
      style: "currency",
      currency: "USD",
      maximumFractionDigits: 0,
    }).format(v)}
/>
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="CPU utilization" value={75} formatValue={(v) => `${v}%`} />
```

### Marks

Set `marks` to show tick marks along the track. Pass an array of stops with optional labels, or set `marks` to `true` to tick every `step`. Snapping follows `step` unless [`snapToMarks`](#snap-to-marks) or [`markSnapDistance`](#magnetic-marks) is set.

While the value sits on a labeled mark, screen readers announce the label as the value text. With `formatValue`, they announce the formatted value followed by the label, for example "68°F, Comfortable".

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Log verbosity"
  hideTextInput
  min={0}
  max={3}
  step={1}
  value={1}
  marks={[
    { value: 0, label: "Off" },
    { value: 1, label: "Low" },
    { value: 2, label: "Med" },
    { value: 3, label: "High" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Every step

Set `marks` to `true` to place a tick at every `step`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Instances"
  hideTextInput
  min={0}
  max={10}
  step={2}
  value={4}
  marks
/>
```

#### Snap to marks

Set `snapToMarks` to `true` to make dragging and clicking land on the nearest mark instead of the nearest `step`. <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd>/<kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> (and <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd>/<kbd>ArrowUp</kbd>) move to the adjacent mark; <kbd>Shift</kbd> + Arrow, <kbd>PageUp</kbd>, and <kbd>PageDown</kbd> skip `stepMultiplier` marks. <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> still jump to `min` and `max`. A `value` set programmatically is not moved onto a mark.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Cache size (GB)"
  min={0}
  max={64}
  value={8}
  snapToMarks
  marks={[
    { value: 0, label: "0" },
    { value: 8, label: "8" },
    { value: 16, label: "16" },
    { value: 32, label: "32" },
    { value: 64, label: "64" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Magnetic marks

Set `markSnapDistance` to pull drags and clicks onto a mark once the pointer comes within that many pixels of it. Unlike `snapToMarks`, every other `step` stays reachable, so a meaningful value such as a default or a neutral point is easy to hit without restricting the control to its marks. Arrow keys still move by `step`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Thermostat"
  min={60}
  max={80}
  value={65}
  markSnapDistance={12}
  formatValue={(v) => `${v}°F`}
  marks={[
    { value: 60, label: "Cold" },
    { value: 68, label: "Comfortable" },
    { value: 80, label: "Hot" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Vertical

Set `orientation` to `"vertical"` to lay the track out along the vertical axis, with `min` at the bottom and `max` at the top. <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> and <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> increase the value; <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> and <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> decrease it. The `max` label sits at the top of the track and the `min` label at the bottom, on the side where lines end: the right in a left-to-right page, the left in a right-to-left one. The text input sits below the track.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Volume" orientation="vertical" value={40} />
```

#### Fluid height

A vertical slider fills the height of its container, minus its label and helper text. Without a container height, the track defaults to about 200px.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box display="flex" gap={7}>
  <Box height="12rem">
    <Slider labelText="12rem" orientation="vertical" value={40} />
  </Box>
  <Box height="18rem">
    <Slider labelText="18rem" orientation="vertical" value={40} />
  </Box>
  <Box height="24rem">
    <Slider labelText="24rem" orientation="vertical" value={40} />
  </Box>
</Box>
```

#### Custom range and step

`min`, `max`, `step`, and `stepMultiplier` work the same as on a horizontal slider.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  orientation="vertical"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  step={10}
  value={100}
/>
```

#### Marks

Mark labels render beside the track, on the same side as the range labels, instead of below it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Log verbosity"
  orientation="vertical"
  hideTextInput
  min={0}
  max={3}
  step={1}
  value={1}
  marks={[
    { value: 0, label: "Off" },
    { value: 1, label: "Low" },
    { value: 2, label: "Med" },
    { value: 3, label: "High" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Snap to marks

Combine `orientation="vertical"` with `snapToMarks` to land on a mark when dragging, clicking, or pressing an arrow key.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Cache size (GB)"
  orientation="vertical"
  min={0}
  max={64}
  value={8}
  snapToMarks
  marks={[
    { value: 0, label: "0" },
    { value: 8, label: "8" },
    { value: 16, label: "16" },
    { value: 32, label: "32" },
    { value: 64, label: "64" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Hidden text input

Set `hideTextInput` to `true` to show only the track and range labels.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Volume" orientation="vertical" hideTextInput value={40} />
```

#### Formatted values

`formatValue` formats the range labels and `aria-valuetext`; the bound `value` stays numeric.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="CPU utilization"
  orientation="vertical"
  value={75}
```

#### Disabled

Set `disabled` to `true` to prevent interaction.

```svelte

  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Volume" orientation="vertical" disabled value={40} />
```

#### Read-only

Set `readonly` to `true` to display a value while preventing changes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Volume" orientation="vertical" readonly value={40} />
```

#### Vertical range slider

`RangeSlider` accepts `orientation` too. The lower handle sits below its value and the upper handle above it, with the filled track between them. Clicking or dragging moves whichever handle is vertically closer to the pointer.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Alert threshold (%)"
  orientation="vertical"
  value={20}
  valueUpper={70}
/>
```

#### Read-only vertical range slider

Set `readonly` to `true` to display the range while preventing changes. Each handle stays in the tab order so its value can still be read; arrow keys leave it unchanged.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Alert threshold (%)"
  orientation="vertical"
  readonly
  value={20}
  valueUpper={70}
/>
```

#### Vertical range slider with fluid height

The upper input sits beside the `max` label and the lower input beside the `min` label, so both stay aligned with the track ends as the container grows.

```svelte
<script>

<Box height="24rem">
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <Slider
      labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
      min={10}
      max={990}
      maxLabel="990 MB"
      value={100}
      step={10}
    />
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Events

Respond to value changes as the user drags the handle, uses the keyboard, or edits the text input.

Use `on:input` to listen for every value while dragging or pressing an arrow key, and `on:change` to listen for committed changes--when the drag ends, an arrow key is pressed, or the text input is committed. Both events dispatch the numeric value directly as `event.detail`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  on:input={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // number
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // number
  labelText="Instances"
  value={0}
/>
```

### States

Reflect validation and interaction states.

#### Invalid

Set `invalid` to `true` to show a validation error. Invalid takes precedence over the [warning state](#warning) when both are set.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  invalid
  invalidText="Value must be a multiple of 10"
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={105}
  step={10}
/>
```

#### Warning

Set `warn` to `true` to show a warning. The warning icon appears next to the input field, with a message below the slider.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  warn
  warnText="Value must be an increment of 5"
  labelText="Concurrency limit"
  min={0}
  max={100}
  value={51}
  step={5}
/>
```

#### Disabled

Set `disabled` to `true` to prevent interaction.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  disabled
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
  step={10}
/>
```

#### Read-only

Set `readonly` to `true` to display a value while preventing changes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  readonly
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
  step={10}
/>
```

### Range slider

Use `RangeSlider` to select a range with two handles. Bind to `value` for the lower bound and `valueUpper` for the upper bound. `RangeSlider` supports the same layout and state options as `Slider`, including a [vertical orientation](#vertical-range-slider).

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider labelText="Alert threshold (%)" value={10} valueUpper={90} />
```

#### Full width

Set `fullWidth` to `true` for the range slider to span the full width of its container.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Alert threshold (%)"
  fullWidth
  value={10}
  valueUpper={90}
/>
```

#### Hidden text inputs

Set `hideTextInput` to `true` to hide both numeric inputs while keeping the slider.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Alert threshold (%)"
  hideTextInput
  value={0}
  valueUpper={100}
/>
```

#### Custom range and step

Set `min`, `max`, and `step` to customize the range.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  step={10}
  value={100}
  valueUpper={500}
/>
```

#### Minimum gap

Set `minGap` to keep the handles at least that far apart. Dragging, arrow keys, <kbd>Home</kbd>/<kbd>End</kbd>, and both text inputs stop a handle `minGap` short of the other. A `value` or `valueUpper` set programmatically that closes the gap is corrected by moving `valueUpper` up (or `value` down when `valueUpper` is already at `max`). Defaults to `0`, which lets the handles meet.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Alert threshold (%)"
  minGap={10}
  value={40}
  valueUpper={60}
/>
```

#### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to select the full value in either number input when it receives focus.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  selectTextOnFocus
  labelText="Alert threshold (%)"
  value={10}
  valueUpper={90}
/>
```

#### Formatted values

`formatValue` applies to both thumbs' `aria-valuetext` and the range labels. Bound `value` / `valueUpper` stay numeric.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Price range"
  value={20}
  valueUpper={80}
  formatValue={(v) =>
    new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
      style: "currency",
      currency: "USD",
      maximumFractionDigits: 0,
    }).format(v)}
/>
```

#### Marks

Set `marks` the same way as on `Slider` for tick marks and optional labels. `snapToMarks` and `markSnapDistance` work the same way too; a handle only lands on marks that keep [`minGap`](#minimum-gap) from the other handle.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Log verbosity"
  hideTextInput
  min={0}
  max={3}
  step={1}
  value={0}
  valueUpper={2}
  marks={[
    { value: 0, label: "Off" },
    { value: 1, label: "Low" },
    { value: 2, label: "Med" },
    { value: 3, label: "High" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Drag the range

Set `trackDrag` to `"range"` to move both handles together when a drag starts inside the selected range. The range keeps its width and stops against `min` and `max`, the pointer shows a grab cursor over it, and both handles are highlighted while it moves. A press outside the range still moves the nearer handle. Useful for sliding a fixed-length window, such as a time span, along the track.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Maintenance window (hour)"
  trackDrag="range"
  min={0}
  max={24}
  value={2}
  valueUpper={6}
/>
```

#### Brush a new range

Set `trackDrag` to `"brush"` to also paint a new range by dragging across the track outside the current one; the pointer shows a crosshair there. Press on the empty track, hold, and drag: the range runs from the press point to the pointer, in either direction. A click without dragging moves the nearer handle, as it does by default. Both handles stay keyboard-operable, since neither mode adds a keyboard interaction.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Price range"
  trackDrag="brush"
  value={20}
  valueUpper={40}
  formatValue={(v) => `$${v}`}
/>
```

#### Handle labels

Set `ariaLabelInput` and `ariaLabelInputUpper` to distinguish the lower and upper bound handles for screen reader users. Defaults to `"Lower bound"` and `"Upper bound"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  ariaLabelInput="Minimum price"
  ariaLabelInputUpper="Maximum price"
  labelText="Price range"
  value={20}
  valueUpper={80}
/>
```

#### Events

Use `on:input` and `on:change` the same way as `Slider`. Both events dispatch `{ value, valueUpper }` as `event.detail`.

`on:focus` and `on:blur` fire for each number input and add `handle` so you can tell which bound received the event.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSlider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSlider
  on:input={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // { value: number; valueUpper: number }
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // { value: number; valueUpper: number }
  on:focus={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // { value: number; valueUpper: number; handle: "lower" | "upper" }
  on:blur={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // { value: number; valueUpper: number; handle: "lower" | "upper" }
  labelText="Alert threshold (%)"
  value={10}
  valueUpper={90}
/>
```

Set `invalid` to `true` to show a validation error. Invalid takes precedence over the [warning state](#warning) when both are set.

```svelte
<script>
```

```svelte
  import { RangeSliderSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSliderSkeleton />
```

##### Without label

Show a loading state without a label.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RangeSliderSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<RangeSliderSkeleton hideLabel />
```

```ts
interface RangeSliderChangeDetail {

};
```
