## TableOfContents

### Scroll spy

Add a `TableOfContentsItem` for each section, with `href` set to the section's id, such as `"#overview"`. As the page scrolls, the bar moves to the last section whose top has passed the top of the window. At the end of the page, the last section is selected, even if it is too short to reach the top.

Clicking an item selects it right away and keeps it selected while the page scrolls to the section. On a top-level page, the click is a native hash jump, so the URL hash updates and client-side routers handle it as usual. Inside an iframe, as in this example, the table of contents scrolls only the frame, not the page around it. The active link has `aria-current="location"`. Each item is a regular link, so Tab moves through them.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Column,
    Grid,
    Prose,
    Row,
    Stack,
    TableOfContents,
    TableOfContentsItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const sections = [
    {
      id: "overview",
      title: "Overview",
      body: "Checkout v2 replaces the three-page flow with a single page that saves progress as the shopper types.",
    },
    {
      id: "measures-of-success",
      title: "Measures of success",
      body: "Conversion, time to purchase, and support tickets tagged "checkout", compared with the four weeks before launch.",
    },
    {
      id: "key-moments",
      title: "Key moments",
      body: "Address autocomplete, the saved-card prompt, and the order summary are where most shoppers stall today.",
    },
    {
      id: "tutorials",
      title: "Tutorials",
      body: "Step-by-step guides for enabling express payment methods and migrating saved addresses.",
    },
    {
      id: "articles",
      title: "Articles",
      body: "Background reading on form design and reducing checkout abandonment.",
    },
  ];
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={0} md={2} lg={4}>
      <Box position="sticky" top={7}>
        <TableOfContents>
          {#each sections as section (section.id)}
            <TableOfContentsItem href="#{section.id}" text={section.title} />
          {/each}
        </TableOfContents>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={6} lg={12}>
      <Stack gap={9}>
        {#each sections as section (section.id)}
          <Box tag="section" id={section.id} minHeight="24rem">
            <Prose>
              <h2>{section.title}</h2>
              <p>{section.body}</p>
            </Prose>
          </Box>
        {/each}
      </Stack>
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Activation line

By default a section becomes active when its top reaches the top of the scroller, so the next heading can sit in view while the previous section stays highlighted. Set `activationLine` to move that line down the visible height: `0.5` activates a section at the middle, and `1` as soon as it scrolls into view. The dashed line marks where sections activate. Clicked sections still land at the top.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Column,
    Grid,
    Prose,
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    Row,
    Stack,
    TableOfContents,
    TableOfContentsItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import lineContainer from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/lineContainer.svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={4}>
      <Stack gap={6}>
        <RadioButtonGroup
          legendText="Activation line"
          orientation="vertical"
          bind:selected={activationLine}
        >
          <RadioButton labelText="0 (top)" value="0" />
          <RadioButton labelText="0.5 (middle)" value="0.5" />
          <RadioButton labelText="1 (in view)" value="1" />
        </RadioButtonGroup>
        <TableOfContents
          scrollContainer={lineContainer}
          activationLine={Number(activationLine)}
        >
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-line-overview" text="Overview" />
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-line-setup" text="Setup" />
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-line-usage" text="Usage" />
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-line-faq" text="FAQ" />
        </TableOfContents>
      </Stack>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={12}>
      <Box position="relative">
        <Box bind:ref={lineContainer} height="16rem" overflowY="auto">
          <Prose>
            <section id="toc-line-overview">
              <h4>Overview</h4>
              <p>
                The reporting API returns usage and billing data for every
                project in your organization, so finance and engineering read
                the same numbers.
              </p>
              <p>It's read-only. To change limits or plans, use the console.</p>
            </section>
            <section id="toc-line-setup">
              <h4>Setup</h4>
              <p>
                Create a project in the console, then generate an API key under
                Settings. Keys are scoped to one project and can be revoked at
                any time.
              </p>
              <p>
                Choose the region your data is stored in when you create the
                project. It can't be changed later.
              </p>
            </section>
            <section id="toc-line-usage">
              <h4>Usage</h4>
              <p>
                Send a GET request with the key in the Authorization header.
                Responses are JSON, paginated at 100 records, with a cursor for
                the next page.
              </p>
              <p>
                Errors return a status code and a message that names the field
                at fault.
              </p>
            </section>
            <section id="toc-line-faq">
              <h4>FAQ</h4>
              <p>
                Requests are limited to 600 per minute per key. Data is kept for
                13 months, and support answers within one business day.
              </p>
              <p>
                When you hit the limit, requests return status 429 with a header
                that says how many seconds to wait before retrying.
              </p>
              <p>
                Export data you need for longer than 13 months to your own
                storage. The export endpoint writes one file per day.
              </p>
            </section>
          </Prose>
        </Box>
        <Box
          aria-hidden="true"
          position="absolute"
          left={0}
          right={0}
          top="min({Number(activationLine) * 100}%, calc(100% - 1px))"
          border="strong"
          borderStyle="dashed"
          borderSide="top"
          style="pointer-events: none"
        />
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Scroll container

When the sections scroll inside an element rather than the window, pass that element as `scrollContainer`. Clicking an item scrolls only that element, where a native hash jump would also scroll the page around it, and moves focus to the section so the next Tab continues from there. Bind `selectedId` to read or set the active section. The `change` event fires with the new id when a click or scroll changes it, but not when the first section is selected on load.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Column,
    Grid,
    Prose,
    Row,
    Stack,
    TableOfContents,
    TableOfContentsItem,
    Text,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import selectedId from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/selectedId.svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={4}>
      <TableOfContents bind:selectedId scrollContainer={container}>
        <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-container-profile" text="Profile" />
        <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-container-security" text="Security" />
        <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-container-billing" text="Billing" />
        <TableOfContentsItem
          href="#toc-container-notifications"
          text="Notifications"
        />
      </TableOfContents>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={12}>
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <Box bind:ref={container} height="16rem" overflowY="auto">
          <Prose>
            <section id="toc-container-profile">
              <h4>Profile</h4>
              <p>
                Your name, photo, and email address appear wherever teammates
                mention or assign you.
              </p>
              <p>
                Changes take effect right away, including in comments you've
                already left.
              </p>
            </section>
            <section id="toc-container-security">
              <h4>Security</h4>
              <p>
                Change your password, turn on two-factor authentication, and
                review the devices signed in to your account.
              </p>
              <p>Signing out a device ends its session within a minute.</p>
            </section>
            <section id="toc-container-billing">
              <h4>Billing</h4>
              <p>
                Update the payment method, download past invoices, and choose
                who receives billing email.
              </p>
              <p>
                Invoices are issued on the first of each month in your account's
                currency.
              </p>
            </section>
            <section id="toc-container-notifications">
              <h4>Notifications</h4>
              <p>
                Choose which events send email, and whether to get them as they
                happen or in a daily digest.
              </p>
              <p>
                Mentions and assignments always notify you, even with digests
                on, so nothing waiting on you gets buried.
              </p>
              <p>
                Mobile push notifications follow the same settings. Mute a
                project to silence it everywhere for a set time.
              </p>
            </section>
          </Prose>
        </Box>
        <Text>Selected: <strong>{selectedId}</strong></Text>
      </Stack>
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Without scroll spy

Set `noScrollSpy` to control `selectedId` yourself, for example when the sections are tabs or steps rather than one scrolling page. Clicking an item still selects it. Here each section is a panel that shows only while its item is selected, so cancel each item's click to keep the browser or router from jumping to the hash.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Column,
    Grid,
    Row,
    Stack,
    TableOfContents,
    TableOfContentsItem,
    Text,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={4}>
      <TableOfContents bind:selectedId={staticSelectedId} noScrollSpy>
        {#each staticItems as item (item.id)}
          <TableOfContentsItem
            href="#{item.id}"
            text={item.text}
            on:click={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
          />
        {/each}
      </TableOfContents>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={12}>
      {#each staticItems as item (item.id)}
        <section id={item.id} hidden={item.id !== staticSelectedId}>
          <Stack gap={3}>
            <Text tag="h4" type="heading-03">{item.text}</Text>
            <Text>{item.body}</Text>
          </Stack>
        </section>
      {/each}
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

### Layout

Place the table of contents beside the content it lists, and pick a row size that fits the length of the list.

#### Right column

Many documentation pages put the table of contents in the rightmost column, after the content. Here it spans 4 of 16 columns on large screens and 2 of 8 on medium ones, and hides on small screens with `sm={0}`, where a sidebar would leave the content too narrow. Content first in the DOM also means Tab reaches the article before the table of contents. Set `labelText` to the heading the column shows, such as "On this page".

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Column,
    Grid,
    Prose,
    Row,
    Stack,
    TableOfContents,
    TableOfContentsItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const sections = [
    {
      id: "installation",
      title: "Installation",
      body: "Add the package with your package manager and import the styles once in the app's entry point.",
    },
    {
      id: "usage",
      title: "Usage",
      body: "Import a component by name and pass it props. Every component works with server rendering.",
    },
    {
      id: "props",
      title: "Props",
      body: "Props are typed. Your editor lists each one with its default value and a short description.",
    },
    {
      id: "events",
      title: "Events",
      body: "Components dispatch events with the new value in detail, so handlers don't read the DOM.",
    },
    {
      id: "accessibility",
      title: "Accessibility",
      body: "Every component is keyboard operable and follows the WAI-ARIA authoring practices.",
    },
  ];
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={6} lg={12}>
      <Stack gap={9}>
        {#each sections as section (section.id)}
          <Box tag="section" id={section.id} minHeight="24rem">
            <Prose>
              <h2>{section.title}</h2>
              <p>{section.body}</p>
            </Prose>
          </Box>
        {/each}
      </Stack>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={0} md={2} lg={4}>
      <Box position="sticky" top={7}>
        <TableOfContents labelText="On this page">
          {#each sections as section (section.id)}
            <TableOfContentsItem href="#{section.id}" text={section.title} />
          {/each}
        </TableOfContents>
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Small size

Set `size` to `"sm"` for a long table of contents, such as a documentation sidebar with dozens of sections. Rows are shorter, and nested rows use smaller type so they read as part of the section above. The default size is `"md"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Column,
    Grid,
    Prose,
    Row,
    TableOfContents,
    TableOfContentsGroup,
    TableOfContentsItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import smallContainer from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/smallContainer.svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={4}>
      <TableOfContents size="sm" scrollContainer={smallContainer}>
        <TableOfContentsGroup labelText="Examples">
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-small-basic" text="Basic" />
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-small-sizes" text="Sizes" />
          <TableOfContentsItem
            href="#toc-small-sizes-sm"
            text="Small"
            level={2}
          />
          <TableOfContentsItem
            href="#toc-small-sizes-lg"
            text="Large"
            level={2}
          />
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-small-disabled" text="Disabled" />
        </TableOfContentsGroup>
        <TableOfContentsGroup labelText="Component API">
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-small-props" text="Props" />
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-small-events" text="Events" />
        </TableOfContentsGroup>
      </TableOfContents>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={12}>
      <Box bind:ref={smallContainer} height="16rem" overflowY="auto">
        <Prose>
          <section id="toc-small-basic">
            <h4>Basic</h4>
            <p>The basic example shows the component with its default props.</p>
            <p>Start here, then add props as the design needs them.</p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-small-sizes">
            <h4>Sizes</h4>
            <p>
              Each size sets the height of the control. Match the size of the
              controls around it.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-small-sizes-sm">
            <h5>Small</h5>
            <p>
              Use the small size in dense layouts, such as a toolbar or a table
              row.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-small-sizes-lg">
            <h5>Large</h5>
            <p>
              Use the large size on touch screens and in forms with plenty of
              room.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-small-disabled">
            <h4>Disabled</h4>
            <p>
              A disabled control can't receive focus. Say why it's disabled
              nearby, so the reader knows what to change.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-small-props">
            <h4>Props</h4>
            <p>
              Each prop lists its type, its default, and a short description.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-small-events">
            <h4>Events</h4>
            <p>Each event lists the detail it carries.</p>
            <p>
              Dispatched events fire after the state changes, so the detail
              holds the new value.
            </p>
            <p>Forwarded events are the native events of the root element.</p>
          </section>
        </Prose>
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

### Hierarchy

Show how sections relate: nest subsections under their section, or split the list into titled groups.

#### Nested headings

Set `level` to list a subsection under its section, such as an `h3` under an `h2`. Each level below the first indents by one more step, and its rows sit closer together so the group reads as part of the section above. `level` goes from 1 to 3, enough for `h2` through `h4`; deeper headings rarely belong in a table of contents, and their indent leaves a sidebar label little room.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Column,
    Grid,
    Prose,
    Row,
    TableOfContents,
    TableOfContentsItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import nestedContainer from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/nestedContainer.svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={4}>
      <TableOfContents scrollContainer={nestedContainer}>
        <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-nested-overview" text="Overview" />
        <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-nested-tokens" text="Design tokens" />
        <TableOfContentsItem
          href="#toc-nested-colors"
          text="Colors"
          level={2}
        />
        <TableOfContentsItem
          href="#toc-nested-contrast"
          text="Contrast"
          level={3}
        />
        <TableOfContentsItem
          href="#toc-nested-spacing"
          text="Spacing"
          level={2}
        />
        <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-nested-type" text="Type" level={2} />
        <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-nested-components" text="Components" />
      </TableOfContents>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={12}>
      <Box bind:ref={nestedContainer} height="16rem" overflowY="auto">
        <Prose>
          <section id="toc-nested-overview">
            <h4>Overview</h4>
            <p>
              The design system is the shared set of tokens, components, and
              guidance behind every product we ship.
            </p>
            <p>
              A core team maintains it. Anyone can propose a change by opening
              an issue with the problem it solves.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-nested-tokens">
            <h4>Design tokens</h4>
            <p>
              Tokens are named values for color, spacing, and type. Design files
              and code read the same names, so a change in one place reaches
              every product.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-nested-colors">
            <h5>Colors</h5>
            <p>
              Color tokens name a role, such as background or text on color, not
              a hue. Each theme maps the roles to its own palette.
            </p>
            <p>
              Use the role that describes the job, and the contrast holds in
              every theme.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-nested-contrast">
            <h6>Contrast</h6>
            <p>
              Text roles meet a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against the background
              roles they're paired with, and large text meets 3:1.
            </p>
            <p>
              Check custom pairings with a contrast checker before shipping
              them.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-nested-spacing">
            <h5>Spacing</h5>
            <p>
              Spacing comes from one scale that starts at 2px and roughly
              doubles at each step.
            </p>
            <p>
              Use small steps inside a component and large ones between sections
              of a page.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-nested-type">
            <h5>Type</h5>
            <p>
              Each type style sets size, weight, and line height together, so
              text stays readable at every size.
            </p>
            <p>
              Pick the style by role, such as a heading or body copy, not by the
              size you want.
            </p>
            <p>
              Long-form text uses the body-long styles, which add line height
              for comfortable reading.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-nested-components">
            <h4>Components</h4>
            <p>
              Components are built from the tokens, so they follow the theme
              without extra work.
            </p>
            <p>
              Each one documents when to use it, what it looks like in every
              state, and how it behaves with a keyboard.
            </p>
            <p>
              Start from the component closest to what you need. If none fits,
              ask in the design system channel before building a new one;
              someone may already be working on it.
            </p>
            <p>
              New components go through a short review for accessibility,
              theming, and naming before they're published.
            </p>
          </section>
        </Prose>
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Groups

Use `TableOfContentsGroup` to split the list under section titles, such as examples and reference. Set the title with `labelText`, or use the `labelChildren` slot for custom content. The title is plain text, not a link. Screen readers announce each group by its title. Each group draws its own track beside its items, and one active bar moves across all groups.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Column,
    Grid,
    Prose,
    Row,
    TableOfContents,
    TableOfContentsGroup,
    TableOfContentsItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import groupContainer from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/groupContainer.svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={4}>
      <TableOfContents scrollContainer={groupContainer}>
        <TableOfContentsGroup labelText="Guides">
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-group-install" text="Install" />
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-group-theme" text="Theme" />
        </TableOfContentsGroup>
        <TableOfContentsGroup labelText="Reference">
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-group-props" text="Props" />
          <TableOfContentsItem href="#toc-group-events" text="Events" />
        </TableOfContentsGroup>
      </TableOfContents>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={12}>
      <Box bind:ref={groupContainer} height="16rem" overflowY="auto">
        <Prose>
          <section id="toc-group-install">
            <h4>Install</h4>
            <p>
              Add the package with your package manager, then import the CSS
              once at the root of your app.
            </p>
            <p>
              The components work in any Svelte app, with or without SvelteKit.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-group-theme">
            <h4>Theme</h4>
            <p>
              Wrap the app in a theme to set the color tokens. Every component
              reads the same tokens.
            </p>
            <p>Switch the theme at runtime, and the page updates at once.</p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-group-props">
            <h4>Props</h4>
            <p>
              Each component lists its props with a type, a default, and a short
              description.
            </p>
            <p>Props that aren't listed pass through to the root element.</p>
          </section>
          <section id="toc-group-events">
            <h4>Events</h4>
            <p>
              Components forward native events and dispatch their own. Each
              event lists the detail it carries.
            </p>
            <p>Listen with <code>on:</code> as with any Svelte element.</p>
            <p>
              Dispatched events fire after the state changes, so the detail
              always holds the new value.
            </p>
          </section>
        </Prose>
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

#### Generated from headings

For rendered Markdown or other content you don't write item by item, read the headings after they render and map each one to an item. Here the content is set in [Prose](/components/Prose), the `h4`s become top-level items, and the `h5`s nest under them.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Column,
    Grid,
    Prose,
    Row,
    TableOfContents,
    TableOfContentsItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column sm={4} md={3} lg={4}>
      <TableOfContents scrollContainer={article}>
        {#each headings as heading (heading.id)}
          <TableOfContentsItem
            href="#{heading.id}"
            text={heading.text}
            level={heading.level}
          />
        {/each}
      </TableOfContents>
    </Column>
    <Column sm={4} md={5} lg={12}>
      <Box bind:ref={article} height="16rem" overflowY="auto">
        <Prose>
          <h4 id="toc-generated-install">Install</h4>
          <p>
            Add the package with your package manager, then import the styles
            once in your app's entry point.
          </p>
          <p>
            The styles include every theme, so you don't need a separate import
            to switch.
          </p>
          <h4 id="toc-generated-configure">Configure</h4>
          <p>Two settings cover most apps: the theme and the base path.</p>
          <h5 id="toc-generated-theme">Theme</h5>
          <p>
            Pick one of the four themes, or follow the system preference so the
            app matches the operating system.
          </p>
          <p>The theme can change at runtime without a reload.</p>
          <h5 id="toc-generated-base-path">Base path</h5>
          <p>
            If the app isn't served from the root of its domain, set the base
            path so links and assets resolve.
          </p>
          <p>Prefix in-page links with the same path.</p>
          <p>
            Server-rendered apps read it from the request, so it can differ
            between environments.
          </p>
          <h4 id="toc-generated-deploy">Deploy</h4>
          <p>
            Build once and serve the output from any static host. Nothing runs
            on the server.
          </p>
          <p>
            Cache the hashed assets for a year and the HTML for a few minutes.
          </p>
          <p>
            Preview deployments work the same way. Each branch gets its own URL,
            which you can share for review before merging.
          </p>
          <p>
            To roll back, point the host at the previous build. There's no
            database migration to undo.
          </p>
        </Prose>
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

### Usage

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Give the scroller a `scroll-padding-top` equal to the height of a sticky header, or set `scrollOffset` and a matching `scroll-margin-top` on the sections. | `scrollOffset` defaults to the scroller's `scroll-padding-top`, so one CSS value moves both the line a section must cross to become active and where a clicked section lands. |
| Lay the page out with `Grid`, `Row`, and `Column`, giving the table of contents 4 of 16 columns on large screens and hiding it on small ones with `sm={0}`. | It lines up with the rest of the page's grid, and a sidebar on a small screen leaves the content too narrow. |
| Raise `activationLine` when sections are short or headings sit low on the page. | A section otherwise only activates once its top reaches the top, so its heading can be in view while the previous section stays highlighted. |
| Give a long table of contents a sticky sidebar with `overflow-y: auto`. | The active item scrolls into view within the sidebar as the reader moves through the page, without moving the page. |
| Sync the URL from the `change` event if you need the hash when using `scrollContainer` or inside an iframe. | In those cases the click scrolls the container itself instead of following the link, so the URL hash doesn't change. |
| Give each section a unique `id` that matches its item's `href`. | The scroll spy finds sections with `document.getElementById`, and skips items whose section is missing. |
| Group items under a `TableOfContentsGroup` when the page has distinct parts, such as examples and reference. | A plain-text title names each part without adding a link that goes nowhere, and screen readers announce the group. |
| Set `size="sm"` when the list is long. | Shorter rows fit more sections in view, so the reader sees where they are without scrolling the sidebar. |
| Keep item text short and matching the section heading. | Long labels wrap onto several lines and push later sections out of view in a sticky sidebar. |
| Set `labelText` when a page has more than one navigation landmark. | It names the `nav`, which defaults to "Table of contents". |

---

### Component API

#### `TableOfContents` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectedId` (Reactive) | `string \| undefined` | Specify the id of the active section.<br />Tracks the scroll position unless `noScrollSpy` is `true`. | _undefined_ |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLElement` | Obtain a reference to the nav HTML element. | `null` |
| `noScrollSpy` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to stop updating `selectedId` from the scroll position.<br />Clicking an item still selects it. | `false` |
| `scrollOffset` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the distance in pixels from the top of the scroll container at<br />which a section becomes active. Match the height of a sticky header.<br />Defaults to the scroll container's `scroll-padding-top`, where a native<br />hash jump lands a section. | _undefined_ |
| `activationLine` | `number` | Specify where a section becomes active, as a fraction of the scroll<br />container's visible height below `scrollOffset`: `0` when the section's<br />top reaches the top, `0.5` when it reaches the middle, `1` as soon as it<br />scrolls into view. | `0` |
| `scrollContainer` | `HTMLElement \| null` | Specify the element that scrolls the sections.<br />Defaults to the window. | `null` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | Specify the row size. | `"md"` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the ARIA label for the nav | `"Table of contents"` |

#### `TableOfContents` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `TableOfContents` dispatched events

| Event       | Detail   |
| ----------- | -------- |
| `on:change` | `string` |

#### `TableOfContents` $$restProps

`TableOfContents` spreads `$$restProps` to the `nav` element.


## Tabs

### Basic

Create a basic tab interface with labels and content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="Dashboard" />
  <Tab label="Monitoring" />
  <Tab label="Activity" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Monitoring content for uptime and alerts.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Activity content for recent user actions.</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to change the tab height. Line tabs support `"sm"`, `"md"`, and `"lg"`; `size` is unset by default, which preserves the original unsized height. An out-of-range value (for example `"xl"` on line tabs) clamps to the type's max -- see [Container sizes](#sizes-1) for the full range on container tabs.

#### Small

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs size="sm">
  <Tab label="Dashboard" />
  <Tab label="Monitoring" />
  <Tab label="Activity" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Monitoring content for uptime and alerts.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Activity content for recent user actions.</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Medium

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs size="md">
  <Tab label="Dashboard" />
  <Tab label="Monitoring" />
  <Tab label="Activity" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Monitoring content for uptime and alerts.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Activity content for recent user actions.</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Large

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs size="lg">
  <Tab label="Dashboard" />
  <Tab label="Monitoring" />
  <Tab label="Activity" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Monitoring content for uptime and alerts.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Activity content for recent user actions.</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Selection

Control which tab is active by a stable id, by index, or by changing how arrow keys move the selection.

#### Selected by id

Bind `selectedId` and give each `Tab` a stable `id`. Prefer it to `selected`: selection stays on the same logical tab when tabs before it are added, removed or reordered. When set, `selectedId` takes precedence over `selected`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Checkbox,
    Stack,
    Tab,
    TabContent,
    Tabs,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedId = "admin";
  let showDashboard = true;
  let showAdmin = true;
  let showSettings = true;
  let showProfile = true;

  $: visibleTabs = [
    { id: "dashboard", label: "Dashboard", show: showDashboard },
    { id: "admin", label: "Admin", show: showAdmin },
    { id: "settings", label: "Settings", show: showSettings },
    { id: "profile", label: "Profile", show: showProfile },
  ].filter((tab) => tab.show);
</script>

<Stack gap={3}>
  <div>
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showDashboard} labelText="Show Dashboard" />
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showAdmin} labelText="Show Admin" />
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showSettings} labelText="Show Settings" />
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showProfile} labelText="Show Profile" />
  </div>
  <Stack gap={4} orientation="horizontal" align="center">
    <Button
      kind="tertiary"
      size="small"
      on:click={() => (selectedId = "settings")}
    >
      Select Settings by id
    </Button>
    <div>
      <strong>selectedId:</strong>
      {selectedId}
    </div>
  </Stack>
  <Tabs bind:selectedId>
    {#each visibleTabs as tab (tab.id)}
      <Tab id={tab.id} label={tab.label} />
    {/each}
    <svelte:fragment slot="content">
      {#each visibleTabs as tab (tab.id)}
        <TabContent>
          <p>{tab.label} content</p>
        </TabContent>
      {/each}
    </svelte:fragment>
  </Tabs>
</Stack>
```

#### Reactive

Use `bind:selected` for a two-way binding with the selected tab index. An index points at a different tab once tabs before it change, so use it only for a fixed set of tabs.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Stack,
    Tab,
    TabContent,
    Tabs,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selected = 0;
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <Tabs bind:selected>
    <Tab label="Dashboard" />
    <Tab label="Monitoring" />
    <Tab label="Activity" />
    <svelte:fragment slot="content">
      <TabContent>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</TabContent>
      <TabContent>Monitoring content for uptime and alerts.</TabContent>
      <TabContent>Activity content for recent user actions.</TabContent>
    </svelte:fragment>
  </Tabs>
  <Stack gap={4} orientation="horizontal" align="center">
    <div>
      <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (selected = 1)}>
        Set index to 1
      </Button>
    </div>
    <div>
      <strong>Selected index:</strong>
      {selected}
    </div>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

#### Query string

Keep the selected tab in the URL so it survives a reload and can be shared. `queryParam` returns a store mirrored to a query parameter: it reads the initial value from the URL and writes changes with `history.replaceState`, so switching tabs does not add history entries. Bind `selectedId` to the store. Use `parse` to reject unknown ids so they fall back to `defaultValue`; selecting `defaultValue` removes the parameter.

Use the query string rather than the hash: a hash that matches a tab `id` scrolls the page to that tab. In an app with a router, pass the router's navigation API as `replace`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { queryParam, Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const tabs = [
    { id: "overview", label: "Overview" },
    { id: "activity", label: "Activity" },
    { id: "settings", label: "Settings" },
  ];

  const selectedTab = queryParam("tab", {
    defaultValue: tabs[0].id,
    parse: (id) => (tabs.some((tab) => tab.id === id) ? id : undefined),
  });
</script>

<Tabs bind:selectedId={$selectedTab}>
  {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
    <Tab id={tab.id} label={tab.label} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
      <TabContent>{tab.label} content</TabContent>
    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Manual activation

By default, tabs use automatic activation: arrow keys move focus and select the tab. Set `activation` to `"manual"` so arrow keys only move focus. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> to select. Use manual activation when switching panels is expensive.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs activation="manual">
  <Tab label="Dashboard" />
  <Tab label="Monitoring" />
  <Tab label="Activity" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Monitoring content for uptime and alerts.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Activity content for recent user actions.</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Events

Listen for tab selection changes.

#### Change

Listen for `on:change` to know when the selected tab index changes, whether from a click, keyboard navigation, or a `selected`/`selectedId` update. `event.detail` is the new selected index. The index and the selected tab can change independently when tabs are added, removed, or reordered, so use `bind:selectedId` to track which tab is selected. For the dismiss event, see [Dismissible](#dismissible).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}>
  <Tab label="Dashboard" />
  <Tab label="Monitoring" />
  <Tab label="Activity" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Monitoring content for uptime and alerts.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Activity content for recent user actions.</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Overflow

When the tabs exceed the available width, the list scrolls horizontally and backward/forward buttons appear at each end. Scroll by dragging, using the buttons, or moving focus with the arrow keys. Resize the viewport to see the buttons appear and hide.

#### Line

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    "Dashboard",
    "Monitoring",
    "Activity",
    "Settings",
    "Reports",
    "Billing",
    "Users",
    "Security",
    "Integrations",
    "Notifications",
    "Webhooks",
    "Audit logs",
  ];
</script>

<Tabs>
  {#each items as item}
    <Tab label={item} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each items as item}
      <TabContent>{item} content</TabContent>
    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Container

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  ];

<Tabs type="container">
  {#each items as item}
    <Tab label={item} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each items as item}

    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Tall

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const labels = [
    "Dashboard",
    "Monitoring",
    "Activity",
    "Settings",
    "Reports",
    "Billing",
    "Users",
    "Security",
    "Integrations",
    "Notifications",
    "Webhooks",
    "Audit logs",
  ];

  const items = labels.map((label, i) => ({
    label,
    secondaryLabel: `(${i + 1}/12)`,
  }));
</script>

<Tabs type="container">
  {#each items as item}
    <Tab label={item.label} secondaryLabel={item.secondaryLabel} />
  {/each}

    {/each}
```

#### Dismissible

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const labels = [
    "Dashboard",
    "Monitoring",
    "Activity",
    "Settings",
    "Reports",
    "Billing",
    "Users",
    "Security",
    "Integrations",
    "Notifications",
    "Webhooks",
    "Audit logs",
  ];

  let selectedId = "tab-1";
  let tabs = labels.map((label, i) => ({ id: `tab-${i + 1}`, label }));

  function handleDismiss({ detail }) {
    tabs = tabs.filter((tab) => tab.id !== detail.id);
  }
</script>

<Tabs bind:selectedId dismissible on:dismiss={handleDismiss}>
  {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
    <Tab id={tab.id} label={tab.label} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
      <TabContent>{tab.label} content</TabContent>
    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Icon-only

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Activity from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Activity.svelte";
  import Add from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Add.svelte";
  import Analytics from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Analytics.svelte";
  import Calendar from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Calendar.svelte";
  import Chat from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Chat.svelte";
  import Dashboard from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Dashboard.svelte";
  import Document from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Document.svelte";
  import Email from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Email.svelte";
  import Folder from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Folder.svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";
  import Search from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Search.svelte";

  const items = [
    { label: "Dashboard", icon: Dashboard },
    { label: "Activity", icon: Activity },
    { label: "Analytics", icon: Analytics },
    { label: "Calendar", icon: Calendar },
    { label: "Chat", icon: Chat },
    { label: "Documents", icon: Document },
    { label: "Email", icon: Email },
    { label: "Files", icon: Folder },
    { label: "Information", icon: Information },
    { label: "Notifications", icon: Notification },
    { label: "Search", icon: Search },
    { label: "Add", icon: Add },
  ];
</script>

<Tabs iconOnly>
  {#each items as item}
    <Tab label={item.label} icon={item.icon} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each items as item}
      <TabContent>{item.label} content</TabContent>
    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Vertical

Below the medium breakpoint, vertical tabs collapse into the same horizontal, scrollable row with overflow buttons. Resize the viewport to see them.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, TabsVertical } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    "Dashboard",
    "Monitoring",
    "Activity",
    "Settings",
    "Reports",
    "Billing",
    "Users",
    "Security",
    "Integrations",
    "Notifications",
    "Webhooks",
    "Audit logs",
  ];
</script>

<TabsVertical>
  {#each items as item}
    <Tab label={item} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each items as item}
      <TabContent>{item} content</TabContent>
    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</TabsVertical>
```

### Disabled tabs

Set `disabled` on a tab to prevent interaction. Keyboard navigation skips disabled tabs.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="Dashboard" />
  <Tab label="Monitoring" disabled />
  <Tab label="Activity" disabled />
  <Tab label="Settings" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Monitoring content for uptime and alerts.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Activity content for recent user actions.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Settings and configuration options.</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Conditional tabs

Tabs can be conditionally rendered using Svelte's `{#if}` blocks. The component automatically maintains correct indices even when tabs are dynamically added or removed.

If the current selected tab is removed, the next tab is selected.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Checkbox,
    Stack,
    Tab,
    TabContent,
    Tabs,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selected = 0;
  let showAdminTab = true;
  let showSettingsTab = true;
</script>

<Stack gap={3}>
  <div>
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showAdminTab} labelText="Show Admin tab" />
    <Checkbox bind:checked={showSettingsTab} labelText="Show Settings tab" />
  </div>
  <div>
    <strong>Selected index:</strong>
    {selected}
  </div>
  <Tabs bind:selected>
    <Tab label="Dashboard" />
    {#if showAdminTab}
      <Tab label="Admin" />
    {/if}
    {#if showSettingsTab}
      <Tab label="Settings" />
    {/if}
    <Tab label="Profile" />
    <svelte:fragment slot="content">
      <TabContent>
        <p>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</p>
      </TabContent>
      {#if showAdminTab}
        <TabContent>
          <p>Admin panel for managing users and permissions.</p>
        </TabContent>
      {/if}
      {#if showSettingsTab}
        <TabContent><p>Settings and configuration options.</p></TabContent>
      {/if}
      <TabContent><p>User profile and account information.</p></TabContent>
    </svelte:fragment>
  </Tabs>
</Stack>
```

### Lazy content

By default, every `TabContent` panel stays mounted and toggles visibility with the `hidden` attribute. Set `lazy` on a panel to defer mounting its slot until that tab is first selected. Set `unmountOnHide` to remove the slot when the tab is deselected -- useful for heavy panels such as a DataTable.

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Set `lazy` on panels with heavy content: tables, charts, forms. | A hidden panel still builds all its markup; `lazy` waits until the tab is first selected. |
| Add `unmountOnHide` when a panel is large and rarely revisited. | It frees the panel's markup again, at the cost of rebuilding it on the next visit. |
| Leave both off when the panel's content must be in server-rendered markup. | Deferred content isn't in the page until its tab is selected. |

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable, Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="Overview" />
  <Tab label="Load balancers" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Lightweight overview content.</TabContent>
    <TabContent lazy>
      <DataTable
        headers={[
          { key: "name", value: "Name" },
          { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
          { key: "port", value: "Port" },
          { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
        ]}
        rows={[
          {
            id: "a",
            name: "Load Balancer 3",
            protocol: "HTTP",
            port: 3000,
            rule: "Round robin",
          },
          {
            id: "b",
            name: "Load Balancer 1",
            protocol: "HTTP",
            port: 443,
            rule: "Round robin",
          },
          {
            id: "c",
            name: "Load Balancer 2",
            protocol: "HTTP",
            port: 80,
            rule: "DNS delegation",
          },
        ]}
      />
    </TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Flush content

Set `flush` on `TabContent` to drop the panel's horizontal padding so content, such as a code snippet or table, lines up with the first tab.

```svelte
<script>
  import { CodeSnippet, Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="npm" />
  <Tab label="pnpm" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent flush>
      <CodeSnippet code="npm i carbon-components-svelte" />
    </TabContent>
    <TabContent flush>
      <CodeSnippet code="pnpm i carbon-components-svelte" />
    </TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Width

By default, each tab sizes to its label. Set `fullWidth` to `true` for tabs to evenly span the full width of the container.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs fullWidth>
  <Tab label="Dashboard" />
  <Tab label="Monitoring" />
  <Tab label="Activity" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Dashboard content with analytics and overview.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Monitoring content for uptime and alerts.</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Activity content for recent user actions.</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Navigation

By default, a tab uses `"#"` as a placeholder href and behaves as an in-page selection control. Provide a real href to make a tab act like a link, useful for routing each tab to a separate page.

| Tabs | Use when | Semantics |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Default | Tabs switch panels on the same page | Tab list, arrow keys move between tabs |
| `navigation` | Each tab is its own page or URL | Links, the current one has `aria-current="page"` |

#### Page navigation

Set `navigation` to render the tabs as page links. The links keep the browser's Tab order and arrow keys leave them alone. Label the navigation with `aria-label` and set `selected` or `selectedId` from the current route. Render the page content below the tabs without `TabContent`. TabsVertical accepts `navigation` too (see [Sidebar navigation](#sidebar-navigation)).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs navigation aria-label="Components" selected={1}>
  <Tab label="Accordion" href="/components/Accordion" />
  <Tab label="Breadcrumb" href="/components/Breadcrumb" />
  <Tab label="Button" href="/components/Button" />
</Tabs>
```

```svelte
<script>
  // The current route, from your router.
  export let pathname;

  const links = [
    { label: "Profile", href: "/settings/profile" },
    { label: "Security", href: "/settings/security" },
  ];

  $: selected = links.findIndex((link) => link.href === pathname);
</script>

<Tabs navigation aria-label="Settings" {selected}>
  {#each links as link}
    <Tab label={link.label} href={link.href} />
  {/each}
</Tabs>
```

#### Links

Provide a real href so that activating a tab by mouse or keyboard navigates to the URL in addition to selecting the tab. The tabs below link to other component pages, so selecting one navigates there.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="Accordion" href="/components/Accordion" />
  <Tab label="Breadcrumb" href="/components/Breadcrumb" />
  <Tab label="Button" href="/components/Button" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Accordion content</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Breadcrumb content</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Button content</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Intercept default

In a single-page app, intercept navigation to route on the client instead of triggering a full page load. Listen to the forwarded click event, call `event.preventDefault()`, and hand the URL to your router. The example below logs the route to the console instead of navigating.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const routes = [
    { label: "Accordion", href: "/components/Accordion" },
    { label: "Breadcrumb", href: "/components/Breadcrumb" },
    { label: "Button", href: "/components/Button" },
  ];

  function interceptNavigation(e, href) {
    e.preventDefault();
    console.log("Navigate to:", href);
  }
</script>

<Tabs>
  {#each routes as route}
    <Tab
      label={route.label}
      href={route.href}
      on:click={(e) => interceptNavigation(e, route.href)}
    />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each routes as route}
      <TabContent>{route.label} content</TabContent>
    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Icons

Add an icon next to the tab label, or render compact tabs that show only an icon.

#### With label

Add an icon next to the tab label with `icon`. The icon renders to the right of the label by default and shifts left when dismissible is enabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Calendar from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Calendar.svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
  import Settings from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Settings.svelte";
</script>

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="Calendar" icon={Calendar} />
  <Tab label="Information" icon={Information} />
  <Tab label="Settings" icon={Settings} disabled />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Calendar content</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Information content</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Settings content</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Icon-only

Set `iconOnly` on Tabs to render compact, square tabs that display only an icon. Set icon and label on each Tab; the label is the accessible name and the tooltip shown on hover and focus. Press <kbd>Escape</kbd> to hide the tooltip without moving the pointer or focus. It shows again on the next hover or focus.

##### Basic

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Activity from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Activity.svelte";
  import Chat from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Chat.svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";
</script>

<Tabs iconOnly>
  <Tab label="Search" icon={Search} />
  <Tab label="Activity" icon={Activity} disabled />
  <Tab label="Notifications" icon={Notification} />
  <Tab label="Chat" icon={Chat} />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 1</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 2</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 3</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 4</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

##### Large

Set `iconSize` to `"lg"` for large icon-only tabs. The tabs and their icons are enlarged to the large scale.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Activity from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Activity.svelte";
  import Chat from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Chat.svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";
</script>

<Tabs iconOnly iconSize="lg">
  <Tab label="Search" icon={Search} />
  <Tab label="Activity" icon={Activity} disabled />
  <Tab label="Notifications" icon={Notification} />
  <Tab label="Chat" icon={Chat} />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 1</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 2</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 3</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 4</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

##### Tooltip placement

The tooltip renders below the tab by default. Use `tooltipAlign` to control placement, with Popover's `align` names: `"top"`, `"bottom-start"` and so on. It replaces `tooltipDirection` and `tooltipAlignment`, which still work and are deprecated. The tooltip automatically flips to the opposite side if there is not enough space.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Activity from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Activity.svelte";
  import Chat from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Chat.svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";
</script>

<Tabs iconOnly>
  <Tab label="Search" icon={Search} tooltipAlign="top-start" />
  <Tab label="Activity" icon={Activity} tooltipAlign="top" />
  <Tab label="Notifications" icon={Notification} tooltipAlign="top" />
  <Tab label="Chat" icon={Chat} tooltipAlign="top-end" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 1</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 2</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 3</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 4</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

##### Container

Icon-only tabs also work with the container type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Activity from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Activity.svelte";
  import Chat from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Chat.svelte";
  import Notification from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Notification.svelte";
</script>

<Tabs type="container" iconOnly>
  <Tab label="Search" icon={Search} />
  <Tab label="Activity" icon={Activity} disabled />
  <Tab label="Notifications" icon={Notification} />
  <Tab label="Chat" icon={Chat} />
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 1</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 2</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 3</TabContent>
    <TabContent>Tab Panel 4</TabContent>
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

### Dismissible

Set `dismissible` on Tabs to render a close button on each tab. Handle the dismiss event to remove the tab from your data. Bind `selectedId` with a stable `id` on each Tab so selection stays coherent without manual index math. The event detail includes `{ id, label, disabled, hasSecondaryLabel, index }`. Press <kbd>Delete</kbd> on the focused tab to dismiss it. Focus moves to the next tab, or to the previous tab when the last one is dismissed.

#### Basic

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedId = "dashboard";
  let tabs = [
    { id: "dashboard", label: "Dashboard" },
    { id: "monitoring", label: "Monitoring" },
    { id: "activity", label: "Activity" },
    { id: "settings", label: "Settings", disabled: true },
  ];

  function handleDismiss({ detail }) {
    tabs = tabs.filter((tab) => tab.id !== detail.id);
  }
</script>

<Tabs bind:selectedId dismissible on:dismiss={handleDismiss}>
  {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
    <Tab id={tab.id} label={tab.label} disabled={tab.disabled} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
      <TabContent>{tab.label} content</TabContent>
    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Icons

Set dismissible on Tabs and pass an icon to each Tab. Icons render on the left of the label; the close button stays on the right.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Calendar from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Calendar.svelte";
  import Dashboard from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Dashboard.svelte";
  import Settings from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Settings.svelte";

  let selectedId = "dashboard";
  let tabs = [
    { id: "dashboard", label: "Dashboard", icon: Dashboard },
    { id: "schedule", label: "Schedule", icon: Calendar },
    { id: "settings", label: "Settings", icon: Settings, disabled: true },
  ];

  function handleDismiss({ detail }) {
    tabs = tabs.filter((tab) => tab.id !== detail.id);
  }
</script>

<Tabs bind:selectedId dismissible on:dismiss={handleDismiss}>
  {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
    <Tab
      id={tab.id}
      label={tab.label}
      icon={tab.icon}
      disabled={tab.disabled}
    />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
      <TabContent>{tab.label} content</TabContent>
    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Container

Set `type="container"` and `dismissible` to `true` for dismissible container tabs.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tab, TabContent, Tabs } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedId = "dashboard";
  let tabs = [
    { id: "dashboard", label: "Dashboard" },
    { id: "monitoring", label: "Monitoring" },
    { id: "activity", label: "Activity" },
    { id: "settings", label: "Settings", disabled: true },
  ];

  function handleDismiss({ detail }) {
    tabs = tabs.filter((tab) => tab.id !== detail.id);
  }
</script>

<Tabs type="container" bind:selectedId dismissible on:dismiss={handleDismiss}>
  {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
    <Tab id={tab.id} label={tab.label} disabled={tab.disabled} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="content">
    {#each tabs as tab (tab.id)}
      <TabContent>{tab.label} content</TabContent>
    {/each}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Tabs>
```

#### Secondary label
