#### `TextInput` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `null \| number \| string` | Specify the input value.<br /><br />`value` will be set to `null` if type="number" and the value is empty.<br />Follows the field when the owning form resets. | `""` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Set the size of the input.<br />Inherits the parent `Form` size when unset.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (the 40px default, which overrides a<br />`Form` size) and `"lg"` (`"xl"`). | _undefined_ |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Specify the placeholder text | `""` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the input | `false` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the input element | `uniqueId()` |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a name attribute for the input. | _undefined_ |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `maxCount` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the max character count allowed for the input.<br />Displays a character counter to the right of the label. | _undefined_ |
| `counterText` | `((count: number, max: number) => string) \| undefined` | Override the counter text read by screen readers. | `${count} of ${max} characters` |
| `limitReachedText` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the text announced when the limit is reached. | `"Character limit reached"` |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `required` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to mark the field as required | `false` |
| `inline` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the inline variant | `false` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the read-only variant | `false` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`.<br />Cannot be combined with the inline variant. | `false` |
| `selectTextOnFocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to select the input's text when it receives focus | `false` |

## Theme

### Setup

Theme supports five built-in themes and custom token overrides. Import `all.css` for dynamic theming, which uses [CSS variables](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Using_CSS_custom_properties).

```css
import "carbon-components-svelte/css/all.css";
```

`Theme` sets the theme for the whole page. To theme one part of it, such as a sidebar, use [ThemeZone](/components/ThemeZone).

### Basic

Create a basic theme component that can be controlled programmatically.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    Theme,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let theme = "g90";
</script>

<Theme bind:theme />

<RadioButtonGroup legendText="Carbon theme" bind:selected={theme}>
  {#each ["white", "g10", "g80", "g90", "g100"] as value}
    <RadioButton labelText={value} {value} />
  {/each}
</RadioButtonGroup>
```

### Persist locally

Set `persist` to `true` to save the theme in [localStorage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage). Use `persistKey` for a custom storage key.

When persistence is enabled, theme changes sync across browser tabs that share the same `persistKey`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    Theme,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let theme = "g90";
</script>

<Theme bind:theme persist persistKey="__carbon-theme" />

<RadioButtonGroup legendText="Carbon theme" bind:selected={theme}>
  {#each ["white", "g10", "g80", "g90", "g100"] as value}
    <RadioButton labelText={value} {value} />
  {/each}
</RadioButtonGroup>
```

### Follow the system

Set `system` to `true` to follow the operating system color scheme. The theme updates when the user changes the setting.

Set `systemThemes` to choose which theme represents light and dark; the default pairs `white` with `g100`.

With `persist` also set, the system preference wins when the page loads and the stored value is updated to match. Choosing a theme from a control keeps that theme until the system preference changes again.

To follow the system without JavaScript, see [Follow the system with CSS only](#follow-the-system-with-css-only).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Text, Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let theme = "white";
</script>

<Theme system render="toggle" bind:theme />

<Text>Current theme: {theme}</Text>

<Button kind="tertiary" on:click={() => (theme = "g10")}>
  Switch to Gray 10
</Button>
```

### Apply before first paint

`Theme` restores a persisted or system theme after it mounts, so a server-rendered or prerendered page first paints the default theme. To avoid the flash, inline `themeScript` as the first script in `<head>`. It returns a small script that sets the theme on `<html>` before the page renders.

Pass `themeScript` the same `theme`, `tokens`, `persist`, `persistKey`, `system`, and `systemThemes` values as `Theme` so both pick the same theme and set the same tokens.

In SvelteKit, add a placeholder to `src/app.html` and replace it in a server hook.

```html
<!-- src/app.html -->
<head>
  %carbon.theme% %sveltekit.head%
</head>
```

```js
// src/hooks.server.js
import { themeScript } from "carbon-components-svelte";

const script = `<script>${themeScript({ persist: true, system: true })}</script>`;

export function handle({ event, resolve }) {
  return resolve(event, {
    transformPageChunk: ({ html }) => html.replace("%carbon.theme%", script),
  });
}
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<!-- src/routes/+layout.svelte -->
<Theme persist system />
```

For other setups, generate the string at build time and inline it the same way. With a Content Security Policy, add the page's nonce to the `<script>` tag.

### Follow the system with CSS only

`all.css` also has a `system` theme. Set `theme="system"` on `<html>`, and the page is White when the operating system is light and Gray 100 when it is dark. It runs no JavaScript, so nothing flashes. It suits static and server-rendered pages, and pages whose Content Security Policy blocks inline scripts.

```html
<html theme="system"></html>
```

[ThemeZone](/components/ThemeZone#system-color-scheme) takes `theme="system"` too.

Use `Theme` with `system` and `themeScript` when you need more than White and Gray 100:

| You need | Use |
| :-- | :-- |
| White and Gray 100, with no JavaScript | `<html theme="system">` |
| Another pair, such as Gray 10 and Gray 90 | `<Theme system systemThemes={["g10", "g90"]} />` and `themeScript` |
| To remember the user's choice | `<Theme persist system />` and `themeScript` |
| A theme control, or `update` events | `<Theme render="toggle" system />` |

The `theme` prop doesn't take `"system"`. It holds the theme that the controls show, `update` reports, and `persist` stores, so it is always one of the five themes. When `Theme` mounts, it sets the `theme` attribute on `<html>` to that theme.

So you can start with CSS and let `Theme` take over. Render `<html theme="system">` and mount `<Theme system />`. With the default `systemThemes`, `Theme` picks the theme that the page already shows, so nothing changes on screen.

### Custom theme

Override default Carbon theme tokens using the `tokens` prop.

`Theme` sets CSS custom properties as `--cds-{token}`. Not every token name maps directly to component styles. Components often use semantic tokens (like `layer-01`) rather than component-specific ones.

For example, primary buttons use `button-primary` for background, with separate `button-primary-hover` and `button-primary-active` tokens. Check component CSS or Carbon docs to see which tokens affect a given component.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Checkbox,
    InlineNotification,
    Link,
    Stack,
    Tag,
    TextInput,
    Theme,
    Tile,
    Toggle,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Theme
  theme="g90"
  tokens={{
    // Interactive elements
    "button-primary": "#d02670", // Primary button background
    "button-primary-hover": "#ee5396", // Primary button hover
    "button-primary-active": "#9f1853", // Primary button active
    "button-secondary": "#6f6f6f", // Secondary button background
    "button-secondary-hover": "#5e5e5e", // Secondary button hover

    // Links
    "link-primary": "#ff6eb3", // Link text color

    // Tags
    "tag-background-blue": "#4a1942", // Tag background
    "tag-color-blue": "#ffb3d9", // Tag text color

    // Form elements
    "field-01": "#2d2d2d", // Input field background
    "layer-01": "#2d2d2d", // Tile background
    focus: "#ff6eb3", // Focus indicator color

    // Text colors
    "text-primary": "#ffffff", // Primary text
    "text-secondary": "#c6c6c6", // Secondary text

    // Notification colors
    "support-info": "#a855f7", // Info notification color
  }}
/>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <div>
    <Button>Save changes</Button>
    <Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  </div>

  <div>
    <Link href="#">View audit log</Link>
  </div>

  <div><Tag type="blue">Production</Tag></div>

  <TextInput labelText="Workspace name" placeholder="Enter workspace name..." />

  <Checkbox labelText="Enable two-factor authentication" />

  <Toggle labelText="Maintenance mode" />

  <Tile><p>Deployment pipeline -- 2 builds queued</p></Tile>

  <InlineNotification
    kind="info"
    title="Sync complete:"
    subtitle="Your workspace data is up to date."
    hideCloseButton
    lowContrast
  />
</Stack>
```

#### Token names

Tokens use Carbon v11 names, matching the v11 Figma kit: `layer-01`, `text-primary`, `border-subtle-01`, `body-compact-01`. v10 names such as `ui-01`, `text-01`, `interactive-01`, and `body-short-01` are not declared, so overriding one has no effect. Carbon's [v10 to v11 token table](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/main/docs/migration/v11.md#design-tokens) lists each rename. The `tokens` prop is typed with `CarbonToken`, so editors complete token names and flag a v10 name as an error.

Components read contextual tokens such as `layer` and `field`, which hold the first layer's value. Overriding a first-layer token (`layer-01`, `field-01`, `border-subtle-00`) also sets its contextual token, unless you set that one too. A `Layer` still reads the numbered token for its own level.

Where a v10 token split into several v11 tokens, pick the one for the role. For example, `ui-03` became `border-subtle-01` for borders and `layer-accent-01` for fills.

### Brand theme

Build a brand theme from one color with `createTheme`. Pass a base theme and a brand color. It returns `tokens` for `Theme`, contrast `warnings`, and a `css` method for static use. Try it in the [theme builder](/theme-builder).

```svelte
<script>
  import { createTheme, Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const { tokens } = createTheme({ theme: "g100", brand: "#d02670" });
</script>

<Theme theme="g100" {tokens} />
```

The brand becomes `button-primary`. The tokens Carbon pairs with its brand blue follow it: the button hover and active states, interactive borders, focus, links, and `background-brand`. Dark themes get lighter link and interactive colors, as in Carbon.

A Carbon palette color, such as purple 60 (`#8a3ffc`), steps through Carbon's own palette. Any other color keeps its hue and takes the luminance of Carbon's steps, so it keeps Carbon's contrast. `support-info` and `link-visited` keep their Carbon values, since Carbon doesn't tie them to the brand.

The tokens suit their base theme only. If users can switch themes, call `createTheme` for each theme and pass the matching tokens with it.

#### Contrast warnings

`warnings` lists each pair below WCAG AA. `text-on-color` on `button-primary` and `link-primary` on `background` need 4.5:1, and `focus` on `background` needs 3:1. Each warning has both token names, the ratio, the minimum, and a message.

Fix a pair with an override in `tokens`. Overrides win over the derived tokens. `text-on-color` applies to every colored surface, not only buttons.

```js
const { warnings } = createTheme({
  brand: "#f1c21b",
  tokens: {
    "text-on-color": "#161616",
    "link-primary": "#8e6a00",
    focus: "#8e6a00",
  },
});

warnings; // []
```

#### Static CSS

Call `css` to get the tokens as a CSS rule for a stylesheet. The rule applies while the base theme is set on the html element, so load it after `all.css`. Pass a selector to scope it elsewhere.

```js
const { css } = createTheme({ theme: "g100", brand: "#d02670" });

css(); // :root[theme="g100"] { --cds-button-primary: #d02670; ... }
css(".brand-zone");
```

### Token data

Import token names and values from `carbon-components-svelte/tokens` to list tokens, build a palette, or pass a theme color to code that can't read CSS custom properties, such as a canvas. The data comes from the same build as `all.css`, so it has the same Carbon v11 names and values.

| Export | Contents |
| :-- | :-- |
| `colorTokens` | Theme colors, with a value for each theme |
| `componentTokens` | Button, tag, notification, content switcher, and status colors, with a value for each theme |
| `typeTokens` | Type styles: font size, weight, line height, and letter spacing |
| `spacingTokens`, `layoutTokens`, `containerTokens`, `sizeTokens` | Spacing and size scales |

Each token name is also a custom property, `--cds-{name}`. Contextual tokens such as `layer` and `field` hold their value on the first layer; inside a `Layer`, read the numbered token for that level.

```js
import { colorTokens, typeTokens } from "carbon-components-svelte/tokens";

colorTokens["background"].g100; // "#161616"
typeTokens["heading-compact-01"]["font-size"]; // "0.875rem"
```

The table below lists every theme color. The [token reference](/tokens) shows every token with a swatch in all five themes, plus the type, spacing and size scales.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DataTable,
    Pagination,
    Stack,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
    ToolbarSearch,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import { colorTokens } from "carbon-components-svelte/tokens";

  const themes = ["white", "g10", "g80", "g90", "g100"];

  const headers = [
    { key: "id", value: "Token" },
    ...themes.map((theme) => ({ key: theme, value: theme })),
  ];

  const rows = Object.entries(colorTokens).map(([id, values]) => ({
    id,
    ...values,
  }));

  let page = 1;
  let filteredRowIds = [];
</script>

<DataTable size="short" {headers} {rows} pageSize={6} {page}>
  <Toolbar>
    <ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarSearch persistent shouldFilterRows bind:filteredRowIds />
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
  <svelte:fragment slot="cell" let:cell>
    {#if cell.key === "id"}
      <code>{cell.value}</code>
    {:else}
      <Stack tag="span" orientation="horizontal" align="center" gap={3}>
        <span class="swatch" style:background={cell.value} aria-hidden="true"
        ></span>
        {cell.value}
      </Stack>
    {/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>

<Pagination
  bind:page
  pageSize={6}
  pageSizeInputDisabled
  totalItems={filteredRowIds.length}
/>

<style>
  /* A swatch, not layout: border-subtle-01 outlines light values on the row. */
  .swatch {
    flex: none;
    width: 1rem;
    height: 1rem;
    border: 1px solid var(--cds-border-subtle-01);
  }
</style>
```

### Controls

Render a built-in control instead of managing `theme` yourself. Set `render` to `"toggle"`, `"select"`, or `"dropdown"`.

#### Toggle

Set `render` to `"toggle"` to display a toggle switch for switching between two themes. By default, it toggles between "white" and "g100" themes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Theme render="toggle" />
```

##### Custom

Customize themes, labels, and other toggle options with `toggle`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Theme
  render="toggle"
  toggle={{
    themes: ["g10", "g80"],
    labelA: "Enable dark mode",
    labelB: "Enable dark mode",
    hideLabel: true,
    size: "sm",
  }}
/>
```

#### Select

Set `render` to `"select"` to display a dropdown menu for selecting from all available themes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Theme render="select" />
```

##### Custom

Choose which themes to include, customize labels, and adjust other select options with `select`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Theme
  render="select"
  select={{
    themes: ["white", "g90", "g100"],
    labelText: "Select a theme",
    inline: true,
  }}
/>
```

#### Dropdown

Set `render` to `"dropdown"` to display a Dropdown component for selecting from all available themes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Theme render="dropdown" />
```

##### Custom

Choose which themes to include, customize labels, and adjust other dropdown options with `dropdown`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Theme
  render="dropdown"
  dropdown={{
    themes: ["white", "g90", "g100"],
    labelText: "Select a theme",
    type: "inline",
  }}
/>
```

### Events

Theme dispatches an `update` event whenever `theme` changes, whether from a built-in control or a bound value updated elsewhere in your app. The initial theme on mount does not dispatch `update`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Theme render="toggle" on:update={(e) => console.log(e.detail.theme)} />
```

### Slot

Use the default slot to access the current `theme` value with `let:theme`, without duplicating local state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Theme } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Theme render="select" let:theme>
  <p>Current theme: {theme}</p>
</Theme>
```

### Exported themes constant

The `themes` constant exports all theme keys and labels for programmatic use.

Import `themes` from the Theme component file in a `script context="module"` block.

```html
<script context="module">
  import { themes } from "carbon-components-svelte/src/Theme/Theme.svelte";

  // themes = {
  //   white: "White",
  //   g10: "Gray 10",
  //   g80: "Gray 80",
  //   g90: "Gray 90",
  //   g100: "Gray 100"
  // }

  // Get all theme keys programmatically
  const themeKeys = Object.keys(themes); // ["white", "g10", "g80", "g90", "g100"]

  // Build custom theme selectors with correct labels
  Object.entries(themes).forEach(([key, label]) => {
    console.log(`${key}: ${label}`); // "white: White", etc.
  });
</script>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Theme` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` (Reactive) | `CarbonTheme` | Set the current Carbon theme. | `"white"` |
| `tokens` | `Partial<Record<CarbonToken, string>>` | Customize a theme with your own tokens. Keys are Carbon v11 token names<br />(`"button-primary"`, `"layer-01"`), set as `--cds-{token}`. | `{}` |
| `persist` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to persist the theme using window.localStorage | `false` |
| `persistKey` | `string` | Specify the local storage key | `"theme"` |
| `system` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to follow the operating system color scheme.<br />`theme` is set from `systemThemes` on mount and on every change;<br />set `theme` yourself to override until the next system change. | `false` |
| `systemThemes` | `[light: CarbonTheme, dark: CarbonTheme]` | Specify the themes to apply for the light and dark system color schemes. | `["white", "g100"]` |
| `render` | `"toggle" \| "select" \| "dropdown" \| undefined` | Render a toggle, select, or dropdown to control the theme. | _undefined_ |
| `toggle` | `import("../Toggle/Toggle.svelte").ToggleProps & { themes?: [labelA: CarbonTheme, labelB: CarbonTheme]; }` | Override the default toggle props. | `{<br />  themes: ["white", "g100"],<br />  labelA: "",<br />  labelB: "",<br />  labelText: "Dark mode",<br />  hideLabel: false,<br />}` |
| `select` | `import("../Select/Select.svelte").SelectProps<CarbonTheme> & { themes?: CarbonTheme[]; }` | Override the default select props. | `{<br />  themes: themeKeys,<br />  labelText: "Themes",<br />  hideLabel: false,<br />}` |
| `dropdown` | `Omit<import("../Dropdown/Dropdown.svelte").DropdownProps, "items" \| "selectedId"> & { themes?: CarbonTheme[]; }` | Override the default dropdown props. | `{<br />  themes: themeKeys,<br />  labelText: "Themes",<br />  hideLabel: false,<br />}` |

#### `Theme` typedefs

```ts
type CarbonTheme = "white" | "g10" | "g80" | "g90" | "g100";

type CarbonToken = import("./carbon-tokens").CarbonToken;
```

#### `Theme` slots

| Slot      | Detail                   |
| --------- | ------------------------ |
| `default` | `{ theme: CarbonTheme }` |

#### `Theme` dispatched events

| Event       | Detail                                |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `on:update` | `{<br />  theme: CarbonTheme;<br />}` |


## ThemeZone

### Basic

[Theme](/components/Theme) sets the theme for the whole page. `ThemeZone` sets it for one part of the page. It paints the theme's background and text color, and every component inside it takes the theme's tokens. It matches Carbon React's scoped `<Theme>`.

`ThemeZone` needs `all.css`, which declares every theme as CSS custom properties. The single-theme stylesheets (`white.css`, `g100.css`, and the others) compile one theme's values into the rules, so a zone has nothing to switch.

```js
import "carbon-components-svelte/css/all.css";
```

Set `theme` to one of the five themes, or to `"system"`. Use `tag` to render another element, such as `aside` or `section`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, TextInput, ThemeZone } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ThemeZone theme="g100">
  <Box padding={5}>
    <TextInput labelText="Name" placeholder="On Gray 100" />
  </Box>
</ThemeZone>
```

### Dark sidebar in a light app

A Gray 100 sidebar keeps its theme whatever the page theme is. Switch the docs theme to see the rest of the example follow it.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Search,
    Stack,
    Tag,
    Text,
    TextInput,
    ThemeZone,
    Tile,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const services = [
    { name: "api-gateway", status: "Live", type: "green" },
    { name: "billing-worker", status: "Deploying", type: "blue" },
    { name: "search-index", status: "Failed", type: "red" },
  ];
</script>

<Box display="flex" minHeight="20rem">
  <ThemeZone theme="g100" tag="aside">
    <Box width="16rem" padding={5}>
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <Text type="heading-compact-01">Services</Text>
        <Search size="sm" placeholder="Filter services" />
        <Stack gap={4}>
          {#each services as service (service.name)}
            <Stack
              orientation="horizontal"
              justify="space-between"
              align="center"
            >
              <Text type="body-compact-01">{service.name}</Text>
              <Tag size="sm" type={service.type}>{service.status}</Tag>
            </Stack>
          {/each}
        </Stack>
      </Stack>
    </Box>
  </ThemeZone>
  <Box grow alignSelf="start" padding={5}>
    <Stack gap={5}>
      <Text type="heading-compact-02">api-gateway</Text>
      <TextInput labelText="Service name" value="api-gateway" />
      <Tile>Last deploy finished 4 minutes ago.</Tile>
    </Stack>
  </Box>
</Box>
```

### Nested zones

Zones nest. Each one takes its theme's full token set, so a White zone inside a Gray 100 zone looks the same as a White page.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Stack,
    Tag,
    Text,
    TextInput,
    ThemeZone,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ThemeZone theme="g100">
  <Box padding={5}>
    <Stack gap={5}>
      <Text type="heading-compact-01">Gray 100</Text>
      <TextInput labelText="Cluster" value="prod-us-east" />
      <ThemeZone theme="white">
        <Box padding={5}>
          <Stack gap={5}>
            <Text type="heading-compact-01">White inside Gray 100</Text>
            <TextInput labelText="Node pool" value="general-purpose" />
            <ThemeZone theme="g90">
              <Box padding={5}>
                <Stack gap={5}>
                  <Text type="heading-compact-01">Gray 90 inside White</Text>
                  <div><Tag type="green">3 of 3 nodes ready</Tag></div>
                </Stack>
              </Box>
            </ThemeZone>
          </Stack>
        </Box>
      </ThemeZone>
    </Stack>
  </Box>
</ThemeZone>
```

### System color scheme

Set `theme` to `"system"` to follow the operating system color scheme with CSS alone. The zone is White when the system is light and Gray 100 when it is dark. It switches as soon as the setting changes. See [Theme](/components/Theme#follow-the-system-with-css-only) to do the same for the whole page.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Stack,
    Tag,
    Text,
    TextInput,
    ThemeZone,
    Toggle,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ThemeZone theme="system">
  <Box padding={5}>
    <Stack gap={5}>
      <Text type="heading-compact-01">Follows your system color scheme</Text>
      <TextInput labelText="Display name" value="Ada Lovelace" />
      <Toggle labelText="Email alerts" toggled />
      <div><Tag type="blue">White or Gray 100</Tag></div>
    </Stack>
  </Box>
</ThemeZone>
```

### Layers

A zone starts a new layer stack, as in Carbon React. The zone's surface is the page surface, so a `Layer` inside it is level 1, even when the zone itself sits in a `Layer`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Layer,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
    ThemeZone,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <Stack gap={5}>
      <TextInput labelText="Page, level 1" placeholder="field-02" />
      <ThemeZone theme="g100">
        <Box padding={5}>
          <Stack gap={5}>
            <TextInput labelText="Zone, level 0" placeholder="field-01" />
            <Layer withBackground>
              <Box padding={5}>
                <TextInput labelText="Zone, level 1" placeholder="field-02" />
              </Box>
            </Layer>
          </Stack>
        </Box>
      </ThemeZone>
    </Stack>
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Portalled content

Menus, tooltips, and other floating content that render in a portal leave the zone in the DOM. They keep the zone's theme anyway: the portal takes the zone's theme class. This covers `portalMenu` on Dropdown, ComboBox, and MultiSelect, and every component that portals a tooltip or menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Dropdown, ThemeZone } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ThemeZone theme="g100">
  <Box overflow="hidden" maxHeight="8rem" padding={5}>
    <Dropdown
      portalMenu
      labelText="Region"
      selectedId="0"
      items={[
        { id: "0", text: "Oregon (us-west-2)" },
        { id: "1", text: "Virginia (us-east-1)" },
        { id: "2", text: "Frankfurt (eu-central-1)" },
      ]}
    />
  </Box>
</ThemeZone>
```

### Custom tokens

A zone declares its theme's stock tokens. Overrides that `Theme`'s `tokens` prop sets on `<html>` don't reach inside a zone. To customize a zone, set the custom properties on it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, TextInput, ThemeZone } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ThemeZone theme="g100" style="--cds-focus: #ff7eb6">
  <Box padding={5}>
    <TextInput labelText="Focus me" placeholder="Pink focus ring" />
  </Box>
</ThemeZone>
```

---

### Component API

#### `ThemeZone` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` (Required) | `import("../Theme/Theme.svelte").CarbonTheme \| "system"` | Specify the theme for the zone. `"system"` follows the operating<br />system color scheme with CSS alone: White for light, Gray 100 for dark. | _undefined_ |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLElementTagNameMap[Tag]` | Obtain a reference to the HTML element. | `null` |
| `tag` | `Tag` | Specify the tag name. | `"div"` |

#### `ThemeZone` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `ThemeZone` $$restProps

`ThemeZone` spreads `$$restProps` to the `svelte:element` element.


## Tile

### Basic

Create a basic tile container for your content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tile>Payments API -- Operational, 99.98% uptime</Tile>
```

### AI label

Put an `AILabel` in the `decorator` slot to mark the tile's content as AI-generated. The tile shows the AI surface, and the label sits in the top-right corner at the `"xs"` size.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tile>
  <h4>Usage forecast</h4>
  <p>Spend is projected to grow 12% next month.</p>
  <AILabel slot="decorator">
    <p>Generated from 90 days of billing data.</p>
  </AILabel>
</Tile>
```

#### Rounded corners

Set `rounded` to `true` to round the corners of a tile with a decorator. Carbon reserves rounded tiles for AI content, so a tile without a decorator stays square.

```svelte
<script>
  import { AILabel, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tile rounded>
  <h4>Usage forecast</h4>
  <p>Spend is projected to grow 12% next month.</p>
  <AILabel slot="decorator">
    <p>Generated from 90 days of billing data.</p>
  </AILabel>
</Tile>
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Layer, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <Tile>Object storage -- 82% capacity used</Tile>
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Full height

Set `fullHeight` to `true` so the tile fills the height of its container. This is useful for tiles placed in a `Row`, where sibling columns stretch to the tallest column by default but the tile inside does not.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Column, Grid, Row, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Grid>
  <Row>
    <Column>
      <Tile fullHeight>Requests per minute: 4,201</Tile>
    </Column>
    <Column>
      <Tile fullHeight
        >Error rate: 0.3% over the last hour, down from 0.8% yesterday</Tile
      >
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Grid>
```

### Small size

Set `size="sm"` for a compact tile with less padding and no minimum height.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tile size="sm">Compact tile</Tile>
```

### No padding

Set `noPadding` to `true` to remove the tile's padding, so media or a chart can bleed to its edge.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tile noPadding>
  <Box fill="layer-03" height="8rem" />
</Tile>
```

### Custom interaction

The tile forwards `on:click`, `on:mouseover`, `on:mouseenter`, and `on:mouseleave` for custom interactions. Unlike `ClickableTile`, a plain tile has no `tabindex` and doesn't respond to <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd>--use `ClickableTile` if you need built-in keyboard accessibility.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Tile } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Tile on:click={() => console.log("clicked")}
  >Storage cluster -- 3 nodes degraded</Tile
>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Tile` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the top-level HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| undefined` | Set the size: `"sm"` for a compact tile, such as a row in a list of<br />choices, with less padding and no minimum height. | _undefined_ |
| `fullHeight` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to stretch the tile to fill the height of its container | `false` |
| `rounded` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to round the tile's corners when it has a `decorator`,<br />such as an `AILabel`. Carbon reserves rounded tiles for AI content. | `false` |
| `noPadding` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the tile's padding | `false` |

#### `Tile` slots

| Slot        | Detail                  |
| ----------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`   | `Record<string, never>` |
| `decorator` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Tile` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `Tile` $$restProps

`Tile` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## TimePicker

### Basic

Create a time picker with period (AM/PM) and timezone selectors.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TimePicker labelText="Cron job" placeholder="hh:mm">
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="pm">
    <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
    <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Timezone" value="pdt">
    <SelectItem value="pdt" text="PDT" />
    <SelectItem value="gmt" text="GMT" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

Give each `TimePickerSelect` a `labelText`. The default variant hides it visually and uses it as the select's accessible name. The fluid variant shows it inside the cell.

### Select on focus

Set `selectTextOnFocus` to select the full value when the field receives focus.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TimePicker
  selectTextOnFocus
  labelText="Cron job"
  placeholder="hh:mm"
  value="2:15"
>
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="pm">
    <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
    <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Timezone" value="pdt">
    <SelectItem value="pdt" text="PDT" />
    <SelectItem value="gmt" text="GMT" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

### Formatting

Customize input validation to match a different time notation.

#### 24-hour clock

The default `pattern` validates a 12-hour `h:mm` or `hh:mm` value. Override `pattern` (and update `helperText` or `placeholder` to match) to accept a 24-hour clock instead. A 24-hour field typically drops the AM/PM select.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TimePicker
  pattern="([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]"
  labelText="Cron job"
  placeholder="hh:mm"
  helperText="24-hour clock, e.g. 14:30"
  value="14:30"
>
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Timezone" value="pdt">
    <SelectItem value="pdt" text="PDT" />
    <SelectItem value="gmt" text="GMT" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

#### Seconds

Update `pattern` and increase `maxlength` together to accept a `hh:mm:ss` value. The default `maxlength` (5) only fits `hh:mm`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TimePicker
  pattern="(1[012]|[1-9]):[0-5][0-9]:[0-5][0-9]"
  maxlength={8}
  labelText="Cron job"
  placeholder="hh:mm:ss"
  value="2:15:30"
>
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="pm">
    <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
    <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

### Events

Respond to edits on the time field and to period/timezone selection.

#### Change

`on:change` and `on:input` forward the native input events from the time field. Read the current value from `event.target.value`, or use `bind:value` for two-way binding.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TimePicker
  labelText="Cron job"
  placeholder="hh:mm"
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.target.value)}
>
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="pm">
    <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
    <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

#### Period and timezone change

`TimePickerSelect` forwards `on:change` from its native select element the same way.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TimePicker labelText="Cron job" placeholder="hh:mm">
  <TimePickerSelect
    labelText="Period"
    value="pm"
    on:change={(e) => console.log(e.target.value)}
  >
    <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
    <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

### Select icon label

Set `iconDescription` on `TimePickerSelect` to change the chevron icon's ARIA label and native tooltip. It defaults to `"Open list of options"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TimePicker labelText="Cron job" placeholder="hh:mm">
  <TimePickerSelect
    labelText="Period"
    iconDescription="Choose AM or PM"
    value="pm"
  >
    <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
    <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
  <TimePickerSelect
    labelText="Timezone"
    iconDescription="Choose timezone"
    value="pdt"
  >
    <SelectItem value="pdt" text="PDT" />
    <SelectItem value="gmt" text="GMT" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

### Helper text

Add helper text to provide additional context or formatting instructions.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TimePicker
  labelText="Cron job"
  placeholder="hh:mm"
  helperText="24-hour, e.g. 14:30"
>
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="pm">
    <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
    <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Timezone" value="pdt">
    <SelectItem value="pdt" text="PDT" />
    <SelectItem value="gmt" text="GMT" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TimePicker hideLabel labelText="Cron job" placeholder="hh:mm">
  <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="pm">
    <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
    <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

### On a layer

Place the component in a [`Layer`](/components/Layer) to put it on the next surface, so it contrasts with the surface below. `Layer` replaces the v10 `light` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Layer,
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Layer withBackground>
  <Box padding={5}>
    <TimePicker labelText="Cron job" placeholder="hh:mm">
      <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="pm">
        <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
        <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
      </TimePickerSelect>
      <TimePickerSelect labelText="Timezone" value="pdt">
        <SelectItem value="pdt" text="PDT" />
        <SelectItem value="gmt" text="GMT" />
      </TimePickerSelect>
    </TimePicker>
  </Box>
</Layer>
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to embed labels inside each field cell. Fluid time pickers work standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), which applies the variant automatically.

Fluid time pickers fill their container using percentage-based columns (25% / 25% / 50% with two selects, 50% / 50% with one). Give the parent a defined width so those ratios resolve as intended.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box width="350px">
  <TimePicker fluid labelText="Time" placeholder="hh:mm">
    <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="am">
      <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
      <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
    </TimePickerSelect>
    <TimePickerSelect labelText="Timezone" value="et">
      <SelectItem value="et" text="Eastern Time (ET)" />
      <SelectItem value="pt" text="Pacific Time (PT)" />
    </TimePickerSelect>
  </TimePicker>
</Box>
```

With a single period selector, the time input and select share equal width.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    SelectItem,
    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Box width="350px">
  <TimePicker fluid labelText="Time" placeholder="hh:mm">
    <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="am">
      <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
      <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
    </TimePickerSelect>
  </TimePicker>
</Box>
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte

    Box,

    TimePicker,
    TimePickerSelect,
    TooltipIcon,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<Box width="350px">
  <TimePicker fluid labelText="Time" placeholder="hh:mm">
    <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
      Time
      <TooltipIcon
        tooltipText="Enter the standup time in hh:mm format."
        icon={Information}
      />
    </svelte:fragment>
    <TimePickerSelect labelText="Period" value="am">
      <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
        Period
        <TooltipIcon tooltipText="Select AM or PM." icon={Information} />
      </svelte:fragment>
      <SelectItem value="am" text="AM" />
      <SelectItem value="pm" text="PM" />
    </TimePickerSelect>
  </TimePicker>
</Box>
```

### Component API

#### `TimePicker` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `string` | Specify the input value.<br />Follows the field's value after the owning form resets, on every Svelte version. | `""` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| undefined` | Specify the size of the input.<br />Inherits the parent `Form` size when unset.<br />Also accepts Carbon v11's `"md"` (the 40px default, which overrides a<br />`Form` size) and `"lg"` (`"xl"`). | _undefined_ |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Specify the input placeholder text | `"hh:mm"` |
| `pattern` | `string` | Specify the `pattern` attribute for the input element | `"(1[012]\|[1-9]):[0-5][0-9](\\s)?"` |
| `maxlength` | `number` | Specify the `maxlength` input attribute | `5` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the input | `false` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to mark the input as read-only | `false` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text. In the fluid variant,<br />the `TimePickerSelect` labels are hidden too. | `false` |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the input element | `uniqueId()` |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a name attribute for the input. | _undefined_ |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`. | `false` |
| `selectTextOnFocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to select the input's text when it receives focus | `false` |

## ToastNotification

### Basic

Display a basic error notification with title, subtitle, and timestamp by default. See [detailed usage](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/notification/usage) and the related [InlineNotification](InlineNotification). For an imperative API to manage multiple toasts with automatic queue management, see [NotificationQueue](NotificationQueue).

```svelte
<script>
  import { ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification
  title="Session expired"
  subtitle="Your session has ended. Please sign in again to continue."
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
/>
```

### Reusable

Control notification visibility by binding to `open` to show, hide, and reuse the same component with different messages. Open defaults to true.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    Stack,
    ToastNotification,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let kind = "error";
  let title = "Session expired";
  let subtitle = "Your session has ended. Please sign in again to continue.";
  let caption = new Date().toLocaleString();

  function showError() {
    kind = "error";
    title = "Session expired";
    subtitle = "Your session has ended. Please sign in again to continue.";
    caption = new Date().toLocaleString();
    open = true;
  }

  function showSuccess() {
    kind = "success";
    title = "Export complete";
    subtitle = "Your report has been exported and is ready for download.";
    caption = new Date().toLocaleString();
    open = true;
  }

  function showWarning() {
    kind = "warning";
    title = "Unsaved changes";
    subtitle =
      "You have unsaved changes that will be lost if you navigate away.";
    caption = new Date().toLocaleString();
    open = true;
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <ButtonSet>
    <Button on:click={showSuccess}>Show success</Button>
    <Button kind="ghost" on:click={showWarning}>Show warning</Button>
    <Button kind="danger-ghost" on:click={showError}>Show error</Button>
  </ButtonSet>

  <ToastNotification bind:open {kind} {title} {subtitle} {caption} />
</Stack>
```

### Autoclose

Automatically close the notification after a specified duration (in milliseconds) with `timeout`. Set `pauseOnHover` to pause the timeout while the pointer is over the toast or while focus is inside it, so users can finish reading (opt-in).

A toast with an action, or an actionable toast, ignores `timeout`. It stays open until users act on it or close it, so the action never disappears before they reach it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import { fade } from "svelte/transition";

  let timeout;
  $: showNotification = timeout !== undefined;
</script>

<Button
  disabled={showNotification}
  on:click={() => {
    timeout = 3_000; // 3 seconds
  }}
>
  Show notification
</Button>

{#if showNotification}
  <div transition:fade>
    <ToastNotification
      {timeout}
      kind="success"
      title="Export complete"
      subtitle="This notification will autoclose in {timeout.toLocaleString()} ms."
      caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
      on:close={(e) => {
        timeout = undefined;
        console.log(e.detail.timeout); // true if closed via timeout
      }}
    />
  </div>
{/if}
```

### Actions

Add an action, such as a retry, in the `actions` slot. A `NotificationActionButton` there renders as a small tertiary button under the text, in colors that read on every kind. The toast's title describes the button for screen readers, with no extra setup.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    NotificationActionButton,
    ToastNotification,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification
  kind="error"
  title="Upload failed"
  subtitle="The connection timed out before quarterly-report.pdf finished."
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <NotificationActionButton>Retry</NotificationActionButton>
  </svelte:fragment>
</ToastNotification>
<ToastNotification
  lowContrast
  kind="error"
  title="Upload failed"
  subtitle="The connection timed out before quarterly-report.pdf finished."
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
    <NotificationActionButton>Retry</NotificationActionButton>
  </svelte:fragment>
</ToastNotification>
```

### Actionable

Set `actionable` to `true` when users must reach an action in the toast, such as a retry after a failed upload. Place the action in the `actions` slot. The toast becomes an `alertdialog` named by its title and described by its subtitle. When it opens, focus moves to the first action, or to the close button if there is no action. Tab stays inside the toast, and <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it. Focus then returns to where it was before, such as the button that opened it.

Set `focusOnOpen` to `false` to leave focus in place, or `closeOnEscape` to `false` to keep it open on <kbd>Escape</kbd>. If the close button is also hidden, Tab can leave the toast, so keyboard users are never trapped. The toast ignores `timeout`, so it cannot close before users act. [NotificationQueue](NotificationQueue) accepts the same options.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    NotificationActionButton,
    Stack,
    ToastNotification,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Stack gap={5} align="start">
  <Button disabled={open} on:click={() => (open = true)}>Upload report</Button>

  <ToastNotification
    bind:open
    actionable
    lowContrast
    title="Upload failed"
    subtitle="The connection timed out before quarterly-report.pdf finished."
    caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
  >
    <svelte:fragment slot="actions">
      <NotificationActionButton on:click={() => (open = false)}>
        Retry
      </NotificationActionButton>
    </svelte:fragment>
  </ToastNotification>
</Stack>
```

### Full width

Span the full container width with `fullWidth`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification
  fullWidth
  title="Session expired"
  subtitle="Your session has ended. Please sign in again to continue."
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
/>
```

### Title, subtitle, caption

All three are optional and can be customized with slots.

#### Optional

Title, subtitle, and caption each render only when provided.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification
  subtitle="Your session has ended. Please sign in again to continue."
/>
<ToastNotification
  title="Session expired"
  subtitle="Your session has ended. Please sign in again to continue."
/>
<ToastNotification
  subtitle="Your session has ended. Please sign in again to continue."
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
/>
<ToastNotification
  title="Export complete"
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
/>
```

#### Custom (slots)

Customize the notification content using slots for more flexibility.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification>
  <strong slot="titleChildren">Session expired: </strong>
  <strong slot="subtitleChildren"
    >Your session has ended. Please sign in again to continue.</strong
  >
  <strong slot="captionChildren">{new Date().toLocaleString()}</strong>
</ToastNotification>
```

### Close button

Hide the close button or customize its behavior and label.

#### Hidden

Create a persistent notification by hiding the close button.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification
  hideCloseButton
  kind="warning"
  title="Elevated error rate"
  subtitle="The payments service is experiencing elevated error rates. This message will remain until resolved."
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
/>
```

#### Translated label

Translate the close button label via `closeButtonDescription`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification
  title="会话已过期"
  subtitle="您的会话已过期,请重新登录以继续。"
  closeButtonDescription="关闭通知"
/>
```

#### Prevent default

Prevent the default close behavior using `e.preventDefault()` in the `on:close` event handler.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification
  title="Session expired"
  subtitle="Your session has ended. Please sign in again to continue."
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
  on:close={(e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    // custom close logic (e.g., transitions)
  }}
/>
```

### ARIA role

Screen readers announce a notification when it appears. The default, `role="status"`, waits until the user pauses. Use it for most messages, such as a finished export.

Set `role="alert"` for an urgent error that needs action now, such as a failed payment. An alert interrupts whatever the screen reader is reading, so keep it rare. Set `role="log"` for a running log of messages.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification
  kind="success"
  title="Export complete"
  subtitle="Your report has been exported and is ready for download."
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
/>
<ToastNotification
  role="alert"
  kind="error"
  title="Payment failed"
  subtitle="Update your card to keep the workspace active."
  caption={new Date().toLocaleString()}
/>
```

### Status icon label

The status icon has a label for screen readers, such as "Warning" for the warning kinds. Translate it with `statusIconDescription`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ToastNotification } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<ToastNotification
  kind="warning"
  title="Maintenance planifiée"
  subtitle="La facturation est en lecture seule samedi de 02:00 à 04:00 UTC."
  statusIconDescription="Avertissement"
  closeButtonDescription="Fermer la notification"
/>
```

#### High contrast

### Component API

#### `ToastNotification` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to show the notification, `false` to hide it. | `true` |
| `kind` | `"error" \| "info" \| "info-square" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "warning-alt"` | Specify the kind of notification. | `"error"` |
| `lowContrast` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the low contrast variant | `false` |
| `timeout` | `number` | Set the timeout duration (ms) to hide the notification after opening it.<br />Ignored when the notification is `actionable` or has an `actions` slot. | `0` |
| `pauseOnHover` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to pause the auto-dismiss timeout while the pointer is over the notification or while focus is inside it. | `false` |
| `role` | `"alert" \| "log" \| "status"` | Specify the ARIA `role` for the notification container.<br />`actionable` overrides it with `alertdialog`. | `"status"` |
| `actionable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` when the notification holds an action that users must<br />reach, such as an undo or a retry. The notification becomes an<br />`alertdialog` named by its title, moves focus to its first action<br />(or the close button) when it opens, keeps Tab inside, and closes<br />on Escape. | `false` |
| `focusOnOpen` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to keep focus where it is when an actionable<br />notification opens. Has no effect unless `actionable` is `true`. | `true` |
| `closeOnEscape` | `boolean` | Set to `false` to keep an actionable notification open on Escape.<br />With `hideCloseButton` also set, Tab can leave the notification.<br />Has no effect unless `actionable` is `true`. | `true` |
| `title` | `string` | Specify the title text | `""` |
| `subtitle` | `string` | Specify the subtitle text | `""` |
| `caption` | `string` | Specify the caption text | `""` |
| `closeButtonDescription` | `string` | Specify the ARIA label for the close button | `"Close notification"` |
| `statusIconDescription` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the label of the status icon for screen readers.<br />Defaults to the kind, such as "Warning". | _undefined_ |
| `hideCloseButton` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to hide the close button | `false` |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the notification to span<br />the full width of its containing element. | `false` |
| `id` | `string \| undefined` | Set an id for the top-level element. The title and subtitle ids derive<br />from it as `{id}-title` and `{id}-subtitle`, so the server and the<br />browser render the same ids. | _undefined_ |

#### `ToastNotification` slots

| Slot               | Detail                  |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- |
| `default`          | `Record<string, never>` |
| `actions`          | `Record<string, never>` |
| `captionChildren`  | `Record<string, never>` |
| `subtitleChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `titleChildren`    | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `ToastNotification` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `ToastNotification` dispatched events

| Event      | Detail                              |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `on:close` | `{<br />  timeout: boolean;<br />}` |
