| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |


## TooltipDefinition

### Basic

Display a basic definition tooltip with the default bottom-center alignment.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition
  tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
>
  SSO
</TooltipDefinition>
```

Focus or hover the term to show the tooltip. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> to toggle it. The term sets `aria-expanded` to match. The tooltip stays open while the pointer moves onto it, so its text can be read or selected. Press <kbd>Escape</kbd> to hide it without moving the pointer or focus.

### In body text

Place the term in running text. It takes the font of the text around it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Text, TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Text type="body-01">
  Every workspace signs in through
  <TooltipDefinition
    tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
    >single sign-on</TooltipDefinition
  >
  and loses access when an account leaves the directory.
</Text>
```

### Placement

Position the tooltip with direction and alignment.

#### Directions

By default, the tooltip is positioned to the bottom.

Position the tooltip with `direction`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition direction="top" tooltipText="Top">Top</TooltipDefinition>
<TooltipDefinition direction="bottom" tooltipText="Bottom">
  Bottom
</TooltipDefinition>
```

#### Alignment

By default, the tooltip is aligned to the center.

Align the tooltip content with `align`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition align="start" tooltipText="Start">Start</TooltipDefinition>
<TooltipDefinition align="center" tooltipText="Center">
  Center
</TooltipDefinition>
<TooltipDefinition align="end" tooltipText="End">End</TooltipDefinition>
```

### Open behavior

Control how and when the tooltip opens.

#### Click to open

Open the tooltip on click instead of hover with `clickToOpen`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition
  clickToOpen
  tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
>
  SSO
</TooltipDefinition>
```

#### Open by default

Open the tooltip by default with `open`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition
  open
  tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
>
  SSO
</TooltipDefinition>
```

### Reactive example

Control tooltip state programmatically with `bind:open`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Stack, TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Stack gap={12}>
  <div>
    <TooltipDefinition
      align="start"
      bind:open
      tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
    >
      SSO
    </TooltipDefinition>
  </div>
  <div>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
      {open ? "Close tooltip" : "Open tooltip"}
    </Button>
  </div>
</Stack>
```

### Dispatched events

The component dispatches `open` and `close` events.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let events = [];
</script>

<TooltipDefinition
  align="start"
  tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
  on:open={() => (events = [...events, "open"])}
  on:close={() => (events = [...events, "close"])}
>
  Dispatched events: {events.join(", ")}
</TooltipDefinition>
```

### Custom delay

Customize hover delays with `enterDelayMs` and `leaveDelayMs`. Defaults are 100ms and 300ms.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition
  tooltipText="Slow to appear"
  enterDelayMs={500}
  leaveDelayMs={500}
>
  SSO
</TooltipDefinition>
```

### Tooltip group

Wrap a passage with several defined terms in a [TooltipGroup](/components/TooltipGroup). Once one definition is open, moving to the next term shows its definition right away, with no enter delay or fade-in. Inside a group, `enterDelayMs` and `leaveDelayMs` default to the group's delays.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Text,
    TooltipDefinition,
    TooltipGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipGroup>
  <Text tag="div" type="body-01">
    Sign in with
    <TooltipDefinition
      tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
      >SSO</TooltipDefinition
    >
    or
    <TooltipDefinition
      tooltipText="Multi-factor authentication: a second check after your password."
      >MFA</TooltipDefinition
    >
    to reach the
    <TooltipDefinition
      tooltipText="Identity and access management: who can use which resources."
      >IAM</TooltipDefinition
    >
    console.
  </Text>
</TooltipGroup>
```

### Custom tooltip slot

Use the `tooltip` slot to customize tooltip content with additional styling or structure.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Text, TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition>
  SSO
  <Text slot="tooltip" tag="span" type="inherit" weight="semibold">
    Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications.
  </Text>
</TooltipDefinition>
```

### Portal

A tooltip that a container would cut off, such as a box with `overflow: hidden`, a scroll area or a [DataTable](/components/DataTable), opens in a portal. Inside a Modal, the tooltip always opens in a portal.

Set `portalTooltip` to `true` to always render the tooltip in a portal, or to `false` to keep it in place. Alignment matches the in-place tooltip. A portalled tooltip leaves its container in the DOM, so CSS that targets the tooltip as a descendant of the container does not match it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition
  portalTooltip
  tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
>
  SSO
</TooltipDefinition>
```

#### Directions

Definition tooltips support top and bottom directions only. With portalling, direction behaves the same as the default CSS path.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition portalTooltip direction="top" tooltipText="Top">
  Top
</TooltipDefinition>
<TooltipDefinition portalTooltip direction="bottom" tooltipText="Bottom">
  Bottom
</TooltipDefinition>
```

#### Alignment

Portalled tooltips use the same alignment options as the default path: horizontal placement along the anchor for top and bottom directions.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipDefinition } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipDefinition portalTooltip align="start" tooltipText="Start">
  Start
</TooltipDefinition>
<TooltipDefinition portalTooltip align="center" tooltipText="Center">
  Center
</TooltipDefinition>
<TooltipDefinition portalTooltip align="end" tooltipText="End">
  End
</TooltipDefinition>
```

### Inside a modal

When a tooltip definition is used inside a [Modal](/components/Modal), it is automatically portalled so it is not clipped by the modal overflow or z-index stacking. Set `portalTooltip` to override this behavior.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    Modal,
    Portal,
    TooltipDefinition,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open modal</Button>

<Portal>
  <Modal
    bind:open
    size="sm"
    modalHeading="TooltipDefinition in modal"
    primaryButtonText="Done"
    secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
    on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  >
    <TooltipDefinition
      direction="top"
      tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
    >
      SSO (top)
    </TooltipDefinition>
    <TooltipDefinition
      direction="bottom"
      tooltipText="Single sign-on: one login for all connected applications."
    >
      SSO (bottom)
    </TooltipDefinition>
  </Modal>
</Portal>
```

### Component API

#### `TooltipDefinition` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the tooltip. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLButtonElement` | Obtain a reference to the button HTML element. | `null` |
| `tooltipText` | `string` | Specify the tooltip text | `""` |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | Set the alignment of the tooltip relative to the icon.<br />`start` and `end` name inline sides, so they swap under `dir="rtl"`. | `"center"` |

| `leaveDelayMs` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the duration in milliseconds to delay before hiding the tooltip.<br />Defaults to the enclosing `TooltipGroup`'s delay, or `300`. | _undefined_ |

Left unset, the tooltip opens in a portal inside a<br />`Modal`, or when a box around it (`overflow` other than `visible`, such<br />as a `DataTable`) would cut it off. | _undefined_ |

| `tooltip` | `Record<string, never>` |

| --------------- |

| `on:focus`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |

| `on:mouseover`  |

| Event      | Detail |
| ---------- | ------ |
| `on:close` | `null` |
| `on:open`  | `null` |

#### `TooltipDefinition` $$restProps

`TooltipDefinition` spreads `$$restProps` to the `span` element.


## TooltipGroup

### Basic

Wrap related tooltip triggers in a `TooltipGroup`. The first tooltip opens after the enter delay. While it is open, or shortly after it closes, hovering or focusing another trigger in the group opens that one right away, without the fade-in, so it looks like one tooltip moving along the row. Moving the pointer off the row hides the tooltip after a short delay, so the pointer can also move onto the tooltip and rest there. Tabbing through the row with the keyboard shows each tooltip immediately, also without the fade-in.

`TooltipGroup` renders no element of its own, so it doesn't affect layout. Use it inside or around whatever arranges the triggers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Stack, TooltipGroup } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Edit from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Edit.svelte";
  import Share from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Share.svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipGroup>
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={1}>
    <Button kind="ghost" icon={Edit} iconDescription="Edit" />
    <Button kind="ghost" icon={Copy} iconDescription="Duplicate" />
    <Button kind="ghost" icon={Share} iconDescription="Share" />
    <Button kind="ghost" icon={TrashCan} iconDescription="Delete" />
  </Stack>
</TooltipGroup>
```

### Members

Any component with a hover or focus tooltip joins the nearest group. Members of different kinds hand off to each other.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    CopyButton,
    Stack,
    TooltipDefinition,
    TooltipGroup,
    TooltipIcon,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Edit from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Edit.svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipGroup>
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={4} align="center">
    <Button kind="ghost" icon={Edit} iconDescription="Edit" />
    <CopyButton text="https://example.com" iconDescription="Copy link" />
    <TooltipIcon tooltipText="Synced 2 minutes ago" icon={Information} />
    <TooltipDefinition tooltipText="Annual percentage rate"
      >APR</TooltipDefinition
    >
  </Stack>
</TooltipGroup>
```

| Component | Joins the group |
| --- | --- |
| `Button` | When icon-only with an `iconDescription` |
| `CopyButton` | Always |
| `TooltipIcon` | Always |
| `TooltipDefinition` | When it opens on hover (not `clickToOpen`) |
| `Tooltip` | Always. A hover-opened `Tooltip` closes when another tooltip opens; one opened by keyboard stays open |
| `PasswordInput` | Its visibility toggle, which opens without a delay but still hands off |
| `Switch`, `Tab`, `ToggleButton` | When icon-only |
| `OverflowMenu` | When it has an `iconDescription` and no `menu` slot |
| `HeaderAction`, `FileUploaderButton` | When icon-only with an `iconDescription` |
| `UserAvatar` | When it has `tooltipText` |

### Built-in groups

`ContentSwitcher`, `Tabs`, `TabsVertical`, `ToggleButtonGroup`, and `UserAvatarGroup` are tooltip groups already, so their own tooltips hand off to each other without a wrapper. Put one inside a `TooltipGroup` to join the group around it: here the view switcher hands off to the buttons next to it.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ContentSwitcher,
    Stack,
    Switch,
    TooltipGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Edit from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Edit.svelte";
  import List from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/List.svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipGroup>
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={4} align="center">
    <ContentSwitcher size="sm">
      <Switch icon={List} text="List view" />
      <Switch icon={Grid} text="Grid view" />
    </ContentSwitcher>
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={1}>
      <Button kind="ghost" size="small" icon={Edit} iconDescription="Edit" />
      <Button
        kind="ghost"
        size="small"
        icon={TrashCan}
        iconDescription="Delete"
      />
    </Stack>
  </Stack>
</TooltipGroup>
```

Nested groups always join the enclosing group. A nested `TooltipGroup` is still useful for setting different delays on part of a group.

### Group boundaries

Only one tooltip is open at a time on the page. Moving from a tooltip in one group to a trigger in another waits for the full enter delay. Hover across from the left group to the right one to compare.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Stack, TooltipGroup } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Edit from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Edit.svelte";
  import Share from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Share.svelte";
  import TrashCan from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/TrashCan.svelte";
</script>

<Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={7}>
  <TooltipGroup>
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={1}>
      <Button kind="ghost" icon={Edit} iconDescription="Edit" />
      <Button kind="ghost" icon={Copy} iconDescription="Duplicate" />
    </Stack>
  </TooltipGroup>
  <TooltipGroup>
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={1}>
      <Button kind="ghost" icon={Share} iconDescription="Share" />
      <Button kind="ghost" icon={TrashCan} iconDescription="Delete" />
    </Stack>
  </TooltipGroup>
</Stack>
```

Tooltips outside any `TooltipGroup` share one page-wide group, so neighboring standalone tooltips still hand off to each other. Add a `TooltipGroup` to mark which triggers belong together, or to set the timing for them.

### Timing

Set `enterDelayMs`, `leaveDelayMs`, and `skipDelayMs` to change the timing for every member. A member's own `enterDelayMs` or `leaveDelayMs` prop, where it has one, takes precedence.

| Prop | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enterDelayMs` | `100` | Delay before the first tooltip in the group opens |
| `leaveDelayMs` | `100` for icon tooltips, `300` for `Tooltip` and `TooltipDefinition` | Delay before an open tooltip closes, so the pointer can move onto it |
| `skipDelayMs` | `300` | How long after a tooltip closes that the next one in the group still opens instantly |

In this group the first tooltip takes half a second to appear, and handoff keeps working for a full second after the last one closes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Stack, TooltipGroup } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Copy from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Copy.svelte";
  import Edit from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Edit.svelte";
  import Share from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Share.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipGroup enterDelayMs={500} skipDelayMs={1000}>
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={1}>
    <Button kind="ghost" icon={Edit} iconDescription="Edit" />
    <Button kind="ghost" icon={Copy} iconDescription="Duplicate" />
    <Button kind="ghost" icon={Share} iconDescription="Share" />
  </Stack>
</TooltipGroup>
```

---

### Component API

#### `TooltipGroup` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enterDelayMs` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the delay in milliseconds before the first tooltip in the group opens.<br />Defaults to the enclosing group's delay, or `100`. | _undefined_ |
| `leaveDelayMs` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the delay in milliseconds before an open tooltip closes.<br />Defaults to the enclosing group's delay. Without one, icon tooltips<br />wait `100` and `Tooltip` and `TooltipDefinition` wait `300`, so the<br />pointer can move onto them. | _undefined_ |
| `skipDelayMs` | `number \| undefined` | Specify how long in milliseconds after a tooltip in the group closes<br />that the next one still opens instantly.<br />Defaults to the enclosing group's window, or `300`. | _undefined_ |

#### `TooltipGroup` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |


## TooltipIcon

### Basic

Display a tooltip with the default bottom-center alignment.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon
  tooltipText="Metrics are aggregated across every workspace in your organization."
  icon={Carbon}
/>
```

### Reactive example

Control tooltip state programmatically with `bind:open`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Stack, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";

  let open = true;
</script>

<Stack gap={12}>
  <div>
    <TooltipIcon
      bind:open
      tooltipText="Metrics are aggregated across every workspace in your organization."
      icon={Carbon}
      align="start"
    />
  </div>
  <div>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
      {open ? "Close tooltip" : "Open tooltip"}
    </Button>
  </div>
</Stack>
```

### Dispatched events

The component dispatches `open` and `close` events.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Stack, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";

  let events = [];
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <TooltipIcon
    tooltipText="Metrics are aggregated across every workspace in your organization."
    icon={Carbon}
    on:open={() => (events = [...events, "open"])}
    on:close={() => (events = [...events, "close"])}
  />
  <p>Dispatched events: {events.join(", ")}</p>
</Stack>
```

### Sizes

Set icon size with `size`. Carbon icons use a 16/20/24/32 scale, but any pixel value works.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon tooltipText="16px" icon={Carbon} size={16} />
<TooltipIcon tooltipText="20px" icon={Carbon} size={20} />
<TooltipIcon tooltipText="24px" icon={Carbon} size={24} />
<TooltipIcon tooltipText="32px" icon={Carbon} size={32} />
```

### Placement

Position the tooltip with direction and alignment.

#### Directions

By default, the tooltip is positioned to the bottom.

Position the tooltip with `direction`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Filter from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Filter.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon tooltipText="Top" direction="top" icon={Filter} />
<TooltipIcon tooltipText="Right" direction="right" icon={Filter} />
<TooltipIcon tooltipText="Bottom" direction="bottom" icon={Filter} />
<TooltipIcon tooltipText="Left" direction="left" icon={Filter} />
```

#### Alignment

By default, the tooltip is aligned to the center.

Align the tooltip content with `align`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Filter from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Filter.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon tooltipText="Start" align="start" icon={Filter} />
<TooltipIcon tooltipText="Center" align="center" icon={Filter} />
<TooltipIcon tooltipText="End" align="end" icon={Filter} />
```

### Custom tooltip text

Use the `tooltipChildren` slot to customize the tooltip content with additional styling.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Text, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon icon={Carbon}>
  <Text slot="tooltipChildren" tag="span" type="inherit" weight="semibold"
    >Metrics are aggregated across every workspace in your organization.</Text
  >
</TooltipIcon>
```

### Custom icon

Use the default slot to fully customize the trigger content, replacing what the `icon` prop would otherwise render.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon tooltipText="Custom icon content">
  <Box width="1rem" height="1rem" border="interactive" />
</TooltipIcon>
```

### Custom delay

Customize hover delays with `enterDelayMs` and `leaveDelayMs`. Defaults are 100ms and 100ms. The tooltip stays while the pointer is on it. Keyboard focus shows the tooltip at once.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon
  tooltipText="Slow to appear"
  icon={Carbon}
  enterDelayMs={500}
  leaveDelayMs={500}
/>
```

### Tooltip group

Wrap related tooltip icons in a [TooltipGroup](/components/TooltipGroup). Once one tooltip is open, moving to the next icon shows its tooltip right away, with no enter delay or fade-in. Inside a group, `enterDelayMs` and `leaveDelayMs` default to the group's delays.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Stack, TooltipGroup, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
  import Filter from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Filter.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipGroup>
  <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={3}>
    <TooltipIcon tooltipText="Synced 2 minutes ago" icon={Carbon} />
    <TooltipIcon tooltipText="Filters applied: status, owner" icon={Filter} />
    <TooltipIcon tooltipText="Metrics cover every workspace" icon={Carbon} />
  </Stack>
</TooltipGroup>
```

### Disabled

Prevent interaction with `disabled`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon
  disabled
  tooltipText="Metrics are aggregated across every workspace in your organization."
  icon={Carbon}
/>
```

### Portal

A tooltip that a container would cut off, such as a box with `overflow: hidden`, a scroll area or a [DataTable](/components/DataTable), opens in a portal. Inside a Modal, the tooltip always opens in a portal.

Set `portalTooltip` to `true` to always render the tooltip in a portal, or to `false` to keep it in place. Direction and alignment match the in-place tooltip. A portalled tooltip leaves its container in the DOM, so CSS that targets the tooltip as a descendant of the container does not match it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon
  portalTooltip
  tooltipText="Metrics are aggregated across every workspace in your organization."
  icon={Carbon}
/>
```

#### Directions

Icon tooltips support top, right, bottom, and left. With portalling, direction behaves the same as the default CSS path.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon portalTooltip direction="top" tooltipText="Top" icon={Carbon} />
<TooltipIcon
  portalTooltip
  direction="right"
  tooltipText="Right"
  icon={Carbon}
/>
<TooltipIcon
  portalTooltip
  direction="bottom"
  tooltipText="Bottom"
  icon={Carbon}
/>
<TooltipIcon portalTooltip direction="left" tooltipText="Left" icon={Carbon} />
```

#### Alignment

Portalled tooltips use the same alignment options as the default path: horizontal placement for top and bottom, vertical placement for left and right.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Carbon from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Carbon.svelte";
</script>

<TooltipIcon
  portalTooltip
  direction="bottom"
  align="start"
  tooltipText="Start"
  icon={Carbon}
/>
<TooltipIcon
  portalTooltip
  direction="bottom"
  align="center"
  tooltipText="Center"
  icon={Carbon}
/>
<TooltipIcon
  portalTooltip
  direction="bottom"
  align="end"
  tooltipText="End"
  icon={Carbon}
/>
```

### Inside a modal

When a tooltip icon is used inside a [Modal](/components/Modal), it is automatically portalled so it is not clipped by the modal overflow or z-index stacking. Set `portalTooltip` to override this behavior.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal, Portal, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Filter from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Filter.svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open modal</Button>

<Portal>
  <Modal
    bind:open
    size="sm"
    modalHeading="TooltipIcon in modal"
    primaryButtonText="Done"
    secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
    on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  >
    <TooltipIcon tooltipText="Top" direction="top" icon={Filter} />
    <TooltipIcon tooltipText="Right" direction="right" icon={Filter} />
    <TooltipIcon tooltipText="Bottom" direction="bottom" icon={Filter} />
    <TooltipIcon tooltipText="Left" direction="left" icon={Filter} />
  </Modal>
</Portal>
```

---

### Component API

#### `TooltipIcon` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the tooltip. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLButtonElement` | Obtain a reference to the button HTML element. | `null` |
| `tooltipText` | `string` | Specify the tooltip text.<br />Alternatively, use the "tooltipChildren" slot. | `""` |
| `icon` | `Icon \| undefined` | Specify the icon to render. | _undefined_ |
| `size` | `(16 \| 20 \| 24 \| 32 \| (number & {}))` | Specify the icon size.<br />Carbon icons use a 16/20/24/32 scale, but any number (pixels) can be used. | `16` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the tooltip icon | `false` |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | Set the alignment of the tooltip relative to the icon.<br />Above and below the icon, `start` and `end` name inline sides, so they<br />swap under `dir="rtl"`. | `"center"` |
| `direction` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | Set the direction of the tooltip relative to the icon. | `"bottom"` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the span element | `uniqueId()` |
| `enterDelayMs` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the duration in milliseconds to delay before displaying the tooltip.<br />Defaults to the enclosing `TooltipGroup`'s delay, or `100`. | _undefined_ |
| `leaveDelayMs` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the duration in milliseconds to delay before hiding the tooltip.<br />Defaults to the enclosing `TooltipGroup`'s delay, or `100`, so the<br />pointer can move onto the tooltip. | _undefined_ |
| `portalTooltip` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to always render the tooltip in a portal, or `false` to<br />keep it in place. Left unset, the tooltip opens in a portal inside a<br />`Modal`, or when a box around it (`overflow` other than `visible`, such<br />as a `DataTable`) would cut it off. | _undefined_ |

#### `TooltipIcon` slots

| Slot              | Detail                  |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`         | `Record<string, never>` |
| `tooltipChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `tooltipText`     | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `TooltipIcon` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:blur`       |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:focus`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `TooltipIcon` dispatched events

| Event      | Detail |
| ---------- | ------ |
| `on:close` | `null` |
| `on:open`  | `null` |

#### `TooltipIcon` $$restProps

`TooltipIcon` spreads `$$restProps` to the `button` element.


## TreeView

### Basic

Create a basic tree view using the `nodes` prop. Each node needs a unique id and display text; icons, disabled state, and nested children are optional.

By default, only one node is selected at a time. For multiple selection, see Multi-select ([Node](#node), [Shallow](#shallow), [Deep](#deep)).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let activeId = "";
  let selectedIds = [];
  const nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
    {
      id: 9,
      text: "Databases",
      nodes: [
        { id: 10, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for Elasticsearch" },
        { id: 11, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for Enterprise DB" },
        { id: 12, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB" },
        { id: 13, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for PostgreSQL" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 14,
      text: "Integration",
      disabled: true,
      nodes: [{ id: 15, text: "IBM API Connect", disabled: true }],
    },
  ];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    <TreeView
      labelText="Cloud Products"
      {nodes}
      bind:activeId
      bind:selectedIds
      on:select={({ detail }) => console.log("select", detail)}
      on:toggle={({ detail }) => console.log("toggle", detail)}
      on:focus={({ detail }) => console.log("focus", detail)}
    />
  </div>
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <div>Active node id: {activeId}</div>
    <div>Selected ids: {JSON.stringify(selectedIds)}</div>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TreeView
  hideLabel
  labelText="Cloud Products"
  nodes={[
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    { id: 1, text: "Analytics" },
    { id: 2, text: "Databases" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to provide custom label content instead of `labelText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<TreeView
  labelText=""
  nodes={[
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    { id: 1, text: "Analytics" },
    { id: 2, text: "Databases" },
  ]}
>
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Cloud Products</strong>
</TreeView>
```

### Initial state

Set the starting active and expanded nodes.

#### Active node

Set the initial active node using `activeId`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let activeId = 0;
  let selectedIds = [];
  const nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
    {
      id: 9,
      text: "Databases",
      nodes: [
```

#### Custom (slot)

Customize node rendering using the default slot with the `let:node` directive. The node object provides:

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| id | The node id. |
| text | The node text. |
| expanded | True when the node is expanded. |
| leaf | True when the node does not have child nodes. |
| disabled | True when the node is disabled. |
| selected | True when the node is selected. |
| checked | True when the node is checked (`selectionMode="checkbox"`). |
| indeterminate | True when the node is partially checked (`selectionMode="checkbox"`). |

```svelte
<script>

  const nodes = [

        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
    {
      id: 9,
      text: "Databases",
      nodes: [
        { id: 10, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for Elasticsearch" },
        { id: 11, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for Enterprise DB" },
        { id: 12, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB" },
        { id: 13, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for PostgreSQL" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 14,

<Stack gap={6}>
```

#### Checkbox

Set `selectionMode` to `"checkbox"` to render a checkbox on every node. Checking a branch checks its descendants, and a branch whose descendants are only partly checked renders indeterminate. Checkbox mode also works with [Virtualization](#virtualization).

Bind to `checkedIds` to read and set which nodes are checked. That is separate from `selectedIds`, which tracks row highlighting and is unused in checkbox mode. Bind to `indeterminateIds` to read which nodes are partially checked; it is derived from `checkedIds` and read-only, so writes are overwritten. Checkbox mode carries its own multi-selection, so [Multi-select](#multi-select) is ignored. Link nodes navigate instead of checking and render no checkbox.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let checkedIds = [3];
  let indeterminateIds = [];
  let expandedIds = [1, 2, 7];
  const nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
  ];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    <TreeView
      selectionMode="checkbox"
      labelText="Cloud Products"
      {nodes}
      bind:checkedIds
      bind:indeterminateIds
      bind:expandedIds
    />
  </div>
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <div>Checked ids: {JSON.stringify(checkedIds)}</div>
    <div>Indeterminate ids: {JSON.stringify(indeterminateIds)}</div>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

#### Inline editing

Use a `contenteditable` element in each tree view node to enable inline editing of node names. The editable region is wrapped in a container with `stopPropagation` to prevent tree node selection when editing.

```svelte
<script>
  import { RecursiveList, Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Edit from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Edit.svelte";

  let nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
    {
      id: 9,
      text: "Databases",
      nodes: [
        { id: 10, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for Elasticsearch" },
        { id: 11, text: "IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB" },
      ],
    },
  ];

  function updateNodeText(id, text) {
    const findAndUpdate = (items) => {
      for (const item of items) {
        if (item.id === id) {
          item.text = text;
          return true;
        }
        if (item.nodes && findAndUpdate(item.nodes)) {
          return true;
        }
      }
      return false;
    };
    findAndUpdate(nodes);
    nodes = nodes;
  }

  function syncContenteditable(element, text) {
    element.textContent = text;
    return {
      update(text) {
        if (document.activeElement !== element) {
          element.textContent = text;
        }
      },
    };
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    <TreeView labelText="Cloud Products" {nodes} let:node>
      <div on:click|stopPropagation on:keydown|stopPropagation role="none">
        <Stack
          orientation="horizontal"
          gap={2}
          align="center"
          tag="span"
          style="outline: none"
        >
          <span
            use:syncContenteditable={node.text}
            contenteditable={!node.disabled}
            on:input={(e) =>
              updateNodeText(node.id, e.currentTarget.textContent)}
            style:outline="none"
          ></span>
          <Edit aria-hidden="true" />
        </Stack>
      </div>
    </TreeView>
  </div>
  <RecursiveList {nodes} />
</Stack>
```

### Events

Use `on:select`, `on:toggle`, `on:check`, and `on:focus` for user-driven selection, expansion, checking, and focus. Each detail is the affected node after the gesture, with the same shape as the [Custom (slot)](#custom-slot) node. `on:check` fires only in `selectionMode="checkbox"`, when the checkbox itself is toggled; link nodes (which render no checkbox) fire `on:select` instead.

Use `on:toggle:change`, `on:select:change`, and `on:check:change` to track every expansion, selection, or check change from any source, including imperative methods and bound ids. Each detail includes the full set plus `added` and `removed` deltas (`on:check:change` also includes `indeterminateIds`). Aggregate events skip mount and no-op updates; bulk operations emit one event.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let treeview = null;
  let lastEvent = null;
  let lastToggleChange = null;
  let lastSelectChange = null;
  const nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
  ];

  function logEvent(type, detail) {
    lastEvent = {
      type,
      id: detail.id,
      text: detail.text,
      expanded: detail.expanded,
      selected: detail.selected,
    };
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    <Button on:click={() => treeview?.expandAll()}>Expand all</Button>
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => treeview?.collapseAll()}>
      Collapse all
    </Button>
  </div>
  <div>
    <TreeView
      bind:this={treeview}
      multiselect
      labelText="Cloud Products"
      {nodes}
      on:select={({ detail }) => logEvent("select", detail)}
      on:toggle={({ detail }) => logEvent("toggle", detail)}
      on:focus={({ detail }) => logEvent("focus", detail)}
      on:toggle:change={({ detail }) => (lastToggleChange = detail)}
      on:select:change={({ detail }) => (lastSelectChange = detail)}
    />
  </div>
  {#if lastEvent}
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <div>Last node event: {lastEvent.type}</div>
      <div>Node: {lastEvent.text} (id: {lastEvent.id})</div>
      <div>detail.expanded: {lastEvent.expanded}</div>
      <div>detail.selected: {lastEvent.selected}</div>
    </Stack>
  {/if}
  {#if lastToggleChange}
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <div>Last toggle:change</div>
      <div>expandedIds: {JSON.stringify(lastToggleChange.expandedIds)}</div>
      <div>added: {JSON.stringify(lastToggleChange.added)}</div>
      <div>removed: {JSON.stringify(lastToggleChange.removed)}</div>
    </Stack>
  {/if}
  {#if lastSelectChange}
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <div>Last select:change</div>
      <div>selectedIds: {JSON.stringify(lastSelectChange.selectedIds)}</div>
      <div>added: {JSON.stringify(lastSelectChange.added)}</div>
      <div>removed: {JSON.stringify(lastSelectChange.removed)}</div>
    </Stack>
  {/if}
</Stack>
```

### Keyboard

The tree is one tab stop; arrow keys move focus between visible rows, skipping disabled rows and rows under collapsed parents.

| Key | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Up</kbd> / <kbd>Down</kbd> | Moves focus to the previous or next row. Selection does not change. |
| <kbd>Right</kbd> | On a collapsed parent, expands it (fires `on:toggle`). On an expanded parent, moves focus to its first child. |
| <kbd>Left</kbd> | On an expanded parent, collapses it. Otherwise moves focus to the parent row. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Moves focus to the first or last row. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Selects the row; on a parent, also expands or collapses it. In `selectionMode="checkbox"`, checks or unchecks the row instead. On a [link node](#links), follows the link. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Selects the row without expanding or collapsing it. In checkbox mode, checks or unchecks the row. |
| Letters | Moves focus to the next row whose text starts with the typed characters. Repeating one letter cycles through rows that start with it. The typed text resets after a short pause. |

In a right-to-left layout, <kbd>Left</kbd> and <kbd>Right</kbd> swap, and a collapsed caret points left, toward where its children indent. See [LayoutDirection](/components/LayoutDirection#treeview).

With `multiselect`, these keys also change the selection. A row's unit depends on `multiselectMode`; see [Multi-select](#multi-select).

| Key | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>CMD</kbd> + <kbd>Space</kbd> | Toggles the focused row's unit, as <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + click does. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Space</kbd> | Selects the range from the anchor to the focused row, as <kbd>Shift</kbd> + click does. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Up</kbd> / <kbd>Down</kbd> | Moves focus to the previous or next row and toggles that row's unit. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>CMD</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Adds every row from the focused row to the first or last row. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>CMD</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Adds every visible, non-disabled row. |

### Multi-select

Set `multiselect` to allow more than one selected row; `multiselectMode` controls the unit each gesture applies to.

For a selection that persists parent and child state instead of highlighting rows, see [Checkbox](#checkbox).

#### Node

With the default `multiselectMode="node"`, each gesture applies to the clicked row only, not its children.

| Gesture | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Plain click | Replaces the selection with that row and sets the anchor used for the next range selection. |
| <kbd>CMD</kbd> or <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + click | Toggles that row's unit: deselect (remove the whole unit from the selection) if it is already selected, add it otherwise. Other selected rows stay selected. The anchor updates to the row you clicked. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + click | Replaces the selection with all visible rows from the anchor through the clicked row, in tree order (only rows under expanded parents count; collapsed branches are not included). If no anchor exists yet, behavior matches a plain click. Holding <kbd>Shift</kbd> together with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>CMD</kbd> still applies range selection, not per-row toggle. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Up</kbd> or <kbd>Down</kbd> | Moves focus to the previous or next row and toggles that row's unit, as <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + click does. |

For selection that includes direct children or the full subtree on each gesture, see [Shallow](#shallow) and [Deep](#deep).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let activeId = 0;
  let selectedIds = [0];
  let expandedIds = [1];
  const nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
  ];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    <TreeView
      multiselect
      multiselectMode="node"
      labelText="Cloud Products (node scope)"
      {nodes}
      bind:activeId
      bind:selectedIds
      bind:expandedIds
    />
  </div>
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <div>Active node id: {activeId}</div>
    <div>Selected ids: {JSON.stringify(selectedIds)}</div>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

#### Shallow

With `multiselectMode="shallow"`, the same modifier keys apply, but each row acts as a **unit** of one parent plus its immediate non-disabled children (deeper descendants are not included).

| Gesture | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Plain click; <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>CMD</kbd> + click | Adds or removes that whole shallow set. Toggle removes every id in that set when the clicked row was already part of the selection. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + click | Walks the visible rows between anchor and target as in [node mode](#node), then expands each of those rows to its shallow set and merges the results in order (duplicates omitted). |

```svelte
<script>
  import { Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let activeId = 0;
  let selectedIds = [0];
  let expandedIds = [1];
  const nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
  ];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    <TreeView
      multiselect
      multiselectMode="shallow"
      labelText="Cloud Products (shallow scope)"
      {nodes}
      bind:activeId
      bind:selectedIds
      bind:expandedIds
    />
  </div>
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <div>Active node id: {activeId}</div>
    <div>Selected ids: {JSON.stringify(selectedIds)}</div>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

#### Deep

With `multiselectMode="deep"`, each row's unit is that node plus **all** non-disabled descendants recursively (full subtree). Disabled nodes are skipped, and subtrees under a disabled node are not traversed.

| Gesture | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Plain click; <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>CMD</kbd> + click | Uses that deep expansion for replace and toggle, respectively. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + click | Takes the visible range between anchor and target and unions each row's deep expansion the same way as in shallow mode. |

```svelte
<script>
  import { Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let activeId = 0;
  let selectedIds = [0];
  let expandedIds = [1, 2];
  const nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
  ];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    <TreeView
      multiselect
      multiselectMode="deep"
      labelText="Cloud Products (deep scope)"
      {nodes}
      bind:activeId
      bind:selectedIds
      bind:expandedIds
    />
  </div>
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <div>Active node id: {activeId}</div>
    <div>Selected ids: {JSON.stringify(selectedIds)}</div>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Node access

Programmatically reveal or query specific nodes by id.

#### Show a node

Use `TreeView.showNode` to expand, select, and focus a specific node.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ButtonSet, Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const nodeSpark = { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" };
  const nodeBlockchain = { id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" };

  let treeview = null;
  const nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [nodeSpark, { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" }],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
  ];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <ButtonSet>
    {#each [nodeSpark, nodeBlockchain] as { id, text }}
      <Button
        on:click={() => {
          treeview?.showNode(id);
        }}
      >
        Show "{text}"
      </Button>
    {/each}
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={() => treeview?.collapseAll()}>
      Collapse all
    </Button>
  </ButtonSet>
  <div>
    <TreeView bind:this={treeview} labelText="Cloud Products" {nodes} />
  </div>
</Stack>
```

##### With options

Configure `TreeView.showNode` behavior using optional parameters. By default, all three actions occur (`expand`, `select`, `focus`), but you can disable any combination. This is useful for expanding nodes without selecting them, or selecting without expanding.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ButtonSet, Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const targetNode = { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" };
  const targetNodeSelect = { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" };

  let treeview = null;
  let key = 0;
  const nodes = [
    targetNodeSelect,
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [targetNode, { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" }],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
  ];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <ButtonSet>
    <Button
      on:click={() => {
        treeview?.showNode(targetNode.id);
      }}
    >
      Default (expand + select + focus)
    </Button>
    <Button
      on:click={() => {
        treeview?.showNode(targetNode.id, {
          select: false,
          focus: false,
        });
      }}
    >
      Expand only
    </Button>
    <Button
      on:click={() => {
        treeview?.showNode(targetNodeSelect.id, {
          expand: false,
          focus: false,
        });
      }}
    >
      Select only
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={() => key++}>Reset</Button>
  </ButtonSet>
  <div>
    {#key key}
      <TreeView bind:this={treeview} labelText="Cloud Products" {nodes} />
    {/key}
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Node lookup

Use `TreeView.getNode` to resolve a node's text or metadata from its id, useful for a breadcrumb or detail pane driven by `activeId`. Unmatched ids return `null`.

Use `TreeView.getNodes` to resolve multiple ids at once, such as `selectedIds`. Unmatched ids are omitted from the result.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let treeview = null;
  let activeId = "";
  let selectedIds = [];
  const nodes = [
    { id: 0, text: "AI / Machine learning" },
    {
      id: 1,
      text: "Analytics",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 2,
          text: "IBM Analytics Engine",
          nodes: [
            { id: 3, text: "Apache Spark" },
            { id: 4, text: "Hadoop" },
          ],
        },
        { id: 5, text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
        { id: 6, text: "IBM Db2 Warehouse on Cloud" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 7,
      text: "Blockchain",
      nodes: [{ id: 8, text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" }],
    },
  ];

  $: activeNode = treeview?.getNode(activeId) ?? null;
  $: selectedNodes = treeview?.getNodes(selectedIds) ?? [];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    <TreeView
      bind:this={treeview}
      multiselect
      labelText="Cloud Products"
      {nodes}
      bind:activeId
      bind:selectedIds
    />
  </div>
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <div>Active node: {activeNode ? activeNode.text : "(none)"}</div>
    <div>
      Selected nodes:
      {selectedNodes.map((node) => node.text).join(", ") || "(none)"}
    </div>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Performance

Scale to large trees by loading, rendering, and measuring only what's needed.

#### Lazy loading

Set `hasChildren` on a node to render it as an expandable branch before its `nodes` are known. Expanding it fires `toggle` as usual; the handler can fetch and assign `nodes` asynchronously.

While `hasChildren` is `true` and `nodes` is empty, the `childNodes` slot renders in place of the (empty) subtree, receiving the same `node` as the default slot. TreeView has no built-in concept of "loading" or "error" -- the slot is generic, so you decide what to render (a spinner, an error message with retry, or nothing) based on whatever fields you put on the node yourself.

With `selectionMode="checkbox"`, a saved id in `checkedIds` can name a node that has not loaded yet. It stays in `checkedIds` while any `hasChildren` node is unloaded, and its row shows as checked once the node arrives. An id that matches no node after every parent has loaded is dropped.

With the default `checkMode="deep"`, unchecking a node that has not loaded, or one of its ancestors, also unchecks the saved ids under it. They leave `checkedIds` as soon as no other unloaded node could hold them, and at the latest when the node's children load.

```svelte
<script>
  import { InlineLoading, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let nodes = [
    { id: "ai", text: "AI / Machine learning", hasChildren: true },
    { id: "analytics", text: "Analytics", hasChildren: true },
    { id: "blockchain", text: "Blockchain", hasChildren: true },
  ];

  const childrenByParentId = {
    ai: [
      { id: "watson-studio", text: "Watson Studio" },
      { id: "watson-assistant", text: "Watson Assistant" },
    ],
    analytics: [
      { id: "analytics-engine", text: "IBM Analytics Engine" },
      { id: "cloud-sql-query", text: "IBM Cloud SQL Query" },
    ],
    blockchain: [
      { id: "blockchain-platform", text: "IBM Blockchain Platform" },
    ],
  };

  function fetchChildren(id) {
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      setTimeout(() => resolve(childrenByParentId[id] ?? []), 1000);
    });
  }

  async function handleToggle(event) {
    const node = event.detail;

    // Only fetch once: a node with `hasChildren` but no `nodes` yet.
    if (!node.hasChildren || node.nodes) return;

    const children = await fetchChildren(node.id);

    nodes = nodes.map((n) =>
      n.id === node.id ? { ...n, nodes: children } : n,
    );
  }
</script>

<TreeView
  labelText="Cloud Products (lazy-loaded)"
  {nodes}
  on:toggle={handleToggle}
  let:node
>
  {node.text}
  <svelte:fragment slot="childNodes" let:node>
    <InlineLoading status="active" description="Loading {node.text}..." />
  </svelte:fragment>
</TreeView>
```

#### Virtualization

Virtualization renders only the rows currently visible in the scroll viewport, improving performance for large trees (for example, file trees and log explorers). Set `virtualize` to enable it. The tree still tracks the full `nodes` dataset; only the on-screen slice is mounted in the DOM.

Row height is fixed and comes from `size` (32px default, 24px compact). Rows do not grow to fit their content, so keep slot content to a single line. Pass `true` for defaults, or an object to customize:

| Field | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `containerHeight` | `maxVisibleRows * itemHeight` | Scroll viewport height. Pass a number (pixels) or a CSS string (`"80%"`, `"100%"`, `"calc(...)"`) when the parent sets height. |
| `maxVisibleRows` | `10` | Rows visible at once when `containerHeight` is not set. |
| `overscan` | `3` | Extra rows rendered above and below the viewport during scroll. |

`expandAll` and `expandedIds` only need expandable nodes (those with loaded `nodes` or `hasChildren: true`). Leaf ids in `expandedIds` are ignored for expansion.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    filterTreeByText,
    Search,
    Stack,
    Toggle,
    TreeView,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Code from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Code.svelte";
  import Document from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Document.svelte";
  import DocumentBlank from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/DocumentBlank.svelte";
  import Folder from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Folder.svelte";
  import Html from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Html.svelte";
  import Image from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Image.svelte";
  import Json from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Json.svelte";
  import { onMount, tick } from "svelte";

  function iconFor(name) {
    const ext = name.slice(name.lastIndexOf(".") + 1).toLowerCase();
    if (ext === "ts" || ext === "tsx" || ext === "js" || ext === "jsx") {
      return Code;
    }
    if (ext === "json") return Json;
    if (ext === "html") return Html;
    if (ext === "png" || ext === "jpg" || ext === "svg" || ext === "gif") {
      return Image;
    }
    if (ext === "md" || ext === "txt") return Document;
    return DocumentBlank;
  }

  const fileNames = [
    "index.ts",
    "utils.ts",
    "config.json",
    "package.json",
    "styles.scss",
    "theme.css",
    "logo.svg",
    "hero.png",
    "README.md",
    "CHANGELOG.md",
    "App.tsx",
    "Header.tsx",
    "index.html",
    "404.html",
    "robots.txt",
  ];

  const rootNames = [
    "src",
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    "scripts",
    "node_modules",
    "dist",
    "build",
    "public",
    "static",
    "assets",
    "fixtures",
    "e2e",
    "lib",
    "packages",
    "apps",
    "types",
    "config",
    "tools",
    "plugins",
    "themes",
    "locales",
    "components",
    "hooks",
    "utils",
    "services",
    "pages",
    "layouts",
    "store",
    "api",
    "db",
    "migrations",
    "seeds",
    "internal",
    "integrations",
    "cli",
    "server",
    "client",
    "vendor",
    "workers",
  ];

  let nextId = 0;
  const id = () => nextId++;

  /** A leaf at the deepest level, used as a `showNode` target. */
  let deepFile = null;

  function makeFolder(name, depth, fanout) {
    const node = { id: id(), text: name, icon: Folder, nodes: [] };
    for (let i = 0; i < fanout.files; i++) {
      const fname = fileNames[(i + depth) % fileNames.length];
      const file = { id: id(), text: fname, icon: iconFor(fname) };
      node.nodes.push(file);
      if (depth === fanout.maxDepth) {
        deepFile = { id: file.id, path: `${name}/${fname}` };
      }
    }
    if (depth < fanout.maxDepth) {
      for (let i = 0; i < fanout.folders; i++) {
        node.nodes.push(
          makeFolder(`${name}/subfolder-${i}`, depth + 1, fanout),
        );
      }
    }
    return node;
  }

  function countNodes(list) {
    let n = 0;
    for (const node of list) {
      n++;
      if (node.nodes) n += countNodes(node.nodes);
    }
    return n;
  }

  /** Expandable ids only -- leaves are no-ops for TreeView expansion. */
  function expandableIds(list) {
    const ids = [];
    for (const node of list) {
      const hasLoadedChildren =
        Array.isArray(node.nodes) && node.nodes.length > 0;
      if (hasLoadedChildren || node.hasChildren === true) {
        ids.push(node.id);
      }
      if (hasLoadedChildren) ids.push(...expandableIds(node.nodes));
    }
    return ids;
  }

  // Defer ~100k+ node allocation so the framed preview shell can paint first
  // (avoids Vite/Svelte DEV OOMing on module eval).
  let nodes = [];
  let totalNodes = 0;
  let ready = false;

  onMount(() => {
    nodes = rootNames.map((name) =>
      makeFolder(name, 0, { files: 8, folders: 4, maxDepth: 4 }),
    );
    totalNodes = countNodes(nodes);
    ready = true;
    return () => observer?.disconnect();
  });

  let treeview = null;
  let searchValue = "";
  let compact = false;
  let dynamicHeight = false;

  $: size = compact ? "compact" : "default";

  $: filteredNodes =
    searchValue.trim() === "" ? nodes : filterTreeByText(nodes, searchValue);

  let expandedIds = [];

  // A new filter resets the view: expand every match and jump back to the top.
  // Gate on the text actually changing. Reactive statements also run on
  // unrelated passes, and resetting unconditionally would fight anything else
  // that scrolls or expands -- `showNode`, or the user's own caret clicks.
  let lastSearchValue = searchValue;
  $: if (searchValue !== lastSearchValue) {
    lastSearchValue = searchValue;
    expandedIds = searchValue.trim() === "" ? [] : expandableIds(filteredNodes);
    tick().then(() => scrollContainerRef?.scrollTo({ top: 0 }));
  }

  let scrollContainerRef = null;
  let domRowCount = 0;
  let observer = null;

  function attachObserver(el) {
    observer?.disconnect();
    observer = null;
    if (!el) {
      domRowCount = 0;
      return;
    }
    const recount = () => {
      domRowCount = el.querySelectorAll('[role="treeitem"]').length;
    };
    observer = new MutationObserver(recount);
    observer.observe(el, { childList: true });
    recount();
  }

  $: attachObserver(scrollContainerRef);
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <ButtonSet>
    <Button
      kind="tertiary"
      size="small"
      disabled={!ready}
      on:click={() => treeview?.expandAll()}
    >
      Expand all
    </Button>
    <Button
      kind="tertiary"
      size="small"
      disabled={!ready}
      on:click={() => {
        treeview?.collapseAll();
        expandedIds = [];
      }}
    >
      Collapse all
    </Button>
    <Button
      kind="tertiary"
      size="small"
      disabled={!ready || searchValue.trim() !== ""}
      on:click={() => treeview?.showNode(deepFile.id)}
    >
      Jump to a deep file
    </Button>
  </ButtonSet>

  <Search
    size="sm"
    placeholder="Filter by file or folder name"
    bind:value={searchValue}
    disabled={!ready}
  />

  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Toggle
      size="sm"
      labelText="Compact size"
      labelA="Default (32px rows)"
      labelB="Compact (24px rows)"
      bind:toggled={compact}
    />
    <Toggle
      size="sm"
      labelText="Container height"
      labelA="Fixed (480px)"
      labelB="Dynamic (60vh, resize window)"
      bind:toggled={dynamicHeight}
    />
  </Stack>

  {#if !ready}
    <p>Building demo tree...</p>
  {:else}
    <p>
      Total nodes: <strong>{totalNodes.toLocaleString()}</strong>
      {#if searchValue.trim() !== ""}
        &middot; matching filter:
        <strong>{countNodes(filteredNodes).toLocaleString()}</strong>
      {/if}
      &middot; rendered in DOM: <strong>{domRowCount.toLocaleString()}</strong>
    </p>

    {#if filteredNodes.length > 0}
      {#if dynamicHeight}
        <!-- A constrained parent gives `containerHeight: "100%"` something to
             resolve against. Resize the browser to watch the DOM count change. -->
        <Box height="60vh" minHeight="240px">
          <TreeView
            bind:this={treeview}
            bind:scrollContainerRef
            labelText="Project files"
            nodes={filteredNodes}
            bind:expandedIds
            {size}
            virtualize={{ containerHeight: "100%" }}
            let:node
          >
            {node.text}
          </TreeView>
        </Box>
      {:else}
        <TreeView
          bind:this={treeview}
          bind:scrollContainerRef
          labelText="Project files"
          nodes={filteredNodes}
          bind:expandedIds
          {size}
          virtualize={{ containerHeight: 480 }}
          let:node
        >
          {node.text}
        </TreeView>
      {/if}
    {:else}
      <p>No files match "{searchValue}".</p>
    {/if}
  {/if}
</Stack>
```

##### With lazy loading

Combine `virtualize` with `hasChildren` to fetch children on expand. This example starts with the same project-folder roots as [Virtualization](#virtualization), but each subtree loads on demand (including nested folders). The virtualized path does not render the `childNodes` slot, so the demo inserts a temporary disabled "Loading..." child while the request is in flight, then replaces it with the fetched nodes.

```svelte
<script>
  import { TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Code from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Code.svelte";
  import Document from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Document.svelte";
  import DocumentBlank from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/DocumentBlank.svelte";
  import Folder from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Folder.svelte";
  import Html from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Html.svelte";
  import Image from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Image.svelte";
  import Json from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Json.svelte";

  function iconFor(name) {
    const ext = name.slice(name.lastIndexOf(".") + 1).toLowerCase();
    if (ext === "ts" || ext === "tsx" || ext === "js" || ext === "jsx") {
      return Code;
    }
    if (ext === "json") return Json;
    if (ext === "html") return Html;
    if (ext === "png" || ext === "jpg" || ext === "svg" || ext === "gif") {
      return Image;
    }
    if (ext === "md" || ext === "txt") return Document;
    return DocumentBlank;
  }

  const fileNames = [
    "index.ts",
    "utils.ts",
    "config.json",
    "package.json",
    "styles.scss",
    "theme.css",
    "logo.svg",
    "hero.png",
    "README.md",
    "CHANGELOG.md",
    "App.tsx",
    "Header.tsx",
    "index.html",
    "404.html",
    "robots.txt",
  ];

  const rootNames = [
    "src",
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    "scripts",
    "node_modules",
    "dist",
    "build",
    "public",
    "static",
    "assets",
    "fixtures",
    "e2e",
    "lib",
    "packages",
    "apps",
    "types",
    "config",
    "tools",
    "plugins",
    "themes",
    "locales",
    "components",
    "hooks",
    "utils",
    "services",
    "pages",
    "layouts",
    "store",
    "api",
    "db",
    "migrations",
    "seeds",
    "internal",
    "integrations",
    "cli",
    "server",
    "client",
    "vendor",
    "workers",
  ];

  const MAX_DEPTH = 4;
  const FETCH_MS = 500;
  const fanout = { files: 8, folders: 4 };

  let nextId = 0;
  const id = () => nextId++;

  // Roots are unloaded folders; children are fetched on expand.
  let nodes = rootNames.map((name) => ({
    id: id(),
    text: name,
    icon: Folder,
    depth: 0,
    path: name,
    hasChildren: true,
  }));

  function updateNode(list, nodeId, updater) {
    return list.map((node) => {
      if (node.id === nodeId) return updater(node);
      if (node.nodes) {
        return { ...node, nodes: updateNode(node.nodes, nodeId, updater) };
      }
      return node;
    });
  }

  function makeChildren(parentPath, depth) {
    const children = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < fanout.files; i++) {
      const fname = fileNames[(i + depth) % fileNames.length];
      children.push({
        id: id(),
        text: fname,
        icon: iconFor(fname),
        depth: depth + 1,
        path: `${parentPath}/${fname}`,
      });
    }
    if (depth < MAX_DEPTH) {
      for (let i = 0; i < fanout.folders; i++) {
        const name = `subfolder-${i}`;
        children.push({
          id: id(),
          text: name,
          icon: Folder,
          depth: depth + 1,
          path: `${parentPath}/${name}`,
          hasChildren: true,
        });
      }
    }
    return children;
  }

  async function fetchChildren(parentPath, depth) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, FETCH_MS));
    return makeChildren(parentPath, depth);
  }

  async function handleToggle(event) {
    const node = event.detail;

    // Only fetch once: expandable and not yet loaded (placeholder or real).
    if (!node.hasChildren || node.nodes) return;

    // Virtualized trees do not render the `childNodes` slot. Put a temporary
    // disabled row under the parent so the expand still shows progress.
    nodes = updateNode(nodes, node.id, (n) => ({
      ...n,
      nodes: [
        {
          id: `${n.id}__loading`,
          text: "Loading...",
          disabled: true,
        },
      ],
    }));

    const children = await fetchChildren(
      node.path ?? node.text,
      node.depth ?? 0,
    );
    nodes = updateNode(nodes, node.id, (n) => ({
      ...n,
      nodes: children,
    }));
  }
</script>

<TreeView
  labelText="Project files"
  {nodes}
  virtualize={{ containerHeight: 480 }}
  on:toggle={handleToggle}
  let:node
>
  {node.text}
</TreeView>
```

#### Large and deep trees

The tree view is optimized to handle large datasets efficiently, as shown here with a large tree (1000+ nodes) and a deeply nested tree (100 levels deep).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    ContentSwitcher,
    Stack,
    Switch,
    TreeView,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import { onMount, tick } from "svelte";

  let treeview = null;
  let performanceInfo = {
    generate: 0,
    expandAll: 0,
    collapseAll: 0,
    showNode: 0,
  };

  function generateLargeTree() {
    const nodes = [];
    let idCounter = 0;

    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
      const categoryNodes = [];

      for (let j = 0; j < 10; j++) {
        const subcategoryNodes = [];

        for (let k = 0; k < 10; k++) {
          subcategoryNodes.push({
            id: idCounter++,
            text: `Employee ${i + 1}-${j + 1}-${k + 1}`,
          });
        }

        categoryNodes.push({
          id: idCounter++,
          text: `Team ${i + 1}-${j + 1}`,
          nodes: subcategoryNodes,
        });
      }

      nodes.push({
        id: idCounter++,
        text: `Business Unit ${i + 1}`,
        nodes: categoryNodes,
      });
    }

    return { nodes, count: idCounter };
  }

  function generateDeepTree() {
    let idCounter = 0;
    let lastId = 0;

    function createNestedNode(depth, maxDepth) {
      const node = {
        id: idCounter++,
        text: `Approval Step ${depth + 1}`,
      };
      lastId = node.id;

      if (depth < maxDepth) {
        node.nodes = [createNestedNode(depth + 1, maxDepth)];
      }

      return node;
    }

    const rootNode = createNestedNode(0, 100);
    return { nodes: [rootNode], count: idCounter, lastId };
  }

  const genStart = performance.now();
  const initialTree = generateLargeTree();
  let nodes = initialTree.nodes;
  let nodeCount = initialTree.count;
  let treeType = "large";
  let lastDeepNodeId = null;
  let selectedIndex = 0;

  $: hasTiming =
    performanceInfo.generate > 0 ||
    performanceInfo.expandAll > 0 ||
    performanceInfo.collapseAll > 0 ||
    performanceInfo.showNode > 0;

  onMount(async () => {
    await tick();
    const end = performance.now();
    performanceInfo.generate = end - genStart;
    performanceInfo = performanceInfo;
  });

  async function handleTreeSwitch(event) {
    const index = event.detail;
    selectedIndex = index;

    performanceInfo = {
      generate: 0,
      expandAll: 0,
      collapseAll: 0,
      showNode: 0,
    };

    const start = performance.now();
    if (index === 0) {
      const result = generateLargeTree();
      nodes = result.nodes;
      nodeCount = result.count;
      treeType = "large";
      lastDeepNodeId = null;
    } else {
      const result = generateDeepTree();
      nodes = result.nodes;
      nodeCount = result.count;
      lastDeepNodeId = result.lastId;
      treeType = "deep";
    }

    await tick();
    const end = performance.now();
    performanceInfo.generate = end - start;
    performanceInfo = performanceInfo;
  }

  function handleExpandAll() {
    const start = performance.now();
    treeview?.expandAll();
    const end = performance.now();
    performanceInfo.expandAll = end - start;
    performanceInfo = performanceInfo;
  }

  function handleCollapseAll() {
    const start = performance.now();
    treeview?.collapseAll();
    const end = performance.now();
    performanceInfo.collapseAll = end - start;
    performanceInfo = performanceInfo;
  }

  function handleShowNode() {
    const start = performance.now();
    const targetId =
      treeType === "large"
        ? 999
        : lastDeepNodeId === null
          ? 100
          : lastDeepNodeId;
    if (treeview) {
      treeview.showNode(targetId);
    }
    const end = performance.now();
    performanceInfo.showNode = end - start;
    performanceInfo = performanceInfo;
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <ContentSwitcher {selectedIndex} on:change={handleTreeSwitch}>
    <Switch text="Large Tree (1000+ nodes)" />
    <Switch text="Deep Tree (100 levels)" />
  </ContentSwitcher>

  <ButtonSet>
    <Button on:click={handleExpandAll}>Expand All</Button>
    <Button on:click={handleCollapseAll}>Collapse All</Button>
    <Button on:click={handleShowNode}>Show Deep Node</Button>
  </ButtonSet>

  {#if hasTiming}
    <Stack gap={2}>
      {#if performanceInfo.generate > 0}
        <div>
          Tree Generation: {performanceInfo.generate.toFixed(4)}ms ({nodeCount.toLocaleString()}
          nodes)
        </div>
      {/if}
      {#if performanceInfo.expandAll > 0}
        <div>Expand All: {performanceInfo.expandAll.toFixed(4)}ms</div>
      {/if}
      {#if performanceInfo.collapseAll > 0}
        <div>Collapse All: {performanceInfo.collapseAll.toFixed(4)}ms</div>
      {/if}
      {#if performanceInfo.showNode > 0}
        <div>Show Node: {performanceInfo.showNode.toFixed(4)}ms</div>
      {/if}
    </Stack>
  {/if}
  <div>
    <TreeView
      bind:this={treeview}
      labelText={treeType === "large"
        ? "Large Tree (1000+ nodes)"
        : "Deep Tree (100 levels)"}
      {nodes}
    />
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Unchanged reassignment

Reassigning `nodes` to the _same_ array reference (the lazy-loading idiom's `node.nodes = children; nodes = nodes`, or any wrapper component or `$:` block that re-runs and hands back the same array) skips the update when nothing was actually mutated. Mutating a node before reassigning still triggers one, so the tree stays correct.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, ButtonSet, Stack, TreeView } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import { tick } from "svelte";

  function generateNodes(count) {
    const nodes = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      nodes.push({ id: i, text: `Node ${i + 1}` });
    }
    return nodes;
  }

  let nodes = generateNodes(5000);
  let lastLabel = "";
  let lastDuration = null;

  async function reassignUnchanged() {
    const start = performance.now();
    nodes = nodes; // same reference, nothing mutated
    await tick();
    lastLabel = "Reassign, nothing changed";
    lastDuration = performance.now() - start;
  }

  async function mutateThenReassign() {
    const first = nodes[0];
    first.text = first.text.endsWith("*")
      ? first.text.slice(0, -1)
      : `${first.text}*`;

    const start = performance.now();
    nodes = nodes; // same reference, but a node was mutated in place
    await tick();
    lastLabel = "Mutate a node, then reassign";
    lastDuration = performance.now() - start;
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <ButtonSet>
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={reassignUnchanged}>
      Reassign nodes (no change)
    </Button>
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={mutateThenReassign}>
      Mutate a node, then reassign
    </Button>
  </ButtonSet>
  {#if lastDuration !== null}
    <div>
      {lastLabel}: {lastDuration.toFixed(2)}ms ({nodes.length.toLocaleString()}
      nodes)
    </div>
  {/if}
  <div>
    <TreeView labelText="{nodes.length.toLocaleString()} nodes" {nodes} />
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Filtering

Filter nodes with the built-in helpers.

##### By text

Combine a search input with `filterTreeByText` to create an interactive searchable tree. Type to filter nodes by name (case-insensitive substring matching). By default, matching nodes and their ancestors are included to maintain valid tree structure.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    filterTreeByText,
    Search,
    Stack,
    TreeView,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const allNodes = [
    {

      nodes: [
        {
          id: "1-1",
          text: "Runbooks",
          nodes: [
            { id: "1-1-1", text: "Incident Response.md" },
            { id: "1-1-2", text: "Deployment Playbook.md" },
            { id: "1-1-3", text: "On-Call Rotation.md" },
            { id: "1-1-4", text: "Postmortem Template.md" },
          ],
        },
        {
          id: "1-2",
          text: "Architecture",
          nodes: [
            { id: "1-2-1", text: "System Design.pdf" },
            { id: "1-2-2", text: "API Contracts.pdf" },
            { id: "1-2-3", text: "Data Model.pdf" },
          ],
        },
        {
          id: "1-3",
          text: "Projects",
          nodes: [
            {
              id: "1-3-1",
              text: "Website",
              nodes: [
                { id: "1-3-1-1", text: "index.html" },
                { id: "1-3-1-2", text: "styles.css" },
                { id: "1-3-1-3", text: "script.js" },

            },

              id: "1-3-2",
              text: "App",
              nodes: [
                { id: "1-3-2-1", text: "main.py" },

              ],
            },
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "2",
      text: "Finance",
      nodes: [
        { id: "2-1", text: "Q1-Invoice.pdf" },
        { id: "2-2", text: "Q2-Invoice.pdf" },
        { id: "2-3", text: "Q3-Invoice.pdf" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "3",
      text: "Support",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: "3-1",
          text: "Tier 1",
          nodes: [
            { id: "3-1-1", text: "Ticket-1042.md" },
            { id: "3-1-2", text: "Ticket-1043.md" },
          ],
        },
        {
          id: "3-2",
          text: "Tier 2",
          nodes: [
            { id: "3-2-1", text: "Ticket-2091.md" },
            { id: "3-2-2", text: "Ticket-2092.md" },
          ],
```
