### Icons

Set `icon` on each avatar to render a custom icon, such as one from [carbon-icons-svelte](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-icons-svelte), instead of a photo or initials.

```svelte
<script>
  import { UserAvatar, UserAvatarGroup } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Bot from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Bot.svelte";
  import Group from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Group.svelte";
  import Password from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Password.svelte";
</script>

<UserAvatarGroup>
  <UserAvatar icon={Bot} backgroundColor="purple" tooltipText="Bot" />
  <UserAvatar icon={Password} backgroundColor="teal" tooltipText="Password" />
  <UserAvatar icon={Group} backgroundColor="cool-gray" tooltipText="Group" />
</UserAvatarGroup>
```

### Background colors

Every example on this page sets `backgroundColor="auto"` on each `UserAvatar`, which hashes a stable color from `name` (or `initials`) -- the same name always gets the same color. See [UserAvatar's background colors section](/components/UserAvatar#background-colors) for the full palette and the other `backgroundColor` values.

#### Exported `getAvatarBackgroundColor` utility

Import `getAvatarBackgroundColor` to compute the same color outside a `UserAvatar`, for example to match a name's avatar color in a legend or a custom rendering.

```html
<script context="module">
  import { getAvatarBackgroundColor } from "carbon-components-svelte/src/utils/avatar-color.js";

  getAvatarBackgroundColor("Richard Hendricks"); // "teal"
</script>
```

### Tooltips

Set `tooltipText` on each avatar to show its name on hover or focus, the same as a standalone [UserAvatar](/components/UserAvatar#tooltip). Within a group, only one avatar's tooltip stays open at a time -- hovering a new avatar closes the previous one immediately, whether it's a slotted avatar or the "+N" overflow chip.

Moving the pointer directly from one avatar to a neighbor whose tooltip is already open skips the usual enter delay, so the tooltip swaps in immediately instead of waiting again. Hover across the avatars in the examples above to feel this.

---

### Component API

#### `UserAvatarGroup` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max` | `number` | Specify the maximum number of avatars to show before collapsing the rest<br />into a "+N" overflow avatar. Set to `0` to show every avatar. | `5` |
| `total` | `number \| undefined` | Specify the total number of people represented. Defaults to the number of<br />slotted avatars. Set this when you render only a subset (large groups) so<br />the overflow count stays right without mounting every avatar. | _undefined_ |
| `gap` | `import("../Stack/Stack.svelte").StackScale \| string \| undefined` | Specify the spacing between avatars. Leave unset for the default<br />overlapping (stacked) layout. A positive value spaces the avatars apart,<br />accepting a Carbon layout scale (`0`-`13`) or a CSS length string. A<br />negative length string (for example `"-1rem"`) overlaps them by that<br />amount. | _undefined_ |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | Specify the size of the avatars. Applies to slotted avatars without their<br />own `size`, and to the "+N" overflow chip. | `"md"` |
| `stackOrder` | `"last" \| "first"` | Specify which end of the stack renders on top when avatars overlap.<br />`"last"` matches the default browser paint order (and most avatar<br />stacks). `"first"` keeps the first avatar most prominent instead. | `"last"` |
| `overflowTooltipText` | `string \| undefined` | Specify the tooltip text for the "+N" overflow avatar. Defaults to a<br />comma-separated list of hidden slotted `name` values. Set this when using<br />`total` for people who are not mounted. | _undefined_ |

#### `UserAvatarGroup` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `UserAvatarGroup` $$restProps

`UserAvatarGroup` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## VirtualList

### Basic

`VirtualList` renders each item through its default slot with `let:item` and `let:index`, but only mounts the items inside the scroll viewport plus `overscan` extra on each side. While scrolling, it also mounts items ahead of the viewport, as far as the last scroll moved and up to one `containerHeight`, so a fast scroll does not show blank space. `index` is the item's position in the full `items` array, not in the rendered window.

Set `containerHeight` for the viewport and `itemHeight` for each row, both in pixels. Every row must render at exactly `itemHeight` for the scroll position to line up.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, VirtualList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<VirtualList
  items={instances}
  itemHeight={40}
  containerHeight={240}
  let:item
  let:index
>
  <Box
    display="flex"
    align="center"
    justify="space-between"
    height="40px"
    paddingX={5}
    border="subtle"
    borderSide="bottom"
  >
    <span>{index + 1}. {item.name}</span>
    <span>{item.region}</span>
  </Box>
</VirtualList>
```

### Fast scrolling

During a scroll faster than the list can render, such as a quick drag of the scrollbar, the rows can briefly disappear. Set `optimizeFastScroll` to keep the rows already rendered in view until the new ones arrive.

The rows then follow the scroll a frame behind, and pause while the page is busy running scripts. Leave it off when the list sits on a page that often does heavy work. `optimizeFastScroll` has no effect with [`scrollElement`](#scroll-container).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, VirtualList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<VirtualList
  optimizeFastScroll
  items={instances}
  itemHeight={40}
  containerHeight={240}
  let:item
  let:index
>
  <Box
    display="flex"
    align="center"
    justify="space-between"
    height="40px"
    paddingX={5}
    border="subtle"
    borderSide="bottom"
  >
    <span>{index + 1}. {item.name}</span>
    <span>{item.region}</span>
  </Box>
</VirtualList>
```

### Item height

#### Measured

Set `measured` to `true` when rows vary in height, such as wrapping text. Each rendered row is measured with `ResizeObserver` and `itemHeight` becomes the estimate for rows not yet measured.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, VirtualList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<VirtualList
  items={comments}
  itemHeight={72}
  containerHeight={320}
  measured
  let:item
>
  <Box
    display="flex"
    direction="column"
    gap={2}
    paddingX={5}
    paddingY={4}
    border="subtle"
    borderSide="bottom"
  >
    <strong>{item.author}</strong>
    <p>{item.message}</p>
  </Box>
</VirtualList>
```

| Do | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Set `itemHeight` close to the typical row height | The scrollbar is sized from estimates until rows are measured; a close guess keeps it from jumping. |
| Pass `getKey` when items are reordered or removed | Rows are keyed by position by default, which is only stable when items are appended. Measured heights are always stored by position. |

### Windowing threshold

Every list is windowed by default. Set `threshold` to render lists shorter than it in full, which keeps every row in the DOM for find-in-page.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, VirtualList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<VirtualList
  items={instances.slice(0, 20)}
  itemHeight={40}
  containerHeight={240}
  threshold={100}
  let:item
>
  <Box
    display="flex"
    align="center"
    justify="space-between"
    height="40px"
    paddingX={5}
    border="subtle"
    borderSide="bottom"
  >
    <span>{item.name}</span>
    <span>{item.region}</span>
  </Box>
</VirtualList>
```

### Load more

`scrollend` fires once when the list is scrolled near the bottom, with `{ scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight }` as its detail. Append the next page of `items` in the handler; the event re-arms when `items` grows. It is a load-more signal, not the browser's native `scrollend`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    InlineLoading,
    Stack,
    Text,
    VirtualList,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const PAGE_SIZE = 20;
  const TOTAL = 60;

  let items = [];
  let loading = false;
  let hasMore = true;

  const actors = ["aisha.khan", "mateo.garcia", "priya.patel", "chen.wei"];
  const actions = [
    "signed in",
    "rotated an API key",
    "updated the IAM policy",
    "deployed checkout-api",
    "exported the billing report",
    "invited a new user",
  ];

  function makePage(offset) {
    return Array.from({ length: PAGE_SIZE }, (_, i) => {
      const n = offset + i;
      return {
        id: n,
        label: `${actors[n % actors.length]} ${actions[n % actions.length]}`,
      };
    });
  }

  async function loadMore() {
    if (loading || !hasMore) return;
    loading = true;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 400));
    items = [...items, ...makePage(items.length)];
    hasMore = items.length < TOTAL;
    loading = false;
  }

  loadMore();
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <VirtualList
    {items}
    itemHeight={40}
    containerHeight={240}
    getKey={(item) => item.id}
    on:scrollend={loadMore}
    let:item
  >
    <Box
      display="flex"
      align="center"
      height="40px"
      paddingX={5}
      border="subtle"
      borderSide="bottom"
    >
      {item.label}
    </Box>
  </VirtualList>
  <Box display="flex" align="center" minHeight={7}>
    {#if loading}
      <InlineLoading description="Loading more..." />
    {:else if !hasMore}
      <Text type="body-compact-01" color="secondary">
        Loaded all {TOTAL} audit events.
      </Text>
    {:else}
      <Text type="body-compact-01" color="secondary">
        {items.length}
        of {TOTAL} audit events loaded. Scroll to the bottom to fetch more.
      </Text>
    {/if}
  </Box>
</Stack>
```

### Scroll container

#### With ScrollGradient

Set `scrollElement` to scroll the list from an ancestor instead of its own container. Bind a [ScrollGradient](/components/ScrollGradient)'s `scrollElementRef` and pass it in so the gradients track the list. Keep `containerHeight` equal to the `ScrollGradient` height.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Box, ScrollGradient, VirtualList } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 5000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `invoice-2026-${String(i + 1).padStart(5, "0")}.pdf`,
    size: `${100 + ((i * 37) % 900)} KB`,
  }));

  let scrollElementRef = null;
</script>

<ScrollGradient height="240px" bind:scrollElementRef>
  <VirtualList
    {items}
    itemHeight={40}
    containerHeight={240}
    scrollElement={scrollElementRef}
    let:item
  >
    <Box
      display="flex"
      align="center"
      justify="space-between"
      height="40px"
      paddingX={5}
      border="subtle"
      borderSide="bottom"
    >
      <span>{item.name}</span>
      <span>{item.size}</span>
    </Box>
  </VirtualList>
</ScrollGradient>
```

### In a list

Set `spacerTag` to `"li"` to render items straight into a list. The list keeps only `li` children: an empty `li` above and below the items holds the scroll height. Each item must render exactly one element, and each `li` gets `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` so screen readers announce its place in the full list.

The list has no scroll container of its own. Wrap the list in a [ScrollGradient](/components/ScrollGradient), pass its `scrollElementRef` as `scrollElement`, and set `containerHeight` to its height. The gradients show that more items lie past each edge.

#### With ContainedList

Render each item as a `ContainedListItem` inside a [ContainedList](/components/ContainedList). Each item overlaps the one above by 1px, so set `itemHeight` to the item height less 1px: 47 for the default size. Set `measured` too, since items wrap onto more lines on narrow screens. Measured heights include the overlap. The list header stays pinned to the top, so set `hideStartGradient` to keep the top gradient off it. Set `background` and `color` to `"background"` to match the header.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    ContainedList,
    ContainedListItem,
    ScrollGradient,
    VirtualList,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const regions = ["us-south", "us-east", "eu-de", "eu-gb", "jp-tok", "au-syd"];

  const instances = Array.from({ length: 5000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `web-prod-${String(i + 1).padStart(4, "0")}`,
    region: regions[i % regions.length],
  }));

  let scrollElementRef = null;
</script>

<ScrollGradient
  height="240px"
  background="background"
  color="background"
  hideStartGradient
  bind:scrollElementRef
>
  <ContainedList labelText="Instances">
    <VirtualList
      items={instances}
      itemHeight={47}
      containerHeight={240}
      scrollElement={scrollElementRef}
      spacerTag="li"
      measured
      getKey={(item) => item.id}
      let:item
    >
      <ContainedListItem>{item.name} ({item.region})</ContainedListItem>
    </VirtualList>
  </ContainedList>
</ScrollGradient>
```

#### With UnorderedList

Render each item as a `ListItem` inside an [UnorderedList](/components/UnorderedList). Pad the list on the left so the scroll container does not clip the bullets. Set `measured`, since items wrap onto more lines on narrow screens.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    ListItem,
    ScrollGradient,
    UnorderedList,
    VirtualList,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const services = ["checkout-api", "billing-worker", "search-indexer"];
  const findings = [
    "uses a key older than 90 days",
    "grants write access it never uses",
    "has no owner on call",
    "logs request bodies",
  ];

  const items = Array.from({ length: 3000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    label: `${services[i % services.length]} ${findings[i % findings.length]}`,
  }));

  let scrollElementRef = null;
</script>

<ScrollGradient height="240px" bind:scrollElementRef>
  <Box paddingY={4} paddingX={5}>
    <UnorderedList>
      <VirtualList
        {items}
        itemHeight={20}
        containerHeight={240}
        scrollElement={scrollElementRef}
        spacerTag="li"
        measured
        getKey={(item) => item.id}
        let:item
      >
        <ListItem>{item.label}</ListItem>
      </VirtualList>
    </UnorderedList>
  </Box>
</ScrollGradient>
```

#### With OrderedList

Only the rendered items are in the DOM, so an [OrderedList](/components/OrderedList) would number them from 1. Set `native` on the `OrderedList` and pass `value={index + 1}` to each `ListItem`. Set `measured`, since items wrap onto more lines on narrow screens.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    ListItem,
    OrderedList,
    ScrollGradient,
    VirtualList,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const databases = ["billing", "orders", "inventory", "audit", "sessions"];

  const steps = Array.from({ length: 2000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    label: `Back up the ${databases[i % databases.length]} database`,
  }));

  let scrollElementRef = null;
</script>

<ScrollGradient height="240px" bind:scrollElementRef>
  <Box paddingY={4} paddingX={5}>
    <OrderedList native>
      <VirtualList
        items={steps}
        itemHeight={20}
        containerHeight={240}
        scrollElement={scrollElementRef}
        spacerTag="li"
        measured
        getKey={(item) => item.id}
        let:item
        let:index
      >
        <ListItem value={index + 1}>{item.label}</ListItem>
      </VirtualList>
    </OrderedList>
  </Box>
</ScrollGradient>
```

#### With RecursiveList

A [RecursiveList](/components/RecursiveList) renders every node, so window its top level instead. Render each top-level node as a `ListItem` with a `nested` `RecursiveList` of its children. Set `measured`, since each item is as tall as its subtree.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    ListItem,
    RecursiveList,
    ScrollGradient,
    UnorderedList,
    VirtualList,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const environments = ["production", "staging", "preview"];

  const services = Array.from({ length: 1000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `service-${String(i + 1).padStart(4, "0")}`,
    nodes: environments.slice(0, (i % 3) + 1).map((environment) => ({
      text: environment,
      href: `#service-${i + 1}-${environment}`,
    })),
  }));

  let scrollElementRef = null;
</script>

<ScrollGradient height="240px" bind:scrollElementRef>
  <Box paddingY={4} paddingX={5}>
    <UnorderedList>
      <VirtualList
        items={services}
        itemHeight={60}
        containerHeight={240}
        scrollElement={scrollElementRef}
        spacerTag="li"
        measured
        getKey={(item) => item.id}
        let:item
      >
        <ListItem>
          {item.text}
          <RecursiveList nodes={item.nodes} nested />
        </ListItem>
      </VirtualList>
    </UnorderedList>
  </Box>
</ScrollGradient>
```

---

### Component API

#### `VirtualList` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the list container element.<br />`null` when `spacerTag` is set. | `null` |
| `items` | `ReadonlyArray<Item>` | Specify the items to render.<br />A browser scrolls only so far, about 17.9 million pixels in Firefox and<br />33.5 million in Chrome and Safari. A longer list ends at the last item<br />that fits, so page or filter a list that large. | `[]` |
| `itemHeight` | `number` | Specify the height of each item in pixels.<br />When `measured` is `true`, this is only the estimate for items not yet measured. | `40` |
| `containerHeight` | `number` | Specify the height of the scrollable viewport in pixels.<br />When `scrollElement` is set, match this to that element's visible height. | `300` |
| `overscan` | `number` | Specify the number of items to render above and below the viewport | `3` |
| `threshold` | `number` | Specify the minimum number of items before windowing activates.<br />Below it, every item renders. | `0` |
| `measured` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to measure each rendered item with `ResizeObserver`<br />instead of assuming every item is `itemHeight` tall. | `false` |
| `getKey` | `(item: Item, index: number) => string \| number` | Specify the key for each item.<br />Defaults to the item's index, which is only stable when items are appended. | `(_item, index) => index` |
| `optimizeFastScroll` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to keep the rendered items in view during very fast<br />scrolling, such as a scrollbar drag, instead of showing blank space until<br />new items render.<br />The items then follow the scroll a frame behind, and pause while the main<br />thread is busy.<br />Ignored when `scrollElement` is set. | `false` |
| `scrollElement` | `null \| HTMLElement` | Specify an ancestor element that scrolls the list, such as the<br />`scrollElementRef` of a `ScrollGradient`.<br />When set, the list does not scroll itself. | `null` |
| `spacerTag` | `undefined \| keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` | Specify a tag to render items straight into the parent element,<br />such as the list of a `ContainedList`, without a container of their own.<br />Two elements of this tag above and below the items hold the scroll height,<br />so use one the parent accepts as a child, like `"li"` inside a list.<br />Requires `scrollElement`. Each item must render exactly one element.<br />Rest props have no element to land on, so they are dropped. | _undefined_ |

#### `VirtualList` slots

| Slot      | Detail                                              |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | `{<br />  item: Item;<br />  index: number;<br />}` |

#### `VirtualList` dispatched events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on:scrollend` | `{<br />  scrollTop: number;<br />  scrollHeight: number;<br />  clientHeight: number;<br />}` | Dispatched when the list is scrolled near the bottom (load-more signal).<br />Not the browser's native `scrollend` (scroll stopped). |

#### `VirtualList` $$restProps

`VirtualList` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.
